It all starts with location.   The hotel is steps from the Tube and the Tower of London.   With its proximity to transportation it was easy to get around London.   
The hotel itself is modern.    The room was as advertised.   Bed was extremely comfortable.   Blackout curtains were a bonus.   
Bathroom is small.  
The lobby has 24 hour food service.   A nice bar and coffee shop.   Plenty of places to relax
In the ‘living room’.  
The staff was extremely helpful and friendly.   
I would stay there again

author: Matthew D
title: Lovely hotel with great views of the Tower of London
text: We had a lovely long weekend at this hotel. The views are amazing of the Tower of London. Rooms are clean and comfortable! The staff were all very helpful and professional. Also a great food truck outside.

author: Daniel Z
title: London Solo Trip
text:
This hotel is in a great location and perfect for a solo traveler.  The Tower Hill Tube stop is located just outside the hotel which makes it easy to traverse London quickly.  The rooms are intentionally small, but there is plenty of storage space for luggage.  The staff was quick to respond to anything I needed.

Highlights:  The lobby was really cool and felt more like a residence than a hotel. The rooftop bar also has a great view of Tower of London and Tower Bridge.  The air con worked great!

author: Alice Y
title: Great Location and Good Amenities Overall
text:
We booked this hotel so we were fairly Central the day after a concert at The London Arena. We could not have asked for a better location. You step out of Tower Hill tube and you are there. 

We arrived early and able to check in our bags to avoid walking around with them. Check in was seamless. The room was adequate and clean with a large bed positioned so you/and or partner could sleep as close to as you normally would as possible. This is hard to explain but trust me..... it's a.real plus. 

Everything is managed from an iPad. We.did struggle with the air con and could not get a low temperature. Given we were in the midst of a heatwave this was a small glitch. There are toiletries and a hair dryer available as well as USB plugs as well as continental options and UK conventional. There are no tea/coffee facilities in the room but there is a 24/7 bar and food service. After getting back from our concert about 1am we were able to get a freshly made pizza and drink. 

You are within walking distance to The Tower of London, Tower Bridge, The Shard, HMS Belfast  and Borough Market if you are relatively active. 

The downside for us was the room temperature and general access downstairs toilets which were messy and not smelling great..

These were minor quibbles given an otherwise positive stay.

author: Rosie O
title: Do not stay here in the Summer. Its a rip-off.
text:
Extremely disappointing experience at CitizenM Tower of London. I had booked a two-week stay but ended up cutting it short because the conditions became unbearable.
The air conditioning did not work for my entire stay, despite the staff moving me to two different rooms. Unfortunately, every room had the same issue. The staff genuinely tried their best and were courteous throughout, but it was clearly beyond their control.
The only compensation offered was a 10% discount, which felt wholly inadequate given the circumstances. Trying to sleep in a hot, airless room during summer was simply unacceptable.
The rooms are already exceptionally small, and without functioning air conditioning they become extremely uncomfortable. What is marketed as a modern, comfortable hotel felt more like a budget hostel charging premium hotel prices while failing to provide one of the most basic amenities.
My advice is simple: avoid staying here during the summer. If the air conditioning fails, there is no meaningful backup or solution. Sadly, after this experience, I will never stay at CitizenM Tower of London again.

author: Charlie V
title: Ali and Tariq - Staff of the year!
text:
I would like to express my sincere appreciation for the exceptional staff at Tower Hill, particularly Ali and Tariq, who were absolutely amazing.

Unfortunately, when we checked out, my mother accidentally left her medication in the room fridge. We did not realise until several hours later while we were at Heathrow Airport. This medication is essential for her health and wellbeing, and without it she would have been in a very serious situation. To make matters worse, we were due to leave London the following morning.

We called CitizenM with very little hope that the medication would still be there and were already preparing to arrange an emergency doctor's appointment late that evening to obtain a replacement prescription. We spoke to Tariq, who immediately confirmed that the medication had been found and safely stored.

Tariq was incredibly helpful, reassuring, and genuinely a joy to speak with. His sense of humour immediately put us at ease during what was a very stressful situation. He showed a remarkable level of care and went above and beyond to help us.

We then spoke with Ali to arrange collection and delivery of the medication. Quite simply, Ali was second to none. He demonstrated outstanding care, professionalism, and a genuine desire to help. He took great care in ensuring the medication was handed to the correct driver, tracked the delivery, and kept everyone informed throughout the process. His communication skills were exceptional, and we are so grateful for everything he did.

At one point, a driver cancelled on us and we were incorrectly charged. Ali once again showed incredible care by advising us to dispute the charge, which was ultimately successful. He was also an absolute pleasure to speak with throughout the entire experience.

I cannot emphasise enough how wonderful these members of staff are, along with everyone else we encountered during our stay. We absolutely adore Ali and Tariq and wish them every success in the future. As dramatic as it may sound, they genuinely helped save my mother's life, and for that I will be eternally grateful.

author: Ruby G
title: Best Service Experience
text: Staying at this hotel was utter bliss !!! Not only was the hotel beautifully curated,  our room, stylish, funky, with breathtaking views and the most comfortable mattress, but the thing that made our stay so special was the service. From the minute we arrived it was like the team were looking to anticipate and understand who we were, why we were there and how they could make our stay memorable , ultimately ensuring that we should feel totally spoiled. There was a wonderful man at the reception area , who when he realised it was a special family trip for myself and my daughter,  went totally above and beyond to ensure we were well looked after. This also happened when we used the roof top bar,  it was like they were one step ahead and looking after us . I must call out a lovely girl who came to us as we went to sit in the rooftop bar and told us ‘there’s a more comfortable table, with a better view’ .  A really special stay and would totally recommend xx

author: Freya V
title: Very central and convenient to everything.
text: A very comfortable hotel in the center of London, very close to the Tower of London, and it even has a subway stop right next to it. As for transportation, I would say it is top-notch. It has a spacious entrance hall, and the check-in and check-out process is self-service and very quick. We also had breakfast, which I personally recommend; it costs a bit but has excellent quality products, both savory and sweet. All the staff is very friendly. The room is very nice; we had one on the first floor with a view of the Tower. There is no possibility to have lunch or dinner there, but there are many places nearby within walking distance, or you can order something to be delivered. Additionally, on the seventh floor, they also have a bar open all evening. The bed is very comfortable, the room is spotless, and everything is controlled from the tablet. Highly recommended.

author: Jessica P
title: A shocking experience at The Citizen Hotel  Tower Hill
text:
Friday June 5th
I have been waiting to speak to a member of staff now for 50 minutes - still waiting 
My daughter, who
Suffers  from the chronic condition Crohns Disease found herself desperately needing the toilet. She has a card but couldn’t access it quickly enough ,   
She ran into Citizen M on Tower Hill and ran towards the toilets.  She literally was desperate and in a state of distress 
She was physically prevented from entering the toilets and a male member of staff blocked her way on the stairs 
She pleaded with him
She told him she suffered from a dibilitating disease. 
She was forced to leave and the inevitable happened.  She was allowed access in the nearby Double Tree Hotel clearly in tears and very distressed 
Irrespective of the fact that she wasn’t a guest the member of staff showed no compassion, understanding or appropriate training.  
To make matters worse I still cannot speak to a member of staff re this issue.  
She is a young woman dealing with a terrible condition and this experience has traumatised her , 
We will never stay at a CM hotel again

author: Pierre M
title: Mistake for 65 year old  couple.
text: I am a Marriott customer for 25 years, we've been quite pleased  95% of the time. This is not the Marriott experience.  For older couples  that need to stretch out -and have some comfort, this did not work for us.  Tiny room, bed with walls on 3 sides, no coffee maker, no water in room,  stiff pillows, tight quarters,  firm bed.  Size of a room on a ship.  Yes, the pictures on the website are accurate. Thought we saw some larger rooms but they are actually the handicap accessible rooms, which we could not have.  Big mistake.  I need my soft Marriott bed and pillows!

author: Ella U
title: Stay here as a solo traveler - nothing else
text:
Came for 3 nights on a work trip, probably a bit too long of a stay given how tiny these rooms are but it fit my needs. Stay here if you are not fussy and want a prime location. Do NOT stay here if you're a family or even couple (unless you're ok being in confined areas). Only real downside is some moron set the fire alarm off at 6 am with their hair dryer and work the whole hotel up who had to evacuate.
Pros: 
Convenient location, walkable to central London for work
Cheap, good value for what you pay compared to other hotels @ 2x the cost
Marriott points
Cons:
Rooms are smaller than an NYC studio. Almost like a prison cell
Bathroom/shower is so small you feel like you're in a submarine. If you need to go in the am like the rest of us, other person will hear everything (see couples note above)

Overall I'd recommend staying here if you are a single dude and don't need space. Women might find amenities missing and nowhere nearly enough closet space.

author: Taylor Q
title: Full service hotel
text: Located by Tower of London, directly by the Thames with the train directly below. Rooftop bar had amazing views of the city. There is also a bar and restaurant that served food and drink 24/7. The main lobby had plenty of seating and tables. There was never a time that we couldn’t sit and relax. There is also an outdoor patio that closed at 11. Breakfast is available for purchase as well and it’s quite good. The hotel is beautifully decorated and there are books everywhere to enjoy. Our room was just a little small, but we knew that based on previous reviews, the oversized bed and the view made up for that.

author: Marco Y
title: Worth a Visit
text:
1st time stay in Citizen M Tower  of London. Have previously stayed at the hotel in Glasgow, so we knew what to expect ie a pod room, remote control for lights, blinds etc. We were in Room 535 with a great view. Good shower and comfy bed. Large tv.  Great self check-in but staff on hand to assist if required. Breakfast was great, hot food, cold meats, cheese, fruit juice, cereals etc something for everyone. Large breakfast area very busy with guests. and with business people having coffee's working on their laptops.  All staff were friendly and chatty. We Njoyed a cocktail after a night out, again luvly staff. The main entrance is the usual quirky CitM style. We thoroughly  joyed our stay. Also in a great location, a tube ride from Kings X.  Also a nice outdoor seating area. also a wee coffee shop just inside entrance. A great area for local restaurants and bars to visit. 
 Highly Recommend a Visit  :)  :)

author: Harper D
title: Very compact layout with no temperature control
text:
Picked this hotel due to reviews, but did not enjoy our stay.  We had a room with a king size bed and view of the Tower.  

The room was tidy and clean, but its compact layout made it feel very cramped.  We only had one luggage with us and there was hardly any room to store and open up to get things in and out.  

The temperature was our biggest annoyance, though.  The iPad app suggests you can control the temperature of the room and turn on the fan, but it did not work at all.  There is no window to prop open and the air was stuffy and still.  I went downstairs to tell the hosts that it did not appear that our thermostsat was working, and they said they would adjust it on their end and it would take a few minutes to get cool.  (There ultimately was no difference whatsoever.)  While talking to the host, another hotel guest came up to complain about the air conditioning not working as well. I understand that they should have control over the AC. but the the inability to override and adjust the temperature while in the room and have to deal with the still air and closed-in feeling was pretty aggravating.  If you have ANY tendency to get claustrophobic, I do NOT recommend this room.  

The toilet and shower is also enclosed only by glass and you can hear everything.  You practically have no privacy while using the bathroom.  

There is a refrigerator, but no cups or coffee maker.  

We had forgotten to bring some toothpaste.  The iPad app indicated we could request some from the front desk, but when I went to ask for some, the hosts looked through their cabinets and determined they were out.  Hotels should always have that stocked.

The plus side for this hotel is that it is in an excellent location.  The Tower Hill train station is right next to to it and it is easy to get to and from places.  You are also right by the Tower Bridge and the views are excellent.  But those perks would not make me want to stay there again.

author: Chloe J
title: Great hotel, close to major attractions
text:
We actually stayed here in January 2025 fir 3 nights. We stayed in a room near the top floor w8th a view of the Tower Bridge which was nice to wake up to each morning. The hotel is very modern and the rooms have a few gimmicky things that other hotels wouldnt have which was a nice touch.
The hotel was quite costly for us but it was a nice treat and for a hotel with these views and practically in the city centre its what to expect. Would love to stay here again when next in London on a special occasion

author: Evan M
title: Bad neighborhood - good security at the hostel
text: The place is in a bad neighborhood with a lot of homeless og drug using people. Luckily security is good at the place.

author: Thomas C
title: Excellent stay
text: I had a wonderful stay at this hostel. The rooms are very spacious, the beds are comfortable, and everything was very clean, especially the bathrooms. The staff were extremely helpful, friendly, and always greeted me with a big smile. The only thing that could be improved is the air conditioning in the common sitting room, as it was quite hot there. Overall, a great experience, and I would definitely recommend this hostel!

author: Olivia W
title: Had a great stay
text: The room was great, big bed, very quiet and with much needed aircon. Nicely designed place with excellent roof bar open till 12. Had a few surprise perks thrown in which was nice. Really helpful and friendly staff. Great location. We used Lime bikes to see everything, 5 min ride to Colosseum, 20 mins to the Vatican and felt safer on the bikes during the night. Near to the train station and the Terravision airport bus drop off. Only advise is to stick to the more populated/wider streets to get to to and from the hostel from the station. As soon as we arrived we walked through the middle of a bottle breaking fight! They couldn't care less about us so we just walked on through, lively ha. But the area was otherwise really nice. Would definitely stay there again.

author: Olivia T
title: GREAT HOSTEL
text: Amazing hostel, It succeded all my expectations, the rooms, the spaces, the rooftop. Everything was amazing

author: Hugo X
title: Amazing stay
text: The location of the hostel is perfect. Very near metro (Orange Line). Near to a lot of restaurants, the Termini Station and famous landmarks.

author: Charlie O
title: A great hostel
text: A perfect hostel, friendly and helpful staff, clean and comfortable. Good price.

author: Louis M
title: Comfortable Stay Near Roma Termini with Friendly Staff
text:
The hotel is about a 9-minute walk from Roma Termini train station. It features a bar and dining area on the first floor, as well as a rooftop bar. The staff speak fluent English, and the check-in process is quick and efficient. The room was clean, and overall we were satisfied with our stay.

Suggestions for improvement: The water pressure in the shower could be stronger. It would also be a nice addition if slippers were provided as part of the room amenities.

author: Diego U
title: Great place to stay
text: Ive stayed for 3 nights in this Hostel in Rome and I didnt have thing to complain about. Staff where great and the rooftop bar is very nice too

author: Matthew M
title: Horrible experience
text:
I didn't have any cleaning done during the 4 days I was there, neither bed making nor towel changes.

The bedroom furniture is old and broken; a large puddle forms in one corner of the bathroom whenever the shower is used because the shower screen is faulty; there's a 3 cm nail sticking out of the floor that's a hazard where there used to be a doorstop, which is no longer there.

On Sunday afternoon, about 40 young Spaniards arrived and spread out throughout the accommodation. In my case, they're next to, across from, and even above my room. Since they arrived, they've been shouting, running around, banging on the walls, and slamming on my door… it's impossible to get any rest. The staff do nothing; they don't maintain order or respect the basic rules of coexistence, including the need for a place to rest.

author: Wyatt Q
title: Great location and facilities, shame other guests are stronzo'sss
text:
Great location, some might not like the ethnic feel of the neighbourhood and slight roughness around the edges but felt safe no issues. Building and private double room nice, maybe a little black mould on shower edges could be improved. Friendly check-in and front desk. Didn't eat or drink, went to Miki's up the street for breakfast but some good other options like Gelataria Fasso and Cafe Ciamei nearby. 

Main issue was sleep. Though bed was very comfy, air con didn't work so was sleeping hot. Improved after switching off scalding got bathroom radiator. But biggest issues were the other guests. 1st night fine, street noise a little louder than ideal but that's the area. 2nd night despite the thick walls, the teenager next door seemed to be making his best attempt at shouting loudly on the phone at 11pm at night. Worst was 3rd night, a Friday night when some Italian boys were drunkenly singing loudly in the corridors intermittently until after midnight. Thankfully they STFU eventually. Maybe being 40 year olds we don't have patience for this sort of behaviour but come on, is corridors and stairway of a hostel the right place for this? Maybe the location of the room next to the stairwell was bad luck I don't know. 

Wasn't much of a hostel feel otherwise as others have commented, no kitchen areas and though there is the relaxation area, full of teenagers being classic teenagers. Getting the double room for a good value of £130/150Eur per night (using a promo code that needed several attempts on different devices) meant I am not completely disappointed. Nice style to the place, room was nicely decorated and furnished though no hand towel, usb chargers or safe within the room if you care about these things. It's a hostel masquerading as something slightly premium so there are compromises. In our case, the other guests left us with poor impression of the place which is a shame.

author: Paolo S
title: Very good place
text: Good place, clean and nicely place

author: Olivia S
title: Nice Stay
text:
Cool Hostel near the Train Station. Clean Room and very Good Service an Staff. 
Will stay again there.

author: Laura L
title: Worst costumer service ever in a horrible part of the city
text:
My experience at Generator Rome was extremely disappointing, not because of an administrative mistake — which can happen — but because of how the situation was handled by the reception staff and the overall conditions of the hostel.

I had made two separate reservations: one for three nights sharing a room with my sister, and a second reservation for myself for the following nights. At check-in, I explicitly asked the receptionist whether I needed to check out and check back in between the two reservations. She clearly told me that it was not necessary and that I could stay in the same bed. Unfortunately, neither of us noticed at that moment that there was a one-night gap between the two bookings.

On the morning my sister checked out, everything seemed fine. Later that afternoon, when we returned to collect her belongings, a member of the cleaning staff informed me that the system showed I should have vacated the bed. I calmly explained that there must be a mistake and that I would go to reception to clarify the situation.

Before I even reached the front desk, a different receptionist confronted me in the hallway and started shouting at me, demanding that I leave the room immediately. He spoke in an aggressive, accusatory, and humiliating manner, without allowing me to properly explain what had happened.

When I reviewed my reservation, I immediately acknowledged my mistake, checked out, and paid for another room without any resistance. However, what I found particularly upsetting was that this receptionist refused to acknowledge that the situation was also the result of incorrect information provided by the hotel staff at check-in. He repeatedly insisted that it was exclusively my responsibility to notice the error, while ignoring the hotel’s responsibility to provide accurate information to guests.

The situation could have been resolved calmly and professionally. Instead, it escalated into verbal aggression. The unprofessional behavior continued when I asked whether I could wait in the common area until the official check-in time. The same receptionist replied in a mocking and sarcastic tone, saying, “Obviously you can already go to the room, that’s your card.”

Beyond this incident, the hostel itself was also disappointing. The location is poor and feels unsafe, especially at night. It is directly across from a market, which means the surrounding area is unpleasant and dirty. If your room is on the lower floors, there is a strong and persistent smell of fish, which was extremely uncomfortable.

Additionally, cleanliness is clearly not a strong point of this hostel. Common areas and rooms did not feel properly maintained, which only added to the overall negative experience.

I never refused to pay nor to take responsibility once the mistake was clear. What was unacceptable was being yelled at, spoken to with sarcasm, and treated with contempt for an honest mistake — especially one that involved misinformation from staff.

Hostels are meant to be welcoming places for travelers. Unfortunately, due to the aggressive attitude of the reception staff, poor cleanliness, and uncomfortable location, I would not recommend staying at Generator Rome.

author: Abigail X
title: Stay at Rome Generator
text: Neighborhood isn't nice, there is a market across the street and people are always waking about. A little bit far from the important points of the city (wouldn't recommend while traveling alone). Don't offer any amenities (shampoo, shower gel, towel). Kind of expensive for what it was.

author: Grace A
title: Brutal Cancelation and Refund Policy: Profit before People
text: I booked for a week in Rome over Christmas 2025 when there was a special Black Friday offer available. The cost was £209 for a dorm bed. My elderly father then got ill and I couldn't make the trip. I informed the hostel asking if I could reschedule the stay for a later date. The reply was courteous and efficient but the answer was a definite NO. Not even the offer of a change of dates with an extra charge to cover this. Even the budget airline that I had booked with offers this facility (yes, at a price). So the company gets this money pretty much for zero effort. I wonder what percentage of their income comes from this source. If I was to book with them again (which will never happen) I would book a night or two and then sort things out when I'm there. Quoting Terms and Conditions is all very well (but who studies them for every hostel?) but a little bit of compassion and flexibility would have been rather more appropriate especially during the season of supposed good-will.

author: Nora V
title: Horrible and with break-in included
text:
The security one an edge, all the time behind us and looking bad, threatened to hit us. A man broke into our room because the security of the doors is terrible, they open with a bang! On top of that, the reception didn't do anything, we couldn't sleep in our entire stay.

I DON'T RECOMMEND IT, ON TOP OF THAT, THE AREA IS TERRIBLE

author: Aaron M

text: Really enjoyed staying in the Generator Hostel, amazing staff, clean and warm room, comfy bed, handy access to metro and trains. Great value for money. 10/10 recommended.

author: Antoine V
title: All right though there is a little BUT
text: Overall everything was great unfortunately the bathroom was not spotless the taps were full of rust el toilet leaked water. After all, everything great

author: Nathan M
title: Many positive experiences but ONE.
text:
The hostel is clean and the rooms are spacious.  I had a group of students and it was simple enough.  The food was not up to my expectations.  I looked forward to breakfast but it was the same for the days we were there.  The worst experience was when the group in-charge got her bag stolen at the reception area.  The receptionist was very polite and she sent us to the police station to make a report, which we did.  When we returned we found a new person at the reception, Lorenzo, if I am not wrong.  He was outright rude and disrespectful.  We called him out for this but he refused to back down and even had the audacity to doubt whether the lady even had the bag in the first place.  I was outright peeved.  The hostel manager, though, is made of kindness and so that kind of made up for Mr. Lorenzo's insolence. 
It seems they know thieves come in from the street when a group arrives, but there is no written warning... they could not allow us to see the CCTV footage because the laws don't allow it.  Eiiih!! 

No matter how broke I am, it will be the last place I think of staying in in Rome.

author: Holly H
title: Good location
text: Good location close too termini station and metro easy to move around the city. Neighborhood can look kind of sketchy people always be alert

author: Julien T
title: Thanks Kyara!
text: Kyara was very helpful and great to work with, also provided he was t customer service. Very polite and friendly!

author: Laura I

text: Brianna is an amazing woman! I really appreciate her exceptional customer service skills as a lobby host. She made me feel at home and safe while traveling solo. I will be recommending her and this hotel to everyone I know. The view on the rooftop is amazing, the best in the city.

author: Katie C
text: We initially had a room on the 4th floor and were a little dissatisfied. Then I asked at the reception and we got a room on the 19th floor for a nightly surcharge. For that, I thank Anthony, Eduardo, and Briona. The three of them gave everything to meet our request. Thank you for the great opportunity and the great stay.

author: Daisy T
title: Very nice hotel! Great staff
text: Fantastic stay, helpful staff, comfortable room considering it’s New York. Good food and location. Shoutout to Lily at the front desk, made everything better!

author: Lucas Q
title: Cash insurance

author: Leo R
title: Thank you Lily! Amazing stay
text: It was a great stay and thank you Lily for making it even more amazing

author: Joseph O
title: 100/10 for the best team ever.
text:
Location-  close to everything especially if you like walking to explore the city. Its just very central. 

Room - yes its very compact ( because its NYC and we couldn't expect much. if you are a traveller, its just the same size as those in Tokyo and Hong Kong). author: Katie N
title: A home
text: Not sure where should I start, this place is like a second home to me. I've been staying here accumulatively for a year give or take. The location is perfect you can reach any subway lines within 2-10 mins by walk (exept Queens/Brooklyn lines G,L,7,J,M,Z). Rooms are well design and very clean. author: Zoe N
title: Cocktails
text: Stopped by Arlo NoMad for drinks and had a fantastic experience. Aryn B made our cocktails and they were absolutely delicious perfectly balanced, flavorful, and beautifully presented. You did your thing girly!!!  Aryn was friendly, knowledgeable, and made the experience even better with excellent service. The atmosphere was great, and I’ll definitely be back. Highly recommend!

author: Isla E
title: Get what you pay for
text:
I stayed at Arlo NoMad for a business trip. It’s definitely on the cheaper side for a hotel in NYC, but unfortunately, you get what you pay for.

The rooms are unbelievably small. There was genuinely nowhere to open my suitcase, there’s no real closet, and the sink is in the bedroom. I can’t imagine staying here with another person—there is barely enough room for one person and their luggage.

Privacy was also an issue. My windows were directly above someone’s terrace and looked into the room next to me, so I ended up keeping the blinds closed for my entire stay. It made an already tiny room feel even more like a box.

I also noticed there was no cover on the peephole in my door, and there were visible gaps around the door. I don’t want to be dramatic about it, but it did make me feel less comfortable and secure in my room. I stay in hotels fairly often, and this isn’t something I typically encounter.

The service was frustrating and inconsistent as well. The hotel frequently texts asking if you need anything, but when I actually did, they weren’t particularly helpful. I asked them to bring a delivery up and was told they couldn’t leave it outside my door for “security purposes” and that I needed to come downstairs with my ID. I offered to show my ID at my room door, but they said no. I finally went downstairs, only to be told they didn’t need my ID after all.

Later, I asked if they could bring utensils up to my room and was told no, I needed to come downstairs and get them myself. It made the constant texts feel somewhat pointless.

Even the clock in my room was five minutes slow. It sounds minor, but when you’re traveling for business and working on a schedule, five minutes can make a difference.

The hotel was clean, and the price is cheap for New York, but that’s about where the positives ended for me. The best way I can describe Arlo NoMad is a clean, private hostel. If your priority is simply finding an inexpensive, clean place to sleep in Manhattan, maybe it works. But if you’re looking for comfort, privacy, space, or actual hotel-level service, I’d spend a little more and stay somewhere else.

And I definitely would not recommend it if you’re traveling with another person. There truly isn’t room for two people and their belongings.

author: Nathan S
title: Hidden Mandatory Fees – Not Transparent Pricing
text:
Be aware that Arlo NoMad does not have transparent pricing.

I booked through my company's travel platform, and my confirmation stated that I owed $0 at check-in. It never disclosed that there was a mandatory Urban Fee or what the amount would be. The fee also wasn't mentioned during check-in.

When I contacted the hotel, they directed me back to the booking platform. However, the booking platform informed me that hotels are responsible for providing mandatory fee information so it can be displayed during booking.

The issue isn't the amount—it's the lack of transparency. If a hotel knows your stay dates and room rate, mandatory fees should be included in the total price or clearly disclosed before you arrive. By the time you check in, it's too late to make an informed decision.

If you book here, be aware that the final cost of your stay may be higher than what you're shown when you reserve.

author: Lucia P
title: Thank you Shanace

author: Hannah L

author: Giulia C

author: Poppy O

Thank you for making my girlfriend’s birthday celebration so special we really appreciate everything you did!

author: Lea G
title: Dream View, Full Circle 💛
text:
A few years ago, I surprised my daughter with a a trip to NYC and a stay at Arlo NoMad because it her dream since birth. I'll never forget the look on her face when she saw the skyline from our room. Those memories became some of our favorites.

Now, we're coming back—but this time, it's even more meaningful. We're staying here again as I help move her to New York for college. It feels like life has come full circle. What started as a special mother-daughter trip has become the place where we celebrate the beginning of her next chapter.

Arlo NoMad has always felt like more than just a hotel. The views are breathtaking, the atmosphere is modern and welcoming, the rooms are comfortable, and the location couldn't be better for exploring the city. But what makes this place unforgettable for me is the memories we've made here.

Thank you for being part of two of the most important moments in our lives. We'll always have a special place in our hearts for Arlo NoMad, and I know this will always be the place I stay. ❤️

author: Sophia N

author: Caleb A

All rooms (I had my friend staying in different floor) stinking of sewer.

author: Evie G

author: Olivia B
title: Horrible

Horrible expérience.
Very arrogant personnel and not friendly at all.
Room dirty and noisy.
Room to small .

author: Ruby K
title: Just ok
text:
Picked this location to have a room with AC, a bathroom, and an elevator for my 46-year-old disabled wife.  Were frequent travelers and know the Europe typical hotel room, so we knew what to expect.  Unfortunately, yes there is an elevator, but you must go up stair to get to it. Then up or down more stairs to get to our room. This was bummer but we made it work. 

The room was about 13X13 feet total. Not that unusual for Europe standards, we understand.  The two twin beds were in horrible shape and very uncomfortable. The AC did not actually blow cold air. You were not able to adjust it and it blew maybe 80 deg. air all day.  By 9 AM, the room was miserable. Again, Europe does not like AC like the West likes. The bathroom was small but it worked out fine.  

The room was so small there is no room to open a bag that's not on the bed. It was very hot, and the beds were a joke. The only positive was it had a bathroom. 

The location is right across from the train station and was good if that's what you need.  Plenty of stuff to do walking distance from this location. Coffee right across the street and tour bus stop a block away. The location was nice, the room was just okay for 1 night. 

We booked it for the elevator, AC, and bathroom. We actually got 1 out of 3 of those.  We won't go back.

author: Joseph S
title: If Hell was a hotel……
text:
⭐️ One star, and that’s only because TripAdvisor won’t let me give zero.

Checking in felt less like arriving at a hotel and more like being processed at a low-budget holding facility. The front desk staff member didn’t speak, didn’t greet, and didn’t acknowledge me in any recognisable form of customer service. Just grunts, paperwork shoved across the desk, and a card machine aggressively pushed in my direction. I half expected a barcode to be stamped on my wrist.

The building itself is a lost cause. It’s tired, neglected, and clearly hasn’t seen investment since optimism was still a thing. The photos online are a complete fantasy. If you’re booking based on those, congratulations, you’ve been catfished by a hotel.

The room was genuinely revolting. Filthy, smelly, and visibly falling apart. Cracked sink, laminate flooring lifting and rotting underneath, and mould in the bathroom that looked well established, like it pays rent. The smell suggested a long-standing truce between damp, decay, and despair.

Sleep was impossible. A constant industrial AC compressor screamed outside the window all night, accompanied by a random broken fan or mechanical noise inside the walls that kicked in intermittently, just to keep my nervous system alert. The bed was equally criminal, uncomfortable enough to make you question your life choices.

Despite the room already resembling the aftermath of a structural collapse, they still demanded a £100 damage deposit. Bold. Impressive, even. Charging guests to protect what is already beyond saving.

No information whatsoever about breakfast. No timings, no location, nothing. I left early and ate at the airport, which was cleaner, calmer, and somehow felt luxurious by comparison.

The only positive is the proximity to King’s Cross, which makes escaping faster.

I’ve stayed and worked in so-called third world countries with better facilities, higher cleanliness standards, and warmer customer service.

Avoid this place like the plague. I wouldn’t let my dog stay here. Honestly, I wouldn’t leave a houseplant unattended in that room.

author: Lucy N
title: Good base to explore from
text:
This hotel isn't modern and looks dated but it is worth what you pay for and I would definitely stay here again. If you are looking for a cheap hotel to explore from, this is right for you. If you want a 4 star or above experience, you will be disappointed. I didn't read the other reviews until I went to write this and am glad that I didn't as otherwise I wouldn't have booked. 
Positives:
Price - it was cheap compared to other hotels in central London.
Reception - 24/7. Great staff, I arrived exhausted and reception arranged for a staff member to carry my luggage to my room for me. I didn't even ask, they just offered the service. They also were happy for me to leave a parcel at reception to collect, and were really helpful with directions when I needed them.
Location - It is literally opposite Kings Cross Station. It is all about the location peoples!
Cleaners - every single day, even though I said they didn't need to. 
Air conditioning - I managed to be in London in the middle of a heat wave. The air conditioner did not miss a beat, I was even cold one night.
Fridge - I tried several other nearby hotels nearby and none had fridges in the rooms. If you need one, it is worthwhile asking the question before you book.
Negatives:
Stairs - there are 4 steps from the road to reception and then more stairs to the elevator. The elevator also only goes to the 3rd floor and there are 4 floors. If you struggle with stairs this is probably not the place for you.
Noise - it didn't bother me but if you are a light sleeper you will probably hear the trains as the underground goes underneath the hotel.
Bed - it is a camper bed so not luxury sleeping, although the mattress was acceptable.
Restaurant - there isn't one. They have an arrangement with a restaurant around the corner where you get 10% off if you mention that you're staying here.

author: Alexander U
title: An excellent, affordable hotel within 5 minutes walk of St.Pancras/Kings Cross stations.
text: We booked in at very short notice. The young man on reception was so helpful carrying our heavy suitcases up some stairs to the elevator. Our room was spacious and with excellent air conditioning. Very comfortable beds and spotlessly clean.

author: Rosie Y
title: Disgusting wet floor
text: Very disappointing stay. The floor in our room was wet with water coming up from underneath, which was disgusting and clearly indicates a maintenance issue. When we reported it, the receptionist was cold and showed no concern or apology. It felt like they already knew about the faulty room. Poor customer service and poor room conditions. I would not recommend this hotel.

author: Owen J
title: The saving grace is the location.
text:
The hotel is old and the furst sight was disappointing.
It looks absolutely rundown from the outside and it is.
To access the lift, you have to carry your luggage down a flight of steep stairs which defeats tge point of wanting to stay in a hotel with lift access.
The room is small and the bed is ubcomforatble.
The toilet though is clean.
The only saving grace is the location which is just across from the train station.

author: Lauren E
title: Great location, that's all folks.
text:
Great location opposite the station to the world. Ground floor room. Two single beds. Window facing on to the street so anyone can see in. They need to put some one way privacy film on.
Sleep quality ok but that may be as we were so tired.
The bathroom had issues. The toilet seat was obviously a replacement and did not fit. The seat kept veering off to the side as it was loose. Not luxurious by any stretch of the imagination but I knew that when i booked it. I would stay again.

author: Emma C
title: Dreadful place- avoid
text: Room was awful. Tired, very cold (I was freezing at night) and although it had a window it looked onto another window so the curtains were closed at all times. There were no restaurant facilities. Breakfast was only available from 8am from the family run eatery around the corner. Misleading photographs.  My advice would be to stay somewhere else. There is a premier in further along Euston Road. Better value for money.

author: Juan A
title: One night stay
text:
Positive location,price room was not to bad clean bedding but camp beds ,bathroom with shower ,shower good had tea and coffee making and fridge .

Security someone at desk 24/7.

Bad was the wooden flooring all chipped ,curtains very poor and underground all the time noise from the tubes ,your not told this also your not told about the 100 pound deposit in case you damage any think that you pay on arrival,I cannot find any think on there websightvabout it ,it’s a puss take for that place

author: Leo A
title: Cheap and cheerful for an overnight  stay but not a first choice place to stay
text:
Whilst its not the best hotel for a number of reasons it does have some positives

If you are taking your partner for a fancy weekend break its not for you, however I was on my own and needed somewhere to stay at a reasonable price, and it was £100 cheaper than everywhere else
Positives are  - the location, the price, I had my own bathroom and toilet, I used my own coffee making stuff provided in the room including my own fridge, and the room was reasonably clean. The desk is staffed 24 hours a day so security is good

Negatives are - the room was so small I could touch both walls with my hands when I was in bed, the mattress was terrible with a sag in the middle, and the bed was a camper bed version, the underground system runs beneath the hotel and I heard the trains every ten  minutes. Doors were banging loud even at 4am in the morning, and the person next door used the hair dryer which sounded like it was in my room. The room was cold (but I like it like that) 
I would only use it again if I had to, but now I know what to expect, its a cheap and cheerful quick fix hotel for a very short stay

author: Joseph K
title: I lasted 45 minutes-1 HR.
text: I am not super picky when traveling. As long as it’s clean and safe. I decided to come a day early before my sister arrives and we go to our hotel. I booked last minute through Expedia, and the low reviews were mostly for noise which doesn’t bother me. Some people wrote that it was clean, and the MUST be paid reviews because I was grossed out the second I walked in. I tried to give benefit of the doubt, but after getting into my room it instantly gave me”pay by the hour” vibes - the white towels were brown tinged, there were gross stains in the sheets, hair, possible bug(s) - I didn’t get too close. The toilet had some slug looking slime ball under it. And the SMELL. My lungs still hurt from the overuse of chemical cleaners and spray.  I told the front desk that it was disgusting. I’ve stayed in hostels, and cots in clinics in developing countries on volunteer trips that were cleaner. With an hour or so I had another hotel booked. Hoping Expedia will at least credit me or my credit card will dispute it.

author: Juan A
title: Not staying again
text:
Room was clean and had all the things we needed for an overnight stay. Staff were polite.
We stayed in room 105. The noise was awful. Big gap in the door.
Not a true double. Bed squashed against wall. The worst mattress ever.

author: Mathis C
title: Disgrace & disgusting
text: I’ve never been to a so unkept hotel! It’s a disgrace to are capital city, don’t ever think about booking this hotel please

author: Abigail J
title: Worst Hotel I have EVER Been Too!!!!
text:
Feeling very misled by the out of date pictures that are on the website. Booked via Booking.com. Lucky only stayed 1 night. 

When walking into the room there was clean water damage on the floor. But that wasn’t the worst. It felt like we were sleeping next to a sewer. The bathroom/ toilet stank. Gagging… 

2 maybe 3 floor tiles broken in the bathroom as well as the sink. Huge crack going right the way across it. No plug hole cover. 

Couldn’t have a cup of tea as there was a dirty cup and the other had a crack going right the way across it. 

I don’t expect 5* but I do expect a standard and this place did not have any standard…

author: Paolo F
title: Noisy and uncomfortable
text: I had a terrible night's sleep here. Noisy - doors that bang shut, fans running all night long, a bathroom that stank and had most of its tiles loose, and an uncomfortable bed with an uneven mattress. The only positives were the wifi worked well enough and the shower was good.

author: Noah S
title: AVOID. WORST HOTEL IVE EVER STAYED IN
text:
Honestly the worst hotel I’ve ever stayed in. AVOID AVOID AVOID. 
There are no locks on any of the rooms, the rooms are falling apart, the bedding is dirty and all split/torn and the bathroom is disgusting. I put towels down on the floor to avoid stepping on the floor! Also freezing, the ‘heating’ is non existent. I had to sleep in several layers and a coat. Doors slamming all hours of the night & the rooms are down very narrow corridors with lots of up and down stairs. God forbid there was a fire because although this hotel is in dire need to being burnt to a crisp, you would too. 

The final straw was they have the CHEEK to ask for £100 damages deposit. I don’t think we could have made it look worse if we tried. 

The ONLY thing going for this hotel is the location to the Eurostar making it easy access. So if you fancy a bush trucker trial for the night, go ahead. If you value cleanliness, warmth & adequate comfort & safety - AVOID.

author: Kyle O
title: Cozy cocoon
text:
From 02/21/26 to 02/25/26
We stayed in this magnificent hotel in the month of February. The staff is very kind and smiling. The room was very good, not very big, but functional. The bed is very comfortable and it is possible to raise the bottom of the bed. The breakfast was very good. The hotel is in the center, very close to Termini station.

author: Chloe W
title: Simple, clean hotel
text: Simple but very locally situated hotel! It is very clean and has great, ALWAYS helpful staff. Our personal highlight was the bed, where the legs and head were adjustable and it possessed a massage function.

author: Evie A
title: Great place to stay!
text: We enjoyed our stay here, the room was larger than we expected for Rome. The room was comfortable and clean, AC and water pressure were excellent. The bed was extremely comfortable. Front desk was helpful. We did not eat breakfast here but it was available.

author: Lucas V
title: Clean and central
text:
Simple, clean hotel. Rooms are relatively small and have seen better days. Nevertheless, the hotel is a good starting point for discovering Rome.
However, a 4-star rating is nonsense.

author: Andrea F
title: Hotels within walking distance of Termini Station
text:
It is within walking distance of Termini Station.
I got one because there was a map of the city of Rome by the front desk.
It also provides information on the two-story sightseeing bus and other services.
There are two elevators, one of which is located on a stepped surface, making it inconvenient to roll suitcases.
The room is beautiful.
It was inconvenient because there was only one electrical socket in the bathroom and one and two below the room, not around the pillow.
The bed mats seemed to be distinctive, and there were advertising posters in the hotel hallways.
It seems that I was able to recline, but I didn't know how to use it and did something wasteful.
The bathroom has a bathtub, but the partition glass plate is only half the width of the bathtub, so if you are not careful, the bathroom will be flooded.
The surrounding area is also a high-rise hotel, so the view from the windows is not good.
It's close to the station, but it's on a road that's one stop away, so I didn't mind the noise of the cars at all.
Breakfast is on the first floor.

author: Morgan Y
title: Good place to stay if exploring Rome
text: This is a small hotel (one of many) in Rome. Very conveniently located two blocks away from Roma Termini. The rooms are small but comfortable (all rooms in Rome are like that - size is at a premium). We had a balcony, full bathroom and a bed which took up most of the room. Still, it did the trick and was very reasonably priced. Breakfast is not included; it is 15 euros a person.

author: Charlotte W
title: A pleasure
text: Nice hotel! Very clean! Wonderful location!

author: Sophia H
title: Not a 4 star experience
text: Convenient location to the train station (10 min walk), but not a 4 star hotel. The room was very large but the furniture was old and stained (sofa) and some of the plugs didn't work to charge devices. The bed was comfortable. This is a 2.5 star hotel.

author: Manon R
title: Give these Beds a try!
text:
We stayed in Rome for 3 days after a Mediterranean cruise.  S-i-L had not been to Rome before, while the wife and I had.  So she booked a 3-day post-cruise extension from the tour operator and had her hotel stay included.  Not wanting to pay the retail rate for her hotel, we stayed around the corner at the Augusta Lucilla Palazzo.  Our goal was to stay close to her and the Termini area.  

This hotel was quite a find for us.  We booked a standard double room and it was fine.  Not large, but you know, Europe.  But what we want to note for the record was: THE BED.  I don't think we've ever stayed at a hotel that had such a great bed.  Not only was it comfortable (just the right amount of softness for her and the right amount of firmness for me), but it was adjustable and had a vibrator to boot!  After two weeks of forced marches on excursions during the cruise, elevating the feet & legs was a real bonus.  The desk staff were very friendly and spoke excellent English.   Roomkeeping was immaculate.  If ever back in Rome again, we will most certainly consider staying here.

author: Lucas W
title: Great location, friendly and helpful staff.
text: The hotel is in a great location, lots of shops and restaurants nearby, close to Termini and easy walking distance to the Colosseum.  By North American standards, the room and bathroom were small but clean and comfortable.  The bed was soft enough to get comfortable, but firm enough to sleep well.  The people were very friendly and helpful.  Breakfast in the restaurant was very good as well.

author: Harper N
title: Among my favorite hotels in Rome
text: has become, over time, one of my favorite hotels in Rome. Very comfortable, recently renovated, very kind and efficient staff, it has all the qualities of a 4-star hotel at prices often a little cheaper than others in the same area. Highly recommended

author: Rosie T
title: Excelent
text: Everething was nice. Good location.

author: Dylan L
title: theft from the safe in the hotel room / theft from the hotel safe
text:
Room theft / robbery in a room:

1,000 euros were stolen from the safe in my room at the Augusta Lucilla Palazzo hotel. The hotel management (the manager is Christopher Rossi, as I was told) treated the situation with complete disregard despite the police investigation, and the reception staff were laughing at our problem. We did not even receive an apology, although everything is obvious: the theft happened on the very first day during room cleaning. They keep talking about negotiations with the insurance company and say they will contact us, but they don't even have our contact details. This is not the first theft from a room in this hotel — just read the reviews on Google Maps. Avoid this terrible place at all costs.
—-
My family and I were robbed of 1,000 euros from a safe in a room at the Augusta Lucilla Palazzo. Hotel management (manager Cristiano Rossi, I was told) spitted on the problem despite the police proceedings, people at the reception laughed at our problem. Not even an apology was made, although it is obvious - the theft happened on the first day during the cleaning of the room, they talk about negotiations with insurance and say they will be in touch (without having contact details). This isn't the first theft from a room at this hotel, read the reviews on Google Maps, avoid it with all your might - not to mention the fact that four stars at this hotel is pure fiction

author: Marco J
title: Augusta, at ease!
text: Nice hotel located close to Termini and with access to excellent gastronomic offers!!  The service is excellent!

author: Connor J
title: Didn’t live up to its reviews
text: The hotel is clean and comfortable with a good location close to the train station, but it does not have anything special going for it. The rooms are functional and lack any charm. The bathroom shower is small. The breakfast is standard fare.

author: Mia C
title: Great choice to stay in Rome
text: Very good hotel choice! Excellent breakfast for all tastes and in honor, helpful staff, I traveled with my 3 year old daughter and everything was very convenient. Very nice spacious room and clean. In the center of the city next to everything on foot and 5 minutes just from the terminal terminal of the train, metro and other means. I would recommend it and if I go back to Rome I will choose it again for my stay!

author: Grace A
title: Jumer was awesome!
text: Cheap and easy hotel. Staff were great especially Jumer who went above and beyond. So grateful for him. I’m not sure where the other negative reviews come from, yes the area is not as prestigious but if you want top class luxury then you won’t pay this fair price. The area felt a little unsafe a night but no worse than any other city, just use your common sense. Would recommend this place to stay for your holiday.

author: Benjamin M
title: A nice place to stay while you explore Rome
text:
Stayed in this hotel for a few days and we were absolutely satisfied with it. 
Firstly, the location is perfect: both the Colosseum and the Termini Station are within walking distance, 15 minutes on foot and you’re there. Secondly, the staff is very welcoming, friendly and helpful. Thirdly, the rooms are spacious, comfortable,  clean and equipped with all you need: from the TV set in the bedroom to perfumed skincare products in the bathroom. Though breakfast is always the same (a typical European breakfast, you know: sausages, eggs, cheese, bread, fruits, vegetables and pastries etc), everything is fresh and tasty and you never leave the hotel hungry. 

I recommend this hotel to those who are looking for a nice place to stay during their visit to Rome.

author: Giulia X
title: We felt very welcome
text: Great location and super comfortable beds. It has everything you need. Front desk people is super nice,  friendly and extremely helpful. We highly recommend

author: Rosie O
title: Lovely hotel near the Termini station 🫶
text:
Very nice hotel near the Termini station. Clean room, helpful staff, free and taste breakfast.
Thank you so much 🙏🙏
We will be back. Sure👍👍👍

author: Alexander P
title: Great value for money
text: We booked a twin & double room for 3 adults staying 2 nights. The hotel was easy to get to from Euston. The reception staff were welcoming upon arrival. The double room was a good size. The twin room was a lot smaller which was disappointing as 2 adults were staying in this room, but for 2 nights it was acceptable & manageable! The location was good as there was a tube stop less than 5 min walk away, with Waterloo being only a 10min walk away. There is a 24hr newsagent next door & a Tesco express less than 5 mins away as well. Overall great stay for the price. Would def recommend & stay again but would make people aware that it sits in a corner with train tracks running down two sides. That being said the trains, whilst frequent, are more like white background noise when inside. Also deliveries happen to the shops underneath so if anyone is a light sleeper then this may wake them up in the early hours of the morning. Another note to be aware of is whilst they have blackout curtains, they still let light in from the top, bottom & sides, so the room is not pitch black. Just something to be aware of if you like it dark! These are things to make people aware of - they did not disrupt our stay at all. I would def consider staying again.

author: Adam J
title: Would definitely stay again…..
text: Bit of a mix up with rooms to begin with but all staff very polite especially Jaz at breakfast who was so lovely - nothing was too much trouble and always happy. Kieran behind the bar was also very nice as well as the guy on reception who I didn’t manage to get the name of as well as the lady who helped him. 10 mins walk from Waterloo station and 3 mins walk from Southwark station so location was great. So many restaurants and a few pubs nearby so if you didn’t want to venture far is perfect. Would definitely stay here again.

author: Thomas G
title: Perfect for a short family break in London
text: Perfect for a short, budget family stay in London. The room was simple but clean and comfortable. Great for 2 adults and 2 children (12 & 8). Despite having a train line right next to it, it was quiet and we had no disruptions during our stay. In regards to location, we were a 10 minute walk from Waterloo in one direction and 10 minutes from Blackfriars in the other. The nearest underground was 2 minutes away and on the Jubilee Line. We could get anywhere we needed to be easily and quickly. Staff helpful & friendly. Will definitely be using again in the future.

author: Daisy E
title: Great Stay
text: Had a great stay, everything was perfect, Thank you!

author: Ethan Y
title: Weekend stay
text: Nathan was especially helpful wi try all our requests. Rhianna was also helpful when planning our day. Highly recommend.

author: Anna Q
title: Good location and value for money
text:
Great location with excellent transport links (we stayed to go to a concert at Wembley and the tube station is literally 2mins from the hotel!)
Room was a decent size and clean.  Got given fresh towels everyday which was a nice touch (only given if you asked for them!) 
We had a 2nd floor room overlooking the railway - we were worried about noise levels however it wasn't an issue.
Would stay again - good budget hotel in a good location

author: Tyler N
title: No issues at all great service
text: All amazing service and rooms were lovely

author: Katie V
title: Great stay
text: Staff were very friendly, kind and helpful. Rooms were tidy and clean, and very comfortable. Great location for access to Waterloo and tubes. Would definitely stay again!

author: Alice I
title: Great location and amazing service from Nathan
text: Great location and amazing service from Nathan

author: Luca T
title: Mario is the best
text: Hotel was good value for money. However Mario Profit was incredible and his customer service was second to none! Amazing guy!

author: Alexander D
title: Thanks Mario
text:
Perfectly decent hotel, only a couple of stops from anywhere on the tube and 24 hour pizza inn the bar.
Mario looked after us on the night shift, very helpful.

author: Mathis E
title: Excellent service
text: Mario done a sterling job behind the bar and fixing some food really late. Food came fast. Thanks for the service Mario top job. I will be back.

author: Mia P
title: Does the job needed. Friendly staff.
text:
Basic, clean, with air con. 
Staff very good. Sinmar's welcome was appreciated

author: Marco W
title: Good experience
text: Booked here to see the weeknd and it was perfect!! station next to it took us directly there. When checking in however we were looked up and down by a staff member with a funny look. Not sure why? We were just two girls coming for a concert. Apart from that no issues

author: Hannah C
title: Perfect
text: Had a great stay. Brilliant location, lovely clean quiet room. Neha and Nikita were great, so helpful and a very warm, smiling welcome. We'll be back again

author: Charlotte Y
title: Overnight stay
text: Great experience, Neha was lovely and very helpful:)

author: Abigail M
title: Overnight stay in London for special occasion
text: Super friendly and kind reception staff. Neha was so helpful and even put us in adjacent rooms!  Thank you ❤️

author: Kyle O
title: Great time here
text:
Thank you Neha and nikitha.
We had good time here

author: Giulia P
title: A great location for sightseeing
text: Southwark Travelodge is ideally located for sightseeing, and is metres away from Southwark tube. The hotel is clean, the staff are very welcoming and the breakfast is very good value for money. During school holidays (when I stayed) it can get busy at breakfast times and the Bar Cafe is quite small, so make sure you go for your breakfast early if you want you want your food in peace.

author: Anna F
title: Our stay
text: The location was perfect , next to a metro station and the staff were all very polite and helpful. In my opinion the rooms should have a small fridge that is necessary especially during summer season.

author: Lily H
title: last minute trip to Rome
text: my husband booked the accommodation and whilst I was expecting more of a hotel, this was more a b and b. Bed was comfortable and we did not lack anything. Breakfast was good. Gianluca was extremely helpful in his advice regarding sights and restaurants etc. My only complaint was that noise travelled through the walls from our neighbours' room (who were quite loud).

author: Emma O
title: Perfect stay in Rome
text:
We've recently spent a great week in Rome at Quod Libet. Host Gianluca was very friendly and helpful providing us with restaurant recommendations and tips for our visit. All the staff were very friendly. Clean and well maintained room with great breakfasts on the roof terrace. Great location for the Vatican and metro stop.  
We can highly recommend Quod Libet for a stay in Rome.

author: Connor C
title: A B and B at the price in a hotel
text:
In this bed and breakfast, the price is too expensive (more than 2 times the price indicated in the rooms) and the services are not those of a hotel.
Breakfast is based on products bought at the nearest supermarket, premium quality and even coffee is not good. A loft for coffee country. The croissant in the morning has no taste is should be replaced by Italian cupcakes Plus if you stay a few days, breakfast will always be the same. Last point as the rooms are in an old apartment, they are equipped with platform to hide the pipes. So on the first day you're gonna bump into the steps. Finally, the fineness of the walls between the rooms does not guarantee any privacy. 
Avoid if you have a motor handicap. Breakfast is on the terrace in a walk-up shed

author: Thomas S
title: We're so thankful we found this listing!
text:
I am going to preface this review with saying that I am not going to go into a lot of detail because I don't want to ruin any of the many wonderful surprises we experienced along the way.  

First off we would 100% stay here again.  With all of the places we have stayed over the years, Gianluca is without a doubt the best host we have ever had.  He did everything possible to ensure our stay in Rome was perfect.

Everything we wanted to see in Rome was walkable from QuodLibet.  The underground train is less than a block away if walking isn't your thing.  

The room was clean and had everything we needed for our stay.  The terrace was  beautiful.  

We're so thankful we found this listing!

author: William I
title: Definitely Recommended
text: This B&B was one of the top 2 places we stayed in our 2 week visit to Italy. The host is extremely thoughtful and helpful. The breakfast on the roof is also very good quality. We cannot recommend the QuodLibet enough.

author: Taylor L
title: Perfect short stay in Rome
text:
QuodLibet was just the best place to stay near the Vatican, I am so pleased we did.
Our stay was brief, but with our main focus being the Vatican this trip, it was a well chosen location.  The staff is also terrific, very friendly, especially Gianluca who is always available for help if and when needed.  Our room size was very large and we appreciated the welcome gift.  You will have to use the buzzer at the entrance and then go through a 2nd entrance as the rooms are located on the 4th floor of the building, but you are given all the access, keys etc. upon check in!  Nice breakfast on the rooftop terrace, where you can also go in the evening to lounge with a drink.

author: Lily Q
title: In the center of Rome as at home
text: We stayed at this B&B in the center of Rome and felt really at home! The location is simply perfect: in the Ottaviano area, well served, a step away from the metro station and very close to the Vatican. Gianluca, the owner, was very kind and always available with valuable advice to better experience the city. The rooms are spotless and attention to detail, and the breakfast is really great, plentiful and quality. A stay that left us only positive memories: we will definitely return and recommend it to everyone!

author: Connor V
title: Great gem of a spot, even better staff.
text: Lucas and the staff were so gracious and fun. We had a great time. All the staff made us feel like family. Thanks for the suggestions on mapping routes for us, Lucas.  Just minutes from the Vatican and Sistine Chapel. Room very well kept with good ac, tv with streaming capabilities and fair WiFi. Stocked minibar. Great shower. Highly recommend.

author: Lucas E
title: Best place. Stay here!
text:
This is the very cleanest most cared for property we have ever stayed in

It’s in a very convenient location near the Metro and 10 minute walk to the Vatican…unassuming building…with the kindest and friendliest hosts/owners.

Breakfast on the roof is terrific! 

I will never stay anywhere else in Rome!

author: Tyler A
title: Unforgettable stay
text: We stayed in this fantastic B&B at the gates of St. Peter's Square for four days and we really felt at home! Gianluca is a fantastic person, always ready to meet every need and guide you in every corner of Rome! The room was spacious and spotlessly clean, the breakfast excellent and plentiful with many choices! Recommended for all those who want to spend an unforgettable stay in Rome! If we return to Rome we would never look for anywhere else!

author: Charlie M
title: Beautiful!
text: What a lovely place to stay in Rome. Here we found a little gem. We had a spacious, quiet and lovingly appointed quadruple room with a large bathroom. USB sockets, smart TV, good Wi-Fi, daily room service, cleanliness, everything was flawless. The breakfast was very generous and varied and is offered on a covered roof terrace, which also invites you to linger at any time. Gianluca and his team are always friendly and extremely warm and helpful. Many little loving details make the stay here just beautiful and relaxing and we keep in our hearts an unforgettable memory of a dreamlike time in Rome. The location, practically almost on the Ottaviano Metro, is unbeatable. And of course: The accommodation is absolutely secure. Thank you for your hospitality!

author: Charlotte N
title: Amazing place !
text:
It’s a hidden gem in a great location, just steps from Ottaviano subway station and a few blocks from Saint Peter’s square. Room was impeccable, specially the washroom; great pillows! 
Breakfast at the rooftop was the perfect way to start your day. Service is 5 stars. Gianlucca goes above and beyond to make you feel at home. 
We travel from Canada to Rome right after conclave and they even arranged pick up service at the airport. A+

author: Louis D
title: When in Rome... stay here
text: Quiet street but just a block from the Ottaviano Metro stop and not far from the Vatican, with several terrific gelato shops right around the corner. Proprietor Gianluca and his crew are welcoming and helpful. Breakfasts on the rooftop deck are especially nice.

author: Abigail Q
title: Rome's Best Hotel
text:
WOW there's no place like the QuotLibet -- the best place in Rome to stay! Grazie Mille to Gianluca and his family and team... Shortly after you make your reservation at the QuodLibet you will receive an email from Gianluca, telling you you that as your trip gets closer he will arrange airport transfer for you. It only gets better from there. When you arrive at the guesthouse, someone is there to greet you at the door, and help take your belongings to the 4th floor check in. 

The bedrooms are SO CLEAN -- everything has been thought of, from snacks and drinks in the mini-fridge, to air conditioning, to fluffy towels and comfortable beds. You also have access to a fully stocked kitchen.

The rooftop breakfast is tailor made to each guest, and includes fresh fruits and yogurts, cappuccino made to order, hot cocoa, fresh breads, meats and cheeses, and omelets made to order. It's really amazing.

Gianluca is your guide to the town. Each day he carefully helps you plan out using public transport, and he points out the best restaurants where only the locals go. If you need anything, don't worry -- someone is just a text away on the What's App. 

I'd just like to thank Gianluca and the staff of the QuodLibet for making our trip to Rome so special. I know we will return to this wonderful guesthouse again and again.

author: Lucy V
title: Great experience in Rome!
text: We stayed for 9 nights here and completely enjoyed our experience.  The owner, Gianluca, was extremely helpful and friendly.  The staff was excellent and breakfast was delicious and plentiful - toast , bread, jams, yogurt, eggs any way you like them, with ham, cheese, juices and coffe or tea.  Our room was modern and  spacious. The property is just a very short walk from the metro station.  We would definitely stay again!

author: Oliver U
title: Just top!!!
text:
That's wonderful! Great location, super nice room! And a grandiose roof terrace with views to St. Peter's Basilica. Gianluca and his people were great hosts!! And you're 
in the middle of real Rome!!! Also: very good breakfast... and if you wanted to make something yourself - a complete kitchen was available! As a journalist, I have been to Rome countless times. In 5 star hotels and in B&Bs... but this one topped everything!

author: Maria R
title: Best choice
text: Visited Rome for the Inauguration Mass of the new Pope Leo. I couldn’t have made a better choice of accommodation. As an elderly solo traveller I wanted easy access to everything . The host Gianluca advised me of the best way to get to my destinations and also good places to eat. QuodLibet was very comfortable and welcoming for a solo traveller.

author: Louis Y
title: Great experience, super!
text: Absolutely recommended, the host very kind and welcoming, even the staff. Great and clean room. Breakfast on the terrace freshly prepared and with fresh food is the top, as is the location, a stone's throw from the Vatican. Congratulations for the excellent management of everything!

author: Gavin F
title: Well located, well kept rooms and very friendly and helpful managers
text: After a stay of 5 days we can say that this is a top B&B. Gianluca and his team are always friendly and helpful: on the first day we got tips on walks, routes, restaurants, sights, safety in Rome, etc. Less than 10 minutes you are at the Vatican and via the metro station nearby you can return to the B&B after a full day of walking by metro. A nice surprise was the birthday croissant for our son. Highly recommended! We will definitely return:)

author: Henry M
title: Gem in Prati!
text: Personalized and thoughtful interactions with owner highlighted our time here.  Lovely breakfast to start the day, along with recommendations to guide our first time in Roma.  Excellent dining recommendations.  Close to public transit, and within walking distance to the Vatican.  Weather permitting, romantic interludes on roof top are a must!

author: Matthew H
title: 40th street DbleTree. Outstanding
text: Most hospitable staff in NYC. Armani, Joanna, Naomi& Aaron. Sorry if i forgot anyone. All deserve a wage increase.

author: Rosie K
title: Unacceptable Front Desk Conduct
text:
Unfortunately, my experience with the Front Desk was extremely disappointing and, in one instance, completely unacceptable.
Throughout my stay, I encountered Front Desk employees who were consistently rude, poorly prepared, unprofessional, and unnecessarily hostile toward guests. Their attitude was not consistent with the level of courtesy and hospitality one would reasonably expect from a hotel operating under the Hilton brand.
More seriously, during one interaction, a Front Desk employee became aggressive to the point of physically grabbing my arm in what I perceived as an intimidating and threatening manner. Physical contact of this nature by a hotel employee toward a paying guest is completely unacceptable and, in my view, crosses a very serious line.

author: Rosie L
title: Great location and amazing staff!
text: Super great hotel with the best staff! Loved the location as it is super close to metro stations and the staff were amazing. Kevin and Austin were super great and helped us out both with the rooms and with trying to locate a card my friend lost. Even more important was also their overall attitude and great service!

author: Evie A
title: A wonderful stay with thoughtful touches, a great rooftop view, and excellent value for the price!
text:
It was my wife’s birthday, and we were truly surprised by the beautiful birthday decorations. We were pleasantly surprised and touched by this thoughtful gesture. Thank you so much for Amalia Lobby decoration
The room was clean and comfortable, and the rooftop bar with its stunning view was absolutely amazing. Overall, an excellent place with a great balance of price and quality. Highly recommended!

author: Erin I
title: The WORST service experience Ever
text:
The WORST service experience Ever. 
We booked 8 nights as Hilton Honors guests and we feel really disapponited about the service of the employees and all the infrastructure of the rooms. Since the first day, the air conditioned and the security box didnt work, as soon as I reported it, a mainteinance man came around and told he couldnt do anything about this problems. Until the fourth day, the front desk lady was able to chance us to another room. What did we got? A smaller room with a dirty restroom. The worst part of everything was the attitute of the Manager on Duty, a lady that simply told me: “I am sorry I havent been here for two days, I dont know what happened to you but I can send housekeeping, contact my Front Office Manager in the address below”.
If you dont want to waste your time and your money in a place where customer service experience is totally not existent, avoid this hotel.

author: Elena W

author: Ethan X

author: Molly M

author: Pablo E

author: Lucia L

I would like to thank  AKIL for the excellent customer service at the front desk, it was kinda late to review but it's not too late to thank him for being professional and kind, nice person.
Also I highly recommend the hotel for the convenience of the places we want to go. Amazing location!

 But overall,the atmosphere and vibes, it was a fantastic stay since it was our first time to NYC.
