author: Pablo Z
title: Terrible, rude staff, poorly maintained and a world away from the standards you expect.
text:
Terrible. 
Check-in initially went well, and I was offered a choice of a high or low floor within the 37-storey building. Opting for high, unfortunately we ended up with an ice machine directly outside the door producing a constant, extremely loud mechanical noise.  Asking for a swap, despite having just been offered a choice of rooms, I was told nothing else was available. I was then referred to the manager, who showed no willingness to help. I switched the machine off in order to get some sleep only for it to be turned on again. 2 days later a sign was placed on the machine saying out of order, and we now had 2 large fans placed on the corridor which sounded like a small jet engine. I genuinely began to wonder whether anyone had considered the impact on guests. 

The room itself also fell well below the standards I would expect from the Hilton brand. The sink was cracked in several places, wallpaper was peeling throughout the room, it was actually screwed in place in the bathroom, the bathroom door was swollen and deteriorated from water damage, and the bed appeared to have damaged springs, making it noticeably uneven and uncomfortable. 

Given all what we had experienced, we wanted to take a look at the rooftop bar and see the views. Our excitement was soon disappointment, as we came out of the lift, a 'host' was slouched on a stool leaning up against a wall whilst playing on her phone. No acknowledgment from her or instructions of where to sit. We walked over to the bar, no staff present. After deciding what to drink and taking in the views from the window, I had to approach the 'host' and asked if anyone was actually working as we had been there a good 4 or 5 minutes without being acknowledged. Her snotty attitude came through saying you could see the staff there talking to guests. Something I would have noticed had said staff being wearing an identifiable uniform, but it just looked like a group of friends chatting. I was ready to leave but my partner insisted we stay and get a drink. 
 
New York was supposed to be the highlight of our trip, spending 6 nights there, something we thought was going to be so special considering the glowing service we received at DT Hilton Tampa prior to coming here. Unfortunately though it has left me with such a sour opinion of both New York and DT Hilton. 

I sent this complaint into Hilton who have chosen not to comment. 

I would recommend you think twice before booking here.

author: Morgan R
title: Extremely disappointing experience at DoubleTree by Hilton Times Square
text:
As soon as I arrived at the property, I was informed that the AC in my room was in the process of being repaired, although there was no confirmed timeline for when it would be fixed. I was advised that if it was still not working that night, I would be moved to another room the following day before 12:00 PM.
Unfortunately, the AC was still not working the next day. What was even more disappointing was the complete lack of visible management support during what was clearly a major operational issue. The lobby was chaotic, with massive queues and frustrated guests, yet there appeared to be no hotel manager available to speak with or assist guests.
I did notice one Front Desk team member doing her absolute best to manage the situation, despite not being a manager. She deserves credit for trying to help guests under extremely difficult circumstances. However, it was difficult to understand why, during such a significant disruption, there was no senior hotel management visibly present to take ownership of the situation and communicate with guests.
We were unable to properly rest on our first night and could not access our room normally on the second day. At that point, we had no choice but to inform the staff that we could not continue our stay and requested to check out.
Fortunately, a Duty Manager eventually arrived and assisted us with cancelling the stay. I am, however, still waiting for the refund and for the credit to appear in my bank account.
As someone who works in hotel operations, I understand that technical issues can happen. What is much harder to accept is how those issues are managed. When a hotel is facing a major guest-impacting problem, communication, visible leadership, guest recovery and ownership become even more important.
Unfortunately, based on this experience, DoubleTree by Hilton Times Square has lost a customer permanently. What could have been an unfortunate technical issue became a terrible stay because of the lack of effective management and guest support.

author: Pablo D
title: Michalyn
text: Michalyn was wonderful! She is very knowledgeable and nice. She gets the highest marks!

author: Ruby I
title: Goated service worker
text: Sunam, sunom. Forget the name but it was something like that had great service and was the best part of the hotel. Give bro a raise

author: Paolo P
title: NYC stay
text: Ayyyb he’s very nice and friendly! Thank you

author: Sean D
title: Broken AC. Non responsive staff.
text:
Dear Hilton Guest Relations,
I just spent the night at the DoubleTree Times Square, and the experience was completely unacceptable.

After checking in around 7:00 p.m., I entered my room (36XX) and immediately found it excessively hot. Because I was in a hurry, I contacted the hotel through Hilton’s text/chat service and asked that someone check the temperature and the air conditioning. The agent assured me that this would be taken care of.

When I returned around 10:30 p.m., the room was 86 degrees.

I called the front desk repeatedly, but for nearly an hour I could not reach anyone. The phone would ring, place me on hold, and then disconnect. When I finally reached the desk, I was told that an engineer would be sent to my room immediately.

By 11:30 p.m., no one had come.

I then spent another hour and a half trying to reach the front desk. I finally got through around 1:00 a.m. The employee offered to relocate me to another Hilton property. Given that I had to be up only a few hours later, I explained that moving hotels at that point was not a reasonable solution. I asked instead for a fan. She assured me that one would be delivered to my room.

No one ever came.

I was left in an 86-degree room with no functioning air conditioning and no assistance from the hotel. Ultimately, I had to take a cold shower in the middle of the night simply to cool down enough to sleep.

What makes this even more troubling is that the employee told me this was a “one-off.” A quick review of the hotel’s online reviews, however, suggests that problems with room temperatures and air conditioning are neither new nor isolated. If this is a known and recurring problem, representing it to a guest as an isolated incident is deeply concerning.

This was not a minor inconvenience. The hotel failed repeatedly at every level: the room was not reasonably habitable, my initial request was not addressed, the front desk was extraordinarily difficult to reach, the promised engineer never arrived, and the promised fan never arrived. I ultimately spent the night uncomfortable, exhausted, and unable to get the sleep I needed.

This experience was beyond inexcusable, and frankly, I would be embarrassed if I were responsible for this property.

I expect Hilton to do more than simply apologize. I believe I should be fully comped for this night, and given the extraordinary failure to respond to the situation—and the fact that I was effectively left without a usable hotel room—I also expect additional compensation or consideration.

I would appreciate a prompt response explaining how Hilton intends to address this matter.

Sincerely,
XXX

author: Megan F
title: Hotel was not our best choice.  Hilton did not live up to expectations
text:
Would not recommend.  Air conditioner didn’t work and room temp was 83.  Went to desk 3 times and asked to be moved since they couldn’t get it fixed.  Promised that our luggage would be waiting in our new room.  Nope.  
One elevator was broke and one was tied up transporting laundry,  only 2 working and lobby was so crowded.  
Staff was pleasant but at any one time you were lucky if 2 people were working the desk and there were at least a dozen people in line.  
Not a good experience at Hilton,

author: Thomas Z
title: Not great cistimer servi e
text: The ac was not working in many rooms.of the hotle and they  kept postponing changing the rooms. They did  not offer a discount.

author: Molly J
title: Shout out to Steph
text: Our flight was cancelled to London due to the bad weather condition and had a very bad day and booked this hotel at very last minute and arrived at the hotel around 1am, Stephanie at the night she is a rock star and an asset to this business made us so relived welcoming. World needs more people like her so kind. Also offered a higher floor with an incredible view.

author: Daniel G
title: Disillusionment and disappointment
text:
Hotel with many floors, two elevators, little infrastructure, mediocre breakfast, and a receptionist named Williams who tells me he cannot guarantee that he will provide a towel for each of us in the family. The rooms are super small and are never cleaned, the outlets are almost falling out with barely any maintenance. They only make the bed. The best part was the service Fredie Rivera gave us; this man is capable of much more just because of the service he provides. 
I do not recommend this hotel.

author: Aaron Y
title: Friendly staff and good experience!
text: We were very happy with our experience!  The location was good.  The staff was so friendly.  They communicated throughout our stay which was appreciated.  We had a warning that the motel was full our last night so prepare for long elevator lines so it was nice to be aware (we never encountered long waits though).  I searched for a lot of rooms in NYC and have stayed at several places.  I thought the deal for a spacious bed was good.

author: Erin R
title: Very average
text: A mixed review for my visit. Great location, not far off Times Square, check in was quick and the guy serving was super friendly and found the same each day as he said hello whenever I passed. 35 stories high, 6 rooms per floor and only 2 lifts so waiting on a lift was sometimes 20 minutes. Unhelpfully there  is no lights or indication where the lifts are on each floor so the lift constantly wizzes past your floor. New mattresses were being delivered and 1 lift taken out to deal with that so the whole hotel working with one small lift. Wasn’t good at all. Breakfast room is very congested, food choice was ok but 2 coffee machines took ages to serve coffee and the 2 toasters are $10 toasters from Walmart and totally hopeless for serving a couple hundred people each day. All utensils are individually wrapped in plastic so tremendous wastage. The rooms were a decent size and standard, AC was excellent. Bathroom was a good size but a tiny sink which was hanging at an angle so water constantly on the floor. Checkout girl barely looked up when I checked out. Very mixed experience, could have been so much better if some basics were fixed

author: Isla L
title: Nothing to complain
text:
We arrived early intending to drop off our bags (they offer free luggage storage, though we didn't use it), but to our surprise, our room was already ready for check-in at 11 a.m. The receptionist on May 6th was incredibly helpful. The $150 security deposit was refunded just three days after check-out, which was impressively fast.

Tip: Keep your room key away from your phone, credit cards, or OMNY card, as they demagnetize easily.

The Room: I stayed on the 11th floor and found it very quiet. The room is small and basic but comfortable. A huge plus was the pillows—they were extremely comfortable, and the pillowcases were labeled "firm" or "soft". There were also plenty of outlets and USB ports near the bed to charge all our devices. The AC worked great, and the Wi-Fi was fast and easy to connect. The room includes a coffee maker, iron, hair dryer, and safe (no microwave, mini-fridge, or kettle, but going downstairs for hot water was never an issue). Housekeeping organized the room daily, though the cleaning felt a bit superficial (the mirror stayed dirty for a few days). Also, the shower water pressure wasn't the best, but the water heated up very quickly.

Breakfast & Amenities: The breakfast selection was great (eggs, sausage, pastries, etc.) and constantly replenished. It gets busy, but going around 8:30 a.m. was perfect. The cinnamon rolls and pancakes were outstanding! A major bonus was the free bottled water, coffee, lemonade, and snacks always available in the lobby.

Location: Fantastic location, just a 5-minute walk to the 42nd St–Port Authority subway. Everything you need (Duane Reade, 7-Eleven, restaurants) is right around the corner. The neighborhood can look a bit rough at night with many homeless people, but I personally had no issues.

Overall, it’s not a luxury hotel, but it’s excellent value for money. I would definitely stay here again!

author: Maria M
title: AVOID LIKE THE PLAGUE
text:
Avoid this hotel like the plague ..

Has to be the worst hotel I’ve ever been to ..

After having two nights in Detroit then two nights in Memphis for a multi centre trip for my husband’s 60th birthday celebrations we arrived at this hotel at 1am in the morning and were totally appalled..

The reception was full of youngsters swearing and wouldn’t move out of the way so we could get to the elevator to get our cases to our room

When we did get to the room I burst into tears .. nothing like the hotel pictures online ! Bathroom mirror surround peeling off, brown stains around the plug hole in bath along with chips in bath that were dirty, pulled bed sheets back and bits all over sheets, furniture looked old and outdated - felt like I was at a run down hostel to be honest 
Later on top of the bed all night looking for alternative accommodation.. 

Went down to breakfast room about 7.30 and was met with what I can only explain as a free for all ! I’ve never stayed anywhere where you have paper plates and cups and as I said a free for all grabbing at drinks and food .. the tables and chairs reminded me of a school lunch room - but worse and not enough for the amount of guests staying at the hotel 
No staff to see guests in to a table or to explain the set up - we walked straight out and informed reception we would be checking out and all the reasons why! We were offered another room as we were told a large group would be checking out later ..

We explained that the hotel was not up to the description online and that we would be checking long out .. the Manager looked at our booking to process a refund but said as we had booked through a travel company that we would have to request a refund upon our return home.

I asked when the $150 hold on our room for the three nights would be released back to my card and she said immediately.  Unfortunately this was not the case ! Not only did this not get released until we arrived back home but a charge of $68.88 was charged to our card ! 

I contacted Holiday Inn customer services and they confirmed that we should not have been charged anything  and that this would be refunded.. 

Obviously the $150 was showing as pending so we couldn’t use these funds whilst away which was annoying and lost on the exchange rate changing back when we got home ..

All I can say is I will never book another Holiday Inn Hotel ever

author: Rosie J
title: Terrible place
text:
The hotel was terrible, I can't recommend it to anyone. There were only two elevators wich were in use all the time, we had to wait really lang time. If you wanted to use stairs, they were really narrow and steep, they were for an emetgency exit. I don't understand how anybody had managed to travel with suitcases from them. The noise fron the old elevators heard in the room. There are only 6 rooms on the floor and we were in the room furthest from the elevators. I can only imagine the noise in the rooms next to the elevators.
The room was terrible, the carpet was really dirty. The bed springs were spongy and the edges were sunken. The was no blanket, just a slightly thicker sheet and a thinner sheet on top of each other. There was no hot water in the shower. The room was really stuffy. The pillows were ok, which was the only good thing in the room.
The breakfast was ridiculus. Few tables, not everyony could always sit down and servings were limited even afret 8 am.
If my feedback helps people choose another hotel, I'm very very happy.
It was great to get out of there.

author: Evie T
title: Don't stay here
text:
One of my most disappointing hotel experiences. I've stayed in several Holiday Inns and been very pleased but this was my first time here. I will say the room itself though dated was pretty clean and the noise on our floor was very minimal. However, I'm not exaggerating when I say this was the worst bed I've ever slept on. We had a room with two beds. Mine jutted upward in the middle and hit me in the back; my friend's dipped downward in the middle. I'm not sure which of us slept worse.

The TV randomly shut off several times while we were watching it. Several of the channels do not have any sound at all.

The bathroom door must have had something wrong with the hinges because we had to shove with all our body weight to open/close it. It was to the point where I thought I might get stuck in there at some point.

We did let the staff know what was going on when they sent a text asking how the room was. They offered to send someone to look at the door, but we were in town for a convention and were in/out of the room all day so didn't have a specific time we knew we wouldn't be there. Unfortunately it was too little too late and absolutely something that should have been resolved before even putting anyone in that room. I can't imagine all of that was something that occurred overnight.

The free breakfast was nice. The location is great for Times Square/the convention center/several tourist attractions. But at the price point, take your money and spend it elsewhere. You'll have a much more enjoyable trip!

author: Zoe R
title: Great service and location
text: The housekeeping service was amazing. They were changing bedsheets for everyday. I forgot a couple of clothes when I leave. But the housekeeping people were amazing. They shipped it to me promptly. I really appreciate it.

author: Poppy T
title: Family trip
text: I recently stayed at a hotel in New York, and I had a generally good time. The room was spotless, super comfy, and right in the heart of the city, making it easy to explore. The people I met when I checked in were friendly and helpful, which really set a great tone for my stay. However, after I left, I found out I’d accidentally left my watch behind. I quickly messaged the hotel to let them know and see if they could track it down, but I haven’t heard back yet. I know things can get hectic, but I’d really appreciate an update on where it might be. Besides this little hiccup, my stay was overall great. I hope the hotel can work on getting better about letting guests know about lost items—a quick reply would really help keep everyone happy.

author: Marta J
title: Decent Budget Stay with an OK breakfast, But Some Improvements Needed
text:
I stayed for 5 nights at the Holiday Inn Express in New York and overall it was an average experience, so I’d rate it about 3 stars.

On the positive side, the bed was very comfortable which made it easy to get a good night’s sleep. The room also had useful amenities like an iron and a hair dryer, which were convenient to have. Breakfast each morning was good with a decent selection, and it was nice not having to worry about finding food first thing in the morning.

However, there were a few issues that made the stay less comfortable. The pillows were very flat and definitely need replacing. I ended up using rolled up towels under the pillows. The lighting in the room wasn’t great either and made the space feel quite dim. One of the biggest problems was the smell of cannabis on the 16th floor during our stay. I was under the impression the hotel was non-smoking, so that was disappointing. Also, the inside of the drawers in the room were quite filthy, which meant we didn’t feel comfortable unpacking and kept our clothes in the suitcase for the whole week.

Overall, it’s an okay budget hotel in a good location, but it could really benefit from a few small tweaks and better attention to cleanliness to make the stay more comfortable.

author: Olivia Q
title: Horrible.
text:
Currently staying in this hotel the rooms (for 4. ) two adults and 2 children 10 years and 4 years are too small and it is very complicated!!!
We're staying on the third floor and we hear everything that's going on in the street... impossible to sleep...
Pros (but at least that I want to say ) very nice staff and clean room.
In short I do not recommend

author: Luke N
title: Good Base to Explore NYC 🇺🇸
text:
Excellent but quiet location. Next to Port Authority Bus Station, 5 minute walk to Times Square, 10 minute walk to Penn Train Station and round the corner from Scallywags, a brilliant bar to hydrate in, after a busy day of sightseeing! 🍺🍺

Check in process quick and efficient. Always seemed to be free cakes/cookies/hot chocolate in reception! Good WiFi throughout. The rooms are dated, but regularly cleaned, with powerful shower and shampoo provided. 

The included breakfast was excellent and great to start your day. Pancake machine, bagels, muffins, eggs and American sausage all there, plus tasty coffee from the machine. It does get busy, and you might have to wait for a seat but not for long. 

The lifts did stall a couple of times whilst we were there. However, after speaking with staff, this was due to, too many people getting in, and failing to read the sign of 6 persons maximum! 🤷‍♂️

Overall, for NYC, a reasonably priced room in almost the perfect location to explore!

author: Ryan Y
title: Successful experience
text: From Touria’s excellent reception to the good disposition of the breakfast staff we’ve spent some beautiful days in NY. That good energy helped to cope with the inconvenience with the elevators. Excellent beds and mattresses. We rest at ease to face the arduous task of enjoying the city in that climate. Thank you.

author: Henry C
title: Don’t be Hispanic w/ an Amex
text:
I’m fairly sure this place is racist.
I sent my 23 year old Guatemalan daughter to NYC with her elderly grandparents as a Christmas gift. I did not travel with them. At check in this is what happens.
1) She gets asked if her Amex is really hers by desk agent Ronald D.
2) He sends her to back of the line when card declined. Odd as she has a few thousand available credit.
3) She gets back to front. At this point I’m on phone with her. We talk he tells me she must pay FULL balance of stay upfront (that’s why her card declined). I’d already reserved the room at IHG and paid for first night to do it. Why? He has no explanation just policy. Then I say I will pay with different card. He says he will have to email the authorization. Hangs up without getting my email. Back of the line she goes again.
4) She gets to the front. I say he didn’t take my email. This time he says it must be a BUSINESS email address not my personal one. I have NEVER had to do any of this at any other hotel ever. I give my business email. Complete the authorization. Pay the ENTIRE ( about $3400) stay upfront. Now he’s polite. Offers her extra snacks.
Look he clearly thought we were some con artists or something. I can not imagine why. I could almost forgive that if he had not been completely obvious about it. He sent her through the line 3/4 times and just kept throwing up random road blocks. It was insane. You could not pay me to book at this property again. If a valley girl showed up with an Amex I doubt she’d have got the same treatment. So Hispanics beware. They have special “policy” for you.

author: Emma Z
title: Questionable safety with indifferent management
text:
I could write of the issues with the cramped room, peeling paint,  unsanitary 'glued' rubber bathmat in the shower, poorly located shower safety bars, and broken mattress (yup... it forms a 'v' shape). But I think it best that I send the message that this hotel has safety issues, particularly for anyone with mobility issues.

There are 20 plus floors. There are TWO elevators, with reliability issues.
 My two mornings of  broken elevator frustration were solve by:
	a. Walking with my cane down the emergency stairs from the 11th floor
	b. Taking an “Up”  elevator to the top and then stopping at each floor in this full elevator on the way “down”.

Management  proved to be 100% indifferent to these issues when approached. 

My next step will be to contact the city inspection services to question the safety of this venue for the allowed number of guests, as well as questionable operating practices.

Book here at your own risk.

author: Oscar J
title: GO ELSEWHERE
text: The people who service the guests are nice hardworking people but they are up against tall odds. The building is dated, the rooms are tiny and the bathrooms are out of the 50’s. (My shower faucet was broken). Worst of all the elevators are mostly non functional and it is a safety issue. I was traveling with a disabled person. One morning the elevator never came. After 40 minutes I went to use my room phone and that was not working. My friend panicked and i helped him down 11 stories. I complained and demanded a credit off a 500 plus nite. Management ignored me. I later wrote and emailed no response. Go elsewhere.

author: Freya Q
title: Positive
text: Strategic location, hearty breakfast, friendly and helpful staff, great for a trip to New York for its central location

author: Marco O
title: Robbery
text:
Awful, at the time of the check out they charged me a pet fee even tho I never had my pet during my stay (all of this without they telling me about this), I only knew about this when I saw my bank account

I tried reaching out, but Michelle Acosta hasn’t been helpful at all

author: Adam B
title: Terrible Stay and Dishonest Staff
text:
The room we had was smelly and had multiple random smudges. On top of that, our room had the fire alarm go off at 4:30 AM. When we went to the reception to ask for help, they told us we would get a 40% discount for the inconvenience.

But when we checked out, they simply cancelled the discount without any explanation.

At that point, it wasn’t just a bad experience — it was dishonest. Definitely one of the worst hotel stays I’ve had, and I wouldn’t recommend it to anyone.

author: Leo M
title: High quality
text: Excellent hotel: far from the center but in a quiet area, reception and bar staff very professional, modern, clean and comfortable rooms, excellent sleep quality (only until the cleaning staff starts moving around, needs improvement), relaxing pool and convenient garage.

author: Dylan W
title: Hotel in the center of Rome
text: Excellent hotel in the center of Rome, welcoming, helpful and courteous staff

author: Owen M
title: Excellent Quality & Location .
text:
From the moment you walk into reception, you’re greeted with a warm smile and offered a welcome drink. Once you’ve checked in and have time to take in your surroundings, you can’t help but notice the incredible attention to detail and the hotel’s exceptional cleanliness — it’s absolutely spotless, which is a real credit to all the staff.
The rooms are immaculate and extremely well appointed . 
The Breakfast menu is excellent and will cater for everyone’s palate.
I would certainly recommend this hotel. It’s small enough to feel comfortable and welcoming, yet large enough to provide a true five-star service. A fantastic hotel with wonderful staff and a real attention to detail.

author: Caleb U
title: Great hotel with lovely rooftop pool.
text:
We were greeted by very warm and welcoming staff, who were happy to give information on the local area, easy ways to get into Rome city centre and offered to help should we need anything during our stay.

Our room was clean and had what we needed, but relatively basic.

The rooftop pool was a good size, with a bar next to it.
The gym is small, but had everything I needed.
The restaurant is nice, with great service, delicious food and came out in good time. The cocktails were also delicious!

You can reach the nearest bus stop in roughly 5-minutes (walk) and then into Rome in 20 minutes. There is also a train station just a 5-10 minute walk away.
The hotel can also organise a taxi for 12 euros each way.

Overall, a great place to stay. We would recommend, and we would return.

author: Caleb G
title: Excellent vacation.
text:
Great hotel, with available, responsive, efficient, and very friendly staff.
The services offered are very good.
Hot tub in the room is great!
Pool and gym very good. 
Room (junior suite) spacious and great.
The hotel even thought of a gift for my wife's birthday.
Restaurant and bar very good too. However, the service there was a bit slow.
But a great experience in a magnificent city.
We will be back!

author: Adam Y
title: Wouldn't stay again
text:
The good - breakfast selection, the bar and cocktails and bar staff. 

The bad- the air con is poor, the rooms were not cool enough and took a long time to get slightly cool. There were 2 toasters at breakfast and half of both them were broken (just fix or replace them, you could have a new toaster delivered next day?!). The hotel is noisy, I had a room next to the elevators and there was a clunking noise frequently. 

The hotel was 'fine' overall but I wouldn't stay here again.

author: Freya L
title: Weekend trip
text:
We have just stayed in this hotel for 3 nights.
I was very pleased with the hotel. The staff were all amazing and the hotel is very clean and well maintained.
The weather was very hot during our stay, so the use of the pool was a blessing. I expected the weather to be this hot so wanted a hotel with a pool.
There were no issues getting loungers around the pool area. 
Breakfast was good, always something there for us to eat.
Bedrooms were kept clean and tidy with fresh towels. Nice complimentary toiletries on arrival. Could not fault the hotel at all.
The district the hotel was in is more of a residential area so used their taxi service to get where we needed to be, which was €12. However there are very good transport links.
I would recommend staying here.

author: Ella J
title: Nice hotel
text:
Very nice stay at the H10 the rooms are modern and clean. The staff are friendly and helpful. We had a small issue with our in room safe but that was sorted within minutes by the staff. 

The location of the hotel is about 30 minutes on 170 bus (€1.50) to Piazza Venezia which is a good place to start exploring.  You are not in the heart of Rome. 

There is a roof top pool which is great to cool
Down after a day exploring Rome.

author: Lucia G
title: Wonderful staff and modern rooms
text:
I really enjoyed my stay here in October 2025. It was my first time visiting Rome and I didn't realise that it was outside of the city centre, but upon check-in the reception team handed me a local map and explained how the bus services worked around the hotel. It was really easy to navigate the local bus service into the centre of Rome. The hotel is lovely with modern rooms and brilliant, friendly service. I slept really well in the comfortable bed and my room was spotlessly clean. 

Breakfast offered a good variety and the food was delicious. I didn't use any other facilities as I was often exploring the city, but I would definitely stay here again in the future.

author: Evan U
title: It lacks heart and soul.
text: Cold atmosphere, detached welcome (professional but not engaging), clean rooms, hard pillows, two people in the room with only one bathrobe, breakfast like in a boarding house.

author: Chloe S
title: Very nice hotel
text:
Beautiful, clean rooms, large bathroom. Great service and wonderful atmosphere. The best transportation option is the bus, which is easily accessible on foot.
In the evenings, it is best to order an Uber for outings and have it take you directly to the hotel.

author: Sydney P
title: Spacious, clean and staff are what make it truly enjoyable! Bring a travel kettle!
text:
Hotel is in a part of city around 15min journey on a bus from main tourist areas. Rooms spacious and bed really comfortable. Breakfast had plenty of variety, im not a meat eater or big breakfast person but still managed something to set me up each day for exploring.
Staff exceptional and pleasant, gave plenty of good travel advice and places to eat locally or outwith area.
Pool area not open during our stay but can imagine would be a nice area to dip and refresh on a warm day. 
All areas spotless at all times and all staff pleasant/welcoming at all times.
Only negative was no tea/coffe making facilities in the room, major let down for me as love to enjoy a coffee in my room in my own time. 
We would definitely stay here again, but bring  my own kettle lol

author: Jessica J
title: Excellent.
text: Immaculate hotel, high-level breakfast and dinner. Kind and helpful staff.

author: Grace M
title: Rome Birthday treat!
text:
We like to go somewhere where the weather will try to kind to us early in the year, so I chose Italy. Bookedthru Jet2  City breaks, and proved to be a good choice! Airport a little frantic, because of this new EES thing, but we managed. Eventually got out to the taxi rank, queued and then got our taxi. The rid in was about 30 minutes and 60 euros( with a 5 euro tip). The area was a little like "Little Beirut", but on entry to the hotel far different! The reception staff were extremely friendly, pleasent and apolegised for the delay while our room was made ready. So we did no more than try the beer. Cold glass with cold beer, excellent! Once the room was ready, it found us not being ready for what we were looking at! The bed was Ginormous! The bathroom facilities excellent. Plenty of storage and a mini-bar hidden away in the wall. There was a TV and hairdryer in the room too!
We ate that first night in the hotel restaurant, and the food was extremely good. Again cold beers to finish our long day. If you want to go out to eat there are a number of places to go and the hotel will give you a city map and mark places of interest and a really good restaurant too. 
The hotel have an agreement with a taxi company that for 24 euros will take you into the center of Rome, and on the map will have shown you where to get your return taxi. There is a rooftop pool, that sadly was being renovated on our trip, but still a place to catch some rays. Things we didn't use was the spa, so don't know about that.
Breakfast in the morning was a treat. Continental and warm food too. Excellent! Coffee machines a little weird to get a full cup, but juice was great! Fresh bread, cold cuts and fried eggs along with scrambled. There was also fresh yoghurt and cereals too!
The hotel will sort out your return taxi to the airport for you too. You will need to know which terminal you want and allow yourself plenty of time to get there if you want a drink or duty frees.

author: Laura I
title: Recommended
text: We stayed only one night in a triple room a bit cramped. The furnishings of the room are a bit neglected. Dents on the furniture and a bit ruined even bed coverings.  The bidet is uncomfortable. Room and bathroom clean and tidy. We expected at least one bottle of water to be offered, as they usually do in 4-star hotels. Friendly and helpful staff. Breakfast very plentiful and varied.

author: Harper X
title: Beautiful experience
text:
I stayed at this resort and the experience was overall very positive.
The rooms are modern and dynamic, with perfect bedding guaranteeing excellent comfort. The TV offers a great medium with a wide choice of content, which is nice to relax.
Breakfast is full and varied, allowing you to start the day well. The staff is available, competent and always ready to help, which greatly contributes to the quality of the stay.
A shuttle service to the centre is also offered, which is convenient.
Regarding the areas for improvement: the hotel is a bit off-center, located in a fairly empty area, which may surprise at first glance. Also, be careful if you buy vouchers for the shuttle: they are not refundable in case of non-use.
In short, a very nice establishment offering comfort and quality of service, despite a slightly off-center location.

author: Maria H
title: To improve the breakfast
text: Very nice hotel, quite convenient location as it is easily reached by bus. The breakfast does not have quality products suitable for a 4 star hotel, especially the croissants were poor.

author: Louis G
title: A halftone experience
text: Very clean hotel, thanks to the people who do the maintenance; friendly staff at the reception. Poor breakfasts: coffee in a vending machine, tasteless, nothing to do with good Italian coffee; pastries too fat; bread of medium quality; liquid jams in vending machines.  The hotel is located in an area not pleasant at all, rather glaucous; without easy communication to the center; fortunately the hotel sells vouchers (12€ each way) for well organized taxis that drop you off Piazza Venezia.  I'm not going back.

author: Brooke E
title: Good Business Hotel
text:
I stayed two nights in this great hotel not too far from Roma Ostiense station.
The size of the building is considerable, the facilities are high standard, the rooms are clean, perhaps only the parquet floor does not look shining.
Breakfast is of a high standard, both sweet and savoury.

author: Lucy I
title: Wonderful holiday
text: and become, our point of reference, are four years that we come to this hotel, we have a great time, for the connections with the metro and bus, great location, central, possibility 'of parking at the same price of the hotel, rooms always clean and well organized, (the only thing I did not find and some diskette to make up remover,) but that is not' a problem. Otherwise everything perfect. From the staff to the reception, friendly and extremely available, on all needs, breakfast buffet varies from sweet to savory, waiting staff at the top attentive to all needs, coktel on arrival delicious, highly recommended, we will return. Thank you.

author: Charlotte Q
title: The BEST hotel in NYC with breathtaking views and customer service
text: I was surprised with a overnight room reservation this past weekend , 8/22, by my family to celebrate my 50th birthday. I cannot begin to describe how amazing this hotel is. From arrival, the entire staff from the valet, to the front desk were so pleasant and kind and even wished me a Happy Birthday immediately.  But what blew me away was when I got into my room, and realized we had been upgraded to the penthouse suite. Wow, Wow, and Wow again. It was absolutely spectacular.  The view had me speechless. And to add, it was duplex with an upstairs private rooftop. I will never ever forget this Birthday and I wouldn't have wanted to bring it in any other way. Thank you to my family for gifting me this experience. I felt loved , seen and special on this special weekend. Thank you to the ENTIRE Ink 48 Hotel staff. And a special shout out and thank you to Sinam, Hotel Manager. She called me the next morning to introduce herself and to inquire how my experience was. I just had to meet her in person. Thank you Thank you Thank you again. I cannot wait to return to stay. This hotel is absolutely beautiful. Not to mention I ended up having a surprise dinner with family and close friends at Hudson Vu, the upstairs rooftop bar. Everything was top tier.  A weekend to remember. Thank you again and I will most likely be back before you even know it.

author: Nora A
title: Victor is great!
text: I understand that during the summer, hotels can get very busy and I just wanted to say that Victor is a great employee! He went above and beyond Customer service to help us out when the other employees were lacking in service, he made up for everything a great service every single day. We appreciated our stay because Victor made it memorable. Promote him!

author: Emma Z
title: Extra Care
text: It was a great experience. Had an issue with my room but Victor at the front desk worked with me and took great care of me. The management went above and beyond to make sure I was comfortable.

author: Jack D
title: Extra fee, loud property!
text:
Beware there is a $40 per night “Amenity Fee” charged.  Given there is no pool and fitness center is tiny, very disappointing to be charged this.  

Second, this property has a rooftop night club across the street that blares music from 3PM to 3AM.  Making the rooms very noisy and not suitable for light sleepers. 

Black out blinds were non operational.  Furniture and lamp controls were broken. 

The rooftop bar is beautiful, but you need reservations and hotel guests DO NOT get priority. 

The positives.   The wine bar on main floor is awesome.  Ian and the other bartenders are fun, friendly, well versed on the wines and make excellent cocktails.

The bed is comfortable.  Water pressure in shower is amazing.  

Location makes it easy to get around.  Walking distance to cruise terminal for those cruising. 

Don’t see how this got rated a 4 star hotel. It’s 2 - 3 Star at best.

author: Owen T
title: Great Hotel
text: Great Hotel we go there every time, spacious room in the Hell’s Kitchen neighborhood I highly recommend

author: Alexander E
title: It was okay. It could have been better!
text:
This hotel could significantly improve its appeal with a more precise and transparent description, to avoid disappointing guests like us who were drawn in by its photos and captions!

Overall, we found the location to be convenient, most of the staff were welcoming (especially the cleaning team), the room was comfortable and the bathroom was tidy. However, there are several aspects we wish we had been informed about before making our reservation.

It is quite misleading when hotels prominently showcase beautiful rooftop images in their primary marketing materials without clearly indicating that guest access is limited to certain evening hours, contingent upon the absence of private events.

During our stay, the rooftop was unavailable due to private parties, yet we assumed that hotel guests could still enjoy the view, even if the restaurant was fully booked, or could visit during the day for photos when the restaurant was closed. Unfortunately, that was not the case, and it was quite disappointing. Many guests choose Ink 48 specifically for that view, only to discover that the dedicated elevator is locked and a 21+ age restriction is enforced when it finally opens at 4:00 PM. Families with children are never permitted access! Additionally, there is a daily "Guest Amenity fee" of $40 plus taxes, which is charged at checkout. While I have no objection to an amenity fee, it is confusing to advertise free WiFi, complimentary daily cleaning service, and free gym access when these are precisely the amenities in the fee. This should be stated clearly. I also read in other reviews about the availability of free bikes, but we did not see any during our stay, nor were they mentioned as part of the amenities.

Please note that lower floors can be quite noisy due to street sounds, and there is no view below the 7th floor. Furthermore, there is no complimentary water, nor is there a coffee or tea machine in the room. We were surprised to discover that two water bottles from the mini bar were charged to our account. During the check out at the front desk, they rectified the mistake, but this should have never happened.
Lastly, the obsolete instructions for using the room card in the elevator. Although the system has transitioned to a touch pad, the instructions still reference the previous method of inserting your card, which can lead to confusion. By the time you figure this out, even if it only takes a few seconds, you may miss the opportunity to select your floor, resulting in a wait for all the stops  already selected before you can reserve yours (the hotel has 17 floors). Simply replacing or covering the outdated label would greatly enhance guests' comfort and reduce frustration.

I truly hoped this would be THE hotel I would return to repeatedly during my visits to NYC, but I prefer other options with a more accommodating policy regarding the rooftop deck (even though it may not be as elegant and stylish as this one).

author: Oliver F
title: Just okay ...
text:
Check-in took an absolute age, the computer was going slowing and receptionist kept apologising. The lifts are old and tepremental, make sure you hold your room key on the sensor for 3 seconds. Our room was large, the AC worked well, but the in-room drinks prices were extortionate. Our shower head was broken and shower gel dispensers empty, which we reported to reception straightaway. The shower was not fixed during our 3 day stay, which was disappointing.

There’s a roof top bar with lovely views of the Hudson river. Make sure you book a table for drinks or food in advance, as being a hotel guest does not get you any preferential treatment.

This hotel is reasonably priced against others in the area and although it’s basically okay, there were too many little things wrong for us to score it above 3 (average).

author: Camille Y
title: GrEAT VIEWS OF THE hUDSON
text:
This hotel could be so much more with some improvements in staff & service. Although everyone is friendly, things don't go as smoothly as they should. Our room, a Hudson Suite, had the spectacular view I was looking for. But it also had only one air conditioner & thermostat for the two rooms, leaving one cold & one HOT ( the bedroom of course). We did ask what could be done & a tall fan was brought up which helped alot.   You also have to ask if you want robes or a coffee maker, both of which took about 5 hours to arrive. And the in-room phones did not work at all & no one ever came to fix them. 

Checking in was also a problem, we missed a planned event because we could not get into our room till 430 in the afternoon. We had been told it would be ready shortly after two, but then told it was delayed by someone else needing a room change ???  

At least they did honor my request for one on a floor with a good view eventually.  

The hotel & attached food venues are actually 2 completely separate entities. ANd one will have nothing to do with the other. So when I thought I lost my credit cards at The Vu, the front desk could do nothing , not even let me up to the Vu floor to look. 

And the food venue does not answer emails or calls or texts.  

Overall the hotel staff is very friendly, but in our short one night stay there were at least 5 different people at the front desk, so no continuity from one to the next. And we NEVER saw a room attendant.   

On a plus side its skeek, clean and a fun place to stay if you need to be on the west side.

author: Connor F
title: Customer Service not up to standard for a 4 star hotel
text: location was ok, easy unload of our luggage. front desk kept talking to his friend on his phone even when I was visibly in front of him waiting. i did not want to ruin my daughters day so i stayed patient. The view was nice. AC did not work, we had to let engineering in at 3am bec it was 80 degrees in the room, we get moved to 3rd floor it was loud, there was a conference going on. and now the phone in the room does not work. i call from my cellphone and they said they will waive the amenity fee bec of all the trouble. tosay i get my amex bill and they still charged me amenity fees. UNBELIEVABLE!! i will never ever stay in this hotel again. its no the hotel its the workers that i would like to never want to experience again. CUSTOMER SERVICE NEEDS TO GET BETTER SPECIALLY IF WE ARE PAYING $400 PER NIGHT! i had to call again to get the amenties waived and if i did not check my cc i wouldve been charged double. valet fee ridicoulously high. will not reccomend this place

author: Leo G
title: Great hotel near Time Square
text:
I stayed in this hotel for one night in May 2026. 
Hotel is located  near Time Square , like 10-15 min walk from actual Time Square , so you are away from hustle and bustle of the area.
Check in process was very smooth, front desk people are very nice. Hotel room is BIG for the New York hotels. It has big panoramic window. 
Beds were very comfortable.
Couple blocks away there is street with many good restaurants with variety cousins and decent prices.
This is solid 4 star hotel and o would definitely stay there again.
Only down side that is worth to mention that next door of the hotel some club / rooftop place. Music was blasting very loud in the evening. So if you are light sleeper that might be an issue. We were so tired during the day that we fell to sleep immediately. so it was not big issue for us. But again that might be an issue.

author: Carlos K
title: Spectacular views and service!
text: We had the best NYC experience by staying at this hotel! The location is very convenient for access to the harbor and Broadway/Times Square. The hospitality and service was amazing at HudsonVu rooftop. Sal the manager and his team (Alfonso, Natasha, Sebastian) are so friendly and accommodating! You’re always greeted with a friendly smile. He made our experience extra special since we were celebrating our anniversary! Unbelievable service and amazing views of the city… this is a hidden gem!

author: Oliver B
title: Visible Mold, Broken Wi-Fi, Electrical Issues, and Poor Management Follow-Up
text:
I am giving 1 star for one reason only: the housekeeping staff and general team were incredibly nice, hard-working, and welcoming. They deserve praise. However, the physical condition of the hotel and the way our complaint was handled by management were extremely disappointing.

1. ROOM 1103: DELAYED CHECK-IN, NO WI-FI, AND SERIOUS ROOM ISSUES

Our stay started badly. Although check-in was scheduled for 3:00 PM, our room was not ready on time. When we were finally given Room 1103, the condition of the room was shocking: water-damaged and swollen furniture, visible mold, a loud and worn-down AC unit, and a stained headboard with unknown marks. The Wi-Fi was also completely non-functional during our stay in that room.

The first night seemed manageable, but on the second night, at around 2:00 AM, the lights started flickering violently and repeatedly. This happened on the morning of my birthday, while I was already dealing with severe jet lag. Instead of sleeping, we spent hours trying to deal with the room’s electrical and lighting problems.

2. FRONT DESK PROMISES AND A ROOM MOVE THAT DID NOT SOLVE THE PROBLEM

When we reported the electrical issue and the broken Wi-Fi to the front desk, we were told that the hotel was already aware of the lighting problem. We were also explicitly told that the resort fees related to the first room would be refunded because of the inconvenience and the non-working Wi-Fi.

We were then moved to another room. Unfortunately, the move did not solve the core problem. The second room did not have the same swollen furniture or flickering lights, but it still felt dirty and had visible mold. We also found mold inside a picture frame on the wall next to the bed, which is completely unacceptable in any hotel room.

3. ROOFTOP BAR ISSUE

The Rooftop Bar is advertised in a way that makes it feel like a hotel amenity, but our experience was very different. We wanted to go up on our first day to enjoy the skyline view and have coffee, but we realized guests cannot simply access it. Later, we planned to celebrate my birthday there and found out it is operated separately, requires an external reservation, and may involve a cancellation or deposit fee if the reservation is missed. This was very disappointing and felt misleading from a guest perspective.

4. MANAGEMENT HANDLING AND REFUND DISPUTE

Because both rooms had serious issues, including visible mold and unacceptable room conditions, we requested a refund. After our discussion with management, we were later assured by email that the refund request had been submitted in the system and that the matter was essentially only a formality awaiting final processing.

Based on that communication, we believed the issue was being handled and that we only needed to wait for the refund to be completed. Unfortunately, after we checked out, the situation changed completely. Instead of receiving a clear resolution, we were met with silence, delays, and references to third-party booking procedures.

From our perspective, it now feels as if those assurances were only given to get us to leave the property calmly, with no real intention of following through afterward. As international guests, we felt misled and left without proper accountability.

Photos of the mold and room condition are attached. Again, respect to the housekeeping staff and the general team, who were kind and welcoming. But based on the condition of the rooms and the way management handled the complaint, I cannot recommend staying at this hotel.

author: Thomas X
title: An expensive disappointment
text:
We stayed at this property when it was a Kimpton hotel and enjoyed it. This stay was completely unsatisfactory. We booked a suite, an expensive room,  to celebrate my birthday. On a first night, we attempted to shower and had no hot water. We reported it to the front desk and were told that that’s just the way it is on the 17th floor. Just let the water run for 20 - 30 minutes. That turned out to be correct, but hardly acceptable - and a complete waste of water.

On the first night, we also discovered that the mechanical equipment above our room was loud and relentless. Again, this is completely inconsistent with a premium room. 

On our final morning, we awoke to shouting and electric tool noise. We looked out and there’s a scaffold with workers just above and to the left of our room. 

The view from our room was fantastic. But it hardly matters if you can’t get a good night’s sleep. 

On the plus side, we had breakfast and separately,  a cocktail in the lobby restaurant (which I believe is not affiliated with the hotel). Both experiences were great. Excellent food and great service. 

We provided feedback to the front desk - they just shrugged. We wrote tohotel management and also did the survey that was sent by email. No reply. We were extremely disappointed, would not stay here again, and would not recommend.

author: Erin B
title: Terrible location, terrible rooms and not a 4 star hotel.
text: We checked in on Thursday and are scheduled to stay until Monday. It's about to be midnight on Sunday and we still have no internet. Have not had Internet the entirety of our stay. Yet somehow the hotel managed to charge our credit card the "amenities" fee that includes the internet. How that is possible, who knows. The AC is garbage and is set to know be on for more than 5-10 minutes and will not go below 70 degrees. It appears set that way on purpose due to either the cheap nature of management or ownership I don't know which. The rooms are outdated bordering shabby. The hotel sits next to an event space that blasts music from 10pm-2am so you cannot sleep. We tried, even with noise cancelling earbuds. The only good things about this place are th staff, which are all really nice and professional people who are lovely. And the restaurant/bar on the ground floor. Good food and great bartender.

author: Abigail A
title: No WiFi in sight at this place
text: Nice place and friendly staff but we're in hour 48 of zero WiFi and the only response is "they're working on it." Absolutely preposterous. Is this place running on a dial-up connection? The Ink 48 Hotel -- stepping back into 1992 one day at a time. Beyond frustrating.

author: Emma D
title: Great place for cruising!
text: We booked this hotel so we could spend a couple of days in New York before boarding our cruise. We arrived before check-in and were able to leave our luggage and begin exploring the city. Everyone was so friendly and welcoming. When it was time to check in, James let us know he had upgraded us. The room was large, clean, and perfect. We enjoyed our stay very much and would stay here again. The location to the cruise terminal was amazing.

author: Abigail X
title: Well done Ink 48
text: The room was clean and neat and spacious for New York City. The front desk attendants were pleasant and helpful.

author: Freya E
title: 1st time Big Apple experience
text: Great hotel. Very nice and clean. Friendly staff. NearTimes Square, Broadway etc. Everything is in walking distance. Definitely will book again.

author: Matthew X
title: Perfect hotel whilst exploring New York city as a solo traveller
text:
I very much enjoyed my stay at Ink 48 Hotel. 

It is located in a quiet safe area of Hells Kitchen and about 15 minutes walk to the 50 St subway and the much more busier Broadway/Times Square area. The M50 and M12 bus stops are a close by and I used them a lot whilst exploring the city.

My room was excellent - spacious, comfortable and had everything I needed. Large bath and a separate shower. They provided a kettle when I asked for one during my stay.  

Altogether a great hotel which I would recommend.  A++++

author: Elena Q
title: Great hotel with very good location and great service
text: Great hotel with great service, especially thanks to Ibrahim!! Centrally located with great views of the city!! A great experience!!

author: William T
title: Hotel is average. Good location!
text: The hotel was okay, good location, the outside of the hotel was slightly scruffy. Rooms were okay quite clean. The receptionist wasn’t very nice. Breakfast was good

author: Megan Y
title: Excellent
text: Good hotel, good value for money, breakfast every day with eggs, meat, breads, juices, the staff is very kind. Excellent location

author: Lucy H
title: Great location but needs attention to basic updating
text:
I don’t know why TripAdvisor describes certain hotels as “recently renovated “ when they are not. This Hampton could use a new look and refreshing small rooms slightly updated look, but except for the fantastic Hilton, the place need some just plain upgraded maintenance. The floors in the rooms had chips and spots. Elevator carpet was so afraid it was revealing the plywood , and the bathrooms seemed nice and slightly updated, but the vanity cabinet was on was chipped and warped I did enjoy the breakfast. I think they have the prettiest breakfast room of any Hampton I’ve been in, but really folks I expect a lot more from a Hilton product.
That said, it’s in a great convenient location close to subways, 42nd Street, Times Square, PennStation. etc.

author: Owen S
title: Good value, family friendly and great location
text: Hotel was in the perfect location - so close to Times Square, theater district, Bryant Park, restaurants, and SO much more! Tons of food options! There was a subway stop maybe 50 feet away from the hotel front door and we were 1/4 mile from the Amtrak station at Penn Station. Area was active but felt safe (as you can be in a big city). We had two rooms (a king size and one with two double beds) for a family of 5 people - 2 adults and 3 teenagers. Rooms were modern and incredibly clean, water was hot with great pressure in the shower. Beds and pillows were comfy! Street facing rooms had a great view of Empire State Building. (See photo) Hotel staff were all so nice and accommodating. Cookies were out every day at 3pm. They held our baggage when we arrived early and the day we checked out. We were on the 11th floor - there was a lot of noise on the street (construction) but we did not hear any of it. The only reason I gave it a 4 out of 5 is because the breakfast was pretty basic. This was a standard Hilton fare - packaged muffins/bread/bagels, powdered eggs, sausage, cereals/milk, yogurt, oatmeal, and a waffle maker. Coffee/water/juice. Not gourmet, but enough to get us going in the morning. Would definitely stay here again.

author: Rosie Z
title: Hampton Inn W 35th Street New York
text: Great location to Times Square and Empire State Building. The Staff was excellent and very helpful in getting Taxis. Rooms are a little smaller, but given the location was a great value. Also, plenty of restaurants close by.

author: Molly L
title: ABSOLUTELY DISGUSTING HOTEL and horrible customer service
text:
