author: Charlie X
title: Weird vibes!
text:
This was such a weird hotel. Lobby was the most visually appealing part. The hallways are dark and cramped. As a woman, this was creepy!

Gave it the benefit of the doubt bc the AM staff was wonderful! Brandon and Hero (I think this was his name) were super welcoming. The two stars are for them! 

My room was ready at 9am which I wasn’t expecting so that was a plus. 

3 stars removed for the extremely small room. Cover is extremely thin. PM staff was a bit strange, almost unapproachable. AND they advertise like 3 different restaurants / bars and you can’t even charge it to the room! Wtf.

Also, they charged me the for 2 nights and the incidental fee of $200 which was fine but there was an additional charge for $278. Apparently this was a preauthorization charge. Very strange bc if the charge for the room went through, what’s the preauth for? I asked about it and they immediately returned it. Imagine if I didn’t ask.

All in all, if you just need to sleep fine. But there’s 20+ hotels in the area to choose from. Avoid this one.

author: Charlotte K
title: Restful stay in Manhattan: practical room and cozy vibe
text: I had an excellent stay at this hotel. My premium room was comfortable and very practical—there was easily enough space to leave my suitcase open without it getting in the way! The air conditioning worked perfectly, so there was no need to run the additional window unit. The Wi-Fi was strong, the bed was comfortable, and the bathroom was in pristine, recently renovated condition with powerful shower pressure. Overall, the room had a very restful & cosy atmosphere.

author: Joseph S
title: Brandon at Freehand
text: Brandon at freehand was really dope and kind to us.

author: Sophia H
title: Good service and convenient
text: A good convenient overnight. Javier at the desk helped with Q’s and getting a king bed on the quiet side of the hotel.  The staff at bars and cafe - totally professional.  It’s a good location for walking to downtown and catching the subway.  BTW - amazing water pressure in the shower.

author: Lily L
title: Excellent customer service
text: The rooms are cozy, clean and comfortable. The bed is very comfortable. I had an issue with an in-window A/C room my first night and the incredibly kind Sharon at the front desk went above and beyond to get me a quieter room with central A/C, even to go so far as walking me to verify the room was ready. Probably the best front desk service I’ve had at a NY hotel in a long time.

author: Morgan I
title: good service
text: Brandon the bell hop -- double this man's pay!!!!

author: Sophia B
title: Freehand Review
text: Consistent, reliable, well priced accommodation in a great location. Plus, there is Javier at the Front Desk. One of the most handsome sights in New York.

author: Sydney Y
title: worst hotel I’ve ever been in
text: Have never been moved to write a review like this before but i have never stayed in a hotel like this.  It is quite simply disgusting.  It’s not even two star let alone four.  The room I was given had black duct tape holding the carpet together, exposed wires thick with dust, no hot water, flickering lights, broken down furniture and the smell of mildew.  I had planned to stay two weeks as I’m here for work but I’m checking out in the morning.  I was moved to another room as that one was intolerable even for a night but it is barely any better. I can’t wait to get out of here.  The staff were pleasant enough but jaded - clearly hear this all the time - indeed there were lots of people trying to change rooms.  Absolutely appalling - stay anywhere but here.

author: Mathis V
title: Fantastic Staff & Great Location
text: The location of his hotel is fantastic, walking distance to everywhere in NYC. Plus the staff is amazing, especially Hero. His energy is contagious, very knowledgeable; he was our concierge while my family and I stayed in New York.

author: Charlotte Q
title: We had a very good time
text: The hotel is well located and on one side it has a well-stocked cafe for breakfast and on the other side an Italian restaurant that has a grappa that they prepare themselves, and I suggest trying the raisin one. The price per night is very reasonable.

author: William B
title: Excellent from every point of view
text:
Highly recommended location. 
Queen room with a really comfortable bed, clean, complete bathroom amenities.
A special mention to the staff, welcoming and smiling even with those who arrive late in the evening a bit dazed from the trip. 
Being welcomed with a smile and two bottles of cold water says a lot about the attention to the customer

author: Daniel G
title: Rude service
text: The air-conditioner/heater did not work, and the receptionists (both of them) were very rude. I stayed in this hotel a year previously and it was ok, but this time it was awful.

author: Emma Q
title: Hygiene & safety concern; Intimidation, rude and confrontational behaviour by staff; stressful experience for a woman
text:
I paid for four nights at Freehand New York. I made a reasonable hygiene request. What I received was dismissal, sustained intimidation, an implied physical threat, obstruction of a legitimate complaints process,  and threat of removal from the premises in the middle of the night — twice.
No woman travelling alone should experience this. No guest of any kind should experience this.

The full context - 

At the end of a really long, tiring day of business meetings, I returned to my room after dinner, and found a medium sized bug on my bed. The room was not the cleanest, and the sheets were torn in a place - this I had ignored for 4 days. But I couldn’t bring myself to sleep in a bed with insect(s?) in it. I made a simple, reasonable request: please change my sheets. What followed was one of the most distressing experiences I have ever had as a hotel guest.

This is the not so worrisome part - First, a member of staff came and handed me the sheets and asked me to do it myself. When requested that someone help me with it, two staff members arrived. Rather than addressing a straightforward hygiene failure, i.e., changing the sheets, one spent several minutes deflecting with irrelevant & condescending remarks - "this is New York," "I tell my daughter that the bug is more scared of you". I continue to repeat my request. Then he finds a bug on the wall, his colleague kills it, and he tries to convince me that's the one. Well how can I know for sure. I continue to state that this is irrelevant and the ask is to change the sheets . By this time, he has started speaking over me. 

Here's where it really got stressful - Now having still not changed the sheets, he asks for me to pack my bags and leave. On a game week in NYC and with the FIFA world cup in a few days, when all the hotels are booked and its already ~10 pm, there is nowhere to go. He said he would put me up somewhere - but I cannot leave until I know where I will stay the night and whether it will be safe. He and his colleague turn their back and start walking away. I call after them to tell me what the new hotel would be. To this he turns around and yells - I am going to get someone to calm you down. As a solo woman traveller, that statement was frightening - what did that mean? Was he going to get someone to physically force me out, or to intimidate me further or to argue more forcefully? They returned with a woman, who was mostly quiet, but asked them to get the sheets changed. I requested an incident report and process to file a formal complaint. She gave me the visiting card of the assistant front desk manager. When I challenged that he was not the right authority and that I needed to speak to the hotel manager, she said this is all she can do for me.

And the intimidation got worse in the early hours of the morning - At checkout the next morning (3:30am), when I asked for an incident report, the same staff member appeared from behind the desk. I was not given an incidence report or a contact of senior management. He defaulted to the same tactic of deflecting with condescending & aggressive verbal comments, but even worse this time - he told me I was "rude, disrespectful, disingenuous, and a liar." I said I would like to wait in silence in the lobby until my cab arrived. And he then very aggressively asked me to get off his property - he physically came out from behind the front desk and started walking towards me, while yelling. It was 3:30am and I was evaluating whether it was safer to wait for my cab on the desolate street or in the lobby with this aggressive man. He also asked another person behind the desk to call someone to force me out. But before this escalated further, my cab thankfully arrived. He was the most senior person on duty, and that every member of staff I had interacted with reported directly to him. There was no neutral path seek help.

author: Pablo S
title: Not Worth the Price.
text:
I paid nearly $500 per night and experienced one problem after another.

Our original room had a known air conditioning issue. A technician told us the TV had to be removed for the AC to work properly, meaning we had to choose between air conditioning and a television.

The hotel’s solution was to suggest that I cancel my reservation while traveling to New York with my two daughters.

We were eventually moved to another room, which also had a malfunctioning AC and water that was so hot it could not be regulated.

Compensation that was promised was never provided.

Poor maintenance, poor management, and unacceptable customer service.

author: Daniel T
title: Dishonest facility fee, no coffee
text: No coffee in the room? Or even in the lobby? $40 "facility fee" for no facilities? Forcing guests to pay the "facility fee" after they arrive is dishonest, it should just be included in the room rate.

author: Sean O
title: Great experience
text:
House keeping was excellent
Rooms were comfortable
Bed was fantastic

author: Harper U
title: Be Careful When Booking Online -- Make Sure You Have Freehand Not a 3rd Party
text: Beware of how you book for Freehand.  Although I'm pretty careful, I got snookered and somehow I booked through a third party when I thought I was booking directly with Freehand, The third party is Guest Reservations.  I booked for multiple days because of a family event, and then tried to change one of the dates for a 100% legit medical reason.  There was no way to change the reservation and it was non-refundable.  Guest Reservations gave me a 10% discount, when I complained by phone, but it leaves a sour taste.  I like the hotel, and I stay there regularly.  My complaint is with the booking system, not the quality of the hotel.  Be careful when booking online and be sure you are not being transferred to a third party booking service.

author: Chloe F
title: Best Customer Service
text: My son was staying for business-he had a medical emergency due to an underlying health condition-I called front desk from out of state-.they called an ambulance and were kind enough to move his car untill he returned from Hospital!  They were nothing short of angels- I wish I got the young man’s name who answered the front desk phone at 5 am-

author: Rosie I
title: Dexter lurking???
text: I am not usually someone to complain, but this hotel other than the lounge on the 2nd floor was not very nice at all.  Dark, very dark, walking down the hallway made me feel as though Dexter might be lurking for his next event.  The room was super small, the bathroom sink was barely larger than the small porcelain thing you spit into at the dentist.  The furniture was like from the 70s, and the room was sooooo very dark and small, with barely any walking room.  The shower was fine but getting up from the toilet and I had to watch I didn't hit my head on the sink which was literally right in front. I get it is a boutique hotel in Manhattan but overall would not recommend...

author: Jessica D
title: Disappointing
text:
We spent 5 nights in a room with a king-size bed.

Pros:
1) very convenient location for visiting Manhattan;
2) very kind reception staff.

Cons:

1) Very noisy room. You could clearly hear noises coming from the neighboring rooms and the hallway and, above all, those from the street, which was very busy at all hours, particularly early in the morning.
2) Small and poorly organized room. A disproportionate part of the space is occupied by the kitchen, which for short stays can be of little use (in our case we did not use it at all). Paradoxically, there is no table with chairs where you could eat even just a sandwich. The wardrobe was tiny (about half a meter wide) and already partly occupied by the ironing board, iron, and hair dryer; furthermore, there was no specific space for suitcases.
3) Inadequate cleaning service. Out of a five-day stay, on two separate occasions we returned in the evening, after a full day out, and found the room not made up and the towels not changed.
4) Exasperatingly slow elevator, which is also shared with the service staff. More than once, after a long wait, the elevator finally arrived but was completely occupied by staff and therefore unusable by guests.
5) Breakfast room definitely too small for the number of guests. Having breakfast becomes a stressful race to manage to find one of the few available tables.
6) I find the choice to give the same name, TownePlace Suites, to two different hotels located in the same area of Manhattan incomprehensible. It is a completely avoidable source of confusion, with the risk of unpleasant inconveniences. A hotel, which by definition welcomes people from out of town, should do everything possible to provide clear and unambiguous directions.

We will not return, and we will advise others against coming to this hotel.

author: James B
title: Great location, good price for midtown, but lots of flaws
text:
I wanted to like this location. We visit Birdland, across the street, a few times a year. Unfortunately, there were several issues to kick this review down to average, maybe below average.

On the positive side, staff are great; the room is clean with newer and comfortable bedding, newer furnishings and recently remodeled bathroom.  The included breakfast had oatmeal, cereal, eggs, sausage, ham and cheese sandwich, small yogurts and actually good coffee. The location is superb, and the price was very attractive for midtown.

On the negative side, the room is small (the website claims 260 sq ft, more like 200), I reserved a king size bed and the room was a queen size with visibly less space than the website picture  (several other reviews here had the same experience with that, what's going on?), I was on the 7th floor, two rooms away from the elevator, but all night long and especially in the morning, hear a mechanical clang-clung-clang every time the elevator stopped on a floor, I could not sleep; the a/c thermostat was defective so that the room setting was a high point and would cool the room down 5 degrees before shutting cooling, so sleeping was either very cold or very hot - a mechanic, who did not understand or speak English very well, drained the a/c of water and left, not fixing the thermostat issue; breakfast fruit was just a small apple and there are tables for about 15 people, so I inconveniently ate on a sofa; the elevator is painfully slow and tests your patience.

author: Sean M
title: Staff is great, and it’s clean, butttttt….
text:
It’s really difficult for me to give this place anything better than a mediocre review. 

First, the good: Hotel staff are friendly and helpful. Also, the location is close to Times Square but not too close. Everything was clean…room, bed, shower…very important, especially in NYC where cleanliness can’t be assumed.

Now, the bad: Everything is cramped. Lobby is small. Breakfast area is tiny. There’s only 5-6 tables in the breakfast area. Breakfast itself was mediocre at best. There’s one elevator. It’s painfully slow and makes banging sounds at every floor. Only seven floors in this building, but it’ll take you forever to get to/from your room. Once you make it to your room, prepare to be cramped. It’s so small, we questioned if it was actually smaller than a basic cruise ship room. There’s no space to do anything. Water pressure in the shower is too weak. Our first night was painfully hot. Maintenance came but couldn’t fix the AC. We later found out the AC was out on the entire 7th floor and wouldn’t be fixed until the morning. Management didn’t fight me the next morning when I asked to have the first night taken off the bill. Guess that should go up in the “good” section.

Kudos to the staff for making the best out of a building they have to know has a lot of issues, so at least there’s that. It’d take a lot for me to stay there again.

author: Kyle E
title: Decent Value Option
text:
The hotel’s location was one of its biggest advantages. It was conveniently located just a couple of blocks from Penn Station, Times Square, and many other popular New York City attractions, making it easy to get around the city.

When I arrived, I was quickly greeted by the front desk attendant and had a smooth check-in experience. One thing to note is that this is a very small hotel. There is only one elevator, and it is extremely slow. If you don’t mind waiting, it’s manageable, but it definitely became an inconvenience during my stay. The elevator was working, but I often chose to take the stairs instead, walking down four floors and up three floors each day, which became a bit frustrating.

The room itself was very clean, neat, and seemed well maintained. I appreciated the small suite-style kitchenette, which was a convenient feature and gave the room a little more functionality, especially for a longer stay.

However, I did encounter an issue with the bathroom. There appeared to be a small gnat issue or nest in the shower drain area, with several gnats flying around. It was annoying and, in my opinion, raised some concerns about cleanliness and hygiene perhaps with the city drain. I contacted the front desk to see if there were any other rooms available, but the hotel was fully booked during my stay, so I had to remain in the same room.

The hotel does offer complimentary breakfast, which included items such as sausage, eggs, bagels, oatmeal, and coffee. It was nothing elaborate, but it was a nice convenience to have available. I only used the breakfast once during my stay since it wasn’t really the type of meal I normally eat, but I appreciated the option.

Overall, this hotel is a decent choice for travelers looking to save a little money while staying in the heart of Manhattan. The location is excellent, and the rooms are clean and functional. However, due to the extremely slow elevator and the gnat issue in my bathroom, I would probably not choose this particular location again for a future New York City stay.

author: Louis A
title: Very Basic with VERY SLOW elevator in the front
text:
I am a marriott titanium so I think I've stayed at a wide gamut of their hotel brands.  This is my first Towneplace and I was prepared for it to be like a residence inn or similar brands.  Yes it was but I can say it didnt necessarily meet up to standards.  This is a smaller hotel in a very convenient location to times square.  I never felt it was noisy and it was clean.  
There are two different sections of the hotel; front and back (back faces 43rd st).  When I checked in I stayed in the front of the hotel in a reserved king room.  I asked for any upgraded rooms and they said there were none available.  After getting the keys it took 3 or 4 minutes for the elevator to arrive.  MIND YOU the hotel is maybe 5 or 6 stories so this is unacceptable.  Got to the room and it was a queen.  Went to the front desk and they said according to the computer it was a king.  I said you're more than welcome to come to the room and see it was a queen bed.  At this point it really didnt matter since I was told it was sold out and we can try to move you the next day.
The next day at 8am I went to the front desk and the person behind the desk was very pleasant and nice and said I can give you the larger room which has a king and is handicap accessible.  I took it.  This room was in the back hotel and the elevators actually worked and didnt take more than a minute to arrive.  THe room was much nicer.
The breakfast was basic and decent...exactly what I was expecting.  Also beware the front doors to the hotel auto locks at 7pm.  That's a little early for the times square area.  I never felt unsafe so not sure why that was even necessary
Lastly, I wish I could post on the marriott website, but you need to be invited to leave a review.  I relied on the above 4 star rating to book this hotel, but it really is a 3 star and I would have selected a different hotel.

author: Molly S
title: Great stay in the heart of Times Square
text:
​I had a really cool stay at the TownePlace Suites Manhattan Times Square. The location is perfect, but what truly made the experience memorable was the staff. Sebastian and the whole team were absolutely great—incredibly welcoming, helpful, and attentive throughout my entire visit.
​Highly recommend this spot if you're looking for an excellent stay in NYC. I will definitely be back and this thanks to the team.

author: Nathan B
title: Great Front Desk and Quality Stay!
text:
Shantel was the highlight of the stay. She was extremely pleasant during each interaction I had and those I could hear. This was my first experience at Towneplace and she made the difference.

Now the elevator literally took forever and I was often on it with handyman with loads of things but because it was too slow I couldn't chance missing it.

Otherwise for the rate it definitely was a surprise quality stay.

author: Anna N
title: Great amenities and a terrific location!
text:
A great Marriott property offering a very fine breakfast, comfortable suites and an engaging front desk team.
The location is awesome.
We had occasion to deal with one of the hotel Managers “Brian” and he was very client focused and sets a great example for the team.
A real gem of a property!

author: Katie E
title: DON’T STAY HERE IF YOU WANT A GOOD NIGHT’S SLEEP!
text: DO NOT STAY HERE IF YOU WANT A GOOD NIGHT’s SLEEP! While the location of this Marriott property was perfect for what we had planned in the theater district we had a horrible stay. On our first night, after driving 18 hours up to New York from Florida and wanting nothing more but a good night sleep, we were met with a room with no air-conditioning and pillows as thin as a cracker and a mattress that probably rivals most prisons. Our room was also facing the street, so the sound of traffic and sirens was also blaring all night. They didn’t move us to a new room until 3 PM the next day and this room is not without its flaws either: Such as two electrical outlets that don’t work, a bathroom door that doesn’t stay closed, which is not great for Privacy and again pillows as thin as crackers. My husband had to actually get up in the middle of the night and go down to the front desk and ask for a new pillows which he finally got after about an hour. I’m posted this same review on Google while we still had one more night stay here hoping that Marriott Management might see this annd actually take some action. NOTHING!! This hotel is in dire need of some corporate intervention and Marriott should be embarrassed to have this property in their portfolio. I have been a Marriott Bonvoy member for many years and I always looked for Marriott properties because they rarely if ever disappoint. This place does not fit in with what Marriott expectations should be. To further add to the aggravation. There is one elevator, which is slower, quite literally than walking up and down the stairs, which we did pretty much every day. Will never stay here again and will definitely do more research next time as apparently I can no longer rely on just the Marriott name! ☹️

author: Hannah F
title: Won’t be a 2nd visit
text:
If you’re from a town or city that has homes with white picket fences & flowers in the yard, you’ll be in for a culture shock! If you take the subway, you’ll have to walk past a pot shop where many of their clients just hang out in the streets. There seems to be a housing project closeby & some of the tenants pull out chairs to just hang out all day. 
Once inside the hotel, it seems ok. The hotel itself isn’t anything special. It fills the need. The only time anyone spoke to us from the front desk was when we checked in the 1st day & out the last. All of the other days, they just glanced at us going in &;out daily. 
Our room didn’t have a safe & was in need of a few hooks to hang towels on in the bathroom.the kitchen was equipped with the very bare basics, which were enough.  The morning free breakfast was pretty standard,but a nice option to get if you wanted. 
Our room faced the street & there were nights where we could hear loud people or music in the middle of the night, and we were on the 8th floor. Our room & the hotel seemed to be clean & decent enough, but honestly, nothing special enough to bring me back.

author: Leo D
title: DO NOT STAY HERE IF YOU WANT A GOOD NIGHT’s SLEEP!

author: Elena H
title: Lied to and dirty
text: There were many MANY issues. We checked in and they didn’t have our room type available (which we booked? Like what) We booked two queens but were given a king. We were told to move to our actual room type tomorrow. That’s fine and if it ended there the review would still be high. I will say though that the woman working the front desk that night was super helpful and it was not at all her fault. The next day we go to move rooms and the guy working the desk says sure and looks into it, says the new room is ready and gives us our keys, we ask and confirm with him we are moving to a 2 queen room. We head up to the room and it’s a queen and pull out sofa. Front desk person straight up lied to us, we called front desk and he said our room type “doesen’t exist” (it actually does he was just being too lazy to fix the issue, corporate confirmed this to us later) not wanting to go down and argue cuz it doesn’t get you anywhere and he was clearly too lazy to fix it anyway we decided to deal with it. The room was also FILTHY. Dog pee stains on the floor, Sticky stuff on the wall for example. I would say that the bed was pretty comfortable. The shower however must have a small water tank connected to other rooms. So if multiple rooms by you take a shower, you do not get hot water. Whatever you do, there are other marriots that are cheaper in the area, do not go here, I did not enjoy a single bit of my 4 nights here. I am a lifetime Titanium member and this is easily the worst Marriott I have ever stayed at.

author: Caleb X
title: Great Place
text:
We had a very good stay at TownePlace Suites by Marriott New York Manhattan. The overall experience was positive the hotel is clean, comfortable, and in a great location with easy access to everything in Manhattan.
A special mention to Jeremy at reception, who was exceptionally good  very friendly, kind, and welcoming. He truly made a difference in our stay with his helpful attitude and warm service.
The only downside was that the Wi-Fi connectivity on the 7th floor was quite weak at times, which made it a bit difficult to work or stream smoothly.
Overall, it was a pleasant stay, and we would definitely consider staying here again, especially because of the excellent staff and convenient location.

author: Poppy A
title: Great experience
text: Great spot near everything we wanted to do. Room was clean and breakfast good. There were two ladies who prepared the breakfast each morning, and did a great job. The rest of the staff was equally helpful and accommodating. We'll be staying here again next time.

author: Sophia D
title: Top notch staff.
text: Had a small issue when I arrived which required another room. Big deal it happens. But Sebastian and Rayven went to great lengths to make sure our room was perfect and apologized many times for the inconvenience. They both need raises.

author: Gavin W
title: Room With A Patio
text:
My husband and I really enjoyed this hotel. We stayed for six nights and this basement room felt like a little apartment. We were supposed to come the last week in January, but due to weather we had to reschedule for the first week in February. Jeremy showed us a few of the patio rooms. He went above and beyond to help us with our room and any questions that we had during the stay. Everyone at this location is extremely helpful and they go out of their way to help. The location is perfect for walking to Times Square, theater district, and a bit of a walk to Central Park. Subway is right there to take to different locations. We had the breakfast for the additional charge and they changed it up everyday. 
Overall, we really enjoyed our stay and will be back.

author: Ruby I
title: Great location, professional staff, rooms a bit small
text:
The hotel is located close to Times Square and is easily accessible by road and subway. We walked from the hotel to almost every location as we could easily get to Central Park, Broadway, downtown, fifth ave etc from the hotel. 

The staff at this hotel were polite, professional and always nice to speak to. The free breakfast everyday was decent, charged everyday and this was a good way to start our days. 

The room was small, the bed not the most comfortable. It was clean and serviced everyday. The bathroom was good and it had a good shower. 

We could store our bags before check in and after checkout if we needed to. 

We enjoyed our stay here, thank you.

author: Lucas K
title: Disappointing check-in experience
text:
Unfortunately, my check‑in experience left a very negative impression. Due to a snowstorm, I arrived at the hotel around noon and asked whether early check‑in was possible. I was told that rooms were available, but that I could not be checked in because someone might arrive later and be willing to pay an early check‑in fee. Being told there was availability but having it withheld on that basis felt unprofessional and inconsistent with what is stated on the hotel’s website.

The website notes that early check‑in is based on availability, which the front desk confirmed existed. There was also no signage at the front desk indicating an early check‑in fee. After waiting an additional hour, I ultimately paid the fee simply to access a room that I already knew was available. The fee was also taxed, bringing it to $54.44, which was not communicated. 

As an event planner who frequently travels and works with Marriott properties, this was an unusual and disappointing experience. I rarely leave negative reviews, but this situation felt mishandled and contrary to standard hospitality practices. I hope management reviews how this is handled in the future.

author: Amelia U
title: Surprisingly good choices
text: Nice and helpful staff, good location

author: Mason J
title: Central and convenient
text: I stayed with my daughter for 6 nights in a studio apartment, small but well equipped. Very convenient location, very friendly reception staff. Highly recommended!

author: Holly O
title: Small but convenient location
text: The room was a bit small and tight, but the location is right around the corner from all Earl's Court Station transportation choices.  Lots of good selection of convenience stores and restaurants around it too. The staff were courteous and efficient.  The bed in our room was really soft and one should be careful when getting close to the edge as you will roll off. Their continental breakfast is OK but nothing special.

author: Charlotte K
title: Overbooking. Cancelled 2 hours before arrived
text: Stay away from this hotel. I booked a room there a few days before my trip. A couple of days later, they asked for confirmation that I would definitely be arriving, which I provided. On the day of arrival, two hours before I was due to get there, I received a message from Booking.com stating that there was no accommodation for me. By that time, I had already been on the train for four hours and had two hours of the journey left. Booking.com isn't any better either, so I advise being careful with them.

author: Michael X
title: Not a trustworthy place !
text:
A very upsetting and unsettling experience. This is not a trustworthy hotel. They cancelled my confirmed reservation without my consent, leaving me with no clear explanation and no support. This is not correct. 

To make matters worse, I noticed that the exact room I had booked was listed again shortly afterwards, but at a much higher price.
Therefore, I would strongly advise others to book elsewhere.

author: Claire M
title: Fabulous stay with a lovely touch
text:
Stayed for one night with my daugher. I emailed the hotel to ask if we could check in early as we had a 4pm pre theatre reservation for my daughters 21st. 
They replied back straight away saying they had noted this on the booking and would try and accommodate if possible.
We arrived at 1pm and room was ready. The most lovely touch was a box of M&S biscuits and a birthday card for my daugher was waiting in the room.
Really friendly staff, great location with a tube station 3 minute walk away. 
Lovely well equipped, clean rooms.
Thank you for a wonderful stay and the biscuits.
Will use again and recommend.

author: Aiden F
title: Total scammed hotel
text:
This hotel is totally scam.
I have done booking and it’s confirmed by hotel but when i reached to hotel for check in they said your booking is cancelled without any reason, i have got my friends came from canada to visit uk and the scammed us, we have no where else to because all the hotel was full in central London and its not only us they scammed everyone who came at that day.

author: Nathan F
title: Bad
text: They said they had no rooms left despite confirming our booking and saying we are arriving late. They did this to the two pairs of people in front of us too and offered no help for us to find other hotels at 1 in the morning left 6 people stranded to find their own place to stay despite confirming our bookings. Had to sleep in the car that night and everything. Awful to overbook and not even bother helping us with somewhere else when we were all clearly not from London too.

author: Pablo Q
title: Would do for a brief visit. Don't expect a hotel, more like a boarding house.
text: Small room, no space to move but clean. The bathroom was tiny, hard to turn around without bumping a body part. Breakfast was woeful, not a cooked breakfast, only continental. There was not enough tables so joined a lengthy queue. Just as well I wasn't rushing to catch a plane.

author: Benjamin X
title: Room cancelled.
text:
On arriving at the hotel the staff were too busy talking with each other to deal with us. 
When they did speak to us she asked when the booking was made. As if that would make a difference. She had our name 
Surely they could see on their computers when the booking was made. 
When we gave the date of the booking we were told there was no booking made as they had been hacked. No apology given just sitting there blankly looking at us. Then leaving us to try and find accommodation (affordable) in London. 
Seems to be a regular thing of cancelling or denying bookings exist from what I can see online. 
I would avoid the place unless you like to hunt for hotel rooms at the last minute. We ended up staying in a pod hotel which was an experience. Sleeping in a box for 3 days with minimal air con, not what I had planned for our stay

author: Abigail G
title: Disgraceful
text: Terrible experience. Turned up at hotel. Receptionist too busy chatting to other members of staff to deal with customers. Then when she could be bothered told us our booking was cancelled as they were hacked. No apology no resolution. Absolutely disgraceful. Don’t book with them. Look elsewhere!

author: Tyler G
title: Avoid this hotel at all costs
text:
We booked two nights through Agoda for £126, which was an exceptionally good price for London. However, when we arrived, the receptionist informed us that our reservation did not exist in their system and that they could not honour the booking. We were told that the hotel’s email had been hacked and were offered only two options: pay a much higher price for the room or contact Agoda ourselves.

The most concerning part was what happened next. Although our reservation had been made through Agoda, the receptionist repeatedly insisted that we call a UK telephone number displayed on a permanent Booking.com sign at the reception desk. Instead of contacting Agoda or trying to resolve the issue directly, they kept directing us to this number. The whole situation felt highly suspicious and raised serious concerns about whether guests were being intentionally redirected away from the platform they had actually booked through.

While we were waiting in the lobby, we met several other guests who were experiencing exactly the same problem. This was clearly not an isolated incident.

From a customer’s perspective, it looked like a classic bait-and-switch. Guests are attracted by unusually low prices, only to be told on arrival that their reservation cannot be found and that the only immediate solution is to pay a significantly higher rate after they have already travelled.

Whether this is the result of poor management or something more deliberate, the outcome is the same: reservations are not honoured, guests are placed under pressure, and their holiday starts with unnecessary stress.

I would strongly recommend choosing another hotel if you want to avoid the risk of finding yourself in the same situation.

author: Michael P
title: Booking cancelled due to "overbooking" while the same room remained available at a higher price
text:
Booked through Booking.com at a very cheap price. I had a feeling there might be a catch, as hotel rooms in London are rarely available at that rate. Sure enough, just two days before I was due to arrive in London, I received an email saying my booking had been cancelled because the hotel was "overbooked".

What doesn't make sense is that when I checked Booking.com afterwards, the same room types, 5 in total, were still available for the exact same dates, just at more than double the price. I've raised this with Booking.com, as it's difficult to understand how a hotel can be overbooked while still advertising rooms for sale on the same dates. 

Trebovir Hotel does not appear to be operating in a reputable manner if bookings made at lower prices are routinely cancelled while rooms remain available for sale at higher rates.

I'd advise others to proceed with caution.

author: Molly M
title: Shady Booking Practices
text:
Booked a room with this hotel on 25 June 2026 for a stay on 03 July 2026

Received a confirmation message via Booking.com on 02 July 2026 confirming the room

At 10am I received a notification that my room had been cancelled as they had "overbooked" which was extremely interesting to see as they were subsequently advertising the same room that they had just cancelled for 5x the price

Extremely poor service and disappointing that Booking.com allow hotels to price gouge like this

Would not consider booking with this shady business in the future

Fortunately I managed to find another hotel, although it was considerably more expensive that what I had originally booked for

Would give 0 stars if I could

author: Maria P
title: Refused Stay
text:
Booked to stay here, turned up and was rejected, they claim they had been hacked and that was the reason for the overbooking.

No alternative accommodation offered, no contact number given to escalate the issue, no refund offered.

To rub salt in the wound, the man behind the desk claimed that they knew about it last week - so why on earth have they not cancelled these bookings?

They have switched off their phone line so no way to contact them despite their legal responsibility in this matter.

author: Leo H
title: Avoid at ALL cost
text:
Booked this hotel for one night while travelling to London for a concert. We arrived to be told our room was no longer available. The man on reception just pointed to a sign saying the hotel had been “hacked”, which meant rooms had been listed at a 50% discount, so they wouldn’t be honouring our booking.

The hotel seemed completely unfazed. There was no apology and absolutely no help finding somewhere else to stay. We booked through Booking.com and our booking was still showing as confirmed. It was only later that I noticed an email sent at 8:45 that morning saying our booking had been cancelled due to “overbooking”, by which point we were already on our way to London.

Whilst we were there, another three groups arrived to be told exactly the same thing. We ended up stranded in London with nowhere to stay on one of the busiest nights of the year. 

Absolutely shocking experience. I genuinely can’t believe Booking.com are still allowing this hotel to be listed when so many people have had similar issues.

Avoid at all cost!!

author: Kyle K
title: DO NOT VISIT
text: Do not book this place! Cancelled on us on the morning of our trip we are now without a hotel for an even we are seeing. Tried to contact the property multiple times on the lead up to our stay to double check our reservation with no luck.

author: William M
title: Be Warned!
text: Booked through booking.com. I was asked to send the property an email as confirmation which I did. After a day or two, the Hotel cancelled my reservation without giving any reason as of why. Checked spam and I had received a very suspicious email telling me they were offering 50% on all reservations, and to follow a link to pay straight away. I messaged the property and I’m still waiting for a response. After reading other reviews this seems to be the modus operandi of this Hotel and I’m actually glad they did cancel my reservation!

author: Gavin O
title: Deceptive offers.
text: I didn't even get to go. I booked through Booking. 50% off, I pay on the day of arrival and free cancellation. Surprise!!! After a few hours, I received an email asking for payment in advance if I wanted to keep the offer. I obviously did not accept it and informed booking. The reservation was still correct in the app. They put me in contact with the hotel to confirm. I never received a response. In the end, they did respond to the Booking messages saying that they did not accept the reservation a few days before my trip! This shows very little seriousness and they are not trustworthy at all.

author: Ruby W
title: Cancelled my booking on the day.
text:
Do not stay here.

I booked this hotel several days in advance and, on the morning of check-in, while already travelling from Coventry to London with my child for a concert, I happened to open the booking messages and saw that my reservation had been cancelled.

There had been no phone call and no advance warning. I then checked my email and found a cancellation email sent only minutes earlier — just hours before we were due to arrive.

When I called the hotel, I was told they had overbooked and had cancelled multiple reservations. No alternative accommodation was offered, no assistance was provided, and the only response was that the booking had been cancelled “free of charge” — as if that solved the problem.

We were left travelling to London with nowhere to stay and forced to find last-minute accommodation at much higher prices.

This was completely unacceptable customer service and created unnecessary stress, especially travelling with a child. If you book here, be aware there appears to be a risk that your reservation may not be honoured even on the day of arrival.
They also seem to lie as they told Booking.com that i cancelled! Even though i have a recorded telephone conversation that where the guy on the phone said they did. 

I will never book with this hotel again.

author: Sophia B
title: Room Cancelled With No Explanation
text: Absolutely abysmal service. I booked my room and was asked to email the hotel directly to confirm, which I did immediately. Two days before I was due to travel, I was told that my room has been cancelled. The room has now been put back on sale, got four times the price I had originally booked for. I can only assume the hotel are doing this in order to try and get more money from me. I have repeatedly called and emailed and been ignored every time. Absolutely shocking service, and I have now been left stranded in London.

author: Jack E
title: Scam
text: Scam! I booked a room during a promotion and it was canceled by the establishment under the pretext of a bug - it’s shameful!!!!

author: Harper H
title: Excellent location
text: Cute, clean hotel, excellent location for visiting the city on foot. Good value for money. Varied, abundant breakfast with the option of takeout. Kind and courteous. I would return.

author: George S
title: Good location
text: 5 nights stay. Outside, a part of the staff who also berated us said 'shame on you' because we were staying there. Not very nice. The staff who did work did their best. The lying is good. Breakfast was really mediocre with little choice.

author: Daisy W
title: New York
text: Good hotel near Times Square, clean.  The reception staff is very friendly. Elevators a bit slow, as there are few compared to the number of users. Breakfast is so-so, with too many people at any time. However, I would stay there again.

author: Maria I
title: GOOD EXPERIENCE
text:
Hotel very close to Time Square, friendly staff at reception. Average rooms, a little small but you survive, super crowded breakfast room, but we always found food that was readily replenished just finished at the buffet. Lifts a bit slow, in fact to go to the highest floors there are only two.
However to recommend.

author: Luke T
title: Uncomfortable and unwelcoming.
text: Avoid at all cost. Management were silent on complaints I brought up during my stay. They respond here but won't return calls. Dirty and Dumpy and rooms that didn't get cleaned. Avoid.

author: Paolo K
title: Poor Service, bad housekeeping, dire breakfast, and disinterested management
text: Be prepared for disruptions, poor service, and a mediocre experience. There's currently a labor dispute happening outside this hotel. Be prepared to be taunted and yelled at when coming and going from the property. Staff were inattentive and dismissive. Housekeeping either didn't visit promptly or when they did visit didn't leave basic things like shampoo and body wash. We had to call down multiple times to have amenities replenished. Breakfast room staff were pleasant and cheerful despite the absolutely mediocre offerings. I complained but management doesn't seem to really care about guest experiences. I would book next door at any of the other neighboring properties before booking here again.

author: Michael F
title: Be prepared to be heckled by protestors as you enter and leave the property
text:
Walking up to the hotel to see an inflatable rat and strikers was not the best experience. Guests have  to enter through a makeshift side entrance and each time one enters an exits the hotel,  the employees on strike jeer at you. This did not make for a pleasant experience. The staff at the front desk were hospitable as usual and the Titanium benefits were appreciated. The hotel allowed guests to cancel without a penalty; however, due to high hotel demand in NY that day, all other properties were prohibitively expensive, so I didn't have a choice. The room itself was a bit dated and I miss the slippers and robes that the property once used to provide. The bathroom amenities are minimal with no lotion, etc.

I do hope that the hotel and the striking workers can come to an agreement as a guest should not expect this type of atmosphere when staying at a property.

author: Oscar M
title: Very Disappointing Stay – Would Not Return
text:
I was extremely disappointed with my stay at the Fairfield by Marriott Manhattan Times Square.

The biggest issue was that there were union protesters outside the hotel every day from approximately 6:00 a.m. until 10:00 p.m. They were loud and, at times, approached guests entering and leaving the hotel in a way that made us feel uncomfortable. This ongoing disruption significantly affected our stay. What was most frustrating is that the hotel never disclosed this situation when I made my reservation. Had I known, I would have booked a different hotel.

The hotel itself was also a major disappointment. The facilities felt run-down and poorly maintained, and the overall condition of the property was far below what I expect from a Marriott brand. The common areas looked worn, and the hotel gave the impression that it has not been properly cared for in quite some time.

Between the daily protests, the lack of transparency, and the poor condition of the property, this was one of the most disappointing hotel experiences I’ve had. I chose this hotel because I expected the quality and standards typically associated with Marriott, but unfortunately, this property did not meet those expectations. I would not stay here again and cannot recommend it.

author: Carlos N
title: Never again
text: So what to say…we stayed 8 nights, and we only received a hello twice while passing by the reception. There are demonstrations in front of the hotel, against the hotel, day and night with drums, whistles, and insults when entering and leaving the hotel… towels and sheets were changed every day but the cleaning was not great, dust and the bathroom were not cleaned for 6 days… we had to ask for toilet paper, shower gel… we had specified upon arrival that we wanted to pay the taxes additionally in cash, we were told no problem it would be at check-out, check-out was done at 5 am while we were sleeping, we received the bill by email upon waking and the credit card was charged. Old hotel. The only positive point was the breakfast, which was complete, and the smile and kindness of Diomarys Correa; otherwise, we will never return.

author: Lucas H
title: Teresa Cruz and Diomarys Correa are delightful breakfast team members
text:
Diomarys Correa, Breakfast Attendant, did an amazing job making us feel at home.  Diomarys went out of her way to find us snacks for us to nibble on in our room. She was helpful answering all our questions and a delightful person to chat with each morning. Diomarys has such a positive attitude.

Teresa Cruz, Breakfast Lead, did a fantastic job as hostess greeting and seating us each morning. Teresa has so much energy and charm. It was a pleasure chatting with her each morning of our stay. She is very professional and she is so sweet.  She has the kind of positive personality that makes you want to be around her.

author: Charlie X
title: Great location and nice accomodations.
text: We were here about 12 years ago and because of the location and rooms we came back. They did not disappoint. The lobby is nice and the staff is very welcoming. They helped me sort out valet parking and the room with two double beds was a nice size. I appreciate that you have to have a key to use the elevator and the breakfast was good. It is right across from the transit station so you can catch a bus or subway. Walgreens is on the corner, StarBucks is close. Check out The Drama bookstore if you like plays and the arts. We will be back.

author: Emma L
title: Great
text:
We received a very warm welcome. The double rooms are excellent and extremely comfortable.
Special thanks to Diomarys Correa and her team, who greeted us every morning at breakfast with a big smile and provided outstanding service. They were always attentive and made us feel truly cared for.

author: Ian W
title: Good location, experience with lights and shadows.
text:
The hotel itself is very well located. Everything is close: subway, bus, attractions.
The reception service was quick and efficient.
The breakfast offered was quite limited and very crowded with people. The assigned area is much smaller than the capacity of guests they have. However, the young ladies who attended were very kind.
The main problem lay in the room:
It is a small room as such, with the basics, but it already shows wear with old furniture and lacks general maintenance. 
During the 3 nights we stayed, they never cleaned the room.
The rooms are moderately soundproofed, so some noise from the outside and adjacent rooms seeps through. 
We were on the 2nd floor, so the view is almost nonexistent; however, it is not something we value much, as we spent our time outside exploring the city. 
Decent hotel with limited amenities, and the best part is the location.

author: Marco R
title: Near Times Square
text: We returned to this hotel after 9 years. Large rooms, friendly staff from reception, cleaning, breakfast room. We had room 2202 (overlooking the view) and room 1108 (overlooking the interior). We received an upgrade for the room overlooking the view, thank you for granting our request. But thanks to Jalissa and Mikey for letting us late check out. The location is spectacular near Times Square and all kinds of subways. When we come back he'll always be here. Value for money optimalz

author: Juan J
title: Excellent stay
text:
The hotel is very good.
Staff always helpful and very kind, Sarita welcomed us on the first day and provided a complimentary basket with water and various snacks with a welcome card, much appreciated.
The room is a good size (it was with two double beds), huge shower room and very comfortable.
Breakfast (also wanting to take away) very varied; there are also waffles to be made independently and filled with chocolate chips or jam.
Maybe there were cold cuts or croissants missing, but there were slices of bread and bagels to heat and stuff with jam jellies or peanut butter. There was also porridge and all the hot drinks, juices at the vending machine.
Also present the gym but not used.
In the basement (LL) there were also dispensers for drinks and snacks, at the reception water (with lemon and ice) available to guests with plastic cups.
 The location is excellent, a short walk from the subway station and not even 10 minutes from Times Square (it's on 40th St).
Really highly recommended, if we return to New York we will definitely stay with them.

author: Juan V
title: They did everything.
text: He did everything. Basic breakfast but very good staff readiness and cleanliness.  We would like to thank Teresa Cruz and Diomarys Correa for their attention, who always attended us out of 10 with a very good disposition.

author: Ethan C
title: Outstanding stay at Fairfield!  Wonderful staff!
text: The staff at the Fairfield were exceptional.  I accidentally left my AirPod earphone on my bed and discovered this 10 minutes after I left the hotel.  I called the front desk and Jonathan took action right away and said he’d work to help locate it.   Imagine how easy it is to miss a white earphone on white sheets).  The housekeeper Jenny was very meticulous and found them and left them for me.   During my stay, the breakfast staff was super nice and helpful.  Teresa was very pleasant and helpful and her staff did a wonderful job managing the seating, ensuring good flow despite a lot of guests, ensuring everything was well stocked, and helping us get what we needed.  I stay at many Bonvoy facilities and this was great not just for facilities, location, but also the staff!  Thank you to Jonathan, Jenny, and Teresa.  Thanks for making for a great stay!

author: Julien S
title: Great Hotel in Times Square!
text: Excellent location! Front desk team were helpful with my hot water requests. A special Thank you to Ms Teresa Cruz and her friendly team for making us feel welcomed and maintaining a lively vibe during breakfast! One breakfast morning I was missing my kids very much however, watching Ms Diomarys Correa dancing while hosting  breakfast cheered me up! Fantastic breakfast team ! Thank you for your hospitality.  Lots of love from Fathima & Shaz ( London)

author: Sophia B
title: Jalissa to the rescue!
text:
I came to NYC as part of a big group. There was an error with the booking as I had planned on having a solo room, but when we checked in, I had been out with three other people. 
Jalissa Jordan at the front desk was so helpful and did everything she could to amend the situation. She was very patient as we explained the mixup and she was able to quickly correct the oversight. It was so nice after a long travel day (TSA delays!) to have one of my first interactions in the city to be one of top notch customer service and courtesy. Thank you, Jalissa!

author: Kyle H
title: Tactical position
text:
Conveniently located for visiting downtown New York. 
Our room was at the back of the hotel, so the city noise was muffled. The room wasn't huge, but it was still comfortable for two people. 
I find carpeting in hotels unsanitary, but unfortunately, it's common in many... Breakfast was quite good, although the space was limited, which can lead to long lines if you don't arrive early. 
Very helpful and friendly staff!

author: Isla L
title: Just perfect
text: Just perfect. The service is great and also it’s clean and has the best location to stay. Directly at Kensington Gardens and Hyde Park you can do nearly everything without getting in the tube or at the bus. It’s awesome. The rooms are great designed and you have everything there for a great stay. The people who working there are always friendly and work with a smile and helps you at everything. All together…we will definitely come back soon and was the best stay in London you can think about

author: Hannah C
title: Still no refund
text:
Had a good stay at NOX Waterloo and hoping for the same. Booked a room with air conditioning months in advance but just provided with a fan and no air con. Complained and asked to be moved but no other rooms available. 34 degrees and the room was unbearable. Moved on the second night to a basement room which was fine.

Complained a number of times and eventually got the offer of a £50 refund. Still waiting for this a month after the offer.

author: Hannah C
title: Personal belongings went missing after luggage storage.
text:
The location of the hotel is very good. It is within walking distance of both Queensway and Bayswater Underground stations, making it easy to get around London.
We were staying in the jacuzzi suite the room itself was okay, but there were several things that could easily be improved. Although there was a kitchenette, there was no tea towel or dish towel, making it difficult to wash and dry dishes. We were only given large bath towels, with no hand towels or smaller towels for our face or hair. We asked the staff if they could provide smaller towels, but they told us they didn’t have any. There was also only one chair in the room, so whenever we wanted to have breakfast together, one of us had to sit on the bed, which was quite inconvenient.
The check-out experience was also disappointing. We were not asked how our stay had been or whether everything was okay. Instead, the receptionist simply asked for our key card.
The biggest issue, however, happened after our stay. We stored our luggage at the hotel after checking out. Before leaving our luggage there, I still had my AirPods. Afterwards, they went missing. When I checked Apple’s Find My app, the AirPods remained at the hotel location after we had left. Later that evening, at around 10:00 PM, the location started moving and has since remained at the same residential address. I contacted the hotel immediately, but the only response I received was that housekeeping had thoroughly cleaned the room and found nothing. They also advised me to file a police report, which I intend to do.
I also came across several reviews from other guests mentioning missing belongings after leaving their luggage in the hotel’s luggage storage. While I cannot say with certainty what happened, the timeline shown in the Find My app, combined with my experience, has made this situation extremely concerning and frustrating.
Because of this experience, I will not be returning to this hotel. I would advise other travellers to keep a close eye on their valuables and carefully consider whether they want to leave their luggage in storage here.

author: Michael L
title: Not conducive to a restful night sleep
text: Whilst attractive, not conducive to a decent night’s sleep with a continuous running toilet however many times I tried to flush.   Gas light by the operating company who said they could not verify a fault, after ‘we carried out an investigation into the issue’  - how was this possible within 18 minutes of receiving my email.   Keep searching for a better place to stay if you are in the area

author: Harper N
title: Excellent
text: Location was perfect few minutes walk from Queensway Underground station. Staff very friendly helpful, room and hotel was clean and well equipped

author: Jessica Q
title: Convenient, clean, uncomplicated and helpful!
text: Easy, uncomplicated and clean. Great for the BST concert. Dropped bag off early, they gave us key card to get in after check-in hours and put bag in room for us. Then also stored our bag next day. Would stay here again x

author: Ella K
title: Special Occasion Ruined
text:
I booked Nox Hotel Kensington Gardens for a special occasion and it turned into a very disappointing experience. From 10pm until 9:30am, the room had no electricity, no heating, no Wi‑Fi, no lighting, and the room was freezing. We couldn’t use any of the facilities we paid for and spent the entire night in an uncomfortable, cold room.

There was no staff present, no communication, and no support during the outage. We only found out what happened after checkout. They also only told us that there was an emergency number on the card. The receptionist said nothing and she looked like she didn’t even wanna be there. Her attitude was a no no and she wasn’t presentable at all! 

What made the situation worse was the hotel’s response afterwards. They insisted the outage lasted only “a couple of hours,” which is simply false. The person replying as “Manager” didn’t provide a name, didn’t introduce themselves, and didn’t offer any solution  which makes me question whether it was even a manager responding.

The way this was handled shows a lack of accountability and customer care. I cannot recommend this hotel based on my experience.

author: Freya J
title: Signature Jacuzzi Room
text: Short walk to Queensway tube station, easy to find, pleasant check in staff. We booked the signature jacuzzi room for my birthday for a reasonable price for the area and were very excited to experience the double hot tub bath. The room was clean, modern, comfortable, has a powerful rainfall shower, quiet, big tv with streaming apps . There was a small kitchenette (no wine glasses) and plenty of soft towels. However the jacuzzi would only send out boiling hot water (the screen read 50C!!) The reception was unmanned at this point and although there was an out of hours number for emergencies, we didn’t warrant this being an emergency. There was no manual in the room on how to use so we had to google the brand and find our own instructions. There was also a panel near the bath on the wall which would not work and we have no idea what this is for. We got the reception lady to look the next morning with the hopes we could use before checkout and she confirmed the temperature tap was broken and would not go round to the cold water side. She said she would report this to the management team. On checkout, she confirmed off her own back that she had spoken to the management team and they will be in contact. Unfortunately, we’ve heard nothing. After a week I sent an email directly to the hotel, and then 3 days later to the general Nox email. Still nothing. Very disappointing and puts me off using the chain again, despite the good parts of our experience. Sadly we have received no compensation or reimbursement for not being able to use our rooms full facility. We stayed at this hotel for the jacuzzi bath but could not use this at all, so would have stayed somewhere else if we had known it was broken (Why were there no checks done by staff prior to guest check in?)

author: Evie Y
title: HORRIBLE.
text:
Horrible experience! We just returned, and I do not recommend this property, the photos they show speak of the beautiful glories of the past. When booking we asked for a room suitable for an allergy sufferer (Asthma) and instead we found a room that is in very bad condition (see photo) the most amazing thing is that we found a cockroach walking in the bathroom!! I immediately objected to the lobby, but unfortunately they had no other rooms, we looked for a new hotel but unfortunately when you do not master the language it is not easy at all and reluctantly we stayed. And unfortunately it does not end here, another thing that unfortunately or fortunately I have noticed, that the fire extinguisher was overhauled in August 2024, and given the facts of the Crans-Montana tragedy I think it says it all!!!

Clearly I have all the photos........

author: Maria T
title: Disappointing customer service
text:
I am staying at NOX Kensington, however, my experience before arrival was very disappointing.

Shortly after making my booking, I contacted the hotel to request assistance with a reservation issue. Despite reaching out immediately, communication was slow, inconsistent, and required several follow-ups via different channels to receive clear responses.

While I will still be staying at the property due to a lack of alternatives, the pre-arrival customer service caused unnecessary stress and did not reflect the level of care I would expect from a hotel.

Based on this experience, I would be hesitant to recommend this hotel, particularly to guests who value responsive and customer-focused service.

author: Maria F
title: WORST STAY EVER
text: I checked into this hotel and I was standing outside for over 30 mins because no one was at the front desk! The lady finally came and said “oh I had to check a room that’s why I was not able to answer” ok fine ! I then went to the room that was Dusty/ Moldy! I called down to the front desk agent who didn’t care at all she stayed I will have to stay in this room nothing she can do! Keep in mind she came up and saw all of this! I asked her to please relocate me to a cleaner room she denied it and said I have to stay in this same nasty room ! I wish TripAdvisor had a way to upload videos so I can post ! Whatever you do, DO NOT ever stay here!!!

author: Dylan V
title: Recommend for events at Hyde Park
text:
We stayed here for one night July 2025. The receptionist was very helpful and the room was ready early allowing for early check-in.
We booked here as it’s within walking distance to an event we were attending at Hyde Park.
The room was exceptionally clean & well presented, the air con was a much appreciated added bonus.
The bed was comfortable and the linen clean.
The room had a good selection of extras such as a microwave, toaster , coffee machine & fridge.
The lighting in the bathroom was good and there were also two full length mirrors.
We would book again if attended an event in the area.

author: Sydney Y
title: Great location, very well designed small room - has everything you need
text:
Location perfect for us (we did lots of walking to include lovely leisurely walk from Sky Garden to the hotel), very close to Notting Hill and practically beside Hyde Park.

Hotel itself is small but lovely, recently refurbished and is clean with all the mod cons - we were very impressed. 

The BEST shower ever and bed really comfortable.  Service staff friendly and helpful.

Only downside to staying here is that there is not a huge choice of places to eat in the direct area.

Would definately stay here again and would recommend

author: Charlotte B
title: Disappointing Stay: Missing items from luggage and Unresponsive Management
text:
My recent stay at your hotel was incredibly frustrating, despite a few positives. While I appreciated that the hotel was clean and in a good location, these aspects were completely overshadowed by a major issue: two of my dresses went missing from my luggage. 

After checkout, I asked and was advised that I could leave my bags with the hotel for a few hours, which I did.Upon collecting them later and returning home, I discovered that two dresses were missing from my luggage. These items were securely packed at the time I left them with your staff.

I've already tried to resolve this by calling the Hotel the following day and emailing the management team, but I've received absolutely no reply. This lack of communication and apparent disregard for a guest's lost property is completely unacceptable.
Losing two personal items isn't just an incoming ; it's a significant disappointment, and the hotel's failure to address my concerns has only compounded my frustration. 
Given my experience, I absolutely do not recommend this hotel.

author: Maria E
title: SUPER POSITIVE HOLIDAY
text: We stayed at this hotel for 5 days and what about the room always spotless (it was cleaned every day), the friendliness of Vikita really made us feel at home, the hotel is located in a nice area connected by both the metro and bus stops. Unfortunately, the only negative note is the size of the room that unfortunately despite also having a small kitchenette is not large enough (we could not open the suitcase and at the same time walk in the room).

author: Ruby O
title: Noisy and small.
text: Good location to enjoy the Notting Hill Carnival, but the other aspects are very improveable: very small room (two cabin bags cannot be left open on the floor) and too basic for two people, very uncomfortable bed, too small closet and dwarf bathroom (your legs crash against the toilet paper when sitting on the toilet). The best, the shower. Soundproofing is nefarious, and not because of street noise, but between rooms, the partitions look like paper. Except for the fridge and coffee maker, we didn't use anything from the kitchen; without it being dirty, we didn't find it very clean. Also, one of the nights the fire alarm went off and no one gave us any explanation of the reason.

author: Marta E
title: Excellent value for money
text: Really modern, clean hotel in a fabulous location and such a bargain for London. The room was exceptional for the price and so well planned out. There was a slight problem with water temperature in the morning I think due to some workmen in the vicinity affecting electricity supply but that is not the hotels fault.

author: Megan M
title: Good central location, great hotel for a few nights stay.
text:
Great Central Location. Staff were really friendly upon arrival, stored our bags until checkout time and when checked in our bags were already put in our room. Room was very clean and cleaners did a fantastic job. Bathroom is modern aswell as the kitchenette which is very useful. Tv is big and has lots of channels plus Netflix. 

 The bed isn’t the biggest double, my partner and I are small yet it was quite tight for space. Also the ceiling is thin and you can hear upstairs quite easily.

author: Diego T
title: Nice location
text:
I took a short solo trip, saying at NOX Kensington Gardens for a couple of nights and arrived before check-in which is at 3pm so left my bags behind the reception desk for a short time. I was given a very clean room with windows which was a nice surprise since I booked a windowless room. It was fairly quiet and the only noise I heard was the cleaners shouting in the morning. The room was cleaned daily and the location of the hotel is nice - being fairly close to Queensway station and Kensington Gardens but not amongst the hustle. 

A couple of things I should mention are the kitchenette lights which are motion censored and only stay on for about five seconds. Secondly, there is no dishcloth or anything similar for drying up etc. I know these are both small things but they make a difference over the course of a few days. Finally the charge for a late check out (from 11am onwards) seemed very steep. 

Aside from that, the staff were nice and the hotel felt safe. I would recommend it if you’re looking for a place to stay in that area.

author: Hannah A
title: Modern, new, very clean, centrally located
text:
Perfect accommodation for two. Room very clean and practically furnished, facilities (shower, hairdryer, kitchenette) very modern and new. Built in a space-saving way. Everything was there, even bottles of water and extra tea were given on request, good underground connection in the middle of London and if you are travelling from Heathrow you can get to Paddington station directly.
We would go back anytime. At night we had the window open and it was quiet, we were very satisfied.

author: Freya V
title: Experience it! YOLO
text: The negative reviews are not wrong, BUT, glamping is still a form of camping, therefore, it is not a hotel where you can expect things to be a certain way. Meaning, remember that you will be outdoors on an island next to a major city, you are sleeping on a comfy bed on wood planks over grass! You did not need to pitch your own tent, it was cleaned and set up for you - with AC, 2 fans, a normal flushing toilet, rain shower, spacious vanity, plenty of seating and room to move around comfortably. (full length mirror was an unexpected bonus!)  And as far as the staff, keep in mind that they do not stay there overnight, they commute there each day. The King Waterfront Voyager tent is the way to go. We were in tent #3 with a great view of the Statue of Liberty and far enough away from the main lawn/restaurants/construction which made us feel like we were in our own little world. You are paying for the view and proximity to NYC. It is experience that we will never forget. It helped that we had perfect weather too. Bring books, games, things to keep you busy as there are no TVs.

author: Liam V
title: Three Chances. Three Disappointments. Never Again.
text:
This starts with a year ago, I booked a stay at Collective Retreats on Governors Island as a graduation gift for my niece and her best friend, who were traveling down from upstate New York.

The day they arrived to check in, they were told there were no tents or cabins available because the entire property had been booked for a wedding. Collective seemed confused as to why we had never been notified. Eventually they blamed a “system glitch” that supposedly prevented us from receiving any cancellation notice or refund.

What made this even more frustrating was that they had sent both a welcome email and a reservation confirmation just days before check-in. Naturally, we assumed everything was on schedule.

As a result, my niece and her friend were stranded in New York City with nowhere to stay. They had traveled all the way from upstate expecting a confirmed reservation. I called Collective and insisted they find them a hotel for the night. I actually had to beg them to book any hotel room in NYC for the peace of mind knowing they’re safe. Evan from Collective agreed and arranged a room.

Unfortunately, the problems continued.

Evan assured me that my credit card would only be used for incidental charges. Instead, I was charged for both the hotel room and the incidentals. After I provided Collective with my credit card statement and the hotel invoice proving the charges, they agreed to reimburse me—but it took nearly three months to get my money back.

Despite that experience, I had always wanted to stay overnight on Governors Island. For my birthday, I decided to give Collective another chance.

They canceled that reservation too.

At least this time they notified me in advance.

Against my better judgment, I made a third reservation for a different week. This time I actually made it to check-in.

Unfortunately, the customer service left a lot to be desired.

I asked where the restrooms were and was simply told to walk down a rocky path. There were no signs—just rows of tents. I wasn’t comfortable opening random tent doors, unsure whether they were guest accommodations or restrooms. I walked back to the front desk for clarification.

The staff member responded, “Use your listening ears,” as though I simply hadn’t been paying attention.

I calmly explained that I am legally deaf in my left ear. That comment was both rude and unprofessional. Only then did she personally walk me to the restrooms—which honestly should have been the response from the beginning, especially considering there is no signage directing guests nor any signage at the restrooms.

Dinner wasn’t much better. We ordered pasta and grilled fish. About 30 minutes later, after we’d already been waiting, we were told the fish had sold out. That pretty much summed up the experience.

Throughout our stay, most of the staff appeared unhappy and disengaged. Even simple requests, like asking for a golf cart ride, were met with visible annoyance, making us feel like we were inconveniencing them.

The location itself is beautiful, and Governors Island is a wonderful place to visit. That’s what makes this experience so disappointing. After three separate bookings—two cancellations, one leaving my family stranded, reimbursement issues, and poor service during the stay—I can’t recommend Collective Retreats. There are simply too many operational problems and too little customer care to justify the premium price.

author: Luca S
title: Summer camp, not luxury
text:
I’ve had several “glamping” experiences that could be defined as luxurious, but this wasn’t one of them. It wasn’t a terrible stay, and even as a native New Yorker the city views at night from Governors Island still feel incredible. I spent one night here with a friend, and I’m glad we did it but I wont be back.

For starters, the staff were all friendly and accommodating and I don’t think any of the issues at the camp are their fault. It seems that this company uses the unique location as their main selling point but doesn’t bother to pay attention to the smaller details. 

Upon arriving to Governors Island, we did see a golf cart ready to transport people to the camp, as expected (we were in communication about arrival time). However, there were six people going to the camp from our ferry and only four seats. My friend and I had to wait (in the rain) for the golf cart to drop off the first guests, and then drive back to pick us up. 

Our tent was as expected, and comfortable. The beds felt clean and the AC kept things cool. The shower was, however, freezing as we didn’t have hot water. We were right next to the lobby tent, which made walking to dinner easy. The dinner itself was expensive and bland, although we ate during happy hour and were able to get two cocktails for $20 total (a good price for NYC). 

I’m familiar with Governors Island, so I expected the near constant noise of helicopters and ferries, but there was also a lot of noise from construction that is happening right next to the camp. The campsite doesn’t feel very private or secluded.

After dinner we asked to be driven to the nearby QCNY spa. We were dropped off, and later picked up, without any issues. It had been raining earlier, so unfortunately the campfires were not happening. In other glamping sites I have stayed at, when activities are canceled they do their best to reschedule or modify - for example, indoor s’mores - but no such thing happened here.
