author: Daisy G
title: Authentic Parisian Experience!
text: We overall enjoyed our stay at the Hotel Joyce.  We took a cab from Gare du Nord which took approximately 15 minutes and cost 11-12 euros.  Check-in was quick and we were issued our room keys.  The hotel is located in a rather quiet neighborhood that features a number of bars and restaurants.  The hotel itself is located in an older building and will definitely offer you a real Parisian experience (Including a small elevator and a winding staircase!).   The rooms are on the smaller side - But are of comparable size to other hotels located in the city center.  Metro stations are a 10-12 minute walk.   Our room offered a nice minibar with snacks and drinks.  Staff were courteous and the rooms themselves were clean.  My one complaint was that the shower leaked terribly all over the bathroom floor every time we used it.  Overall we would stay in this hotel again - we feel that it offers a good value and an authentic Parisian experience.

author: Julien S
title: The best hotel in Paris for price and quality
text: I've been to Paris many times, but this time was simply magnificent! The room was large compared to Paris, with a large balcony, a complimentary bar replenished daily, and a free buffet not only in the hotel but also at chains throughout Paris. The staff is truly a special treat.

author: Ella L
title: Dream stay!!
text:
The staff is particularly welcoming, warm, and helpful. They really did everything to make our lives easier, whether it was answering our requests or even booking an excursion for us.

The room was very spacious for Paris, impeccably clean, and well air-conditioned. The elevator and the breakfast service were also very appreciated.

The location is exceptional: in a magnificent, quiet, and safe neighborhood, while being close to delicious restaurants (like Duvin, La Petite Charlotte/Dame Charlotte), an excellent authentic bakery (Cyprien), a wine shop (PhiloVino), and also near public transportation and the main attractions. The Galeries Lafayette near the Opéra are about a 12-minute walk away.

In short, a very nice package: location, comfort, and above all, attentive service that makes all the difference. I recommend it without hesitation!

author: Carlos W
title: A Perfect First Stay in London—We'll Definitely Be Back!
text:
This hotel was the perfect choice for the first part of our London vacation before we sailed from Southampton on a cruise to Norway. Since this was our first trip to London, we spent countless hours watching YouTube videos trying to decide where to stay. Surprisingly, we couldn't find many videos that really explained this hotel's location, so we decided to take a chance—and we are so glad we did.

We couldn't have been more pleased with our stay. The hotel is absolutely lovely. We booked a Classic Superior Sky View room, and it exceeded our expectations. As Americans, we had heard that London hotel rooms can be quite small, so we were a little concerned about space. Fortunately, our room felt comfortable, well-designed, and had more than enough room for the two of us.

After our overnight flight, we arrived around 11:00 a.m. expecting to leave our luggage until check-in. To our surprise, the front desk had a room ready for us and checked us in early without us even having to ask. That thoughtful gesture made a wonderful first impression.

To help adjust to the time change, we took a walk along the South Bank of the River Thames. The walk to Big Ben and the Houses of Parliament was beautiful, and simply strolling along the river was one of our favorite experiences in London.

When we returned to the hotel, we discovered the rooftop bar and it quickly became one of the highlights of our stay. The views are absolutely stunning, with the London Eye visible in the distance along with an incredible view of the city skyline. The scenery alone would have been worth the visit, but the food, drinks, and service were outstanding as well. We enjoyed it so much that we returned every evening for dinner.

The service throughout our stay, from check-in to check-out, was exceptional. Every member of the staff was warm, welcoming, and genuinely helpful.

One small note for fellow American travelers: as I mentioned in another review from the second part of our London stay, we didn't realize that many hotels in London do not typically provide washcloths, as they are considered personal items. It certainly wasn't a problem, we had plenty of bath towels and hand towels but it's helpful to know before you pack.

I hope this hotel receives many more reviews because it truly deserves them. We had a wonderful experience and would not hesitate to stay here again. Thank you to everyone on the team for making our first visit to London so memorable. You made us want to come back!

author: Alice K
title: THIS is the place to stay
text: This is just the loveliest place, completely outside of the tourist area. That's important if you make the error of going to Rome during the tourist season. The room was very large and nice, old and clean, reeks of history in a good way. Bed comfy. Breakfast area, both indoor and outdoor, is just lovely. The rooftop pool and view are really nice. And oh, the flowers are everywhere. But the best, and I mean the best, is the wonderful owner. We arrived late in the evening, and our taxi driver tried to take advantage of us and charge an insane price. Well, the owner came and had it out with him, as he was trying to pull a fast one. author: Luca B
title: A Charming Stay at Palm Gallery Hotel
text:
I had a wonderful stay at the Palm Gallery Hotel. The property is a beautiful villa located in a quiet residential area of Rome, which makes it perfect for relaxing after a day of sightseeing.

I particularly enjoyed the tasteful decoration of the rooms and the overall cleanliness of the hotel. The staff were exceptionally friendly, welcoming, and always ready to help with any request.

Considering the quality of the services and the atmosphere of the place, the price/value ratio is excellent.

I highly recommend the Palm Gallery Hotel to anyone looking for a charming and peaceful stay in Rome

author: Brooke A
title: Family of 4 on Summer Vacation
text:
Family of 4 (2 adults, 2 kids) visiting Rome on vacation. 

Rome is so vast that it was hard to choose a "perfect" location where to stay. We ended up choosing the Palm Gallery since it seemed like a nice small hotel and still convenient enough to everything. 

Key thoughts:
1) Location -- In a very quiet residential neighborhood with some very nice restaurants within walking distance. This is not a tourist area, which is great to get a more authentic feel for the city, to enjoy "real" Italian restaurants, etc. For travelling during the day, we initially arrived using the metro and that was quite a bit of a walk. But using the buses was very convenient as there were main bus stops just a few minutes away and the buses were easy to take to get to main attractions like the Colosseum, the Vatican, etc. 
2) Food - Breakfast was served on the terrace. The hotel strongly appreciates knowing what time you will dine at. This caused us some issues when we forgot to tell them the day before when we would show up, so they seemed surprised when we should up early for breakfast. This is a small operation and not some corporate run kitchen. 
3) The room (large panoramic) served our needs well -- 3 beds + a desk. 
4) The kids loved having an outdoor pool. Such a rare treasure to get in the city. 

Would we stay again? Maybe. The neighborhood was great. The pool was unique to have. The location is a bit out of the way.

author: Hugo T
title: Wonderful Hospitality
text: We had a great two-night stay at the Palm Gallery Hotel. The atmosphere was homey, the room comfortable and well-equipped, the breakfast tasty. The pool and sun deck out back were a treat. But what we appreciated most was the hospitality. Daniel and Lorenzo were both very welcoming and concerned that all our needs were met. Daniel also arranged a shuttle for us to the airport at an ungodly hour that worked out beautifully with driver Davide, who showed up half an hour early, which we appreciated. Whenever we're back in Rome, we'll stay there again!

author: Adam F
title: Best Hotel staff out there
text: Had an amazing experience over there and the staff there are amazing. The hotel has the best service out there and amenities in Rome.

author: Rosie I
title: Palm Gallery of Regrets
text:
I regret booking this hotel. I had initially booked in May and thought I had cancelled, but I never received any reminder emails leading up to my stay—unlike every other hotel I stayed at in Italy and London on this trip, and unlike what I’ve experienced in decades of travel. The only communication I received was an email on the evening of check-in asking what time I would be arriving. That was the moment I discovered my cancellation hadn’t gone through. By then, it was too late, and I wasn’t allowed to cancel because of the 15-day policy.

Although my limited interactions with the staff were pleasant, the experience itself was frustrating and disappointing. My niece ended up staying there for two of the three nights we had booked, but she couldn’t sleep because the guest in the next room snored so loudly it kept her up at night. Had our whole family of four stayed there as originally planned, it would have made for a very unhappy trip.

The pool is the feature the hotel seems to advertise most, but it was not enjoyable. While the space was quiet and private, the water was very cold, and both hot tubs were out of order. The location is also inconvenient—there are some restaurants within walking distance, but it is quite far from the main tourist attractions.

We booked the Oasis Room, which I understand is one of the nicer rooms, but it would have been extremely uncomfortable for a family of four. For a property that advertises itself as family-friendly, this was disappointing.

Most people’s trip to Rome is a once-in-a-lifetime experience. I would not recommend spending it here unless having a weird tiny kitchenette is essential for you.

We absolutely loved our stay at the Palm Gallery Hotel. It was the first stop on our three-week family trip from Rome to Sicily, and it turned out to be one of the best places we stayed.

Temi made our visit unforgettable with his warm welcome, friendly smile, and genuine kindness. Daniel was equally fantastic, open, friendly, and attentive. In fact, every member of staff we met was wonderful.

We arrived early and were greeted with a refreshing drink and plenty of tips for exploring the area. Our son, Stan, enjoyed chatting with Temi so much that he’s still talking about him now!

The décor is stylish, and the pool area was a highlight, perfect for cooling off after exploring Rome’s hot streets. Even when the hotel was full, it never felt crowded.

We truly loved it here and will definitely be back. Thank you for giving us such a perfect start to our trip—you were our No. 1 stay in Italy!

author: William J

It is a couple of kilometres outside of the centre of Rome which has many pluses. The nearby restaurants and bars are not tourist traps but places where real Romans eat and drink, and as such we found them excellent and very well priced. There is a Metro station a 10 minute walk away which takes you to all of the main attractions in minutes.

author: Evan L
title: Not Hyatt Quality
text: This was not a quality Hyatt experience.    The hotel did not provide the upgraded room we booked even after considerable discussion.    The room we received was very small. The lobby was jammed with people because it was undersized for the number of people in the hotel.    Wished we had stayed in the Embassy Suites which was the same price, centrally located and generally more comfortable.   I would not recommend this hotel.

author: Ian P
title: Excellent location
text: Great hotel. Excellent location close to Times Square and the subway. Very clean. Friendly and professional staff. Would definitely stay here again.

author: Juan R
title: Very Friendly / Hot Room
text: The hotel is clean and modern and the staff are friendly.   be prepared that the breakfast is very very busy and closes ridiculously early - at 9:30 during the week. We ended up only going one day on our three day stay. The worst part of this stay was how hot our room was and it didn’t seem there was anything they could do about it. Thermostat doesn’t go lower than 68 but there’s no way it was below 70 in our room and it was very warm at night when we were trying to sleep.

author: Kyle Y
title: A stone's throw from Times Square
text: Hotel on a side street a stone's throw from Times Square and the subway. Clean but tiny room, microscopic bathroom with a shower without hot water... If you are lucky, maybe it gets lukewarm😩 Elevators almost always full and a long wait, but I think they are like that a bit everywhere in New York. Breakfast was neither good nor bad: scrambled eggs, bacon, fruit, bread, and bagels to toast with jams and butter, coffee, and juices. Go early or you won't get a seat.

author: Oliver H
title: Good but don't expect anything great!
text: I was a guest with a disability and specifically requested interconnecting rooms when booking so our family of five could stay together. Additionally, as this trip was a birthday celebration, my wife asked if the hotel could do anything to make the occasion special. Unfortunately, the hotel failed to acknowledge either request. As a loyal Hyatt guest who has stayed at properties worldwide, this first experience in NYC was deeply disappointing, making me hesitant to book with Hyatt again. During our trip, we visited the Ritz-Carlton Central Park for light birthday refreshments and were blown away by their service. While I realize the Hyatt is a 4-star property compared to the Ritz’s 5-star standard, basic acknowledgement of our requests would have made a world of difference.

author: Hannah R
title: Family Birthday Trip
text: Helpful and friendly and welcoming staff; breakfast was great selection; room cleanliness and housekeeping were great.  Crowd control was smooth and flowed nicely.  Would stay again.

author: Maria U
title: Great Experience
text: It was a pleasant experience.I would visit again.The rooms were spacious and clean.The staffs were friendly n pleasant

author: George J
title: Great Family Hotel
text: Excellent location, Breakfast was very good with plenty of seating too. Restaurants and Theater in a short walk. Best time in visiting NYC

author: Lucy Z
title: Good Location, Decent Hotel Option.
text: Hotel was in a good location (garment district) just off the busiest avenues (7th & 8th) bit close enough to the heart of Times Square. While hotel was clean, there were just too many people both inside and out the hotel at times. The lobby literally became a traffic jam of sorts at certain times of the day, particularly morning.

author: Caleb F
title: One of a few hotels, Without resort fees
text:
When I discovered this Hotel three years ago, it is the only place I stay in New York City when I visit friends. Beware in many large cities that the hotels advertise reasonable rates online but then when you book and arrive you find out, they have a resort fee for each  day up to $100 a day for Ameneties you don’t even use. 
THIS hotel does not do that and it’s one reason why they are always very full so book way ahead.  
the breakfast is great. I would recommend staying on lower floors when the elevators are  difficult to get up or down.

author: Ruby R
title: Crowded and Worn out
text: The hotel has way too many rooms relative to its common areas.   Breakfast lines are long, and food items continually run out, so you have to go back several times.  Too many people means elbowing and shoving and cutting, and it's just a miserable experience.  The hotel laundry is not on-site, so when the delivery was late, we ended up with no towels.  When towels arrived, they were delivered to the room around 8 pm.  Then we had them delivered again around midnight, waking us up.  We ended up with one room with no hot water and another that was scalding.  The overall condition of the rooms was run-down.  Plugs are worn out and loose, fixtures marred, baseboards and carpet near the end of their life.

author: Isabella X
title: False advertisement
text: I paid for a high floor and a city view. Which I should have gotten. Need to take the city view photos out of the website. It is false advertisement to have city views which I paid for and didn't get it. This is the 2nd time this has happened to my family with Hyatt hotels. Maybe is just me being Latino and having my last name Garcia. It seems like I'm always having this problem at Hyatt hotels.

author: Chloe S
title: Well Located, but Serious Disability-Access and Operational Failures
text:
One star.

I stayed at Hyatt Place New York City/Times Square with my disabled minor son while my family was relocating to Hell’s Kitchen. The location is excellent, and several individual employees were genuinely helpful. Unfortunately, our stay also involved repeated disability-access, safety, maintenance, and internal-communication problems serious enough that I ultimately escalated my concerns in writing to the General Manager, Hyatt Consumer Affairs, Hyatt’s ADA channel, and Hyatt’s Office of the General Counsel.

I am a non-ambulatory, full-time Permobil power-wheelchair user. During our stay, large laundry bags, vacuum cleaners, and other housekeeping equipment were repeatedly left in the corridor outside our room in locations that prevented me from passing in my wheelchair. On several occasions, my disabled minor son physically moved hotel equipment so that I could get through. Had I been traveling alone, I would not have been able to do that. After I raised the issue, the General Manager confirmed in writing that the hotel’s existing procedures require hallways to remain clear of obstructions affecting ingress and egress and that those procedures had been reinforced with housekeeping.

Elevator access became another serious problem. On one occasion, I waited approximately 28 minutes before finally boarding an elevator traveling upward so that I could remain aboard and eventually travel downstairs. On another occasion, I waited approximately 13 minutes without being able to board at all and returned to my room. Management subsequently informed me in writing that certain elevators were temporarily out of service for maintenance and acknowledged that this was contributing to congestion.

That distinction is particularly consequential for a wheelchair user. I cannot substitute the stairs when elevator service becomes effectively unusable. During the second incident, I had been trying to reach the lobby to retrieve a food delivery while my autistic minor son remained safely in our locked room because he did not want to accompany me downstairs. After I could not board an elevator, I returned to the room and asked hotel staff to bring the order upstairs.

I subsequently requested a standing arrangement for food deliveries for the remainder of our stay so that I would not have to attempt the elevators, discover that I could not board, return to the room, contact staff, and explain the situation again each time. After substantial written correspondence, the General Manager confirmed that food deliveries arriving for our room would be brought directly upstairs and that the front desk had been informed to deliver them upon arrival.

There were significant internal-communication problems as well. I provided disability-related housekeeping instructions to the front desk, including information concerning entry to the room because I cannot readily reach the door in my wheelchair. Those instructions did not reach the individual housekeeper who subsequently came to the room. I ended up explaining the situation directly to her in Spanish. Once she understood what was required, she was helpful and professional. My concern was with the failure of the hotel’s internal communication system, not with her conduct.

Our accessible-room shower also had extremely low water pressure and completely cold water on two consecutive evenings. On the second evening, my disabled son discovered the problem after he was already in the shower and was unable to complete his shower with the water in that condition. When I reported it, a front-desk employee began explaining that water pressure in accessible rooms was lower “because of the need.” I asked that the problem simply be repaired rather than explained as a feature of accessibility.

Maintenance employee Clay arrived shortly afterward and deserves specific praise. I explained the accessibility considerations concerning the water temperature. He restored the hot water and pressure, measured the temperature at approximately 102°F, allowed my son to verify that the water was comfortable, and handled the entire interaction professionally and respectfully. I thanked him directly for his help. The General Manager subsequently confirmed to me in writing that all guestrooms are supplied by the same plumbing system and that water pressure is intended to be consistent throughout the hotel.

Several individual employees were helpful once they had the information necessary to act, especially Clay. I want that reflected accurately in this review. My one-star rating concerns the cumulative experience and the hotel’s operational systems: corridor management, elevator access during reduced elevator capacity, transmission of disability-related instructions between departments, maintenance problems, and the amount of escalation required to obtain prospective accommodations rather than repeatedly seeking assistance after a barrier had already occurred.

I raised these concerns contemporaneously and in writing, identified specific incidents and times, and preserved the hotel’s written responses. Hyatt ultimately corrected or addressed several immediate issues, and I acknowledged those corrections when they occurred.

Nevertheless, I should not have had to spend this much of an active hotel stay documenting recurring disability-access problems and escalating them through property management and Hyatt corporate channels in order to obtain workable procedures.

The location is very convenient. Some employees were excellent. My documented experience of the hotel’s disability-access operations during this stay was not, and I cannot recommend the property on that basis.

author: Juan N
title: If you are not thin and an early riser, forget it...
text: We stayed at this hotel for 7 days, booked months in advance, attracted by the good reviews on the booking platform. Nothing could be further from the truth. The hotel is central, behind Times Square, near the subway and the main attractions of New York. That is where the positive aspects end. As soon as we arrived, we immediately realized the mistake we had made: we found ourselves in a lobby crowded with people, with suitcases, without suitcases, thrown everywhere. Confident and devastated by the trip, we approach the desk where a hurried and rude clerk immediately asks us for the card to pay.  They assign us a room on the 20th floor since we had requested a high floor, and so far so good, if it weren't for the fact that to take one of the 4 elevators present you have to be particularly lucky...finding one there and free is like winning the lottery🤑! We go up. I should premise that there were 3 of us, two average-sized adults and an 11-year-old boy. We arrive in the room and find a cubbyhole where either the suitcases fit or we did! My son's sofa bed was closed with the sheets inside, which I had to fix myself. A tiny closet where two things fit😭. We had to put our suitcases on the desk and on a makeshift cabinet. Once the sofa bed was opened, the path to the bathroom was practically nonexistent, like the bathroom itself: a cemetery plot with the toilet separated from the bed only by a sliding door. Practically from the bed you could reach the toilet without even touching the floor🙈. If we had been wider than we were long, the bathroom and the room would probably have been unusable. The shower was hallucinating: no extension (also considering the absence of a bidet, a great classic) and if you wanted hot water you had to turn it on all the way, so goodbye hair...and not even a shower cap🥺! After shelling out the substantial sum, we resigned ourselves to living for 7 days in the cubbyhole🤨. On the other hand, the bed was very comfortable. The air conditioning was a tractor that brightened our sleep with the noise of a starter motor in the middle of the night, along with other sinister, unidentified sounds 🚜🛵. In the morning, thanks to jet lag, we woke up at 6...and thank goodness! We immediately realized that going down for breakfast after 7 was equivalent to not having it: a lack of seats, so much so that you could see lines of people at the elevator 🫩 with their breakfast plates to take to their rooms because there was physically no room, not even standing room. So if you intend to take it easy, don't pay for it at all, as you wouldn't be able to use it anyway. Even if you don't like American breakfast, forget it: only eggs and bacon, sausages, pancakes, and lots of bread...no sweets, no cookies, the coffee...well, let's not even go there, but that's common knowledge☕️! Even if you are the type of people who want to go back for a moment to rest after a morning of walking, forget it! Before 5 PM, your room will never be done: prepare to be out from 8:30 AM until evening because no one will clean the room and remake the bed before late afternoon, even if you beg them on your knees. The elevator was a real ordeal: going up and down from the 20th floor was like going through all the stations of our Lord's torment multiple times a day. And if by chance you need to use the restroom, avoid the lobby bathroom: they probably haven't cleaned it in years 🤢; on the other hand, the rooms appear clean. In short, if you can, go elsewhere...I warned you 😜

author: Miguel N
title: Great Location and Friendly Service
text: I had a great stay at Hyatt Place New York City / Times Square. The location is excellent—just a short walk to Times Square and many major attractions. The room was clean and comfortable, and the staff was friendly and welcoming throughout my stay. I would definitely stay here again and recommend it to anyone visiting New York City.

author: Hugo T
title: Don't choose this hotel for breakfast.
text:
The location is excellent. The hotel room was spacious and quite comfortable, compared to many similar hotels. The bed and towels were very good. 
However, the breakfast menu was very poor and inadequate. However, the hotel is very crowded and you always have to queue at breakfast. Get ready for paper plates and plastic forks.

author: Ryan B
title: A nice hotel in the centre of New York.
text: A decent accommodation at the the heart of NYC; few blocks away from PABT station and Times Square. Penn station is within walking distance. The room and bathroom were clean with all basic amenities. But both were very small by any standards. The breakfast was fine with enough choices. The staffs were courteous and helpful. Overall, a good experience considering the price.

author: Antoine V
title: Great location
text:
Location, location, location! Very well situated to discover Midtown and Manhattan.
Breakfast is poor and all served on disposables.

author: Molly C
title: Exceeded expectations
text: The service was incredible from check-in to restaurants to departure. Breakfast was amazing with so many choices. Bell staff incredible. Great location. Would definitely stay again! Thank you Hyatt for taking customer service so seriously

author: Ella E
title: Service before arriving could be better!
text: My experience with Hyatt started negative with not being able to pay in full through their website. Once expressing this displeasure with Janahia at the front desk at this Hyatt Place she took my displeasure personal and started to get irate. Seeing you lacked customer services skills I immediately asked for a manager. I was transferred to Michelle and she was very professional and understanding.

author: Zoe G
title: Elevator
text: The hotel itself has a good location, but the breakfadt is horrible( not a vegitable or a ham or sousage, only egg and sweet items) the elevators are out of order almost every day, our room was on 9th floor.The city view is a lie , we were seeing a nother building 🥲The staff is ok!Compare to the price we paid i think the hotel should provide better service thinking more about the European guests!

author: Freya O
title: Excellent stay!
text:
We nearly didn't book this hotel because the reviews seemed a bit hit-and-miss, but we're very glad we did. We’ve previously stayed in a bunch of different places around town.
Pros:
No “destination/resort” fee!
The location felt really safe throughout our stay, and there is visible security around reception during the overnight hours. The hotel is in a nice neighbourhood, just a few minutes' walk from the subway, making it easy to get around the city and away from the crazy of Times Square.
Breakfast was genuinely excellent and far exceeded our expectations. The hotel arranged gluten-free bagels for us on request at check-in, which was greatly appreciated after our emails prior to the stay went unanswered. There was a wide variety of rotating hot and cold options each morning, and honestly, the breakfast was better than what I've experienced in many executive lounges at full-service US hotel brands. The breakfast team worked incredibly hard keeping everything stocked and refreshed, even during the busiest periods.
Housekeeping was fantastic. They always respected the Do Not Disturb sign and never interrupted us unnecessarily. Gloria deserves special recognition for doing an amazing job freshening up our room when we needed service.
Bryant on the afternoon/evening reception shift was also lovely, and incredibly helpful throughout our stay. A special thank you as well to the manager, Dawn, who was outstanding from start to finish and made a real difference to our experience.
One concern we had before arriving was reports of construction noise, but we didn't see or hear any construction during our stay. We actually stayed in two different rooms and both were exceptionally quiet, with no outside noise at all. Some rooms also feature a double-door arrangement that helps reduce noise from the hallway and other guests. With only around 10 rooms per floor, the hotel felt quiet.
Air conditioning was excellent, we had a heat wave whilst there and the rooms were lovely and cool.
And for anyone wondering from a previous review —we checked carefully and found absolutely no signs of bed bugs.
The guest laundry facilities were also very useful, with a single washing machine and dryer available for guests.
As for the negatives, room sizes do vary slightly by shape but are compact as advertised and reported.
Some reception staff were grumpy and unhelpful, which was inconsistent compared to the excellent service we received from others.
Also, one elevator appears to be permanently out of service, leaving only a single lift operating. If you're staying on a higher floor, it's worth allowing extra time, especially during busy periods.
Breakfast can also get quite busy, and you may occasionally need to wait a minute for a table, although the breakfast staff do an outstanding job keeping everything refreshed and flowing smoothly.
Overall this was a great stay for us. The excellent breakfast, quiet rooms, convenient location, strong housekeeping team, and standout staff members made this a very enjoyable stay, and we would happily stay here again. Many thanks to Dawn and the team!

author: Sofia Y
title: Do not recommend
text:
As a Marriott Lifetime member, this is probably one of the worst hotels, not just within the Marriott brand but among all the hotels I’ve stayed at.

I booked a high-floor room, but at check-in I was told none were available. The room had no complimentary water, and when I asked about it, I was told that water is provided “at the hotel’s discretion.” I was eventually given two tiny bottles.

To make matters worse, the room didn’t have air conditioning. Charging nearly $400 per night for a room without AC is simply unacceptable. The lack of basic amenities, combined with poor service and untrained staff, made this an extremely disappointing stay.

author: Olivia C
title: The elevator is a major issue
text: I am currently staying here. The elevator issue is a major problem. I wasn't notified upon check in that my room would be directly  across from the elevator and that I would hear a  clicking noise all night long. I tried to switch rooms the next day but I had online meetings and didnt have a minute to switch at that time. I tried to switch in the evening but all rooms were sold out. I had conversations with the guy who had to sit in the elevator pushing buttons all day and night and he mentioned they were servicing the elevator we were using next week. This is a major issue:(

author: Daniel N
title: Worst Marriott experience I've ever had in my life - after being Titanium Elite for 10 years
text:
One of the worst hotels I have ever stayed at in my life. I am Marriott Titanium Elite. They were extremely difficult about providing an early check in - even at 1:30PM. The lady who checked me in even lied and said they were sold out so couldnt switch me to a king bed room, despite there being plenty of rooms on sale online. How can they not clean even 1 room between the check out time of 11AM and 1:30PM? I don't expect this inability to provide a room given my loyalty status. 

Only 1 elevator works and takes forever!! The working elevator causes so much noise I can hear it go up and down loudly from inside of my room - its woken me up so many times that my whoop sleep score is the lowest I've ever seen it. 

There is EXTREMELY LOUD DRILLING construction on the road in front of the hotel - i guess this is not their fault, but they should warn guests. The walls are thin and you can hear every single thing outside the room - even if people are chatting you can hear ever word. 

Room is tiny and generally quite awful, even for NYC standards. I presumed it would be bigger given this is a suite hotel, but I didnt check the measurements beforehand. Its basically the same as a Moxy. If you are overweight, you definitely will not fit in the bathroom.

author: Charlie W
title: Good Service, great location, but rooms are very small.
text:
Pro:
-Service was quite good. The staff from check in and check out  were very helpful.
-The room itself and breakfast area was clean.
-Location is great, very close to 6 line and Q line.
Con:
-We were surprised by how small the room was. The room has space for the beds, but no room for a table and chair, so there was no space to do anywork on your laptop.
-The lifts were slow and during half of the time of our stay, only one of the two elevators was working. It took a long time to get back to our floor during checkout time.

author: Freya M
title: Nope
text:
Pretty dismal. Sparse staff; small, cramped, uncomfortable lobby. Impossible to reach staff from room
(No TV remote).

author: Louis L
title: Megha was MEGA!
text: I just reserved a room for a quick nap during a break in the work day. I had trouble booking at first through the app and called the hotel directly. Megha who was at the desk proceeded to be a great help in adjusting my time to accommodate me! I’ve travelled many places and have asked for similar accommodations only to either be told it can’t be done or having to explain it numerous times with numerous reps to get it done and Megha simply said “it’s done! Enjoy your stay!” Oh man what a relief! I wish ALL reps at all places were like this! Thanks again and again Megha!

author: Nathan F
title: Never staying here again
text:
Horrible place.  The rooms were so tiny, there is no room to walk around the bed.
My room rate included breakfast... they had pre-made omelettes - they were disgusting.  they had tea/coffe, juice, yogurt, boiled eggs, toast.  Bur for the price they are charging I would expect better breakfast.  The gym so small... 2 treadmills, 2 elliptical, some weights and 2 mats.  That's it... sufficient if you want to have a quick workout.

author: Giulia Q
title: credit card along with mileage account was compromised
text:
It's a shame because I did like my stay...
but when I returned home, I found that my credit card was used (day of check out and after) to purchase gift cards at Nordstroms. Then I looked into my mileage account and 14000 miles was used for GC's at Walmart. The thieves had to have access to my home zip code and email to achieve this. The only place it could have happened was at this hotel :(

author: Brooke K
title: An abysmal Marriott
text:
After experiencing nice rooms & service at two Marriott Hotels in the US, it is ironic that our worst experience was at another Marriott, the Springhill Suites on East 24th Street, Manhattan. Let me address all the issues:
Arrival: Bell desk is absent, so I had to move four heavy bags on a decrepit luggage cart which stubbornly resisted movement. Moving it through the cramped hallways was a challenge, and the hotel staff were bemused onlookers.
Check-in: Staff was curt and refused to entertain any requests for upgrades/ higher floors. We were generously given 500 ml of drinking water to last our 4 nights here. I requested for a wine bottle opener, and they declared that they didn’t have even one available. Strange.
Room: Reached through poorly-designed narrow hallways with sharp turns, reminiscent of Egyptian catacombs. We had booked a Studio with King Bed, which was super-expensive but microscopic in size, with the bed occupying 80% of the room. A large TV was mounted on a side wall, and would have resulted in a twisted neck if we had chosen to view anything.
Amenities: The coffee maker had some operational issues, which got fixed after three days of complaining.
Bathroom: Poorly designed, with the shower cubicle leaking water into the dry area.
Complimentary breakfast: This was marked by staff behaving as if they were running a soup kitchen doling out freebies. Rude, arrogant, and stubbornly refusing to refill spent items. They had a distinct air of being prison wardens with an attitude to match. 
Other issues: Our friends had another room, and they couldn’t sleep well due to mosquitos. They complained, but the issue never got fixed.
Conclusion: Will never stay here again, will never recommend. It is a blot on the hospitality industry.

author: Ethan H
title: Great Stay!
text: The rooms are clean and new and the staff is friendly. Megan and Bryant are very accommodating and kind! Was perfect for my solo stay, I’ve stayed here many many times and have always really enjoyed it. Safe, laundry machine, cute breakfast setup. Lots of good here!

author: Sean K
title: Disappointing experience
text:
The rooms themselves are not bad. The complaint we have already conveyed at the reception.......in general is the complaint about breakfast and the treatment of workers who do not know or want to say “Good morning”.We do not expect a breakfast from a 4 or 5 star hotel.......always missing! To replenish little desire or a NO MORE! We must come first! If I go at 8:30 we're still supposed to have...
Do I understand that workers do not work at ease, earn little? or do you have tourists left over? It may be, of course they're interns won't come a second time. We have come a second time but not to this hotel! 
The only one who later reacted positively was Nivea a dining room girl at least a smile and a good morning!

author: Anna O
title: Hotel in New York City, NY
text:
Stayed here two nights recently—got a Studio King Room.  The room was fairly small but not terrible for two people.  Decor itself seems modern, room was clean and bed was comfy.  They have amenities like fridge, microwave, coffee maker and a safe!  Bathroom is small—the shower leaks water out so the floor can get super wet and the sink drain was extremely slow.

The walls in the rooms are very thin, we can hear everything outside in the hallways which was disruptive to our sleep—there’s also a gap between our door and the floor so that probably made it worse.  Service here was okay, some staff were friendly, some not so much.  They do offer complimentary breakfast, and coffee/water in the lobby as well as popcorn!  And there’s a small shop to buy snacks/drinks by the front desk.  

Overall, location is great and room was okay.

author: Lucy H
title: You won’t sleep well: Elevator
text: Do yourself a favor and search for “elevator” on reviews.  For several years people have been providing feedback on the constant loud noise from the elevator that won’t let you sleep.  Their response is “noted” but don’t do anything about it.  Don’t stay here if you value your sleep.

author: Gavin R
title: I liked it!
text:
The hotel is in a much quieter area of the city but still quite convenient and central and that I enjoy quite.
Upon arrival, we received bottles of water and found it very friendly. 
Breakfast is appropriate. Nothing special but it is enough and is included then another point p hotel.
Spacious room and bathroom. And quiet!
The only negative point was that I tried to get in touch via email (before arriving) and no one answered me, and I sent about 4 or 5 messages. I was ignored and found unprofessional. Fortunately it was nothing super important and I was able to solve it in another way. Anyway, I still think they should have answered me.

author: Paolo L
title: Great stay here
text:
This hotel is very good.  Friendly staff, spotlessly clean and modern.  Big(ish) rooms for New York and in a good location well away from the buzz of Times Square area but close to broadway for cafes, shops and restaurants.  Shower room was clean and the shower itself, powerful.  Good facilities including microwave and fridge and USB ports.

The only negative I have really is that the breakfast was served using single-use plastics and throwaway plates.   Not a great statement of sustainability.

author: Rosie Q
title: Nice for one or two nights
text:
Rooms were nice and clean but very tiny. Staff was very friendly. Fresh ice cold lemon water available downstairs which was nice after a day of lots of walking. 
My finger got jammed from the bathroom
 barn doors. I asked them for a bandaid and the first aid kit at the front desk had one single bandaid which is really odd imo. 
Location isn’t too bad. Walking distance from quite a few different places.

author: Ella W
title: Awful from the start!
text: Awful from the start. Bathroom sink clogged, would not drain. Only one elevator working. Walked down 10 stories because it was faster. Breakfast is adequate, but room far too small. Guests crammed in the breakfast room. This is the worst Marriott I have experienced. Cannot recommend. Will not stay again.

author: Freya S
title: Very good staff, but room disastrous in major ways
text:
I’ll make it quick. Room way too small. Space around bed by wall when you get out of bed inadequate. Even worse is the miniscule space at foot of bed, where I banged every part of my upper body and head trying to squeeze through, particularly at night. Sound insulation from outside noises almost non-existent. Loud to extremely loud all day and most of night. Starting at maybe 11Pm through maybe 2AM, incredibly loud banging noises like pile drivers running, made sleep very difficult. Starngely, no noise from other rooms or outside of room.Bed ok, not great. Ditto for pillows. Comforter really not very good, at all. Had small couch which was good, but room so small all it could be used for was to dump luggage on and we only had one carry-on and one 24” piece of luggage.Had a small table that proved useful. Night tables on side of bed pretty large and good for as we have great need for space. Sharp marble corners a bit dangerous. Sufficient outlets and USB ports over night tables on both sides of bed.Phone stopped working last day we were there. Had reasonably sized refrigerator which was very welcome and useful. Ditto for microwave, in cabinet above fridge. Keurig machine has good quality coffee and hot chocolate. Big TV with good choice of channels.  Bathroom was also claustrophobic. Have to sit on toilet at angle as toilet paper holder will obstruct and jab your right leg and metal supprots for sink are so close your left leg will hit bang into them, as well. Shower so narrow I could barely fit in and I am a small guy. Otherwise, shower head good, flow of water and temperature control good and floor of shower nice and rough so not slippery, at all. Water seeps out of shower. Will need to sop up with towels. Light blocked out at night effectively by secondary shades.

Breakfast adequate, not great, except little egg quiche thing which was superlative, better than in most restaurants. Packaged muffin not bad and muffins when they don’t run out are ok. Typical eh machine OJ. Cereal with berries, actually pretty good, as was athe tosted bagel with cream cheese. Toaster set at perfect setting. Kudos for that. They had some yogurt and apples. And some other stuff.

Staff, as I said were very friendly and glad to help out. Outside of a couple of times requiring an extra phone call to get ice and towels and things, which happens in most hotels, service was very, very good, best part of stay, really. We’re grateful for that. When my wife had to take a taxi and was not feeling well, the woman from the breakfast room was at the front desk and she offered to help. There was a machine for ordering the taxi and she input all the information in asking my wife questions at each step. Then while my wife sat and waited, the woman went outside and waited for the taxi, then came in and ot my wife when it arrived. My wife is sorry she didn’t get her name so she could mention her name here.

Location very good. Restaurants and supermarkets close by.

If deficiencies could be fixed, it might be a very good mid-range hotel, but as currently configured, for price of room, I would imagine there might be better places to stay. Regardless, For us, it’s a no-brainer. We won’t be coming back.

Well, maybe it wasn't that quick.

author: Lucy E
title: Still the best!
text:
Having visited this accommodation many years ago. I knew what to expect and as always it hit the mark.
The room was  big  and comfy, air con , great wardrobe and storage , fab shower and a wee fridge too it was ideal.
Wi-Fi connectivity was brilliant too.
The location is in a great district. Lots of facilities around the corner. 
And a stroll to the Vatican and Castel Angelo.

Luca and his son are charming and helpful hosts. 
Our taxi he arranged to the airport was superb, prompt service lovely car. Driven by Roberta.

We will be back. Ciao !

author: Louis X
title: 10 out of 5 stars
text: We had an absolutely wonderful stay at Rome Armony Suites. The room we stayed in was a large family room which was cleaned daily and had bottled water left each day which was very kind. We travelled as a family and found it a safe, lovely area to stay in, so close to all the major tourist sites that we walked to the Vatican and used the subway for further travels with no issues. Luca was an exceptional host who helped us with everything. He gave us assistance in finding allergy friendly and gluten free places to eat. He booked transfers for us to and from the airport and the drivers did a fantastic job. There was a massive traffic jam on the way to the airport and our driver went miles out of his way through countryside so we made our flight. Likewise, the breakfast place he booked for us each day was very convenient and we really liked it. We really loved our stay and cannot recommend it enough as a place to stay. Many many thanks !!

author: Olivia V
title: Luca is the Best!
text:
Luca is one of the nicest people I’ve ever met
Very detailed and cares deeply about your stay
Location is perfect. Very safe and quiet neighborhood 
About 15 min walk to Vatican, 50 min walk to coliseum, 30 min walk to piazza navona 
Room is clean and easy to rest in
If he offers the airport pickup, take it!  Mercedes Benz for reasonable rate 
Definitely will stay here again when I return to Rome

author: Sara T
title: Our new favorite hotel in Rome
text:
First let me say that I traveled internationally for most of my career and I have stayed in hundreds of 5 star hotels with tons of amenities. While this is not a 5 star hotel, Luca and his family provided the best customer service of any hotel I have ever experienced. His dedication to his clients is the best ever, bar none. The room was immaculately clean, well-appointed, with the biggest bed I have ever seen. The location is perfect; close enough to walk to the Vatican, the Spanish steps, and other famous attractions, but in a real neighborhood. It is the perfect balance for those who love to experience cities the way a local experiences them. 
Luca gave us suggestions for tours and attractions that we never would have considered but are delighted that he told us about. His restaurant recommendations were perfect. We had delicious food at great prices. We were there for a week and we will be coming back before we fly home. 
When I couldn’t figure out how to book a train ticket online (Italian train tickets  are clunky using  their website and hard to understand) Luca handled it all for me before I even arrived. His knowledge of the city and its attractions is invaluable and his patience and kindness are unparalleled. I told him that I had read a negative review and fell in love with him based upon his intelligent and hilarious response. Clearly the person writing that review was a jealous competitor. 
If the rating scale goes to 5 stars, this place is a solid 10. We feel like we have made a friend for life. If you are considering this hotel for your trip to Rome, book now. You will be elated that you made the right choice!

author: Noah V
title: Stay by Luca!
text:
Staying with Luca was a pleasant surprise in the capital!
Highly recommended for services, room, location and especially for advice on what to see and where to eat!
The location is quiet convenient to the Vatican and Lepanto metro, the clean room with XXXL bed😄, spacious shower, bedroom slippers and bottle of water on the bedside table every day (much appreciated)
Thanks Luca!

author: Ana O
title: Third time staying. Like going back home!
text: The hotelier Luca is the best. Prati section is the best IMHO. A safe neighborhood with shops and restaurants and 10 min walk to the Vatican. My family stayed over by Train Terminal  where it’s very busy. No thank you. Believe all the positive reviews. Ciao

author: Lily U
title: Exceptional
text: The location is perfect. Close to metro. The shuttle bus to Fumicino airport is just a few meters away, which is very convenient. Vatican is only a 10 min walk away and so is Piazza del Populo.  The area is very nice, safe and quiet. A supermarket is also a corner away from the guest house. The room was very clean and the bed was comfortable. Bed slippers are provided. Coffee and tea facilities and water are replenished every morning at no extra charge.  Luca made us feel welcomed in his guest house even before arriving in Rome, as he promptly answered any questions we had and was always available through what's app or a phone call. Luca was a great host and made our stay very pleasant. He provided us with great tips of places to visit and nice restaurants.  Thank you Luca and we look forward to coming again and recommending your guest house.

author: Molly D
title: Extra large bed😃
text:
Large room with comfortable extra large bed (you don’t even meet by accident).😁
Bathroom with large shower.
Wonderful surprises: in the room there are disposable slippers and every day on each bedside table a bottle of water 🔝
Excellent cleaning
Luca, the owner is very kind and excellent dispenser of advice on what to see in Rome off the usual tourist routes and places to eat. You can ask him.
The location is good and convenient if you are interested in the Vatican, Castel SantAngelo and Piazza del Popolo.
The guest house is 500 meters from the Lepanto metro station (very convenient to go to Roma Termini)

author: Nora P
title: A guarantee
text:
Returning here to Luca is Andrea is synonymous with guarantee.
Nice and clean environment, rooms furnished with everything you need, availability in 'welcome and find solutions to any type of problem. All this in a location a stone's throw from the Vatican.
We will definitely return in our next chapter stages.

author: Aaron A
title: Great structure
text: I want to thank the owner Luca who has always been close with kindness and competence. We were always well advised. The location of the property is strategic in a great neighborhood, not far from the most picturesque places in Rome.

author: Diego R
title: Excellent address in the heart of Rome!
text: Wonderful stay in the eternal city. Luca is an incredibly available host who takes pleasure in sharing his Roman experience for both sightseeing and gastronomy. The accommodation is very comfortable and very clean. Perfect location to visit all the monuments on foot. Lots of shops and restaurants within minutes. As for the restaurant, I recommend the “3 Quarti” and the “Tacito”. In short, a superb address that I will hasten to share with all my friends! Thank you again Luca, we will definitely come back 🙏😊

author: Oscar O
title: Memorable Rome Visit!  Excellent Stay and Hospitality!
text: This was an excellent stay for our 25th anniversary!  Nice location in calmer neighborhood within walking distance to Castel Sant' Angelo, Vatican Musuem, and great restaurants.  The room and amenities were very comfortable, clean, quiet, and well-maintained.  The welcoming hospitality exceeded expectations!  Good communication by Luca and Andrea even before our arrival to make sure things were ready.  Upon arrival, Luca was so helpful and caring to ensure our stay was the best!  Thank you for helping to make our visit memorable!  From dining/attraction recommendations to setting-up direct transportation to the airport - we appreciate your kindness and attention to detail, Luca.  Everything was perfect!

author: Tyler M
title: Wonderful location and hospitality!
text:
From the moment we arrived in Rome we knew we were in the hub of everything at this amazing hotel! We walked everywhere and were able to get to all of our destinations easily and at the end of the day were greeted with clean quiet rooms and comfortable beds!

Day one Andrea was in touch, making sure he was there to welcome us. He and his father Lucca continued that hospitality all throughout our stay. Great recommendations for dinner, things to do or not do and tips on navigating the city!

Lucca and Andrea, if we are back in Rome, we will see you both!!!

author: Louis M
title: Gem in Prati—Great Stay, Great Vibe, Reasonably Priced!
text:
My husband and I had a great stay here. Let me enumerate the reasons why:

1. We had a sweet ride for our airport pick up. It was a Benz. It wasn't some shoddy looking, smelly car. The driver was polite and helpful. The rate was reasonable, not highway robbery. 

2. The owner, Luca, was warm and very hands-on. He gave us tips on how to go about Rome, good restaurants and bars, etc. He would ask how our day was. You can tell the guy genuinely cares about his customers. We also met his son, who seems to take after his Dad. Top notch customer service!

3. The room was large, had a good view, and was generally clean. Water bottles were replenished everyday. I saw little mold spots under the shower door which were not noticeable unless u looked closely. I noticed them coz I'm OC about cleanliness but it was nothing to lose sleep about.

4. For our last day, we had an evening flight but Luca was kind enough to let us stay in our room even way beyond the check out time (no one was checking in after us). We appreciated this kind gesture. Other hotels would have charged extra. 

5. Loved the vibe of this area! The location of this accomodation was close to Vatican, good restaurants, pharmacies, supermarket, and shopping area. We felt safe walking around here. 

Thank you Luca for your hospitality! If we get a chance to visit Rome again, we know where to go. We're telling our friends too! 

Ciao, Jen & Marko

Tip:
-Book the Deluxe King Room.
-Book airport transfers thru Luca. Worth it, less hassles, comfortable ride.

author: Louis Q
title: Fabulous stay with incredible hospitality!
text:
My wife and I had the great pleasure of staying at the Rome Armony Suites for nine nights in April 2024. As already indicated in the tremendous number of excellent TripAdvisor reviews, this guest house is extremely well located and provided us a restful oasis during our Roman holiday. Our large and quiet room was perfectly comfortable, with its high-quality mattress ensuring  a great night’s sleep after long days exploring Rome or our day trip destinations and a well-appointed bathroom with reliable hot water and great water pressure. We appreciated that our room was cleaned and bottled water replenished daily. In short, the room was exactly as pictured on the website and provided us with everything we needed. 

We highly recommend Rome Armony Suites. We couldn’t have been happier with its proximity to fantastic coffee bars, restaurants, gelaterias, pizzerias as well as a wonderful array of shops.  The rest of Rome is easily accessible either on foot or public transit. 

Even more important than any of these features of Rome Armony Suites, what made this one of our best vacations ever was the incredible hospitality of Luca and his son, Andrea. We have never received such tremendously thoughtful and personal service in any other hotel. Both Luca and Andrea were exceptionally responsive from the moment we contacted them before leaving home and throughout our stay. Luca arranged for transportation from the airport when we arrived and he and Andrea were constant sources of expert guidance of where to eat delicious Roman specialties and recommended hidden gems not to be missed in Rome and beyond. Not even in five star establishments could one hope to receive better service. Luca even helped us secure train and concert tickets and provided us with advice about several day trips, too. Do not hesitate to reserve your stay at this very special guest house!

author: Evan K
title: Awesome!
text: Luca was an amazing owner and we had a wonderful experience. The room was clean and nice and a fantastic location. He handled all questions and helped us with anything we asked.  The location was so close to the Vatican and the Spanish steps that we were able to walk everywhere!

author: Hannah C
title: Relaxing weekend in Rome with a friend
text: The room was perfect, clean and spacious, with space to store clothes, which also allows for longer stays. The location is excellent, very well connected by bus to/from the airport, central and perfectly connected by public transport to visit Rome. But above all the hosts were very kind, available for any questions and gave us useful advice on where to eat and what to visit in Rome. I would go back tomorrow!

author: Luke J
title: Fabulous stay in Rome, a stone's throw from the Vatican.
text: Fabulous stay in Rome, we were welcomed by Luca who surrounded us with his kindness, his kindness, his professionalism and his good addresses. The room was very large, very clean and even though overlooking the main street, very quiet. Bed made every day, small bottles of water replenished and calm guaranteed. Thank you Luca, looking forward to coming back..

author: Oscar C
title: Fantastic stay!
text:
When we arrived at the apartment building, we were warmly welcomed by the owners Luca and Andrea. They gave us a very nice overview of areas, tips and sights worth visiting in Rome. We also received many tips for good restaurants with authentic Italian food. The apartment itself is of a good standard, is located in a quiet area, is cleaned daily, and is within walking distance of most everything. If you don't want to walk, the metro is also a short distance from the apartment.

All in all, very happy with our stay! Would definitely stay here again on my next visit to Rome.

author: Chloe J
title: Almost Perfect
text: Our friends and I stayed in Rome Armony Suites from April 25-28th.  We absolutely loved our stay here as well as the host Lucas.  He is kind and knowledgeable with great communication as he gives you his cell number for anything you may need.  His recommendations were spot on.  Your room is clean with some very nice amenities included.  My reasoning for the 4 star review is a problem that occured while we were there.  The boiler/hot water tank was not working properly.  Lucas was definitely on top of getting someone in to work on it.  However, one morning we had no water as it was being worked on, then later only had cold water.  The following morning again only cold water.  Paying for cold shower was not in my plans nor enjoyable. Lucas apologized for the inconvenience but I definitely felt we should have been compensated in some way.  Perhaps the drive to the airport....but definitely something.  Lucas has high standards on customer service as I do being in the travel business.  I would have had to do something for my customers to make up for this.  Would I stay here again and recommend to stay here, absolutely!  I just would have handled this a little differently.

author: Lucia Q
title: VERY GOOD HOTEL
text: Very welcoming staff, top-notch cleanliness, very varied breakfast, I recommend it 100% except unfortunately for the exterior which is not up to the hotel. GO THERE WITHOUT ANY PROBLEM.

author: Wyatt K
title: 5 Star Service, Location & Hospitality
text:
5-Star: 
Excellent Location, Outstanding Service, and True Marriott Hospitality

My wife and I recently spent a few days at the Element Times Square West during our visit to New York City, and the experience exceeded our expectations.

The location is hard to beat—just a short walk to Times Square, Madison Square Garden, Broadway theaters, restaurants, and multiple subway lines. It made exploring NYC incredibly easy without needing a taxi.

What truly stood out, however, was the service. Anjelita at the front desk was exceptional throughout our stay. We interacted with her several times, and she was consistently friendly, professional, knowledgeable, and eager to help. She made us feel genuinely welcome and was one of the highlights of our stay.

I would also like to recognize Brianna, the General Manager, for her outstanding hospitality. She took the time to assist us personally and arranged a thoughtful room upgrade that made our visit even more special. The communication and attention to guest satisfaction were evident throughout our stay and reflected positively on the entire team.

I should also note, John E in the breakfast area was exceptionally friendly and helpful. He even surprised my wife with hash browns that were not out that day and she mentioned she wanted some in passing… John E showed up at the table with some minutes later. Wow! Salamat, John! 

As a Lifetime Titanium Elite member with more than 2,000 nights at Marriott properties worldwide, I have stayed in many hotels over the years. What keeps me loyal to Marriott is the people, and the team at Element Times Square West exemplifies the hospitality that has made the brand successful.

Thank you to Anjelita, Brianna, and the entire staff for helping make our New York City trip such a memorable experience. We would gladly stay here again on a future visit.

One bonus tip for fellow travelers: If you’re a pizza lover, don’t miss the pizza shop directly across the street called Square Pizza. During our trip I sampled pizza from several well-known NYC locations, and surprisingly, my favorite slice was right there across from the hotel. The classic cheese slice was outstanding, and the garlic knots were the best I’ve ever had. We enjoyed it so much that we went back twice!

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

author: Andrea N
title: 3 day New York break
text: Lovely hotel, clean and tidy. Staff were very helpful and polite. Bathrooms were spacious and clean. Bedrooms were ideal size with very comfortable bed. Room had a hob cooker , full size fridge and dishwasher. Rooms were cleaned everyday. Breakfast was a buffet style with pancakes ,omelette ,scrambled eggs which Was lush , sausages and muffins to tea coffee and juices. Hotel is located close to Times Square probably about a 10 minute walk . I would definitely stay at this hotel again

author: Katie A
title: GREAT LOCATION, PRICE AND VIEW!
text:
The location was perfect, short walk to Broadway/Times Square.  The price was reasonable and the view was AMAZING!  Extended stay with small kitchenete, full fridge, stovetop, microwave - save money on meals!  Higher floor (35) no noise and great view of the skyline.  Great HOT breakfast and evening Happy Hour (Beer/wine).  I never had any problem with the slow elevator.
Con - no drawers for my clothes, terrible lighting in the bathroom, no vanity or ledge in the shower to hold my stuff.
Overall, I would stay here again for the price and location, nothing fancy but more than suitable for a Broadway weekend!

author: Andrea U
title: I'll definitely stay here again!
text:
Excellent Location. Just a block from the subway station. Quiet enough street despite being in the Times Square area. Great place to feel that New York City energy.
Clean room equipped with everything you could need, including fridge, dishwasher, stovetop, glassware, and cooking utensils. 
Excellent Value. 
Great breakfast buffet. 
Also, one of the better hotel gyms I've seen

Special shoutout to Damien at the Front Desk, he is amazing.

author: Kyle Y
title: Good experience
text: Good experience. Central hotel in Manhattan, not far from Times Square. Clean and spacious rooms, a large and very comfortable bed (I think the rooms are the strong point of this hotel), the view from the room wasn't the best but it's fine anyway. We had read negative reviews regarding the use of the elevators, but fortunately, we never had any problems. The only downside was the breakfast, which was sparse and had few sweet products (for what we paid, I expected better), but the pancakes and waffles were good. The staff at the reception was a bit cold but polite; I would still return to this hotel, it was a good experience that I would repeat.

author: Daisy E
title: Fantastic Views, Disappointing Breakfast
text:
The biggest advantage of this hotel is its location. It is very close to Times Square, making it a convenient base for exploring New York. Our room was comfortable, and the highlight of the stay was definitely the view. We stayed on the 27th floor, and the nighttime skyline views were spectacular, especially considering the price we paid. The heating and air conditioning also worked very well.

Unfortunately, the breakfast was a major disappointment. The selection was extremely limited, with only one type of ham, one type of cheese, and a few hot items. Most of the options were sweet, with very few savory choices. As a European traveler, I found the variety particularly poor.

I was also surprised to see breakfast served almost entirely with disposable plates, cups, and plastic cutlery. For a large international hotel chain in 2026, this felt outdated and unnecessarily wasteful.

The shower water pressure was not the best, and the elevators became crowded very quickly during busy periods.

Overall, this hotel offers a great location and fantastic views, but the breakfast experience and some operational details could be significantly improved.
