author: Jack A
title: Not recommanded
text: The hotel cancelled our reservation we made throught booking. We ended up in the meeting room to finish the nigth. They also kept our damage guarantee (250 dollars). I do not recommand them.

author: Holly O
title: Lovely hotel close to Times Square
text:
Lovely hotel close to Times Square. Room was spacious, quiet and clean. Having the kitchenette was useful. Most of the staff were helpful and friendly (we especially found Arthur helpful).

Breakfast was good. Cooked breakfast mostly consisted of egg and sausage or a variation thereof! There was also toast, cereal, porridge, muffins, bagels, fruit etc. 

The dining room is not big enough and on occasion there are no tables available. Also, on occasion, there are queues for the lifts which can be frustrating. 

For a hotel priding itself on being "eco friendly" we found it very strange that breakfast was served on disposible paper plates with plastic cutlery (we took the metal cutlery down from the room to try and save on the waste).  Further, staff would push over flowing bins past your table whilst you were eating which wasn't very appetising.

We enjoyed our stay and would recommend this hotel.

author: Anna S
title: Disappointing
text: Disappointing stay in NYC.  Asked for an early check in via the app.   Stay 60 plus nights at Marriott a year, very disappointed in the service. No effort was made to accommodate me.  Came to hotel at 10 am actually did not get me in a room until after 3 pm.  Texted numerous times via app and no reply.  Was on hold on via telephone  for over 20 minutes. Show up back at hotel there are four people at the front desk not doing anything to help customers. Later in day, there was a line of people 10 people deep at check in at 4 pm to get rooms, no sense of urgency at hotel to help.

author: Rosie I
title: Windows do not seal. Street noise is the same as just sleeping outdoors.
text:
Nice room, well-furnished, thoughtful touches. Plugs in all the right places, comfortable bed, decent shower.

Surprisingly large room for NYC at that price point.

All worthless. 

It's impossible to sleep because the hotel skipped out on five dollars worth of sealant so that street noise doesn't leak through gaps in the windows.

This is an easily fixable problem, so I hope the hotel will listen and this review will cease to be true.

author: James Z
title: Element New York Times Square West - Great Stay!
text: I had a client meeting nearby so I decided to return to this property after an absence of several years. What a wonderful surprise - THE ELEVATORS HAVE BEEN REPLACED! BRAND NEW! AMAZING! This is a huge deal for those of us who endured the unspeakable horrors of the old, constantly malfunctioning elevators. Equally - if not more - importantly (for me), the Front Desk person (Gio) gave me the warmest of welcomes and put me in a room with a spectacular view. So, huge thanks and shout out to GIO! My room appeared to have been recently renovated. Everything was spotless and perfect. For those on vacation, the FULL kitchen in every room makes self-catering a fun, healthy, and cost-effective option in the heart of Manhattan. Very enjoyable stay.

author: Sofia E
title: Not up to Marriott standard
text: Hotel is not up to Marriott Bonvoy standards. Our room has multiple issues including cracked bathroom sink, loose faucet and missing microwave plate. Suggesting passing.

author: Rosie B
title: Gross
text: There are no words to describe how disgusting this hotel is!

author: Sara G
title: Trapped on 9th Floor
text:
I will NEVER again be staying at this property.  It’s such a shame.  It used to be my favorite hotel in NYC when it opened under SPG years ago.  As a New Yorker, having moved out of the city it always felt like coming back to a NYC apartment.  But over the years, service became terrible, the rooms became dirty and run down, the HVAC got loud and barely functions.  

But the biggest problem, the unforgivable, is the elevators.  There are simply not enough elevators to service that many floors and that many people.  Waits can take on average take up to 5 minutes.  It’s wholly unacceptable.  And as Bonvoy Elite member, I’ve never encountered anything like this before.  

But this last week, during my stay, i encountered a problem that is making me write a review (which I NEVER do).  One of the elevators was shut down (I’m assuming due to servicing) at 10am on a Wednesday.  This is PRIME elevator time, after breakfast, as people head out to work or to explore the city.  I needed to leave the hotel 9;55 to get just across the street to work at 10am.  I left my room at 9:30 to give myself time.  Every elevator that came was packed.  I would have taken the stairs even from the 9th floor but I had two huge suitcases as I was leaving from work to the airport.  At 9:45 i called the front desk.  I was basically told there was nothing they could do but the attitude of elevator. I had already tried that, but every single elevator that stopped going up or down was completely packed.  At 10 o’clock I called again. I told them I was stuck on the ninth floor then I needed help. They said they would see what they could do. At 10:20. I called again. I’m really angry. I was trapped on the night floor. They finally had a bellman key off the elevator to come get just me.  Finally at 10:30 someone came to get me. One hour. One whole hour. I was trapped in the building. I missed my first meeting…that Inwas supposed to lead. Besides the money lost on the space that I had rented, I look unprofessional and have severely damaged my reputation. Because of this hotel. Because of this property. The damage done is not just monetary, but this professionalism lapse will take years for me to recover from.  I’m angry and disheartened.  And I’ll NEVER stay here again and make sure no one I know ever does.

author: Lea V
title: Excellent hotel!!!
text:
Excellent hotel, improved breakfast, put receptionist who speaks Spanish and work with a car company to facilitate the return to the airport
All very kind, it's my third stay and I'll be back this year

author: Michael B
title: A wonderful stay!
text: I had a delightful stay at Element! I was visiting New York for a week to catch some Broadway shows and this hotel was perfect. The hotel is roughly 10 minute walk from Times Square and lots of theatres. The hotel is just around the corner from the 42 St-Port Authority Bus Terminal subway station and it was very easy to travel from JFK to the hotel! I arrived quite late at night and was checked in by the friendly and helpful staff at reception. The hotel room is incredible for a New York hotel - full kitchen including a full size fridge / freezer, hob, dishwasher all the utensils you could need and coffee machine. Truly everything you could need to cook all of your meals during your stay. Breakfast was also excellent - a selection of hot food which was different almost every day - pancakes, waffles, french toast, bacon etc. There is also a bagel station, chobani yogurt, pastries, fruit and cold meats and cheese. The drink selection was also amazing - hot coffee and plenty of tea bags, hot chocolate powder as well as fruit juice. I ate as much as I could at breakfast and quite often wasn’t hungry again until the evening. Breakfast was surprisingly quiet most days even at 9-10am. My flight home got cancelled due to the blizzard so I had to stay an extra couple of days but fortunately the hotel had availability so I was able to book the extra days and stay in the same room! The breakfast staff were also superb on the day of the blizzard - despite it being busy they were bringing out hot food as fast as possible which was very impressive. I didn’t find the lifts in the hotel being an issue - I was on the 26th floor and a couple of times I had to wait a few minutes for a lift but it was never too bad. Rooms are cleaned every other day which worked fine for me! The bed was very comfortable and I slept really well during my stay. The bathroom was clean and the shower was lovely - shampoo, conditioner and body wash are on the wall of the shower and you also get a bottle of lotion in the bathroom. Would highly recommend this hotel for solo travellers  looking to see some Broadway shows! Huge thanks to all of the staff at Element for making my stay so great :)

author: Brooke O
title: Poor care
text:
Bad experience. They charged me twice for the room because they had no will to correct a problem with the travel agency. Poor care from the counter staff, zero willingness to help me and the agency. 

There were cockroaches in the room too.

author: Henry G
title: Extra nice hotel for the price
text: Stayed here for a short break from the UK. 3 ladies in their 60s first time visitors to NY. The hotel was more than we expected for the price we paid, comfortable, clean rooms. The kitchen area was a bonus although we didn't use it. The staff were really nice and were extremely helpful. I booked through a well known travel company but emailed the hotel directly, when our other friend decided to join us, to ensure our rooms would be close together, when we checked in our rooms were directly opposite each other. The breakfast included was enough to keep us going for the day with lots of choice, cooked, cold meats, pastries, fruit and my favourite,  porridge. The rooms are well equipped with iron, ironing board, hair dryer and kitchen utensils also coffee making facilities. On our last day there we were able to leave our cases in a locked room ( we were given a ticket that we had to hand back to getour cases) so that we could have one last walk around Times Square. The Location is centrally located, about a 5 min walk away from Times Square. If Im ever lucky enough to visit NY again I would definitely look at booking this hotel again.

author: Grace U
title: Clean, comfortable, good-sized rooms near Times Square
text:
This hotel is an absolute winner! We're on an extended trip around NYC, visiting different parts of town and staying in a variety of hotels. I can tell you from experience that the Element's rooms are the best we've seen by all measures: size, condition, amenities, and overall comfort.

We were welcomed warmly and found the location to be perfect for quick access to Times Square. Each room has a refrigerator and freezer that, while not as large as the one you have at home, is definitely more than adequate for all the drinks, leftovers, snacks, and so forth that you may have. There is also a two-burner cooktop with utensils, cookware, plates and so forth in case you want to safe a few bucks on meals.

I'm struggling to find a single negative here and I simply cannot. Highly recommended!

author: Harper H
title: Would Definitely Return
text:
Had a most enjoyable stay with my teenage daughter last month; there for 5 nights.
Lovely room, quite spacious for NY, very comfortable beds, all that we needed.
Stayed on floor 33; had a little wait for the lifts but didn’t not experience too long a delay during our stay.
Excellent location away from Times Square, etc yet with good subway links close by.
Plenty going on in the vicinity.

author: Andrea U
title: Good hotel for a short stay
text: Stayed at this hotel for two nights. Spacious room with King size bed. Bathroom with shower. No bath. There was no view. You were looking at a wall. Hotel is near Wallstreet, the 9-11 Memorial and Brooklin Bridge. All sights are easily accessible by metro.

author: Liam R
title: NY Doubletree hilton
text: Rooms too small. Toliet wouldn't flush properly. Towels scratchy. No conditioner. Rude girl at elevators. Hard to get an elevator up or down. Grace at front desk was nice.

author: Caleb Z
title: Enjoyable stay
text: Loved our stay! Great location, clean comfortable rooms. Perfect for our trip to New York. Would stay here again!

author: Giulia J
title: The right place for a comfortable stay
text: I am giving this review for two main reasons-The customer service experience I had with Daniel and Maia.  I felt compelled to give the review because they made me feel at home right away.  From advising what options where available while we waited for our room to accessing the WiFi to handle my business calls.  These may seem like small things to some but they thought of these conveniences without me asking.  It shows that the embody double trees mission to proved a first class hotel experience where professionalism is a not taken for granted.  This is part I part II is after my stay is over.  I have no doubt Daniel and Maia and double trees in general won’t disappoint.

author: Tyler F
title: Decent choice is  you are coming without car
text:
We stayed as a couple mid March and wanted to explore the area for a few days
 Pros: 
Location- only if you are using public transportation or taxi/uber. Close to major attractions, shops, bars, food and subway stops
Clean hotel
Very nice view, booked river view king room and asked for higher floor
Staff was professional, very pleasant and made us feel welcome 
Luggage storage on the ground level
Sufficient breakfast that was included with our stay
Cons:
Location- if you are coming by car
Misleading info on website about self parking. 
No parking on site at all, was recommended a valet parking 2 blocks away(did not used)
Absolutely no place to unload the car. 
Cars parked multiple hours in front of the hotel, I.e. loading zone, and hotel does not enforce them to move. 
Reception in the second floor, which doesn’t make it easier to check in when you have luggage
 3 elevators , but only 2 worked most of the time
Bed is way smaller than king, I’m hardly over 5 feet, and if my head was down the pillow, then my feet stick out from the bed. 
Plus some minor issues, like safety deposit lock didn’t work, iron was not heating at all, tv channels didn’t work - for those we called reception and they tried to  resolve. 
In conclusion, if you are coming without car, want to  explore the area, it’s a  decent choice due to location  and cleanliness of the hotel. Make sure to leave the luggage downstairs, go up one floor for check in(stairs), then come back for your luggage and take the elevator. 
Higher floors are better than middle ones, at least we could catch an empty elevator.

author: Gavin E
title: Great location and great staff
text:
We had a wonderful stay—the room was comfortable and the hotel is in a great location. The staff were friendly and very helpful throughout our visit.

The only downside was the elevator service, which could be quite slow at times. It seems there may not be enough lifts for the number of rooms, and the system itself feels a bit outdated.

author: Ryan U
title: Daniel is the man!
text: Daniel is the man! Everytime we came in he always offers us water and asked us about our day. He made check in super quick and easy, and anything we needed he was always ready to help. Great staff here!

author: Jessica Y
title: Awesome costumer service-Vanetta
text: Great location, clean rooms, Vanetta at front desk is the kindest, most helpful human. Costumer service is off the charts

author: Ruby I
title: Clean, tidy and very comfortable
text: Hotel is well kept and is clean and tidy. The option to keep bags before check in and after check out was appreciated. Staff were always friendly and welcoming and the hotel room we had was on the 41st floor of 44 floors. The room was nice, comfortable and had a view of the city. We have Hilton Honors so we had some snacks on arrival and water which was a nice touch. The hotel is close to the subway and has easy access to Wall Street, Brooklyn, One world observatory and the airports.

author: William X
title: On top!
text:
Very decent hotel, very nice staff, clean and comfortable room, varied breakfast, hearty and good.
Incredible location: close to wall street, ferry states Island and metro 50 meters! 
No complaints about this property, I recommend it.

author: George M
title: NYC Experience
text:
The hotel is in an excellent location - just steps from the subway, a supermarket and Battery Park. The staff were friendly and welcoming throughout our stay. The room was warm, clean and comfortable, with regular housekeeping and a beautiful city view at sunrise and sunset. In-room amenities were very satisfying. Overall, we had no complaints and highly recommend this hotel to other travelers.
Before my stay, I was concerned by reviews mentioning slow elevators. However, during my visit in February, they worked fine due to the lower number of tourists. In peak seasons, they may be busier and less able to meet guests’ needs.

author: Sydney B
title: Impressive NYC stay
text:
First time in a Doubletree in NYC and was suitably impressed!  The welcome from the front desk was exceptional; warm, professional and funny - those ladies are a hoot! We arrived early morning and were given a room straight away - so appreciated after a 17hour flight - with warm cookies too.
The room is big by NYC standards, spotlessly clean with a comfortable bed and good shower pressure/lots of hot water and coffee/tea machine.
The surrounding area has lots of great restaurants, bars and a few shops and has good access to Metro. I would definitely recommend a stay here.

author: Evan V
title: Good location. Terrible horrible elevators.
text: Room was nice enough for a quick trip for a solo person. There were only three elevators in the building and they are very small and run slowly. The morning of checkout two of three elevators were not working. After waiting 20 minutes for an elevator to arrive at the 14th floor, I had to lug  my heavy suitcase and my backpack down 14 flights of stairs.  The only explanation given about the elevators was “sorry“. It was a good location for me to walk to my business meetings that were within a few blocks. Also a good location to stay if you are going over to the 911 Memorial and museum. Other than for the location, I would not stay here again

author: James Q
title: Nice New York hotel!
text: We enjoyed our time at Doubletree by Hilton New York Downtown.  The rooms were clean.  The staff was friendly and helpful, with recommendations.  The hotel is located close to the metro so it is easy to get anywhere in NY.  I would definitely stay here again.

author: Mia V
title: Disappointing for the high cost. Chose a different hotel.
text:
Visited NY to celebrate my birthday and for site seeing. 
Chose this hotel as back home (Uk) these are of very high standard.
Unfortunately this wasn't the case for this hotel.
The room was very small to say it was supposed to be a king sized bed room. 
A very small wardrobe only big enough for 1 person. 
The shower leaked onto the bathroom floor as the doors opens out onto the floor plus the water is only tepid, no hot water.
We had zero heating for the duration of our stay even after reporting it. 
On our last night at 2am the room phone rang with banging on the room door with engineers attending to fix the heating problem. A bit late on our late night? 
For the size of the hotel and volume of guests there aren't enough lifts to travel to and from rooms. 
We were told they had a roof top bar but each time we went it was closed or being used for private parties. 
False advertisement.
Reception were helpful and friendly but the hotel in all needs a huge communication re-think and product quality improvement. 
We won't be choosing the Hilton again no matter which country as it was a rip off for what it was.

author: Oliver T
title: Nice hotel but plan ahead around the elevators you’re going to wait
text: Hotel is good. Rooms are good, clean and size was good for us but the elevators are why we won’t stay again. It’s a ridiculous wait which actually makes coming and going a dreaded task. We ended up just lugging around the things we bought because going back to the room real fast to drop things off was not an option. You hear them wooshing past you but they never seem to stop and if they do they’re full so you wait again. I wish they’d figure it out, otherwise it’s good.

author: Ian D
title: To be recommended
text: We stayed at this hotel for the NYC Marathon and were very pleased with the size of the room (above the average of other hotels of the same category in New York), the impeccable daily cleaning and its location in the quiet area of the Financial District just steps from Wall Street and subway stops. Sometimes the wait for elevators has been prolonged but there are always stairs for those in a hurry!

author: Nathan T
title: New York stay
text:
Great stay at the double tree by Hilton during the week of the New York Marathon.
The hotel is conveniently located in South Manhattan.
All subway lines within 5 minutes walk and ferry departure to Staten Island within 5 minutes too.
The only downside is the endless wait at the elevators.

author: Olivia V
title: Stay if you like long elevator waits
text:
The elevators were terrible! Very slow and tiny!  The location isn’t the best. Not much close by for restaurants or shopping. 
Shower was too complicated. Took a scalding shower on the first day.

author: Giulia S

The rooms were clean and large enough for our stay. Breakfast is tasty.
We can recommend the President Hotel.
Thank you!

author: Mathis D
title: Great hotel

The beds and pillows are super comfy we had such a good sleep, you get coffee, teabags, sugar, milk and 2 bottles of water in the rooms. The body was and shampoo smells so nice the showers lovely. We woke up feeling really refreshed. We even got room of the day which means we got a free complimentary breakfast would definitely recommend and stay again x

author: Zachary V
title: Friendly,  Very welcoming, pleasant, helpful and funny
text: I’ve stayed at the President hotel many times over the years and have never been welcomed in with such humour as I got from Letisya, Karina and Achung at the reception. Thank you all so very much and I really hope at least one of you guys are there to check me in again when I return. Michael

author: Luke C
title: Cosminas review
text:
The atmosphere in the lobby was amazing!The room smelled like flowers and the bed was comfortable.
The staff was amazing!Special shoutout to Cristi that helped us find the nearest landmarks and told us all the details we needed to know!
The locatiob was perfect,near The British Museum and Covent Garden.It is also a few stations away from City Center.The price was amazing for the high quality of the room and you don't have to pay for the bed the kid sleeps in.The halls were empty and everything was quiet.The cleaners would come every day to clean our room,iron our sheets and make our bed.You could not see any dust in this room.There were nicely scented body and hair products.Breakfast was also delicious.

author: Manon E
title: Aleksandar! You fabulous human!
text:
Exceptional Service, Care and Local Knowledge

I would like to take the opportunity to give special recognition to Aleksandar, the hotel concierge,for the exceptional level of care, compassion and professionalism he demonstrated throughout my stay.

From the moment I interacted with Aleksandar, it was clear that he genuinely takes great pride in his role and is passionate about providing an outstanding experience for hotel guests. His approach goes far beyond simply answering questions or providing directions. He takes the time to listen, understand what guests are looking for and provide thoughtful, personalised assistance with genuine warmth and enthusiasm.

What particularly stood out was Aleksandar’s excellent knowledge of the local area and the businesses within it. His recommendations felt authentic and considered, rather than simply being standard tourist suggestions. He was able to provide useful insight into local restaurants, businesses, attractions and services, helping to make the experience of exploring the area much easier and more enjoyable.

Aleksandar also deserves recognition for the clarity and accuracy of the information he provides regarding the hotel itself and the services available. He communicates information in a clear, direct and professional manner, ensuring that guests understand what is available to them and how they can make the most of the hotel's facilities and services. This level of communication is extremely valuable, particularly when staying somewhere unfamiliar.

Above all, what makes Aleksandar stand out is his care and compassion. He creates the impression that helping guests is something he genuinely enjoys, rather than simply something required as part of his job. His friendly manner, patience, attentiveness and willingness to go the extra mile make a significant difference to the overall guest experience.

It is people like Aleksandar who can truly elevate a hotel stay from being simply good to being memorable. His passion for his profession, his knowledge of the local community, his professionalism and, most importantly, the genuine care he shows towards guests are qualities that deserve to be recognised and celebrated.

I would have no hesitation in recommending Aleksandar and believe he is a tremendous asset to the hotel. His commitment to providing excellent service reflects extremely well on the hotel and demonstrates the high standard of hospitality that guests hope to receive.

**Thank you, Aleksandar, for your exceptional service, genuine care and for making the experience that much more enjoyable. You are a credit to the hotel.**

author: Aaron X
title: Super location to visit london

author: Hannah H

author: Mia D
title: Good option
text: The hotel is well located.  Clean and the breakfast is fine. The rooms are small. It does not have air conditioning and you must open the windows no matter what at this time of year. That is why it is somewhat noisy. Recommended at a good price, clean, well located, and with good service.

author: Leo F
title: Good hotel but lack of AC an issue
text:
I had used this hotel before with work, and found it a good, convenient place to stay, so decided to stay again with partner, on an "impromptu" weekend in London. We stayed room only.

I echo a lot of the points already raised, hotel is well located for central London, handy for the British Museum and central London (Russell Street Tube very handy to the hotel) and a Pret a Manger on almost every corner.

The room was small put practical. Comfortable bed and a small but modern bathroom. However the lack of AC was a issue. We did have a fan supplied but it was noisy and circulated, rather then refreshed, the air in the room. We understood why the 2 windows were tethered, but this meant that we could not open them wide enough to get any cool air in, so the room was like a oven. This meant foe the 2 nights we were there we did not sleep much. 

I see this as a hotel that, for me, is great for a winter/spring break but I would not stay their again in the Summer/Autumn, unless the AC issue was rectified.

author: Luke G
title: HOTEL PRESIDENT
text: Excellent hotel experience in a very central area near the Russell Square station, and it is very easy to get around. The bed is comfortable; the only flaw is that there is no air conditioning, but it does not get too hot. At the reception, we met a super welcoming and nice girl named Karina, and she also helped us with travel, advised us on what to visit, and was available 24/7 for information about the hotel.

author: Hannah K
title: Beautiful hotel, great business sense.
text: Beautiful hotel, very well located. Very clean room and perfect, very hearty breakfast. Lots of friendly and smiling staff everywhere in the hotel. Furthermore, having had to return to France earlier than expected for family reasons, I was fully refunded for the nights already paid for without any problem!  If I return to London, I will book a room in this hotel again. Note the presence of a safe in the room, allowing you to go for a walk without carrying documents and valuables.

author: Pierre V
title: Excellent
text: She was so nice! Her name is letisya

author: Sara T
title: Great location. Good hotel
text: Good hotel. Great location. Staff very welcoming ( especially Karina on check in) only issue is rooms need AC in summer.

author: Chloe V
title: Good value
text: Nice simple clean hotel....great lounge. And a very helpfull staff, even in Rush hour. Yasmina was a Delight.

author: Camille P
title: Good hotel
text: good service comfortable room，location is very convenient. Staff here like Karina very friendly.

author: Juan J
title: Family vacation in London
text:
Hotel in an excellent location; you can reach tourist attractions on foot in just a few minutes, such as the British Museum. The lobby is welcoming, with air conditioning that provides relief after a trip in very high temperatures. The quick check-in is very professional. The rooms are truly very clean, as is the bathroom. Towel changes can be requested every day, and the rooms are cleaned every day in a truly professional manner. There were three of us, and the room they assigned us was clearly two single beds with an extra bed, so it turned out to be a bit small; it was even difficult to open the closet doors. We pointed this out at the front desk; the guy who was on duty was very eager to find a solution, but there were very few rooms left and the sizes are the same, so we decided to stay.
There is no air conditioning in the rooms, but they had two fans waiting for us upon our arrival. Despite this, however, it was really very hot; one evening we asked at the front desk if they could unlock the window latches so we could open them completely, and they told us that someone would come later, but it didn't happen. The next morning we asked again, leaving a note for the housekeeping staff who told us to ask at the front desk again; when we found Isha (I hope the name is spelled that way) on duty, she was not only kind but truly professional, empathetic, and efficient; after a few minutes, a lady came to unlock them and we were able to open them completely. The breakfast was absolutely perfect, varied, and they were very attentive to allergies. There are even alternative milk drinks. There is also the possibility to refill water bottles. Fantastic! Overall, we liked the hotel a lot; it is absolutely recommended. Thanks again to Isha.

author: Pablo N
title: Patricia was phenomenal!
text: I was a visiting scholar in the area and Patricia’s service was absolutely incredible. The room was exactly what I wanted, clean and cleaned well each day. Location was perfect and breakfast was a highlight also!

author: Giulia O
title: One of the best hotels to stay in Central London
text:
It was my first trip ever to London, UK. I stayed at the President hotel for 10 days. Such a central location! Close to the British Museum, SoHo, and Chinatown!

Had a great experience. The check-in process was easy and smooth. The front desk staff including Divyang, Karina, and Yasmina were so welcoming and helpful. They were very accommodating to my needs, as I preferred a room facing the sun. They were able to find a room to my preference.

The hotel rooms are clean and quiet. Had great sleep. Highly recommend! I will definitely stay here again next time I am in the city!

author: Charlotte Z
title: Gladly again on the next NYC trip.
text: Great stay, very centrally located, and the staff is always helpful and competent!

author: Freya U
title: A gem of a hotel in NYC!
text:
What a gem of a hotel! We were originally staying at a larger chain hotel closer to Times Square and made a last minute change to Pestana, and my goodness are we glad we did this!! From arrival, we were greeted with smiles and our flight came in early so we thought we’d have a long wait to check-in, but the lovely Ricardo got us in a room ready for us to start our trip asap. The rooms are spacious, I can’t compare to others in NYC as it was our first visit but it was already better than what we had planned! The sink was in the room which was different but it actually worked nicely! Aircon was fab as it was hot when we stayed, the only slight issue is it kept switching on and off the first night and we realised it was set to auto so after changing it was perfect!!

The hotel was in walking distance to so much and grand central is a 5min walk which was just incredible! With Bryant park also so close, it was the perfect location to see so many sights but be away from the chaos!

We will absolutely stay here again if we return to the city and highly recommend it! Also, the smell as you walk in the hotel was gorgeous!! They provide complimentary breakfast snacks like bagels and fruit which are first come first served. All the staff greeted us with smiles every time we left and returned to the hotel. We didn’t use it, but there’s also a terraced area to sit out and relax if needed. A must stay if you’re in NYC!!

author: Marta I
title: Great location in NYC
text: I stayed at Pestana Park Avenue for a week in July 2026. The hotel's location is excellent; it's on 39th Street, between Madison and Park Ave, a quarter from 5th Ave and two blocks from NYC Public Library, Bryant Park and Metro Station. My room was the Classic Room, works well for one or two people, but only for two bags. Room with comfortable bed. Bathroom with good shower. Good TV. Air conditioning. Dryer. Amenities such as shampoo, conditioner and liquid soap. The hotel offers a paid service in which you have access to a table area with a kitchen where, daily there are bread and croissants, coffee machine, water, microwave, teas, butter, jelly, milk, fruit (in my stay, it was mandarins). Simple but functional. Do not expect a big breakfast, the menu did not change throughout the week. The staff are very attentive and kind. I found my stay excellent!!!

author: George N
title: Great stay
text:
We had a great family stay at this hotel! The staff was friendly, welcoming, and always willing to help.
One of the managers was especially kind and took the time to speak Spanish with me, which made me feel comfortable and appreciated. The hotel was clean, the atmosphere was relaxing, and the service exceeded our expectations. We truly enjoyed our stay and would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a pleasant and comfortable experience.

author: Holly J
title: my stay
text: I always stay here when I’m in the city, and I honestly love it every time. The service is great, everyone is so nice and welcoming, and they always make my stay feel comfortable. I definitely look forward to coming back!

author: Elena S
title: Great place to stay
text: Great experience in Murray Hill. Very close to Grand Central and the staff is really friendly. Coffee and bagels were great!

author: Lucia W
title: Gem in Nyc
text:
Great experience, the hotel is well located and offer coffee and bagels in the morning.
Staff is really helpful and makes you feel at home.

author: Daisy A
title: A substandard hotel
text:
OK, it is true that I did not actually stay overnight...BUT,  HERE IS WHY!!....
When we saw the room, it was TINY!!..a queen bed with perhaps 2 feet from the edge of the bed to the wall!
The bathroom was super small....the sink was OUTSIDE the bathroom...
There was no closet...only a few spots to hand things against the wall....certainly inadequate for a wedding gown and tuxedo, and if you had coats, forget it!
There were just a few drawers UNDERNEATH the mattress...very inconvenient and of course no space for much at all...not chest of drawers....
Therefore, we left the hotel and stayed elsewhere....a great move!!!
SO, if you are a solo traveler with very little luggage and nothing it hang, this MIGHT be adequate...
For a seasoned traveler like myself, probably the worst room I have seen...yes, it was clean...
How this hotel got such a high rating, I will never know!!!!
Please stay elsewhere.....

author: Giulia A
title: Wonderful hospitality.
text:
Everything was wonderful, the room was large and very comfortable (I absolutely loved the incredibly soft sheets).  Great location, truly central, but away from the real chaos. Kind and helpful staff, always ready to assist you with a smile. A special thanks to Mauro and Rita ❤️
Plus, having a common area with drinks (really excellent coffee and cappuccino, as an Italian I can say that!) always accessible, and in the morning bagels/croissants.
PS: Since it is our honeymoon, the staff prepared a heart of petals on the bed and some chocolates, a gesture that was truly appreciated 😍
Thank you from the bottom of my heart

author: Noah H
title: Perfect location for quiet and still close to everything!
text:
We recently stayed here and would definitely recommend!
We were greeted by friendly reception staff after a long journey and were given a room on the 11th floor.
Yes the room was small, however, if you’re not spending much time there it isn’t a problem. It was clean and the bed was very comfortable.
There is 24/7 coffee, tea and filtered water available and first come first served pastries each morning.
The location was perfect. 5 minute walk from grand central station. Far enough away from the main hustle and bustle to be quiet at night but still very walkable to all main attractions and areas.
The only slight issue I would say was the daily room cleaning. One day we had to go and ask for towels (which took a long time) and another day we had to ask for coffee pods, however, I would still give 5 stars. 
Would stay again if we visit NYC in the future

author: Julien Z
title: Lovely hotel,  good location

Lovely hotel, everyone was friendly, good location 

Cons - small room

author: Daniel D
title: All smiles!
text: Great location. Nice room. Clean. Friendly helpful staff. Would definitely recommend and stay again!

author: Evie A
title: Best Experience Ever!
text:
We had an absolutely exceptional experience at Pestana Park Avenue in New York! Without a doubt, one of the best hotels I’ve ever stayed at in the city.
The location is simply unbeatable — just steps away from iconic Manhattan landmarks, with easy access to everything you might need, whether for leisure or business. It truly makes all the difference in a trip.
However, the real highlight is the staff: extremely attentive, friendly, and always willing to help with absolutely anything. From check-in to small day-to-day requests, I was treated with a level of care and kindness that is rare to find. Congrats specially to Francisca Pereira, guest manager, and all the staff (Rita, Julia, Andre, and everyone else!).
The accommodations are impeccable — the rooms are very well maintained, organized, and exceptionally clean. Everything feels new, comfortable, and thoughtfully designed to provide a relaxing and pleasant stay.
Another point worth mentioning is the availability of coffee, water, and other amenities throughout the day. These small touches make a big difference and show how much the hotel cares about its guests’ well-being.
In summary, a perfect stay! I highly recommend it and will definitely return on my next trips to New York.

author: Katie H
title: Room was not large, but our welcome was!
text: My husband and I needed to stay overnight in the city and after reading reviews of many hotels in the area , we chose Pestana. It was a great choice in terms of a very walkable location, small, but immaculate, well appointed room ( thanks for a lovely hot shower!), and a very friendly, accommodating desk staff ( shout out to Ricardo).  Coffee and complimentary morning bagel was certainly a plus . Would definitely return and highly recommend. Great value !

author: Miguel E
title: Fun time in nyc at Pestana
text: Very centrally located. Extremely helpful staff, great free coffee choices  and Clementines! Great price too.

author: Lily B
title: Gregory And Carlos 👑
text: Just to start, as soon as I entered the hotel I was greeted with two smiles, those smiles being Gregory and Carlos. Not only did they make my night, they made my trip! What a pleasant experience and service overall. If I could do 10/10 I would. Take my word when I say this, you’re going to LOVE it! Oh and good location too.

author: Zoe Y
title: Great Experience
text: Hotel is nice. When I came in Carlos and other front desk agents services are great l.

author: Ella R
title: Stay away- Ricardo, front office manager, will assault you
text: Hi everyone- yesterday I was hit by the front desk manager at Pestana hotel park avenue, Ricardo Jose Sousa. For starters, the staff is really rude. They don't have a smile on, are not friendly, and very entitled. My room had a leak coming from the corroded pipe and washer of the sink. I fell when I got back to my room at 11 pm. When you first walk in, the sink is right there and it was dark and I didn't see the water and slipped. I called downstairs but they didn't have maintenance, maintenance came the next day at noon (no sense of urgency.) room was still getting wet due to the broken sink. Further, the heat doesn't work in the room. You can set it to 90, but it will only go as high as 72. author: Miguel H
title: The Gem That Is The Jewel Hotel
text:
I almost don’t want to share about this gem, The Jewel Hotel!  After staying all over the city (and even just over in NJ), this is our go-to for short stays and longer ones.
Location is perfect.  You do have to walk a little for a subway station but we don’t always take the subway.  Walking from this spot can get you almost anywhere as it’s so central.
The rooms are varied and this time I had a mini-fridge which was great.  Rooms have always been clean with beds and pillows that are super comfortable.  I stayed on a higher floor where traffic was  somewhat muted but I could still hear the bells of St. Patrick’s Cathedral.
I will say some surfaces (like the wood base of an ottoman) show some wear but I did not think that it was getting tired.
The price is very reasonable.  I’ve stayed in worse places for much more money!
The staff is 100 percent what makes this hotel such a  pleasant place to stay.  
If you are used to chain hotels or fancy boutique ones, please look at the photos so you manage your expectations.  
Oh and the refillable water stations are great to have when you need.

title: Very poor quality
text:
This was one of the worst hotel stays I have had in a long time, and I travel quite a lot. When I checked in, the front desk associate told me I would be on the 4th floor, but that the elevator button for 4 did not work, so I should take the elevator to 5 and walk down. No offer to help me with my luggage to do this.

Then arrived at my room and there were dirty room service dishes outside my room (which stayed the entirety of my time at the hotel). My room was a single and it was the smallest room I’ve ever had at a hotel. Barely room for one twin bed and I had to shove my suitcase under the half desk thing they had in there. Before I went out for dinner, I used the bathroom and washed my hands and noticed that the sink didn’t really drain, so I figured I would mention it at the front desk on my way back.

I went to dinner, returned to the hotel around 9, and told the front desk about my sink issue, and they said they would send someone right up. He did arrive promptly and then he had to basically take apart the entire sink over the next 1.5 hours in order to get it to work properly. The maintenance man was the only good part of the entire stay—he was very kind and diligent. When he left, it was after 10pm and I just wanted to take a shower and go to bed. The shower was also terrible! The size was minuscule and I felt like I was drowning under the shower head and, go figure, the shower didn’t drain properly either. It came very close to overflowing and flooding the bathroom. 

I was able to get a decent night’s sleep, but that’s probably the only positive to take away from this stay. I would avoid this hotel, the surrounding neighborhood is fine though.

author: Adam A
title: Not great!
text:
This is a pretty ropey hotel. I just wish I had looked at trip advisor first before booking.
The location is great I have to say, some nice places to eat literally just outside the hotel, including a great coffee house. Tube station a 2 or 3 min walk and the high St less than that. That's where the good points end unfortunately. There is no breakfast or food available in the hotel (I was told this on arrival) so a lot of the stuff you see on booking websites is false. The hotel is really run down, loads of repair work needed, everywhere you look there are bodged repairs. My room was like a furnace as there is no AC. Impossible to sleep in the current summer heat. Lots of homeless people sleeping rough near the hotel and plenty of shady people walking around. To be honest London is getting worse week by week, its a proper grotty city these days and reminds me a lot of the the big US city's where poverty is hidden just a street or two back from the main tourist areas and business districts. 
The staff are friendly enough and the rooms were clean so I cant really blame them for the hotels main misgivings.
Massively overpriced for the a three star hotel. Even based on the location £80 a night would be a fair price to pay.

author: Grace C
title: Unsafe
text: We stayed two nights at this hotel. We had checked into our room on the ground floor and then went straight into town. In the evening we came back. When I pulled up the curtain there was a homeless man AGAINST our window doing drugs. There were also five other people next to our window, who made a lot of noise. We did not feel safe as it is a very thin wooden window that anyone can open with a little effort from the outside. After reporting it to the staff there was no refund possible as they offered us a new room. The new room was fine but very noisy and not well cleaned. I do not recommend this hotel unless you have little to spend.

author: Antoine H
title: Misleading Photos, Poor Service, and an Extremely Disappointing StayA
text:
Our experience at Cheshire Hotel was extremely disappointing from start to finish.

The hotel bears very little resemblance to the photos used to advertise it. The rooms we received were of a much lower standard than expected, outdated, poorly maintained, and completely different from what was shown online. We chose this hotel based on the advertised images, and the reality was nowhere close.

The customer service made the situation even worse. The reception staff were dismissive, unhelpful, and unwilling to understand or address our concerns. Rather than trying to resolve the issue, they insisted that we pay extra for an "upgrade." The upgraded room was nothing special—a small room with a basic double bed—yet we were charged a total of **£470**, which was completely unreasonable for what was offered.

The payment process for the upgrade was also highly concerning. Instead of providing a secure payment link or accepting a bank transfer, we were asked to provide our credit card details over the phone. This felt unprofessional and did not inspire confidence.

Throughout our stay, the staff were rude, dismissive, and made us feel like our concerns did not matter. Instead of acknowledging that the rooms did not match the advertised standard, they simply refused to help.

This was one of the worst hotel experiences we have had. Misleading advertising, poor-quality rooms, unreasonable additional charges, an insecure payment process, and extremely poor customer service made this stay unacceptable. We would not recommend this hotel to anyone and strongly advise future guests to look elsewhere.

author: Samuel Z
title: Please consider another hotel
text:
I booked a room with a kitchenette (Studio) on check in I was handed a piece of papers which said cooking was not allowed in the room. Despite it having the microwave and freezer there were no plates or cutlery. They also asked to scan my ID, this is not permitted for UK residents in a UK hotel. 

Once in the room I found evidence of bed bugs in the mattress. I was then moved to another room where the extractor was so loud and again no way to cook or eat in the kitchenette. I was then moved to a third smaller room where the wall paper and the door frame had been tapped up. The door was also already open as we approached.

The receptionist knocked the door again, offering a room change. This would have been the fourth change.

I contacted the hotel with my concerns who responded with. Cooking is not allowed due to fire risks, this suggests the rooms are not fit for purpose and are a fire risk and that the photos do not match their room and appear to be old. 

This means that they were selling rooms that could not be used as their intended purpose a breach of the customer rights act 2015 "A kitchen that cannot be used for cooking is a facility that is "unfit for purpose." 

As well as Consumer Protection from Unfair Trading Regulations 2008 which prohibits "Misleading Actions" and "Bait and Switch" tactics.

Advertising a room with a "kitchenette" implies it is a facility you can use to prepare food. By banning cooking after you paid, they misled you into a contract under false pretences. 

There also also signs staying that if you do not request a safe of give valuables to a manager then items (in rooms) are left at own risk as well as signs with hand sanitizer for covid - 19

These concerns have now been passed on to the council and health and safety for investigation

author: Joseph W
title: Reasonable and passable
text:
I was always expecting to pay vastly inflated prices for December in central London. I paid £225 for a single solo room. The room itself was fairly clean but small. Bed extremely soft which I liked but I would gander that most people would find it too soft. The bed was I would say a small double bed and had a comfortable soft headboard and two pillows 

It was nice having a bath in the room with a shower also. The bathroom was really about the same size as the room and was very clean. Good water pressure and dispenser of shower gel. 

Initial impressions were it seems modern and cleanish but on closer inspection: The room could do with some TLC- wallpaper coming away from the wall. No TV remote- they got me one but the TV had no signal and didn’t work. Hairdryer was a nice touch but only blew cold air so not useable. 
Biggest complaint is there was no plug socket next to the bed which in 2025 isn’t very good at all. 
Being on street level next to the street meant to was noisy. No privacy curtain/nets so curtain had to be shut at all times so no natural light. Pleasantly surprised that was  an iron and ironing board. 

When I get asked to provide photographic ID on check in I already know it’s not going to be amazing as inevitably it tells me that the hotel has problems around damages etc potentially some antisocial issues. I also felt annoyed we couldn’t bring food to eat in our room which is unheard off nowadays with all chains of hotels allowing this generally.

Taking the London factor out of the equation, I can’t say it was good value for money with the room size and no food available. However for being in central London during the Christmas period I guess it was reasonable and by far the cheapest. However outside of London I would not pay more than £100 a night for this room. 

Outside of the Xmas period I would say this room in central London should be no more  than £135 a night.  It was somewhere to sleep and I felt safe. I probably wouldn’t return unless the price was right. It did what I needed it to do

Horrible hotel, room, service, help and safety issues from the top down.
We checked in and had an issue with the door not locking right off the bat, after talking to the “service desk” we were advised to “just slam it” which appeared to work. After returning late at night to shower we found all towels had dust and fibers embedded in them- like they were washed with rugs or dog beds. When we asked for clean towels we got only one towel and one bath mat. Upon rerunning our second day we found our room wide open and the door lock broken. It was 11 pm and when I tried to use the phone to call for help to fix the door and check our stuff- the lock was stuck in the open position- we found the phone in the room did not work, there was no WiFi  to call for the help either. I was traveling with my young son and could not leave him alone. This place is a trap and upon complaints the hotel is stating that unless I can prove the statements they can’t do anything. They claim to have CCTV but won’t use that to show me asking for help, showing my phone to the concierge or asking why the phone doesn’t work etc placing an impossible burden on the customer to get away with a terrible experience.

title: Couples weekend
text:
We booked a budget hotel in the centre of London but for the price we were still left a bit disappoint. Over £270 for two nights is too expensive for what you get considering the other hotels locally and their prices. 
If you are looking for luxury then this is far from it. 
The hotel appears to be undergoing renovations as most of the entrance and downstairs looks like a building site.
The lack of curtain in the bathroom meant we didn’t have a great deal of privacy when in there as it looks straight out onto the main road. 
All of that  said, we had a clean bed and the room was cleaned and made up during our stay.  It wasn’t fancy but it had what we needed.

author: Rosie Q
title: location of this hotel is it's best part
text:
The first thing that is very good about this hotel- IT'S LOCATION.

I did not know much about London areas, but I did my research and got to know that, you should book around Central London, so I booked at this hotel. Little did I know the location would be perfect for any destination/ direction.

Everything is like a 2-10 minute walk from the hotel. This budget hotel is situated in the heart of the London West End, near the junction of Tottenham Court Road Tube Station, and Oxford Street.

Tottenham Court Road Tube Station - 2 min walk and now you are off to any location. 
Covent Garden, The British Museum- 5 min walk
Leicester Square, Oxford St: 5-7 Min walk
Trafalgar Square: 10 Min walk

We were here for 4 nights and 5 days. The room is very compact and you can not walk freely. It's good for small luggage and we had not very nice time, unpacking /packing medium-sized bags every day while getting ready.

The bathroom was quite good in size compared to the room size. All rooms have ensuite facilities, Freeview television, free wifi, hairdryer, iron & ironing board, complimentary tea & coffee facilities, and are designated non-smoking. 

Elevators are there and a luggage storage facility too. Great café around the corner with a good breakfast and also a pharmacy on the corner

I got a room facing the road and this is a busy road and let's just say you can't sleep peacefully, there is always noise outside, so avoid room-facing roads. 

Smooth checkin-checkout. They kept the deposit of 100 pounds but it's fine, it's their policy. Throughout our stay, we came at 3 AM and even left at 4 AM- no issue with that. Someone was always there at the reception.
Even they were okay with our early check-in. 

Overall - 3.5/5

author: William R
title: Decent location... that's about it
text: tiny room, hideous rates and a surprise deposit charge at check in. the only good thing about the hotel was that it is central and easy access to many things.  We needed to book in emergency otherwise this would never b our choice neither has been after ever again.

author: Carlos P
title: For shirt stays its fine
text:
Having just read the recent reviews it seems that this place is not popular!

I have no complaints. I don't know if it depends on which room you get. It got 14. On the downside, it's in the basement, so you get very limited natural light. But I was staying 1 night, literally for a bed, then leaving. So no problem. For a few days, maybe not.

But in this room, everything was very modern, very nicely done out and actually high quality. It had a NEFF induction hob for instance...this is not budget end of the range.

Bed was very comfy, I'm fussy about that too. Seriously, based on my room I don't recognise anything about what the reviews are saying.

But equally, I'm not about to claim its the best hotel I've stayed in. But what it was, was the cheapest room available in the west end at short notice on a Saturday night. And for that  it was fine.

author: Charlie E
title: Worst hotel we've stayed in.
text:
We arrived at 10:30am left our bags there as we knew check in was not until 15:00, we returned at 17:00 to be told our room was still not ready, so had to sit and wait another 20mins.
As we approached our room, it looked like the door had been kicked in and badly repaired.
The room was dated and dark, although the bed was comfy and clean, the room had been badly repaired inside, we were in a ground floor room right next to the road, although there were curtains up, there was no privacy blind.

No mirror in the room, one glass tumbler, broken ironing board, no toiletries.
No plugs in the bath or sink, water from shower was freezing cold, broken tiles in the bathroom had not been removed, just tiled straight over. 
When we told reception, all we got was if you're not happy we'll give you a full refund and you can leave.

We couldn't do that as it was now 18:00hrs. The photo's on there website and Booking.com website were totally different to the rooms.
The cost was £162 for one night, not worth the money, it's a shame as the location was great, we have stayed in better £70 hotels with breakfast.

Very disappointed, only consolation it was for one night only, else we would have moved hotels.

author: Marta C
title: Southwark Classic! Luxury and Service brings comfort!
text: My husband and I stayed at The London Bridge Hotel from June 24th through June 27th, 2026. This was during a huge heatwave in London and we were very glad to have the air conditioning in our room and great service provided by the hotel. There is not air conditioning in some of the main areas of the hotel, as is to be expected for London and older buildings. As most people will not be here during a heat wave, this will not matter to most people. The location of this hotel is a key attraction, as you are just a short walk from the London Bridge Tube and Train station, as well as Borough Market, The Shard (it towers over you at the end of the street), Southwark Cathedral, HMS Belfast, Hay's Galleria, and Southbank. It is a slightly longer, but not by too much, walk to London Bridge, All Hallows by the Tower Church, The Tower, The Monument, and all the wonders of the City of London and the Thames in this historic original part of London. Staying where the Romans first set up Londinium, but with all the luxuries a posh 21st century hotel can offer, is quite something. We had reserved afternoon tea for our first day which could not have been more perfect. Coming from the US on an overnight flight, we were graciously allowed to check into our room early, got to take a brief nap and then came down to afternoon tea for our first meal in London. The hotel bar where you are served this is quite lovely! Breakfast is served in the basement restaurant and is delicious and plentiful. Mere steps away from the hotel are many restaurants and cafes, and of course the world famous Borough Market. The staff could not have been more friendly and accomodating. Our room was cozy but full of nice things like a fridge (hidden in a credenza), some fresh fruit and water, and an attentive front desk staff to bring anything else your heart could desire. I could not recommend this hotel any more highly. It is an oasis of luxury in one of the best locations for historic London lovers to stay.

title: Good location but a tad noisy - ask for a quiet room
text: This hotel is really good value, welcoming staff, clean and comfortable room. However, our room was at the top of the stairs and also looking over the street (and train station). So my advice would be to ask for a quiet room.

author: Molly D

author: Nathan U
title: London weekend stay August
text: This hotel is in a brilliant location and the rooms were a good size. Check in was really good and I had contacted the hotel to see if we could leave cases prior to check in and they advised we could with the concierge service which was a good plus. However when we arrived at 12 oclock ish the rooms were ready which was great. I just have a couple of complaints, we only had one bottle of water in the room and when asked for more was advised we would need to pay!!!.  We also had breakfast included in our booking and that was disappointing.  It was buffet style and most of the hot plates were empty and when asked we were told bacon would be another 10 minutes as well as fried eggs. Why when you are providing breakfast you should be checking and restocking so there is enough for everyone.  Also the fruit selection was very small and disappointing.  The breakfast room also needs some music or something playing in the background as was strange room to be in.  Overall nice stay good location but could have been better

author: Ruby R
title: Unfairly charged
text:
This was our first time visiting London, and while the hotel was in a great location with friendly staff, our check-in experience was extremely disappointing.

When we arrived, the staff immediately told us we had to book an additional Executive Room because our reservation was for two adults, without first allowing us to see the room we had already booked. We understand it was our mistake not to include our two children (ages 4 and 5) in the booking, but instead of offering any alternative, we were pressured to pay an extra £718 for another room. We contacted Agoda to cancel, but were told we would have to pay a £400 cancellation fee, leaving us with no realistic choice.

What disappointed us most was the lack of flexibility or empathy. We had just arrived after a long journey and simply wanted to rest. We can’t help but wonder what would have happened if we had been a family who couldn’t afford the extra room. Overall, despite the good location and friendly staff, this experience means we will not be staying here again.

author: Isabella B
title: Ripped off
text: Booked the hotel for 2 nights for 1 person and assumed at £540 breakfast would be included. At no time during booking process was I told this didn’t include breakfast WHAT A RIP OFF. When querying this the duty manager was most rude and didn’t want to have a conversation about this. Was there with family for a wedding 6 of us in five rooms at cost of £2700 and the manager wouldn’t include breakfast. I’ve stayed in better hotels for less with breakfast. Don’t stay there plenty of other 4&5 star hotels that are better value

author: Juan S
title: Good option value for money
text:
Well-located near the underground and borough market, the hotel requires a walk or a tube ride to reach typical places. Since breakfast wasn’t offered at the hotel (I believe they don’t), we opted for the borough market or a nearby coffee shop.

The hotel is small, and our rooms are even smaller. The windows were small, so natural light was limited. However, the shower and bed were great.

Overall, it’s a good value for money, especially for a short stay of no more than four nights.

author: Sara Z
title: Hospital visit.

author: Alexander P
title: Lovely hotel in a great location
text:
Great hotel. Location perfect, located next to the Shard and London Bridge station. Nice area too. 
Not sure what people are moaning about in regard to noise from trains - we were level one on the front of the hotel and didn’t hear anything, and don’t book a hotel next to a busy station then moan.
Staff are very friendly, we had an early check in to a lovely room. Very spacious for London, great AC, comfortable bed and immaculate. This hotel will be my go to when staying in London. Also loved that they provided robes and slippers.

author: Wyatt O

author: Leo D
title: ⭐ The Perfect Stay for Study, Business, and Exploring London
text:
I had a wonderful stay at Hilton London Euston during my time studying in London, and it provided the perfect balance of comfort, convenience, and exceptional hospitality. Its prime location, just a short walk from Euston Station, made commuting around the city and attending my studies incredibly easy.

From the moment I arrived, the staff were welcoming, professional, and always willing to assist. Their friendly service made me feel at home throughout my stay. My room was clean, comfortable, and well equipped, offering a quiet and relaxing space to unwind after busy days of lectures and exploring London.

The breakfast was excellent, with a wide variety of fresh and delicious options that gave me a great start to each day. I also appreciated the hotel’s elegant atmosphere and its close proximity to museums, restaurants, shopping areas, and many of London’s iconic attractions.

Hilton London Euston was an excellent choice for my stay, whether for study, business, or leisure. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for outstanding service, a convenient location, and a comfortable experience in the heart of London. I would gladly stay here again on my next visit.

author: Chloe W
title: Good location

author: Matthew Z
title: Not a good stay
text:
. This was easily one of the worst hotel stays I have ever experienced. I paid a premium to stay at this Hilton, opting for it over the nearby Travelodge where my friends were staying because I wanted a comfortable, high-quality night's sleep after a concert at Finsbury Park. It failed on every level.
​Since I am a light sleeper, my single request ahead of time was to be placed in a room away from the elevators. Instead, I was assigned a room directly opposite them. Sitting on the bed, I could hear the lift's automated voice announcing "Floor 2, lift doors opening" as clearly as if I were standing inside the elevator itself.
​When I went to reception to flag the issue, the staff member literally smirked at me and said they were fully booked, eventually telling me to come back at 10:00 AM the next day to swap rooms after check-out.
​The night that followed was a nightmare. Between the non-stop elevator traffic and the street noise at the front of the building—which sounded like being parked on the M25—I barely slept a wink and felt like crying.
​The next morning, I went downstairs with my luggage and explained the situation to a manager. There was no apology whatsoever. They simply told me they would move me later once rooms had been turned over.
​If you want a basic night's sleep and standard customer care, do not stay here. The rooms are incredibly noisy, and the staff simply do not care.

author: Hannah O
title: Better than the reviews suggest — a solid, honest base near Euston
text:
I booked this hotel with some trepidation, having read a number of unenthusiastic reviews here, and I’m glad to report that my worries proved entirely unfounded. Yes, it is a smaller and slightly dated Hilton — a typical example of the chain that probably hasn’t had a refresh in fifteen years or so, and is no doubt due one before long. But for what it sets out to be — a four-star, centrally located terminus hotel — it does its core job very well.

The room matched its photographs on the website exactly, and everything in it was clean and functional. As a Hilton Honors Gold member I was recognised at check-in and automatically upgraded to a Deluxe room a couple of days ahead. I also received a welcome text acknowledging my status and asking whether I needed anything — a nice touch for those who notice such things. The app check-in was painless, and its real advantage was that the room was ready early, just after midday, with a digital key issued straight away; I was grateful the property doesn’t default to releasing rooms only at 3pm, as some do. An extra hour’s late check-out was granted without fuss, and reception handled everything quickly. The service isn’t especially personalised — with the notable exception of breakfast, where the staff were genuinely hospitable and faultless. The breakfast itself was surprisingly good and comprehensive.

We were down for a weekend break to see Avenue Q at the Shaftesbury Theatre, an easy and pleasant twenty-minute walk away through the West End past the British Museum (we ate perfectly well at the Byron opposite the theatre). King’s Cross is only about eight minutes on foot through the back streets. After breakfast we walked across to the Wellcome Collection, an excellent free museum a couple of minutes away and a real gem if you have an hour or two to spare. The bed was very comfortable and clean, and I appreciated being able to open the windows for some fresh air.

A couple of honest caveats. The traffic can be noisy, as others have noted, though my fourth-floor room facing Endsleigh Gardens was perfectly fine. And the water pressure is on the weak side — short of a new boiler, water-saving shower heads would help make the most of what there is — but it remained entirely acceptable and didn’t spoil a decent shower.

On balance, for what it is and for the value, this hotel does its job well, and I’m happy to give it a fair five stars.

author: Emma Z
