author: Samuel X
title: No knowledge of coeliac disease
text:
Stayed at the blakemore for one night and had everything was lovely.

However I have coeliac disease and had emailed the hotel beforehand without reply. On arrival I told reception and was advised to speak to staff at breakfast time. They had a few slices of gluten free bread and on asking about a separate toaster the waitress took it away but came back and put it in the toaster alongside the wheat bread. When challenged that I could not risk eating this bread, and os her speaking with her supervisor it was quite clear they had no knowledge of CD. Be aware.

author: Sydney V
title: Top notch
text: Nice and quiet hotel, very helpful and friendly staff. Super breakfast, nice rooms and prime location

author: Nora X
title: Worst night of my life and dripping water from the ceiling
text: This is BY FAR the worst hotel I have ever stayed at - we were away and when we came back, it turned out our room was flooded from upstairs. Our room was wide open, without any member of the staff, so at first we thought we were robbed, because all of our things were there. All of our belongings are ruined, including electronic devices. No one from the hotel contacted us there was a problem, even though they had all our contact details. We got no explanation, not even a sorry from the staff and all they said is that we can try writing to an email with a complaint. Considering I am also pregnant, this is beyond anything I have ever experienced and I cannot imagine a worse reaction from the hotel and the staff, so I would avoid this place at any possible cost. From what I know, a couple of other rooms were also flooded, so the problem with the condition of the hotel is much bigger.

author: Megan H
title: Great Hotel with 1 or 2 minor issues
text:
This is a very impressive looking hotel when you approach, the foyer and terrace area is really lovely, the staff on reception are superb, the location for central London is really excellent, in my opinion there were 2 issues (albeit minor but my rating would have been an easy 5 without doubt if these were not an issue)

issue one we stayed in room 113 and it has everything you need but it is very small and a bit tired and certainly not representative of the wow factor you get on entry, I would have said it was a single room rather than a double, but we pretty much only slept there.

Issue 2 my bigger gripe was the breakfast staff, now I'm a northerner and we are pretty friendly and accommodating (in the main) but the two staff we interacted with wouldn't be working for my firm if they dealt with clients in the way they spoke, now it could be that they are foreign or they haven't been trained properly although is think the lady who was possibly Chinese looked like a manager so id be surprised, again I say minor issue because they were not rude but very curt and then walked away, we tend not to have that issue in London, I've actually had better staff in some premier inns,

However please do not let my minor issues put you off staying here, like I say its in a great spot and nearly every other staff member were great, I will mention 1 in particular a lady called Aran, now she is a master in dealing with the public and a true asset to the hotel.

author: Claire P
title: Well situated and comfortable hotel
text: The Blakemore is well situated (nearby 94 bus straight through to Oxford Circus) and comfortable. The junior suite had a large, firm bed and a useful second room with a sofa. The breakfast was adequate, with the usual buffet style setup. The bathroom was clean with a good shower. However, there were some negative aspects: during our four day stay one or other of the two lifts was out of action for three days. Getting service on the Terrace was all but impossible. The two televisions in the room shared a remote, which meant both had to be on at the same time... not ideal if your partner is trying to sleep while you watch in the next room. A fault with the desk light switch (meaning it was constantly on) was reported on the second day, but never got fixed. Lunch was supposedly from midday - but we were told that food would not be available until about 12:15 "as the chef doesn't arrive until 12:00"! Also, guests could not add drinks bills to their final room bill - they all had to be paid separately at the time. Overall, pretty good, but definitely could do some things better.

author: Ella J
title: Excellent location, super friendly staff
text: Staff was friendly and incredibly helpful, moved our rooms around so that our family could be on the same floor, bar was a great place to take a break in the evenings, location is perfect bc it’s out of the busy rush of the center of the city (and only a few minute walk from Hyde Park) and located less than 10 minutes walking from 3 tune stations. Rooms were clean and nicely sized for European hotels

author: Sydney N
title: Great hotel with perfect location
text: Our third stay at this hotel and we will be back again. The location is perfect with easy access too both tubes and buses. Only a short walk away from hide park.

author: Camille D
title: Blakemore Hyde Park
text: Our family group of five stayed for 3 nights (3 rooms). This hotel is well located near tube and bus lines, is attractive, the breakfast wonderful, the bed comfortable, friendly staff. The only negative was the WiFi, which was hard to connect to, and dropped frequently. This happened in each of our rooms, and in the lobby also. Staff were sympathetic, but were unable to remedy it. So many tasks are now done on the internet that this was a problem.

author: George J
title: Exceptional Stay at Notting Hill Hotel
text:
From the moment we walked into the Blakemore we loved it; lobby was stunning, staff cheerful, friendly, and exceedingly helpful.  

The restaurant was great (service and food).

Our room was spacious, well appointed, quiet, and the bed extremely comfortable and the bathroom a dream.

We definitely recommend The Blakemore Hyde Park and will stay again next time we’re in London …

author: Alexander V
title: EVERYTHING PERFECT
text: Flexibility and hospitality at the highest level with Paola, Cristian, and Daniela, truly super and very patient, as well as extremely professional and available

author: Abigail C
title: June 6th 2026
text:
We stayed in room 215, firstly let me say the room was immaculate & clean, but dated & tired decor & furniture,  the bed was comfy, but old sash windows drafty & didn't block any road noise.
The bathroom was small but functional,  had to virtually get in shower to close door to access the sink but again absolutely spotless,  room serviced daily.
Didn't complain at the time as not much the hotel could do to rectify these nit picky issues.
But will definitely be staying there again.

author: Charlotte Q
title: Dirty.
text: The room we were given the first night (because we requested a change) was not like the photos when I booked; the bathroom was small, very old, and dirty, with a lot of black hair everywhere, the curtains were so old that they were torn, both in the bathroom window and in the room window, which was so old that the wind came in, a disaster, and what can I say about the carpet, it was impossibly dirty. The next day, they moved us to a larger room with a bigger bathroom, but it had the same cleaning issues; entering and seeing hair is disgusting, and the bed also had hair. And in the first room, the Wi-Fi did not work.

author: Sara D
title: Beautiful hotel
text: The hotel is spotless clean, all the staff were very helpful and friendly. We were celebrating our 40th wedding anniversary and on arrival we were upgraded to an amazing suite. Thank you so much

author: Adam D
title: Great location.
text:
Superbly located very near 2 tube stations, Queensway and Bayswater. Many bars, shops and  restaurants within easy walking distance as is Hyde Park.

Checking in very easy, room was OK, perhaps a bit tired, needed a lick of paint and new furniture but for 2 nights perfectly acceptable. The bathroom was modern and a very good size.

author: Evan C
title: Hyde Park nearby
text: Great location. Close to Hyde Park. There's a shopping street nearby. Good breakfast. But it does not change. I spent 5 nights and it was the same every day. Excellent service with a Brazilian at the restaurant. I made tours with hop-on hop-off which has a stop near the hotel. I like it.

author: Chloe D
title: old and tired
text:
Very old and tired and a bit grim and the curtains falling down,
On the plus side the staff were very helpful and friendly, the location is great, bed was comfortable and water pressure very good.

author: Samuel U
title: The worst hotels I've ever had in London.
text:
Booked and paid for Standard Room, 19 m2. In fact, at the time of settlement got a 10 m2 kamorka category Single, half of what he paid for. When I pointed it out at the reception, I started openly claiming that I was wrong, that this was the number that was declared, until I showed the pictures with the real dimensions.

After that, I was "transferred" first to a room on the ground floor with windows that do not open at all and do not know where, then to another room, which turned out to be only 15 m2. I mean, I've been moved in three times and never given what I actually paid for.

And now for the condition of the rooms themselves: no air conditioning, no fan, the fridge covered in chips and scratches, like I've been in an accident, the drawers of nightstands and chests of drawers falling off or completely broken, the walls stained with black divorces and scratched, and at the end they gave me torn towels - as if that were normal.

Breakfast, which in a Booking.com photo looked varied, in reality turned out to be a couple of scarce hot dishes, one kind of sausage, one kind of cheese, three kinds of fruit and cereal with milk. OK.

As if that weren't enough - the floor is undergoing a full renovation: drill, hammer, workers constantly walking down the hall. There was no mention of this on the hotel's website, Booking.com or check-in.

I approached the front desk with each problem separately, repeatedly, and each time I got a denial - even when I showed the photos as direct evidence. No one was solving anything or helping.

For that kind of money and the four stars you're claiming, it's a real horror. Don't believe the photos on the site, the reality turned out to be completely different.

author: Abigail W
title: Had a lovely stay, would recommend.
text: I had a wonderful stay at south Kensington. The staff was very friendly and helpful, and I felt very safe and welcome as a solo traveller. The hotel has a great location, and it’s very close to Gloucester station. I hugely recommend.

author: Lauren A
title: Highly recommended hotel
text:
Excellent hotel
Excellent location
Excellent staff
I highly recommend it

author: Ian N
title: Great breakfast, convenient location
text: I stayed here in the summer for Hyper Japan at Olympia as the location is very convenient. The hotel is great, amazing breakfast with dairy free options like soya milk and coconut yoghurt. The staff are all very friendly, the room was comfortable and clean with a nespresso machine, hairdryer, mini fridge and toiletries like shampoo, body lotion etc. Nearby there is the museums and Kensington only a few mins walk away. Overall nothing bad to say, highly recommend for sightseeing London and also for events at the Olympia.

author: Marta E
title: Friendly staff but hotel needs a bit of nauntenance
text:
Friendly staff but the hotel seems to need a bit of maintenance
Our room fridge didn t work  and although the room was clean the carpet was stained
It took a long time running the tap to get hot water from the basin

We spent Sunday evening at the hotel and the Scoff and Banter was shut so we had to eat in the bar area

Staff were friendly and the food was OK

author: Olivia W
title: Pretty poor
text:
Poor - rooms are in need of a major renovation and deep clean. Photos on hotel website do not reflect reality and are likely 10 years old. Walls are paper thin so noise in next room (kids) carried a lot.
Good - comfy beds, aircon, location near tube.
Won’t be staying again!

author: Miguel F
title: Disappointing
text: Good location, comfy beds, good breakfast, bedroom was tired and a bit tatty. Reception team very friendly and helpful. One member of bar staff was very unhelpful and rude. Also booked a table for dinner to be told that on Sundays they sit you in the bar area which only has about 6 tables you could sit comfortably at to eat as the rest are sofas and low tables. If I had known this I would have eaten elsewhere.

author: Kyle I
title: Big old hotel in prime location.
text: Great location, walking distance to a lot of touristy places and services. Rooms were a little run down. Our room was "Japan small" but others in our group had bigger ones. It was big and historic. We were there on a Rick Steves' Tour. Staff tried hard, but didn't always succeed. Breakfast was just average. Airconditioning was barely adequate.

author: Morgan T
title: Really good experience in London
text: Really nice experience. I definitely repeat some stay with you.

author: Nathan O
title: Branded ….. poor experience
text:
Convenient location 
Pleasant atmosphere despite some older features
Helpful staff 
Poor, dated rooms, inappropriate even for a budget hotel

author: William J
title: Shocking! Cant believe this is a Radisson. Save your money and go to Premier Inn! Cleaner, more modern and better value!
text: .We paid to upgrade to a premium room. Upon arrival we went to our room which clearly was not a premium room. It was nothing like the photos on the website and it was also dirty. We immediately called reception who moved us to another room. This also was very different to the photos and looked exactly like a basic room apart from slippers and robes. We went to reception again because this room did not appear to be a premium room and was also dirty, although not as dirty as the first room. We spoke to a manager who didn’t appear to care. He took my husband to a third room which was identical to the room we already had. We said we would stay where we were. I am so upset and annoyed at the price we paid. I could have stayed at a Premier Inn for a fraction of the price but because this was a special occasion we paid more to stay here. I really wish I hadn’t. The hotel is very tired and in need of an update. It didn’t feel like a Radisson at all. In terms of our room, there were hairs in the bed and in the bath. The headboard was dusty. The furniture was dated, dirty, scuffed and damaged. The carpet was hacky, dirty and stained and had not been hoovered properly. I was very grateful for the slippers as I would not have wanted to walk barefoot around the room. Sadly, the staff did not appear to care or be bothered and didn’t really do anything to rectify the situation. Upon complaining to Radisson customer services, they emailed the hotel, copied me in and asked the hotel to email me to sort it. They have said they will refund the cost of the upgrade. Two weeks later and I’m yet to receive the refund. A dirty, run down hotel which does not seem to fit with the Radisson brand. Overpriced with staff who just did not appear to care. Wish we’d stayed elsewhere and wish I’d read some of the reviews first!

author: Benjamin A
title: Dirty rooms! And rundown
text:
Me and pregnant sister came away for 1 night to see a concert, before the baby comes. We had a stressful time coming down due to the hot weather and our trains was cancelled, but we eventually arrived on Saturday the 27th to South Kensington Radison blu. When we arrived at the hotel, all the staff was lovely and the inside and the outside of the hotel and reception was lovely and clean. So first impressions was really nice. 
I did ask before we checked in was it possible to get a upgrade and I will pay the extra as we really didn’t think about it in a double room and I didn’t want to knock my sister’s tummy being so close together in bed, They said if they could, they would try and give me a free upgrade. We left the bags and then arrived back at check-in time. We got our keys and went to the room and it was like a tiny dark little room with the smallest double bed. I went back to reception and the lady showed me another room and it was a little bit bigger so she went to get me the keys and unfortunately we was told we couldn’t have that room. I even asked, could we put a put up bed in there and they told us no, but they could give us a twin room as she said she was fully booked and there was no other rooms left. So we accepted the twin room. When we got in the room it was still very small, but it’s only until we sat down in the room and realised how dirty and stinky it was. We were so disappointed and angry because we’ve booked this hotel as we was going to Hyde Park and it wasn’t too far for my Sister to travel and especially in all this heat didn’t make it any better. Firstly, the Carpet we noticed and our shoes were sticking to the carpet and they were stained all over the chair to the desk was stained all over it.the desk had some sort of stuff on it I didn’t even know what it was thank God we had Dettol wipes in our handbag as we cleaned the room ourselves It was disgusting. On the front of the fridge door was all dirty and again some sort of drip marks all over it, everything looked like it really needed a good clean. It smelled old and musty. The headboard was all worn off like it had been their years. It didn’t even feel cleaning enough to put me on head up against it. There was also dried snot stuck to the walls, which was absolutely disgusting, and there was peoples names written on the walls, The bathroom the sink was cracked inside and on the outside with all Brown black muck that was in the crevice. Outside on the bath panel had all soap and drip marks all over it and inside the shower there was black hairs. You can see the photos attached, I have never experienced this in any Radisson hotel that I’ve stayed in and we have stayed in quite a few Manchester Leeds and Edinburgh being my favourite one on the Royal Mile, none of these hotels was as disgusting as this. It was on the first floor room nine, we were so appalled as I have worked in hospitality before in a very small hotel, but it was very clean. It just ruined our whole weekend thinking we’ve got to go back to that dirty Hotel, this was meant to be a lovely Sister‘s trip before my sister had the baby and it turned out a nightmare! Please see the photos attached, it would only let me add so many photos. This is not what you expect for a £300 night Away. Don’t be fooled by their own photos as it did not look like that at all, but I have to say we did have standard rooms but it was absolutely disgusting.

author: Jessica T
title: 3 star at best.. awful run down hotel
text: This is not a 4 star hotel whatsoever.  3 star at the very best. Rundown old wood furniture thats tired. Small rooms.poor decor.  No aircon just awful.  There are plenty else to go to for better..  avoid.

author: Louis X
title: Great all-round hotel with easy access to all the major London sites!
text: I have stayed at this hotel 5 times since 2018 for a mix of business and personal holiday trips and enjoyed every stay due to the welcoming hospitality and professionalism of the management and staff. During each stay the staff have been more than accomodating to address any questions or issues. The buffet breakfast is good but I have noticed over the many years that the selection of food has declined a little (compared to our very first stay in 2018!). Having a bar and restaurant within the hotel makes it practical with a good selection of beers and cocktails. The hotel's central London location and proximity to Glouchester Station Tube make it easy to get across to all areas of London due to several lines passing through it. There are plenty of cafes, restaurants, pubs and general shops near by. Easy walking distance to Hyde Park, Kensington Palace, Harrods, Museums. I recommend this hotel for business or for pleasure. Looking forward to my next stay in July!

author: Thomas O
title: Good hotel, worth it if you're paying less than GBP 140-ish per night per person.
text:
Amazing hotel with fantastic staff and an excellent location. The team were incredibly friendly, welcoming, and very flexible with things like early check-in, which made the start of my trip so much easier. The location is one of the hotel's biggest strengths. It's right next to Gloucester Road Tube station, making it incredibly convenient to get anywhere in London. There are also plenty of great food options within a few minutes' walk, along with both a Tesco Express and Sainsbury's nearby, so grabbing groceries or a quick meal was never an issue.

My only real criticism is the size of the room and bathroom. The room itself was very compact, which is fairly common in the most expensive boorugh in central London, but the bathroom felt exceptionally cramped and small. I'm only 5'6" and not wide at all, and even then my knees would touch the sink while sitting on the toilet. The shower was also extremely small. I could just about fit comfortably, but anyone noticeably taller or wider would probably struggle. The bed was comfortable, but the room was so tightly laid out that I found myself accidentally hitting my ankles on the surrounding cupboards during the night. That said, these were really the only downsides. Everything else was spotless, well maintained, and exactly what I was hoping for. If you value a great location, friendly staff, and easy access to transport over having a large room, I'd definitely recommend staying here.

author: Louis Q
title: Great hotel close to the centre.
text:
Had a great 2 night stay here in June. Stayed alone but free upgrade to a single. Good clean facilities. Great breakfast. Helpful staff. A bit of a vibe going on in the bar watching the World cup in the evening.
Would love to come again.

author: Tyler I
title: Tired decor; good location for V&A, Natural History Museum etc. Was a better hotel under Radisson Edwardian franchise
text: I preferred this hotel when it was the Radisson Edwardian some years ago. As Radisson Blu, the staff were pleasant and reasonably helpful, the deluxe room we had was clean with everything we required, though the decor, including the carpet, was murky in tone and the room itself, being situated at the back of the hotel, lacked natural light. The door of the room looked as though it had been kicked in several times too many- hence we felt the need to test its locking effectiveness! The bar area did not impress me at all, though the staff were fine, I did not like the atmosphere. There were frequently unpleasant odours around the hotel, which smelt like stale cooking fumes and blocked drains. I would not choose to stay at this hotel again.

author: Samuel N
title: Below standard for the area and price
text: Way below standard, especially for a premium price. You aren’t allowed to use the coffee machine in the dining room before 7 am. The bathroom in my room was almost too small to maneuver at all. I had to remove the towels I was not using to have space to hang up the towel I was. Insufficient room for my personal items in the bathroom, broken lamp, no well-lit chair for reading, etc. I recommend that travelers look elsewhere.

author: Adam A
title: Poor hotel
text: Rm 124. Next to kitchen extractors. Fire detector flashes. Not a good place to stay

author: Alexander E
title: Great Base for Exploring London at a Great Price
text: Was expecting a lot more basic for the price so was very happy with this find on secret escapes. Good value for money. Only stayed 1 night as it was just somewhere to sleep whilst we visited the Theatre but would have been happy to stay longer. Budget room had a decent sized bed and the room was a very good size. Facilities were a good standard - could tell it had just been refurbished. Located on the basement level but that didn't bother us (room perfectly nice) Air con was excellent and needed in the heatwave. Tube station was 3 min walk and very convenient to get around. Lots of restaurants/eateries in the area too. Hotel on a lovely street. Would definitely stay again next time we visit.

author: David F
title: My Go-To Hotel in South Kensington – Always a Wonderful Stay
text:
I have stayed at the Gainsborough Hotel many times while travelling to London for medical treatments at the hospital, and it has become my go-to hotel whenever I need to be in the area.

The staff are excellent — always incredibly welcoming, friendly and helpful. The rooms are consistently clean and comfortable, and the hotel offers excellent value for money, especially considering its central London location. It is also very conveniently situated near South Kensington Tube station, making it easy to get around.

After many stays, I genuinely don’t have anything negative to say. Every experience I have had at the Gainsborough has been positive, and knowing I have somewhere comfortable and welcoming to stay makes my trips to London for hospital treatment that little bit easier.

Thank you very much to everyone at the Gainsborough for everything you do and for always making me feel so welcome. I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend this hotel, and I will certainly continue to stay here whenever I am in London.

author: Ethan U
title: Great value hotel in lovely quiet area of London
text: Great value hotel booked via Secret Escapes, we had a standard double room and a single. Both rooms were very clean and well equipped with good air conditioning. Much better than expected, quiet area and friendly staff. Bathroom was small but had a great shower and luxury toiletries including body lotion :) fluffy white towels and quality bed linen. Would recommend and hope to stay again.

author: Mason R
title: Great location and value.
text:
Just spent two nights at the Gainsborough Hotel,  and booked our next London stay before we left with the helpful Sakura on reception. We booked this trip through Secret Escapes but I think it’s worth booking direct with the hotel.   This hotel is very good value for London and not grand but does not compromise on comfort. Given the heat in London at the moment I will firstly say the air conditioning was excellent.   Bottled water was also provided. The bed was comfortable, the room clean and well equipped, with a proper wardrobe and drawers, not a rail. The bathroom was small but the shower excellent, as were the  toiletries.   There were two hand towels provided, which meant I had a hair towel, a simple touch that makes life easier,
that is often skimped on.    The sister hotel over the road has a bar and serves breakfast, and gave us a small jug of fresh milk for tea when we asked. 

The location is excellent. The South Kensington museums are practically on the doorstep, South Kensington station is a few minutes walk away,  making access to the west end and south bank very quick and easy. 

Our next stay is booked and we are looking forward to returning. Thank you Sakura for your help today.

author: Emma T
title: Great value and location
text:
Very well positioned hotel for South Kensington tube and the museums. 
Lovely room with good aircon / tea making facilities and clean bathroom. 
Reception was very friendly and held our suitcase. 
Lovely full breakfast at the the exhibitionist hotel opposite. 
Very good value for money - highly recommend and would stay again.

author: Ella S
title: Good location at a fair price
text:
Very good location, close to the Underground and within sight of the Natural History Museum. Friendly and helpful staff at the reception. An ironing board could be borrowed for free and was brought to the room and picked up again. Two complimentary bottles of water were provided upon arrival. The room on the ground floor spared us the arduous climb up the stairs with two large suitcases. 
The breakfast at the hotel across the street was fine. The cocktails during Happy Hour were good and reasonably priced for London standards.

author: Wyatt N
title: Excellent location & very professional staff .
text:
Returned again to the Gainsborough Hotel and again very happy with our visit .
Very helpful professional staff .
Sparkling clean rooms and the location is excellent. 
Just a few minutes walk to the Natural History Museum ,V&A Gallery ,South Kensington Tube Station and many more attractions .
Really good food options in the neighbourhood .
Look forward to returning .
The hotel very clearly informs visitors that the elevator is not working .
Thanks to all for memorable stay .

author: Sophia L
title: Simply Sensational.
text:
My wife and I booked this incredible hotel through Secret Escapes. Perfectly located. A short walk from the  tube and museums. 15 minute walk to Royal Albert Hall and the Royal Parks. The same to Harrods, if you need a retail fix. 
The sister hotel just across the road, 'The Exhibitionist', is great for top quality breakfasts during your stay. Continental, but with sausages, bacon and scrambled eggs. All good quality, and as much as you need to set yourself up for the day. 
We've never seen such friendly, helpful and happy staff. The rooms are kept spotless, and cleaned every day. 
You're made aware that the lift is out of order at the moment on their website. So there are a few stairs to climb to get to your air conditioned room. There is always help available to get your cases up and down the Victorian staircase. However, 'The Exhibitionist' across the road does have a lift, just in case you may have mobility issues. Restaurants, bars, pubs, there's even a Tesco's a few minutes walk from the end of the road. Everything you need for your London break is literally at your fingertips. No matter how hard you look, it'll be impossible to find fault. OK...no lift, but a bit of exercise will help to digest the big breakfasts. Next time we get the 'London Bug' to see a show or whatever, we'll  be back. Check out both of these two, very posh, very nice, once Victorian townhouses before you check out anywhere else.

author: David U
title: Cool budget room
text:
We came up to see " les mis" at the Albert Hall, this hotel is 20 min walk away and only 10 from the natural history and science museums. 2 minutes from local shops, restaurants and pubs. 
We had a budget room in the basement it was spacious with a good size shower room and toilet.  The aircon was very effective and quiet ( left on all  night ) the room is quiet and the bed comfy . As with all my reviews I'm balancing my score with what we paid ,

author: Antoine O
title: Extremely good value
text:
I was very impressed with my short stay here. I asked for a quiet room, and got one. The staff were all really lovely. The room was spotless, the bed was comfortable, and the shower very good. And arriving into London in a heatwave, I was very pleased that the A/C was excellent! Bottled water and biscuits were also provided, and the location in South Kensington is brilliant.
Overall, I felt that for the price, this hotel offered exceptional value for money.
(The only downside is the lack of a lift - this did not affect me, but might not be ideal for some people).
I would definitely stay here again, thank you for a great stay.

author: Zachary X
title: Great Hotel & Location
text:
We booked the hotel, through Secret Escapes. It is in a very good location, minutes from the Royal Albert Hall, The Natural History Museum ( free, advisable to book your ticket on line) and South Kensington underground, seconds away. On arrival we were greeted by a pleasant lady on reception, who checked us in. 

Our room was on the ground floor, as I noted on the hotel website, the lift is not working. My husband has recently had a knee replacement surgery. 
The room was spotlessly clean, with air conditioning , tea, coffee, biscuits and bottled water. Shower gel, shampoo, handwash and body moisturiser are also supplied. 

In the Exhibitionist Hotel, ( Sister Hotel) across the road, Breakfast was served up until 10.30 a.m. with cooked breakfast and full continental, including smoked salmon, cheeses, hams and various pastries and breads. I also note that the items were being freshly replenished around 10.00 a.m. which is always a good sign. 

Tea & coffee ☕️ were served to the table, and all the staff, were very pleasant and accommodating. Nothing was too much trouble. 
They were very attentive. Well done to them all 😊

Cocktails are served in the Exhibitionist Hotel, ( sister hotel across the road) between 5.30 p.m and 9.00 p.m. 2 for 1, and I enjoyed a few pina colada, and tasted delicious and definitely full of spirit. Not watered down, like most of the cocktail offers, you see about. 

They also serve pizza and light snacks. 
I’ve read some reviews, I think it’s fair to say, this hotel, has recently been refurbished and is fairly priced for the area, of South Kensington. 

You only need to look at the cars or estate agents, to see, how expensive the area is. Location is in a very safe area, and we felt safe, walking back from the RAH, and restaurants at night. 

We look forward to returning later in the year. 
Well done to all the staff, in an ever demanding industry. 🤩

author: Zachary Y
title: Speechless
text:
The elevator has not been in operation for a long time and, according to the receptionist, needs to be completely renovated. Oh dear. I am 66 years old, slightly limited in mobility; however, I was assigned a room on the 4th floor!!! I was assigned a room on the 4th floor. Catastrophic. In response to my complaint, I was then given a room on the 1st floor, which no longer corresponded to the booked category. In response to my complaint, I was then given a room on the 1st floor, which did not match the booked category. Concessions on the price: None, since I already had the budget rate through Secret Escape (171 € per night). In the room, there was only a minimal small skylight. Cozy is something else entirely. Then you look around and are astonished that a self-proclaimed 4-star hotel has no safe and no refrigerator, but does have a hairdryer that weighs so much you could easily skip the gym.
At the reception, there are always nice friendly conversations among the staff, but never with a guest who is just leaving the hotel. One had the impression that everyone was very embarrassed about the limited options in the hotel.
For breakfast, you have to cross the street to the neighboring hotel, The Exhibitionist. This is then advertised as a 5-star experience. Well then: Self-confidence is also a form of existence. Compared to my best 5-star hotel breakfast in London (Shangri-La London), The Exhibitionist would be rated with 2 stars. There is clattering and banging when clearing the tables; supposedly my breakfast was "not included," leading to lengthy discussions, along with many other issues that push a proper breakfast experience far out of reach. But at least the coffee was hot. Bravo.
There is much more to report, but that would exceed the scope here. Conclusion: NEVER again.

author: Mason E
title: Poor
text:
Good location but that the best bit. 

Was given a room on the 4th floor. Lift is out of service (and they’ll tell you that the website states this. 

However, when I enquired about the details, they stated it’s been broken for months. No sign of getting it repaired. Beware. No porter services either, they have to come from another hotel.

8 flights of stairs with a heavy suitcase isn’t fun after a long day.

Together with a broken phone and countless customer service failures, I’d only recommend if you’re seeking pack backer adventures and have a good sense of humour.

author: Harry P
title: Good hotel in a brilliant location.
text:
Excellent location. Lovely room. Very good breakfast opposite. Friendly staff.
But no lift because its out of order and there are a lotbof stairs! 
Very good price and would goagain.

author: Juan E
title: Not recommended.
text: Room was very rundown and was next to the public toilet area which was awful with 1 cubicle and 2 urinals . Felt very claustrophobic as the tiny window opened to what looked like a large pole. Very noisy with people passing the door to use the bathroom. I Asked to move and was offered a slightly bigger room in the basement also with no window. I was offered a complimentary breakfast when I went to reception. The reception area was nice and the staff friendly. The location was the best part of it . Check where your room is before you arrive as also the lifts have been out of order for a long time .

author: Zachary R
title: Only book if you are not fussy!
text:
Room and bed very tiny.  My room was next to the downstairs toilet!
The shower does not fit even a tiny person, it is a shower designed for a barge boat.
Generally pretty poor apart from the location.

author: Pablo Z
title: Great value hotel.
text: Spent a night here after picking it up cheap on Secret Escapes. Hotel clean and tidy. Close to South Kensington tube. Bathroom good.

author: Nora Z
title: Very nice
text: First time at this hotel. Arrived early and were allowed to leave our luggage so we could go out and about. Smooth book in and our room was very comfortable. Breakfast was across at the sister hotel across the road, plentiful, warm food as well as Continental. Staff at both locations were very warm and friendly. Stayed for 2 nights. On the morning of our departure again left our luggage so we could visit the National History Museum at the end of the road. Ideal location for the tube to explore further and plenty of places to eat nearby. A good stay.

author: Gavin T
title: Absolute English Elegance & Five-Star Hospitality in the Heart of South Kensington! 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟
text:
I am still reminiscing about my wonderful stay at The Gainsborough! I spent a week here exactly a month ago, and it was truly one of my most memorable experiences in London.
From the moment I arrived, I was blown away by the hotel's generosity—they surprised me with a complimentary upgrade to a stunning Double Luxury Suite. The room was exquisite: a perfect blend of sophisticated decor, impeccable cleanliness, and that authentic, charming London atmosphere that makes South Kensington so special.
The location is unbeatable. Having world-class museums and cozy cafes just a few steps away while enjoying such peace and privacy inside the hotel is a rare find. A special mention must go to the staff; their professionalism and genuine warmth made me feel like a truly valued guest.
The Gainsborough has won my heart. If you are looking for a place where style, comfort, and sincere hospitality meet, this is it. I cannot wait to return! ✨🇬🇧

author: Lucas K
title: Good value.
text: Great location, good value hotel. Across the road from natural history museum. 10 min walk to Harrods. Nice area to stay in , quite at night. Rooms comfortable and clean. Breakfast is across the road on sister hotel. Plenty to eat and nice coffee. Staff all lovely in both hotels.

author: Oliver I
title: Great stay
text: Great location only a few minutes from Earls Court tube station, lots of pubs, places to eat, shops etc so everything you would need, we had room 8, lovely & clean, nice balcony, could do with a few upgrades here & there & we had no hot water in the morning but apart from that absolutely would stay again, guy who checked us in very friendly & helpful

author: Jessica P
title: Fire safety risk and very expensive for poor quality room
text: As with many of the other reviews this hotel was outrageously over priced for a Saturday night in July and in poor condition. We were on the 4th floor up very steep narrow stairs so completely inappropriate for anyone with lots of luggage and unfit; thankfully we weren’t.  There was no fire safety information in the rooms and it was abundantly clear we wouldn’t have stood a chance in a fire, nor know where to go other than down the main staircase.  Very unsafe.  My mattress was ancient with springs sticking through into my back and stains on it.  We checked them for signs of beds bugs given previous reviews, which thankfully did seem to be absent and the linen was clean.  The room was very hot and had old fashioned halogen lights which made it even hotter.  We were able to fully open windows after standing on chairs and had a fan, which helped.  No bedside tables or lamps and very poor room security with key lock boxes outside each room that could easily be broken into and door locks with no secondary locking mechanism.  I felt like I was in a hostel not a hotel room that cost us £250!  Should have been more like £50!  No safe for valuables . These are old buildings with the limitations that come with them which includes poor room to room insulation.  The new manager, who was helpful,  certainly has a job on his hands to upgrade this hotel which I understand was closed earlier in the year due to complaints.  I am surprised the authorities allowed it to be reopened on fire safety grounds alone.

author: David W
title: Terrible customer service - unable to make simple changes
text:
!! BEWARE !! if you book and want to add extra nights or make any changes their system can't cope with it so you might be stuck.

This company is the worst I have ever had the misfortune to dean with.

I originally booked a single room for one night but a few days later I wanted to change it to a double room for 4 nights. Booking.com were unable to make the change due to the hotel not enabling such changes so I contacted the hotel and they claimed they can't change a room or change dates on their system! I have never heard of a hotel that has a system that's unable to make basic changes like that.

They said I must pay for the 4 nights first then I can put in a request to cancel the 1 night. So that means I'm paying for 2 rooms on the first night....... Sounded suspicious to me..... I asked them to email me confirming that they would refund the single night once I paid for the 4 nights but they gave me all sorts of flannel about this and that and just kept trying to get me to pay for 4 nights without any guarantee of getting a refund for the first night.
I lost all trust in them - one person told me one thing and the next person had a different story..... Nobody would actually guarantee I would get a refund once I paid - I think they are untrustworthy.

It would have been the simplest thing in the world to change the room type and charge me for 3 extra nights like any other hotel would - but they said that was impossible to do on their system!!!

author: Charlotte E
title: TOP position for the rest FLOP
text:
PROS: Well served area and a hundred meters from the metro stop. Host (not always present) who tries to accommodate all needs.

FLOP: 4 floors on foot, with sloping and creaking staircase, dirty and smelly carpet. Stinky room with tiny bathroom, which loved smelling like sewage. You can hear the sounds of people going up and down, it looks like the ceiling could fall upstairs at any moment

The thing that bothers that it is not written anywhere that has no elevator, there are people who had to arrive even on the 5th floor with large suitcases.

When I return to London, I will choose this neighborhood but not this structure

author: Jack Q
title: Not a delightful stay, but a useful location.
text:
We frequently have short stays in London for concerts, and are aware that you either have to stay a long way from the centre or pay a lot of money to get decent accommodation. Accommodation in London is very expensive. For a one night stay we accept that we will pay £100 plus for very limited, scruffy, tired, and cramped accommodation. So it is important to have realistic expectations when booking accommodation in a popular central location well served with transport and a range of restaurants and eateries. There are plenty of negatives about the Amsterdam Hotel, but there are positives as well.
It is a good location - Earls Court station just around the corner, plenty of buses, and a varied choice of eateries. It is a quiet and attractive street. The men who are paid to sit in the lobby and greet guests are very friendly and helpful. The TV has a good range of channels. And the free WiFi is strong and stable. We paid less than £200 for three people for two nights over the Easter weekend.

Though we are used to tired and scruffy accommodation, the Amsterdam Hotel did surprise us by how run down and scruffy it is. There appears to be little effort in keeping the place smart. The tired stair carpet has clearly not been hoovered for days. There are broken doors, rubbish, and general clutter left in corners and alcoves. It's not a good look. And it wouldn't take much to make it look better. Fix the doors or put curtains over the alcoves. Hire staff to hoover the carpet every day.
We had a room on the fourth floor. The building has high floors, so in reality it is more like climbing six floors. To be fair, it is quite common for accommodation in London (same as in Paris) not to have lifts. But if you have trouble climbing stairs, be aware that it's a long haul to the top!
The room was very tired and basic, and has no view to speak of, as the window looks out onto the balustrade. So you see the concreate balustrade and some sky. Beds had little support, so not good for someone with a bad back. The table is insecure and unreliable to support a kettle with boiling water. Take care. The room is generally tired and scruffy, but not dirty or smelly or damp. The toilet and shower are usable, although the space is quite cramped. The switch for the extractor fan is on the right above the door and light switch.
There were no toiletries when we arrived, and only two cups in the room; but, on being told, the chap downstairs brought us up a third cup and a bottle of shower gel.

author: Pablo C
title: Several issues
text:
Before arriving I was phoned, WhatsApped and emailed by different people asking what time I would be arriving by. During the stay I was phoned in the evening by the hotel which I didn’t answer as I was out at a show. No message left for why they called. Since checking out I’ve had multiple messages asking to leave a review. Including  5 messages from the manager, apologising for a couple of things, asking me to leave a lovely review for their “struggling”hotel and that if I want to come to London again he has 5 more hotels he could offer me at prices I would never see online. This feels unprofessional and a bit weird and I’ve felt the need to block the number. I don’t normally leave reviews but feel I have little choice after being practically begged for one by the manager  

Great location for the tube, room was clean and check in was easy -  The hotel advertises rooms that have been refurbished and unfortunately we did not get one of these rooms. The room itself had two deck chairs?! The wall mounted tv was not mounted and instead leaning against the wall unplugged. After we arrived a man came to the door and offered to mount the tv but we politely declined as we weren’t going to use it and we were in the middle of getting ready to go out. The radiator crackled persistently and could not be turned off so the room was boiling. Luckily there was a fan so we had that on during the night, not only to block out the radiator noise but to keep the temperature bareable. The bathroom floor was damp and mouldy by the sink - probably because when you turn on the sink taps the water shoots over the side of the sink. There was no hand soap or shower amenities. Also no milk for coffee /tea and the first plug socket we tried for the kettle didn’t work so had to use another one which meant boiling the kettle on the floor. Some of these things probably could have been sorted but we weren’t too bothered by them as we were only staying for one night. Also there is no receptionist/reception so we’d have to call or WhatsApp staff - just feels like a more complicated process than having a receptionist that you could quickly grab amenities from. It also feels like by not having a receptionist they are very over bearing via text messages and phone calls. It was ok for one night but will not be back. We have previously stayed in the hotel next door to this one before and it was much more pleasant.

author: Charlotte B
title: Simply the best! (Pun intended!)
text:
By far the best hotel I’ve stayed at in London!!

Please note that the photo’s above are no longer accurate! The hotel has new owners and are undergoing MASSIVE renovations!! The listing on Booking.com is accurate and the pictures look exactly like the rooms!! 

The Amsterdam Hotel is nice and central - Earl’s Court Tube station is right around the corner making it the perfect London getaway hotel! Within 15 minutes you’re in the heart of London. 

It is a more simple / budget hotel, but London is expensive so that’s all the better. We had a room with a double bed (around 140x200), a Tv, ensuite bathroom, 2 chairs and of course some Coffee and Tea facilities - which not every budget hotel offers!! The pictures on Booking.com is exactly what you get, small and simple but SPOTLESS! It was so clean. It smelled clean as well. The bathroom was probably newly renovated, the tiles looked super new. The shower was nice and spacious and super hot - just how I like it! 

Probably the best thing about this hotel was the friendly and helpful staff, in particular Aziz. The man of the house. He welcomed us into the hotel, helped us with our luggage up the stairs (such a gentleman!). Told us about the hotel, the neighborhood and showed us how to use the lockbox for the keys and the doorcodes and how to use that. 
Every time we ran into him, he’d be all enthusiastic and ask about our day. What we did and if we needed anything. He was there for all the questions but also for some small talk. Upon checking out we had a lovely talk with him about our journey back but also about our stay at the hotel. He is kind and caring, he made us feel welcome and safe -  a huge hotel chain like Hilton will not make you feel that way. 

There is no elevator (as far as we know) and no breakfast service - but that did not bother us at all.  We are not big breakfast people anyways! A quick meal from the M&S down the road was fine! 

Would recommend this place! I can’t wait to stay here again🫶🏻

author: Sophia E
title: Great hotel –
text: Great hotel. Very nice staff. The rooms are being renovated but completely unaffected. Rooms were now fine and a top bed. Bathroom was clean and if you needed anything you just had to ask and it was taken to your room.

author: Alice S
title: very nice stay
text: Had a great stay with friends! Staff were very helpful and checking in and out was made very easy. The hotel is walking distance from shops and lots of places to get food and the shower was great :) there are quite a lot of stairs so i wouldn’t recommend to someone who has trouble walking but other than that it was great.

author: Lauren T
title: Horrible experience
text: Run away from this horrible place. One towel for 5 nights. On line for over hour for the call number. Forget about security.

author: Samuel W
title: Horrible worst hotel for life!
text: It's a tourist catch, don't trust the pictures, it's old and dilapidated besides being extremely dirty. There is no air conditioning. We had booked and paid in advance for 10 nights, there was no question of staying there, they would not know anything about refunding us, but we still preferred to pay another hotel rather than stay in this hovel!

author: Benjamin R
title: It needs total reform.
text: Well connected hotel, metro and buses, but have no service does not have elevator breakfast etc., old rooms, very old bed and uncomfortable room with old carpet with rare smell. It is not recommended, it needs total reform.

author: William E
title: This hotel has bed bugs and is a fire hazard
text:
Horrific. Bed bug infested.

Please - for your own safety, don't stay here. 

We booked through Hotels.com, which clearly doesn't vet the hotels. When we arrived, we were taken into the basement to a room that stank of rotten, wet carpet. We soon learned why - the carpet was mysteriously wet for no reason. Later, we noticed the door looked like someone had smashed it open, no locks on any doors intact, including the bathroom. 

We noticed bed bugs on the floor, which we killed. Woke up with bites. There is NO ONE on the 'desk' to help or who will pick up the phone. Stains on every surface, including the bed, which is mainly just springs. We were in pain the following day from the bed.

Also, as we left, we noticed rubbish piled up outside the fire escape so would have died if anything happened. Then, as we left, a giant dead cockroach on the reception floor. Not to mention, a homeless person strung out on drugs is asleep on the couch there,e too. She got up when we did and left. 

No one to talk to about any of it nor is Hotels.com taking any responsibility. Walk away and pay extra for somewhere else immediately. This hotel is DANGEROUS and should be reported for hygiene and also safety.
