author: Oscar K
title: Good value for money
text:
Very clean, impeccable service and welcome.
Very well located.

author: Hannah O
title: Nice place and good location
text: The room was rather small, but we were only there to sleep (2 adults and 3 children). It was also very hot, but it was 30degrees outside and its an old building. They did provide a fan, breakfast was ok and the staff were friendly and helpful. We dropped our bags early and picked them up late. Also good location for tube access

author: Caleb L
title: Good choice near Paddington
text: Very convenient hotel 3 minutes from Paddington station. Stayed in a room for 5 people. Everything according to expectations. Breakfast just a little repetitive in its offering, but more than sufficient. Rooms with a fan, it was needed in August. No elevator available.

author: Miguel D
title: Shakespeare Hotel Paddington London
text: Great location for access to rail and tubes.   Room was a little small but it did have air conditioning and we felt it was value for money.  Vibrant area with plenty of restaurants/cafes. Staff were welcoming.

author: Caleb Z
title: Well located but expensive for the services offered
text: Very small room. No air conditioning but a fan. Minimalist welcome. Minimal breakfast....special mention for the waffles cooked as needed. But above all a nauseating smell of sewage in the room on the 3rd floor...nothing done or offered despite our report. Very good location in immediate proximity to Paddington station.

author: Freya I
title: More like a cheep hostel
text:
The rooms are very cramped. I stayed there two times over a week. The first time I was put in a  very small room on the top floor. Almost impossible to get up the tiny staircase with my suitcase. Before I made my way up there, I explained that I have a bad hip and stairs therefore are very difficult for me, but there was no help to get. The room was very small and the shower had very poor water pressure. I could not wash the shampoo out of my hair. 
The second time I got a room on the ground floor after asking for it in advance, with a little bit more room for movement and a shower with water pressure. So I recommend getting a double room and not a single, if deciding to stay there. 
The breakfast is very bland and not with much variety nor taste. 
The hotel is somewhat clean. Not clean like I would expect a hotel to be, but not dirty enough for me to use sanitiser every time I touched something. And I am not one who is too fussy about things like this. But it was not the standard of a hotel if I’m being honest. 
As it is London the noice level is quite high. But the hotel’s doors are heavy, so you can hear every time someone goes in or out and the walls are thin, so you can hear everything if your neighbours are speaking just a bit over average. 
So overall for it being London and the price it was acceptable, but it was more like the standard of a cheep hostel than a hotel’s. 
The location and the price is the only reason I am giving it two stars and not one.

author: Mathis Z
title: Enjoyable stay.
text: Handy for the station. Friendly and helpful staff. Room clean, nice fruit basket.

author: Zachary L
title: Terrible
text: Excellent location for getting around by public transport to visit the city. Otherwise, I consider the hotel stay below my expectations; it has no elevator, and getting to the second floor for seventy-year-olds becomes a problem. It would have been enough to take the guests' age into account during room assignment. The room is very small with a sloping full-size bed, the floor is sticky and in poor condition, the wardrobe door does not close well when the drawer is open, the bathroom door does not close, the shelf under the mirror is not stable, and the sink is very small. The staff is almost absent and unfriendly. I would certainly not recommend staying at this hotel to friends and relatives.

author: Evan X
title: Paddington Station
text: Located a few minutes walk from Paddington Station & tube so an ideal base. The building is huge and  nicely decorated.  Lots of stairs though as I was on 3rd floor. Single room was clean and comfortable with tea tray, and very narrow but comfy Single bed.  The bathroom was 4th floor, clean but wet floor from shower as there's no shower mat & the shower door is right next to the toilet so bit awkward to use. Needs a hand towel for the sink too. Great breakfast included in cost,  plenty of choices but the scrambled eggs & beans weren't very hot. I would stay here again if I got a good early booking deal again.

author: Zoe U
title: Worth seeing
text: The decor is very quaint. The food portions are kept very small.

author: Paolo E
title: Reyskie dublin
text: Not bad nice near an convenient to shop and train station.🇮🇪🇵🇭🫶

author: Ryan L
title: Beautiful stay
text: Very friendly environment, excellent staff, excellent location, decent breakfast. I would definitely prefer it again and would recommend it to others.

author: Rosie P
title: Thanks to the staff at The Bloomsbury Thistle
text: Great place to stay, central and very easy to get to subway. Staff at front desk Genevieve very helpful with directions and ensuring we were comfortable whilst Liudmyla was always smiling and cheerful  at breakfast. Thanks for a lovely stay.

author: Joseph L
title: Stay in London
text: I booked a double room. The room is not very big but well-structured with the bare essentials. It doesn't have air conditioning but a fan that would be sufficient if the windows could be opened more than 20 cm in height (in fact, one of the windows wouldn't stay open and you had to put something to hold it up). The breakfast is excellent and varied for both sweet and savory. Overall it was a pleasant stay.

author: Mia G
title: Excellent stay
text: Located close to amenities and the tube, staff were always happy and cheerful, breakfast lovely and room spotless

author: Jack P
title: Great stay
text: Location excellent. Easy to get to places we wanted to see. The hotel was peaceful and calm. The rooms were clean and met all of our needs. It was a great price as we got hotel and train fares together. Genevieve needs a special mention. She was helpful, friendly always smiling and easy to talk to.  Thank you for a lovely stay. Would definitely return x

author: Luke M
title: Great location for Euston and west end
text: Had a good stay at Thistle Bloomsbury for a theatre break in London. Overall was very good and would return. 10 mins walk from Euston station and 10 mins to Dominion theatre. Bloomsbury is a lovely area and the hotel in the centre of it. I was glad I upgraded to a deluxe room which had air con and much nicer. Breakfast was spot on.

author: Chloe J
title: Stayed for The Weeknd Concert
text:
Was worried due to other review but our room 603 was beautiful. Air con included although would be good to be able to adjust yourself as it wasn’t quite cold enough for our Scottish bodies 😆
Bathroom beautiful, well ventilated. Towels clean and fluffy. Beds very comfortable and double bed was more a king size. 
Nespresso machine a bonus, as was complimentary water.

author: Lily G
title: Great location share about the room
text: Great location near Covent Garden and convenient for Euston Station. Comfy bed but room very small even for London standards. Room needed to be repainted

author: Ana O
title: Great location and stay  - helpful staff
text: The welcome and check-in was so easy and the staff recommended lots to see and do. Great oomphy beds and cleanliness 100%

author: Sofia F
title: From Jeanette King, and Margaret Kemp
text: The location was perfect. Everything we needed was so close. Even the Hop-on Hop-off Bus stopped right at the door.

author: Marco J
title: Nice friendly hotel
text: A bit worries by reviews but hotel nice and friendly.  Stayedin Basic rooms whcih were clean and tidy good tv clean towels.  Lovely breakfast!

author: Carlos K
title: Overnight Stay
text: Well I clearly should have read the reviews before booking at this hotel, it certainly was not worth paying £194.25 for 2 for one night! And be warned room 701 is extremely small and very hot, I think I was scammed by the hotel. Considering I booked this reservation in April of this year, I was shocked that we were staying at the top of the hotel in a pokey room with absolutely no character,  it was dated, worn and old, I feel you owe me a refund! Absolutely Shocking

author: Evie Q
title: Reasonable and Functional Hotel
text: First of all this is not a 4 star hotel but we found the experience excellent for our needs and it was very reasonable for a couple which included breakfast. (I did have a Blue Light Card which helped). Check in was quick and easy. The room was clean and the bathroom made the most of the small space with a good shower and lotions included. There was a kettle with tea and coffee and the TV worked! No air conditioning but there was a fan and you could ask for another if you wanted. It was quiet and breakfast was more than adequate (buffet style, not cooked to order and no porridge). The hotel was an excellent location for transport links and there were plenty of restaurants and shops nearby. Recommend the 'Shell Restaurant' next door.

author: Matthew A
title: Bloomsbury Park Hotel
text:
Great stay at the Bloomsbury Park Hotel (Thistle)
25% off and free delicious breakfast with my Blue Light Card.
Great value for money in the heart of Bloomsbury.
Rooms are clean fairly spacious, Tea Coffe in room. No air con but even on a very hot day we had windows open in room and big bathroom and a breeze flowed thru. Quiet fan did the job. Room cleaned every day. Free breakfast was delicious hot and plentiful. Dining room staf bright and cheery. In fact all staff were a pleasure to meet. Situated on the Southampton Row it is surrounded by restaurants. Busy bar in Cosmo lane  The Swan, our room overlooked it, noisy till 11.00 ish then quiet, not a problem in fact it added to our enjoyment as it felt like a bit of a party going on most days.
Great selection of restaurants around including a new concept restaurant first Swiss Butter!
I score The Bloomsbury Park a 9 out of  ten. If it had  a wee fridge in the room it would be a ten. Will def return. Loved it. Not a fancy Ritz, but clean, friendly and located in a lovely borough.

author: Paige G
title: avoid if you can
text:
staff very unfriendly  and rude - no air co - small rooms and tiny shower with nearly no water - no service - 
good point : huge bed very comfy
very expensive for what it offers

author: Lily I
title: Exactly what was promised - no more, no less.
text:
We spent 5 nights at this hotel. The location is perfect, in the center of London, close to everthing. And we got exactly what was advertised: a double room, no AC but we did get a fan, en-suite bathroom, and a fairly good breakfast (but, as usual, with no fresh vegetables). 
However, the room was VERY small. The shower head was just an inch above my head, and I'm not particularly tall. It was HOT in London, and yes, I knew there was no AC, but the window would not open more than a crack, and when I asked, I was told that that was for safety reasons. The hallway outside my room, which had more windows open, was MUCH cooler that our room! They did give me a second fan, but that led to the next problem: since the building is old, the rooms have very few electric outlets, and they are almost all near the desk. So no outlets by the beds, and it was either the fan or the television, and the second fan had to be placed on the desk. In general, the hotel seems old, the carpets are worn, the lift is small and slow. So yes, they provided what they promised, but just that and no more. At 200 GBP a night, I would have expected a bit more.
And one more thing. In the room, they have the usual card asking guests to skip housekeeping "for the environment". In fact, they offer a 7 GBP voucher for each day that we do so. However, the vouchers can be used ONLY in the hotel's not very well stocked snack bar (or towards breakfast, if not paid for in advance), and ONLY exactly 7 GBP at once. In other words, if you buy something that costs 4, you lose the entire 7!

author: Lauren I
title: Smallest Double bed/room in the world, No Air Con,
text:
Stayed here weekend of 17th July 2026.  Check in is 3pm.  We arrived at 2:45pm to find a small queue (about 4 people) waiting to check in.  We took our turn to be told "Your room isn't ready until 3pm".  How amazing then at dead on 3pm all our rooms became ready! 

The hotel doors are closed at 7pm at night so you must have your key.

Our Cat will be glad we didn't bring him because we could not have swung him around in the smallest double room on the planet.  Never seen a Double bed as small either.  

At the time of writing we are in the middle of a heatwave in England and this hotel does not have aircon.  Just a table fan!

There's no bar in this hotel.

We saw another 10 hotels in this area at similar prices and being honest I wish we would have picked one of them. 

Can't fault the staff themselves who were all polite and helpful.

author: Freya Q
title: Lack of power outlet and fridge,
text: The location is brilliant but sadly for us, we found it disappointing that there was only one power point in the room, nil in bathroom either with no air conditioning or fridge,  unable to but any food or have cold beverages due to not having fridge.we had to turn of small portable fan to charge our iPads other devices, when questioned about the air conditioning or whether they could supply a power board to keep the fan on while also charging our devices, the lack of customer services at the front desk was appalling. We paid good money for this hotel, certainly will not be staying here again.

author: Oliver M
title: Great stay
text: Stayed here as I know the area. The room didn't have air con but a fan was provided and was much needed a very hot couple of nights.

author: Evan P
title: Wonderful staff and great location
text: The staff were so welcoming and helpful. Always a smile and offer of help if needed. The location in Bloomsbury was perfect and meant we were in walking distance of everything but also had some lovely parks to visit for some peace in the city.

author: Lily W
title: Worst hotel experience ever
text:
I can honestly say with absolute confidence this is the worst place my sister and I have ever stayed at… so bad we checked out early.
My sister booked this hotel on booking.com months ago for 4th - 6th July. After booking for a few weeks our plans changed and we no longer intended to check in on 4th but called twice to ensure this would be ok. We didn’t want a refund for the night as we needed to be in London early on the 5th to get ready for an event and normal check in is a 3pm which wouldn’t be an issue for us as we had paid from 4th!…WRONG!!. My sister and I arrived at the hotel at around 8-8:30am and we’ were immediately told we were too early to check in. The lady behind the counter was rude abrupt and gave off a strong can’t be bothered attitude. There was nothing welcoming about this experience. We explained that actually we were supposed to check in yesterday which she just wasn’t understanding (hadn’t even asked our name yet for the reservation) when she did eventually ask she said she could see a note saying that we wouldn’t be checking in until 4th. She then immediately asked for payment (we had already paid in full) she then said she needed to get the manager with no explanation (this wasn’t about the payment issue and funnily enough wasn’t brought back up). The manager, a man came out and while the lady was trying to explain whatever she seen wrong on the screen he held his hand up to her face to indicate for her to shut her up! Now as much as I didn’t find the lady particularly helpful in anyway shape or form his manner was absolutely appalling there’s no circumstances he should be treating another colleague like this especially a women and in front of guests! What is he like when he's in private?
He then told my sister and I that we cannot check in as the room wasn’t ready for us as housekeeping hasn’t started the room yet or hasn’t arrived for work yet (this wasn’t clear). We couldn’t believe what we were hearing as again we had the room booked since yesterday. When we questioned him on it he said there was a bad leak durning the night now I’m going to stop right here and say this was a load of lies. There was no indication whatsoever of a leak especially as on as drastic as he was describing saying people were moved to another hotel etc. he then said the room will be ready at 3 and well I’ll be honest we did start to get a little frustrated as we had said well what if we did show up yesterday? The room is supposed to have been ready since 3pm the day before. He then said he would have the room ready working the next hour and then later on said next hour and a half. It’s pretty obvious the room was sold and if he had just been honest it would have made the situation a little better. As compensation for this he offered complimentary breakfast for our stay which we refused several times as we had other arrangements but he kept going on and on about this free breakfast.
Once we did get to check in the room fell nothing short of disappointing. From the minute you get out the lift it’s clear the whole hotel is in dire need of a revamp the hallway are badly painted and dull. The room itself was tiny with no room for someone to sit at the desk and get into their side of the bed. The room was also very grubby and dusty which lead to a pest problem later in the night we seen several spiders which we are both terrified of! 1 is fine but to have seen 3 is a bit concerning. The bathroom was a narrow room with the smallest shower you have ever seen. There was no way to wash without getting your hair wet and if you are a larger person forget about taking a shower. This hotel also doesn’t have any sort of air conditioning in the rooms which is stated but there was a fan in the room which was not a suitable substitute for 30 degree weather it was so hot and stuffy even with the window open we couldn’t sleep.
We both checked out yesterday before 9am. I don’t normally write reviews but this hotel needs 1) employee training, 2) a deep clean 3) a revamp

In the morning as I was awake anyway I went down for breakfast as it was free and I wouldn’t have time to grab something before my train outside the hotel. Breakfast is supposed to start at 7am I was down for around 7:15am and it was still being set up I was told this was due to a party last night (there was definitely no party last night) myself and my sister came back from our event around 12am and the breakfast room was closed and in darkness the lobby was also empty so again another lie. The breakfast options were slim but you could find something to eat they have sausage, bacon scrambled eggs, beans and a choice of cereal and fruit. The beans were cold and the sausage was bland overall not the worst hotel breakfast I’ve had but by far the best.

author: Charlie B
title: Good location very poor conditions and dirty
text: Horrible!!! The only cute thing is the street facade (all the entrances to these hotels are the same) no air conditioning, a fan that is useless, from the balcony you can enter the adjacent room if the window is open (so it could be dangerous) the mattresses are horribly old, the springs hurt, the carpet is super dirty and old, the shower is smaller than in a cruise ship cabin, about 50 cm on each side, the bedding looks old and don't even get me started on the terribly old pillows, the hotel in general looks old and dirty everywhere, plus expensive for what it is. Good location because you can walk from the Victoria metro terminal.

author: Freya O
title: Seriously avoid- ignorant and dismissive to guests
text: The location is the only good thing. About 2 hours after we checked in a stream of water poured into our room’s from the top of the window. We checked it had been fully closed when this happened, then went to report it to the front desk. The staff member they sent down with us to check it repeatedly dismissed us saying it wasn’t inside, while mopping the puddle up from the window sill- something my partner tried to explain multiple times but was just ignored and dismissed every time. Considering that treatment, the fact you have to hand in your own room key any time you want to go outside and the clear uncleanliness and lack of security of the place, we quickly booked a different hotel and left. Since then our complaint has been completely ignored- clearly a trend considering their lack of responses to complaints on Booking.com

author: Chloe E
title: Frustrating Disgust and feeling of being ripped off
text: Hotel is  a tacky tourist trap  it’s outdated carpet is shabby paint peeling off the wall in the room, bed is uncomfortable mattress is non existent couch in the reception area  look like it’s skip find  it’s battered. Staff is telling you to leave your key when ever you are going out the hotel , when we query the reason we were told that no one would trouble our things  we may loose the key and would have to pay between £5 to £10 we told them we would rather pay if we loose the key than leave it. We paid £120 to spend a night in a dump. A seedy lodging, dilapidated Inn. Don’t waste your money do not book this hotel if l could give it a 0* l would is not a 2*  as a matter of fact it’s no * at all.

author: Poppy P
title: You get what you pay for….
text: Staff very friendly and helpful. Property was  in a fabulous location. However, our room and bathroom were pretty dire…you get what you pay for! One night was ok, but that was enough! And breakfast…free or not was awful…

author: Lauren L
title: If you know them you avoid them. A nightmare.
text:
I swear if I could put zero stars on this "place," because it doesn't deserve to be called a hotel, I would put them on. Upon our arrival it seemed to me to have entered a nightmare, the room was in a basement, the stairs to go down were all covered with plastic, until you get to room n. 25 in which we were placed: the floor at our entrance was dirty, full of dust and hair (something reported and for which no solution was found), the walls of the room peeled and with moisture seepage, the bathroom sink is smaller than a goldfish tank, the shower dirty and malfunctioning (hot water practically absent). We refused to try breakfast the next morning because the hygiene and health regulations of this place are non-existent! Really sucks, having spent about 120 euros for such a room
STAY AWAY IF YOU CAN from this place.

author: Katie M
title: Very basic, and a very poor breakfast...
text: Nice hotel, though very basic. Don't pay extra for the breakfast, it's just fried/boiled eggs, beans, and a chicken sausage, not even bacon/tomatoes or hash browns. Would choose elsewhere in future.

author: Michael B
title: A few days in London
text:
The hotel is very old and also quite neglected, as there are various objects, wardrobes and mattresses around the corridors where there is carpet not particularly clean and fragrant. The room was very small but enough to sleep. The bathroom was clean. Every day they changed towels and stocked shampoos and soaps. As for breakfast there was not much choice, we had toast with jam and butter, milk, coffee, cereal, juices and tea. They also ask and prepare eggs, sausage and beans which are very good for the classic English breakfast.
However, the hotel is close to Victoria Station from which in 15/20 min walk you can reach central London

author: Marta F
title: Pleasantly suprised
text:
I booked this hotel as it was a lot cheaper than any other and very good location for theatre I was going to with my teenage kids.
In the run up to Christmas I didn't get time to check reviews until we were on our way there. I was a bit freaked out at some of them particularly mention of bed bugs. However my experience, for the price of the hotel was completely positive.
Check in was easy and the guy very friendly. The room had been recently refurbished and while not to the highest standard was clean and quite practical. We were in room 20 a triple room on the first floor. We all had a bedside light. The bathroom was new, mold free and could only be improved by a shelf for toothbrush etc as the sink was quite small. 
One thing I wasn't keen on was you had to leave your key at reception when you went out. I felt uncomfortable with this, particularly as there wasn't anyone there when I went to leave my key to go for dinner. The outside door is locked and noone can enter without being buzzed but I would have still preferred to have my key with me when I went out.
After reading the reviews I did a thorough check for bed bugs and found no signs. The linen and towel were clean, the mattress new, although a bit cheap and I had a good nights sleep.
I was very impressed with the breakfast. The plates and cutlery very clean. There was a table where you could help yourself to tea, coffee, juice and ceral. Big plates of toast came out and there were packets of jam on the table. I only had eggs but you could have vegan sauage and beans as well. You can see into the kitchen and I noted this was very clean. The staff very friendly and helpful. The dinning room was full so the hotel is obviously being well used. I have stayed at many 4 star hotels and paid for breakfast that were not as good as this one and it was free. The wall paper was pealing but the tablecloth new and clean so it seems like the right way of doing things.
I don't leave a lot of reviews but I felt some up to date information about this hotel is needed. To me it seems like they are working hard to refurbish and get this into a nice cheap hotel in a prime location. They still have work to do and the entrance and landing carpet hasn't been decorated yet but I am glad they are starting with the bedrooms and not the reception rooms. If you want somewhere in a great location at a great price and you aren't too fussed about decor but you still want it clean, I would recommend Stanley House Hotel.

title: BED BUGS DO NOT STAY
text: DO NOT STAY - found bed bugs after only being in the room less than 30 minutes. Was offered to change rooms but found tiny blood spots on the beds sheets in the second room as well but we didn’t check very well as we were not staying there.

author: Mason Q
title: Quality/Price the ideal accommodation
text:
Great place to visit London
Hotel located in an ideal place to move back and forth
5 minutes from Victoria Station, 12 minutes walk from Buckingham Palace 
The staff is super nice, the service is exquisite 
Recommended 100x100%

author: Marco Z
title: Never again.
text:
We stayed at the two-star Stanley House Hotel on Belgrave Road in London. Sorry, but it gets a star. 
The location is perfect and very central, the coffee is good and wi-fi works most of the time. There is cleaned bed and laid clean towels every day. Staff are nice and welcoming. But that was it. 
The hotel is completely worn out, the TV can be turned on, but the picture is so blurred that you do not know what you see. The bathroom is the size of a kitchen cabinet, there is a 30-cm step up the room, smells of sewage and the door can neither be closed nor locked. The “double bed” is max 140 cm wide and so miserable to lie in that the floor would have been better if there had been room. The photos on the website must have been taken many years ago. 
All in all a disappointing experience, but we still had a grip over our heads. From harm you become smart, but rarely rich - next time we read TripAdvisor before we book and choose a hotel with a minimum of three stars.

author: Giulia S
title: Pretty grim, stay elsewhere... probably needs condemning...
text:
Stayed here for 1 night out of convenience as I was working nearby - I knew it wouldn't be 'great' but prices for the area are high and we just needed a bed.

It was so far from 'great', in fact it's pretty grim.. so run down and uncared for and unsure why it hasn't been condemned. I would be embarrassed to present this as an offering to tourists / guests. Peeling wallpaper, ratty carpets, mouldy bathrooms. Based on the whole condition of the building we avoided breakfast for our safety.

I don't like leaving bad reviews but this 'hotel' warrants one. I have only given it two stars as the bed linen smelled clean, a blessing in the circumstances.

Do yourself a favour and pay a bit extra for a better place to rest your head. And if you run this hotel, sort it out or shut it down - this should not be what tourists experience in London. Hopefully EHO will come knocking soon.
