text: I was truly awestruck by the service given by keerthi. Beds are super comfy I thank each and everyone who made my stay truly awesome. Very convenient for all the tube and train stations

author: Ella U
title: Pleasant stay
text: Very nice worth staying  Keerthi and yasir are very professional with friendly nature. Rooms are comfy and comfortable close to all stations. Receptionists guided through out our stay

author: Erin D
title: Insufficient room
text: Rooms not equipped with air conditioning, no minibar, the bathroom sink faucet was very inconvenient, and water would spill out onto the floor. Very small room for 2 people, even if it was clean. The common areas like the restaurant and lobby were equipped with air conditioning, so that was okay; breakfast was good and plentiful.

author: Michael G
title: Great stay and service by keerthi
text: Very good hotel. The breakfast is fantastic. Very clean. I thank Keerthi for her service

author: Gavin I
title: keerthi is nice
text: i had a great stay at this hotel. everyone is super nice this is my 2nd visit to this hotel. they've upgraded a lot.  special mention to keerthi. she is super nice . she is the best of all.  absouletly service from her.

author: Claire Y
title: A Wonderful Staff Member at Tavistock Hotel *EYERUSALEM*
text:
I would like to give a special mention to **Eyerusalem**, who works as a Food & Beverage Assistant at Tavistock Hotel.

Every morning when she saw me, she would greet me with a warm “hello” and a big, genuine smile. She is such a polite, respectful, and well-mannered lady, and her kindness really made my mornings more enjoyable.

I particularly loved sitting outside for breakfast, and Eyerusalem was always happy to assist me with anything I needed. Her friendly attitude, professionalism, and genuine care for guests did not go unnoticed.

**Tavistock Hotel is very lucky to have someone like Eyerusalem on their team.** She is a wonderful representative of the hotel, and I truly appreciated her kindness and excellent service. Thank you, Eyerusalem, for making my breakfasts so pleasant

author: Lauren L
title: A confy experience with a pleasing welcome
text:
The hotel's very-well located in a not so busy street in Russel Square; near the most important monuments in London you can take a stroll to anywhere you want in a few minutes!
A really chic atmosphere and accomodation with greatly distribuited seats and umbrellas in the entrance of the hotel in case you want to relax.
It's rooms are medium-sized and nicely decorated with simple but essencial furniture offering a confortable experience, although i want to mention the lack of air conditioner in the uppered level rooms. It was quite hot in here!
Cleanning is a must in this hotel, its always flawless! Every time you leave your room and come back, it gets tidy in an instant.
The room is pretty quiet with the noise cancellation level which is perfect for a little nap ;)
The service is for me the best part, with kind employes and essential needs such as a toothpaste offered in the reception for free if you forget it.
And to top it all of, the value is reasonably cheap for a place with such a beauty.
Really recommend!!! :]

author: Isabella T
title: Fantastic Stay.
text: Stayed for 4 nights.Fantastic break.amazing staff who got to know to bring our tea for 4 on to the terrace in the afternoon.loved the tiffin box at lunchtime.Seabass was cooked to perfection.Amazing breakfast.Each and every member of staff were very friendly helpful and very pleasant.This is our 3rd visit and cant wait to return.lovely room with big window and comfy bed.

author: Freya X
title: Great service by Keerthi
text: We come to this hotel very often. Very convinent for all. Staff are super Nice with everyone. We had a fantastic stay. Big shot out to Keerthi at reception. She made our stay beautiful.

author: Lucia D
title: Excellent in every way.
text: Stayed for Five Nights in this excellent Hotel, upon arrival we were told we had been upgraded from a park view double to a Park view Kingsize, the Room was clean, well equipped with an extremely comfortable bed, ear plugs were provided because of Traffic noise at night, but we never need them, location of the Tavistock could not be better for visiting most of the major sites, but it's the Staff that make this place, everyone for Reception to Bar staff to the cleaning staff were helpful, friendly and go above and beyond to provided their Guests with the perfect stay. We will definitely be back, and if looking for your perfect stay in London, then come here, you won't be disappointed.

author: Chloe D
title: Keerthi is very kind at reception
text: Excellent receptionist Keerthi. Kind and warm and very helpful.

author: Samuel O
title: keerthi is super nice at reception
text: The hotel was really clean and iloved rhe stay here. keerthi did a great job very kind nd helpful

author: Harper F
title: Missed opportunity.
text:
We stayed on the first floor and had noise pollution from the bowling which is located in the basement of the hotel. The noise was unbearable until midnight.
The staff, the room, the bar certainly met our needs but we were unlucky with the room on the 1st floor.

author: Pierre Z
title: Good stay
text: Very nice girls on the reception😍special mention to Keerthi.

author: Miguel P
title: Warm
text: Bon accueil et bon standing. Keerthi helped us through our checkin and checkout. She is a great staff in this hôtel.

author: Evie T
title: Warm welcome
text: Very good stay. Welcome is sooo warm. Plenty of breakfast options. Keerthi at reception is thé best of all. A big shout to keerthi. We'll come back again.

author: Zoe X
title: Great little hotel
text:
Fabulous little hotel - highly recommend! Stayed here for one night in between returning from Disney and travelling home.

Polite staff, clean room, greet location and price.

author: Leo S
title: Really love this hotel
text: I loved my stay here I even made a video about it too . Staff were very friendly room was small but cozy and super comfortable bed . Glad it had Netflix on the tv too and water refill in the hallway . Super affordable and would definitely stay here again when I’m in London

author: Henry M
title: Good stay
text: Very quick and easy check in. Staff really friendly. Rooms clean and well equipped but a little on the small side.

author: Alice S
title: Excellent choice for an overnight stay
text: I was seriously impressed. Whilst small, the room was well furnished, the whole hotel looked in great condition, comfortable bed and excellent air conditioning. Perfect for an overnight stay, and likely to become my new first choice in the area. I didn't actually believe all the positive reviews I'd read given how well priced it was but they were fully merited.

author: Megan X
title: Overnight stay
text: Spotlessly clean! The bathroom is beautiful. Room is snug but has everything you need. Great location between three tube stops. Staff are very friendly and helpful. Would stay again.

author: George C
title: I had a great stay!
text: I had a great time at this newly renovated hotel that is very close to Kings Cross / St. Pancras. The room was very nice, albeit a bit small (which is the norm in London). The staff was very friendly and attentive and allowed me to check in earlier. The room was quiet and the bed very comfortable. The free filtered water system was a great touch. The only downside was that the hotel does not offer breakfast, but there are numerous great options nearby. Finally, the elevator was out of order during my stay but I was placed in a room on the first floor so that was not a problem for me. Overall I would highly recommend this hotel.

author: Lucy U
title: Would 100% stay here again as a business traveller
text: Fantastic location, comfortable room. So convenient for King's Cross St Pancras and Central London, excellent value for money

author: Taylor Q
title: Newly refurbished
text: I had a very nice stay, and liked the newly refurbished rooms. I got excellent help from the people I met in the reception, and extended my stay by two nights because I was so satisfied with the hotel.

author: Mia U
title: Fantastic
text:
Very happy with my stay, the room was great, very clean tidy, good air conditioning, no faults at all.
10/10

author: Mia B
title: Not designed for anyone over 35.
text: First time in NYC. Hotel is in a great location. Friendly staff and great drinks. Lovley rooftop bar. The hotel itself however is not designed for anyone over 35. Dark halls and low to the floor beds makes navigating the place difficult. Everything is placed in the room in the most difficult to access areas. Like the hotel phone on the wall next to the bed that u have to crawl to get to. The lamps in the rooms all have different ways to turn them on so its a game of how do I get this to work just to get lighting on and off. No towel racks near the shower and the shower is see thru from the bed area.its all very cool to look at but not functional to stay in. Makes for great pictures but you risk your life trying to get up and use the bathroom during the night. I would recommend for the younger crowd but not for anyone over 35.

author: Elena X
title: Horrible; Avoid AT ALL COSTS
text:
Hotel Alameda looked promising, but the experience dealing with their staff and policies was unbelievably frustrating.

Their cancellation policy is vague, confusing, and seemingly designed to prevent guests from understanding what they’re actually agreeing to. I tried repeatedly to get a straight answer about cancellation terms and refund eligibility, and it was nearly impossible to get anyone competent on the phone. Calls went unanswered, messages weren’t returned, and when I finally did reach someone, I got conflicting information every single time.

For a hotel charging premium New York prices, the customer service was shockingly bad. Transparency should be the bare minimum in hospitality, especially when guests are making expensive travel decisions. Instead, Hotel Alameda created an experience that felt evasive, disorganized, and completely indifferent to customer concerns.

A reputable hotel makes policies clear and treats guests with professionalism. Hotel Alameda did neither. If you value honest communication and responsive service, book elsewhere.

author: Ryan Y
title: Terrible!
text: Terrible, terrible service. First, we asked for service to fix lights that were not working. We were told, "no problem"..but no one came! W e asked for a quite room. We were told this would not be a problem. The noise/dance music was SO loud, we could havre been dancing. We called (i) the service desk repeatedly and then, (ii) the outline "landline"... and NO ONE answered. Terrible! book at your own risk. Jon C 5/10/2026

author: Isabella M
title: Do not stay here!!
text:
Edited to warn: They also charged me $1,149.95 inexplicably and when I inquired why, I got no response. I have had to move the matter to the police & better business bureau. DO NOT STAY HERE.

Original review: I can say, unequivocally, that you should never stay at this hotel. I booked the loft, Suite, AND deluxe room for me and my party in June 2025--for a trip in May 2026. I reached out a week before arrival to ask to switch the suite and loft reservations. Instead of replying, they canceled the Loft and rebooked to someone else. So, first clue is that a reservation at this hotel, even one made it advance, does not matter. It also doesn't matter if you are bringing in multiple customers. Upon learning this at check-in, I requested to speak to the manager, who looked me in the eyes after reviewing my numerous communications with the hotel, and said "what do you expect me to do?" I asked to honor MY reservation from a year ago and he let me know he wouldn't and that there was nothing else to do or say. I have never been treated like this at a hotel. If you want to be sure your trip starts off poorly and continues that way... this is the place. Aside from that, the bed caused intense back pain, anytime I had a question for the front desk they were rude, and I am usually happy to pay a resort fee, but at this hotel, it literally provides nothing. Just another money grab because this place is so horrible they wouldn't be able to stay in business without charging fake fees. Stay away. There are tons of boutique hotels that actually care about customer service

author: Amelia X
title: Terrible Experience! Way Overpriced! Poor Quality
text:
I stayed at Hotel Alameda for two nights. Thursday and Friday, April 23-25, checked out today, Saturday.
My room rate was $629.00 for each night. I booked this in November and did not see lower prices listed for those dates which I reserved last November. I was expecting excellence and luxury, a splurge for my retirement. Not quite! The Hotel offered little to no complimentary amenities. The room was very basic. The rooftop bar was closed for my first night for a private party so there was no access my first evening. I saw a mouse or a rat early in the morning in the hotel lobby. When I told the hotel clerk, he said, “yeah, it’s Manhattan”.
I did write an email to hotel management about the above incident and my dissatisfaction with the hotel services, that I was paying  $629. Plus taxes and fees for each night. The hotel took off 10 percent of my first night’s stay since there was no rooftop access. I thought this was minimal at best. In addition on Friday afternoon I came back to my hotel room to find it open. The lock was resting against the door. There was no cleaning staff still on floor but apparently they had forgotten to close and lock my door. Good thing I hadn’t left any valuables in the room. The hotel staff and management offered no apologies. The unapologetic manager did take off $70.00 dollars from the resort fees. They took a total $180 off my original bill. Minimal. This was a very stressful, unsatisfying stay. For the price it was a complete rip off. I have stayed in other hotels in New York for less money that have offered far superior experiences. I would not recommend staying here.

author: Thomas L
title: Do Not Stay at the Alameda!
text: The location was close to the High Line, Whitney and some nice restaurants.  However, the room was small, dark, and dingy - not what was pictured on the website.  When first using the shower, the water coming out of the pipes was brown.  We could never regulate the temperature of the water in the shower, thus the temperature was either too cold or too hot and never enough water pressure to thoroughly rinse your hair/body.  No dresser to store clothes. We had to store most of our clothes in our suitcases, having to open/close the suitcases every time you want change clothes.  Hooks and four hangers were provided, but not adequate storage if spending more than one night.  The walls are thin and not insulated.  I could hear the person next door talking on the phone at 2:30 am.   Mattress is on a very low platform, you feel like you're sleeping on the floor.  Beware this hotel charges a $35 per night "resort fee" (this hotel was definitely not a resort), so please note you will be charged an extra $35 per night for the hotel room.  We will never stay at this hotel again....

author: Gavin P
title: A suboptimal experience.
text:
My wife and I recently stayed at the Hotel Alameda to enjoy a fun weekend in New York City.  We were very disappointed.  From the start, the entire experience was poor.  The street where the hotel is located in Chelsea is run down, deserted, dark, and unwelcoming, especially at night.  The receptionist was friendly but spouted off a series of times for coffee service, bar service, rooftop bar and restaurant times that were impossible to remember.  It would have been much better if they had a handout. The hallways were painted black making it hard to see and the lighting was poor.  It was depressing when you walked out of your room to the elevator.  The room had a platform bed with abut a foot of wood framing all around.  Be careful when getting to the bathroom in the middle of the night; you might trip and fall!  You could not keep a bathroom light on because the entire bathroom was glass enclosed and shone out into the sleeping area.  And, yes, even the shower was exposed to the  sleeping part of the room.  How's that for privacy!  There was no facial tissue box in the room and no body lotion and none was available from the staff.  But the receptionist said that CVS was nearby where we could purchase those items.   
Reception also did not have a guide to local restaurants other than the single pizza restaurant directly across from the hotel. Coffee service was not present two mornings at around 8 AM when we could have used some, but water was available.  
Wear your winter coats if you plan on going to the rooftop bar.  It was freezing up there.  No heat was on or it was inadequate. 
And one night, after returning to our room late in the evening, and getting in bed to sleep, the fire alarm went off at 11 PM!  We all trudged down the fire stairway and out the fire exit.  The New York Fire Department responded with a ladder truck and battalion chief, who eventually determined that the alarm was false and we were then able to return to our rooms.  Another guest staying on our floor told us that she had the same experience with a false alarm a year previously when she stayed at the Alameda.  
To boot, it was not a cheap hotel; rates were pretty high.  We are definitely not going back nor recommending this hotel.

author: Brooke S
title: Extremely spartan accommodations
text: The only positive thing I can say is the room was clean. But it was literally a mattress on a small platform on a cement floor. The bathroom is basically what you would find on a commuter train, but with worse lighting. Suffice it to say, unless you are under the age of 25 and traveling to NY on holiday, stay somewhere else.

author: Ana G
title: Don't stay here!!!
text: Do not stay at this hotel if you want to sleep at night!!!  They book this hotel out for raves and you’ll get np sleep. I highly recommend you look elsewhere.

author: Ella Q
title: Not worth your money.
text:
Not sure how they got 4-stars, when the experience was more like 2-3 stars.  
Room was small, which was not an issue since I was traveling alone.  However, the room was not very well maintained, please see the attached pictures.  
The rusted sink stand in the bathroom was crazy, not even close to vintage.  
Not a great experience, as I have stayed at 3-star hotels with better offerings.  
Highly disappointed.

author: Harry F
title: Unprofessional, Noisy, and Unsafe Atmosphere
text:
I chose this hotel for its location near the activity I was attending in Chelsea, but the experience fell far below expectations.

PROS: The shower had excellent water pressure and temperature. The mattress itself was comfortable. The location is convenient for the High Line and Penn Station.

CONS: The room design is impractical and uncomfortable. The bed sits almost on the floor, which makes it unsafe for anyone with mobility or health issues. The bathroom has frosted glass walls, a sliding closet-style door with no lock, and a ceiling-hung curtain that feels like a hospital divider. There is no privacy.

The lighting is terrible. Hallways are painted black with dim lights, creating a gloomy atmosphere. The bedside lamps look “chic” but don’t provide enough light. Maintenance is poor: scratched floors, chipped sink, cracked walls, and cheap finishes.

Security is unacceptable. The elevator requires no key card, so anyone can reach guest floors. During my stay, I saw a local resident escorted out while cursing, and also suspicious activity that looked like escorts entering with “protectors.” This is not what I expect from a Manhattan hotel.

Service was equally bad. There is no refrigerator in the room, even for medication. Bottled water costs $6 each. At 6 am, the front desk was empty for my check-out. The only person present was a cleaning employee who had to call the receptionist. He eventually appeared from the sidewalk, apologized, and smelled strongly of marijuana.

BOTTOM LINE: The hotel sells itself as new, but it is visibly deteriorated and poorly managed. It offers boutique facade with hostel-level service. If you need professionalism, accessibility, and basic security, stay at a Hilton, Hyatt, Marriott, or any other reputable chain.

author: Amelia Y
text: The housekeeping staff was friendly and efficient. The the rest of the staff— front desk, bar tenders and wait staff were disconnected, disinterested and distant. My standard room was ridiculous. You need advance acrobatic skills to negotiate the tiny spaces along side the platforn bed. The bathroom is a phone booth

author: Hugo G
title: Great location, Terrible Service & Lack of Amenities.
text: So, I had a bit of a rough time during my stay. The rooftop bar was closed both days, and I was still charged a resort fee. On top of that, I had to pay an early check-in fee of $50 to get into my room an hour early. And guess what? The AC in the lobby is broken! On the first day, there was a private party in the lobby bar, which was a bit of a nuisance. On the second day, housekeeping completely forgot to clean my room. And to top it all off, the self-check-out drink and snack refrigerator in the lobby was broken and asking for a password. Even the free coffee in the lobby was broken on day two, which was confirmed by the staff. The receptionists seemed a bit rude and weren’t very helpful about the included amenities and availability. They couldn’t even give me directions to the Vessel, which was just a few blocks away. Breakfast here was yummy however. Will not stay here again.

author: Lea B
title: Not a destination. A place to sleep.
text:
Chelsea location convenient to the High Line, but little else. Room was spartan/minimalist, with a platform bed on the floor. Clean and modern, but if you’re older or have mobility issues not for you. Bathroom small, tiny sink, tiny shower. Bathroom was again clean and modern but 2 people cannot use it at the same time. 

I can’t see myself staying here more than a day or so.
Bed was comfortable and room was quiet.

Fun rooftop bar and lobby space.

author: Laura H
title: Terribly Loud Rooftop Ruined Stay
text: Title says it all. Hotel threw private rooftop parties on both Saturday and Sunday that were insanely loud. I don't know how something like that is allowed, but our windows were shaking at one point. Room was unusable during these parties. There are only 2 tiny elevators, so they also became overrun with the party goers.

author: Connor F
title: Amazing Stay at Selina Chelsea
text:
Best shakshuka for breakfast in NYC. Really, it's not a US dish, but they really know how to prepare it. Delicious.

The hotel is super well-designed and furnished. It is located on a beautiful street close to Chelsea Park, where you can easily find yourself relaxing. There is an Amazon Whole Foods grocery store just a 7-minute walk from there, where you can buy everything from drinking water to pet food. 

Hudson Yards is also a good reference point for this region. The closest subway station is the 34th St-Hudson Yards, right under the mall. Three very famous attractions are nearby: the Vessel, the Shed, and the Edge (a rooftop with a vast view of New York).

However, Selina has the best view of the city because the bar on the hotel rooftop is a plus. I got my two courtesy drinks over there.
I can only say that I had a great time staying at Selina Chelsea.

author: George W
title: Budget friendly but could be better
text:
Cons: The rooms were quite small and the bedding was a bit low quality for any type of proper hotel. Maybe the other weak point was the food was generally awful.  

Pros:  That hotel is pretty and the spaces are pretty. The location is great for exploring the area, the staff are friendly and the rooftop bar is accommodating and the drinks are fair priced. 

It was not a bad budget ish way to see NY but the hotel vibe made the spot not feel super Selina ish and the cheap bedding seemed a bit too much to make me think about staying again.

author: Chloe J
title: Will be back.
text: Can't beat this location and convenience! It is a small room, but fantastic for solo travel on the go, and the option to meet up with friends on the rooftop bar was appreciated. Hotel was clean and cleaning team were on top of things. The staff was incredibly accommodating and helpful; Martin, in particular, made me feel right at home and put in effort to meet all of my needs. I will be back here.

author: Emma W
title: That's a big NooooOOOOOooooOOOOOOOoooooooooOOOooo!!!!!!!!!!!!
text:
It's HOOOORRRRRRRRIIIIIIBLE.

The Selina hotel brand seems to be about being Young!  And Fun!  And Having Adventure!  That's fine.  In the event, the hotel is overpriced and really bad.  With the room they're going for a boho-chic kind of feeling but it's just cheap and uncomfortable - no expense has not been spared - it actually feels sub-IKEA.  There's nowhere to work in the room - you have to go to bars with their relentless ever-throbbing house music.  

The staff also seemed to be whatever could be cobbled together. 

It's really, really unimpressive.

Now you know!

author: Juan E
title: Great value for a central location but outside the hustle and bustle.
text: I'm glad I ignored the bad reviews. I found The Selina to be an exceptional value for the location and experience. The staff was terrific, and the free welcome drink was a real treat - the margarita option was a very quality cocktail, not a cheap mix. Most importantly I appreciate they don't extort pet owners with exorbitant extra fees and were truly welcoming to my pup (we were in town for an AKC event at the Javits Center). Also the morning coffee in the lobby was a really good brew - I normally would go out to one of the many specialty cafes for coffee, but was more than happy with the complimentary cup. The room was small, as are most NYC rooms at this price point. I did not have a problem with noise other than the to be expected occasional street noise which was barely discernible. Music from the lobby area traveled up the elevator shaft but could not be heard inside the room. While I could hear the sound of other room doors opening and closing, I find that to be fairly common in hotels and was not bothered by it, nor was my dog. The room temperature was easily adjustable. I did initially feel a draft and some cool air but soon realized the window had been left partially open. I will definitely be back to the Selina for the AKC event next year- the proximity to Javits and Hudson Yards without being in the gritty really busy Times Square area was perfect.

author: Owen D
title: Good option for families due to great location and good breakfast.
text: Great central location close to Kings Cross Station and Euston stations. Easy check in and check out procedures and a very good breakfast spread.

author: Adam S
title: Dreadful
text:
A few years since we last stayed in a Premier Inn but have never before had any complaint.
What has happened to the company????
The rooms were shabby and the bathrooms in dire need of refurbishment. Stayed at Duke Street, Euston for 3 nights.
Arrived early and paid £15 for early check in. Was not given any information about restaurant, bar or the breakfasts we had pre- booked.
After unpacking we headed into the city not returning until 10:30pm. The heat hit us as we entered the room . The slightly open window and the fan provided did nothing to reduce the room temperature of over 30degrees.
Upon visiting Reception was told that all rooms were the same, the air conditioning didn’t work and to roam the corridors for spare fans! None to be found.
After less than 4 hours sleep and after complaining at length, the manager finally agreed to move us to a ground floor room which did have air conditioning and had just become available.
Do not book this location if like us you have health conditions which are exacerbated and possibly life threatening during high temperatures.

author: Harper P
title: Grim. Not very clean.
text: I chose this hotel because it is very close to London Euston train station. That's really about all it has going for it. It's dated,  not very clean at all, the curtain in my room wasnt properly attached at one end, the lift didnt work when I arrived and the stairs were dark and hadn't apparentlybeen cleaned for some time. There were very few visible staff, I'd paid for early check in but by the time it took for the single receptionist to explain to some people who hadnt that they couldnt check in yet, I may as well have not bothered. There was no air conditioning (and it was very warm) -  this wasnt made clear when I booked, just mentioned nervously by reception when I checked in. The room came with a kettle, two glass mugs and a sticky teaspoon. The handsoap (over the toilet because that's just where you need it) didnt work so i had to use shower gel to wash my hands. The room was tired and dusty. I know that hotel chains like to upsell but is it really necessary to lower standards to such an extent that you can only get a room at Premier Inn that meets basic acceptable hygiene standards if you upgrade to a Premier Plus room? I booked with Premier Inn in part to avoid Travelodge (I was travelling alone) but this experience genuinely makes me wonder how bad they could really be.

author: Dylan R
title: Not up to expected standard
text:
The location is about the only good thing at this hotel.
We arrived on Thursday having booked and paid for early check in from 11am to be told they didn’t have that and come back after 3pm. We were able to leave luggage. When we did check in , they couldn’t confirm if we’d be refunded for lack of early check in . 
Once in room, it was like walking into a sauna , temperature over 30 degrees, apparently the air con is broken and has been for some considerable time. The provided fan blew hot air around, the small gap from opening the windows provided no relief. 
The room itself was basic and functional, if dated in appearance. Bed was comfortable enough when finally fell asleep. Having to keep the window open in the  hope of cooling air meant we had the constant noise of a main road. 
Tea and coffee facilities were provided in the room , the UHT milk was off. 
Bathroom - shower worked. Single sheets of toilet paper from a dispenser rather than a toilet roll. 
Breakfast was decent , staff there friendly. 
On checking out on Saturday, witnessed a number of people checking in early. When duty manager did eventually appear to approve refund , she couldn’t understand why we didn’t get the sevice on Thursday. Still waiting to see if promised refund hits my card.
Overall, would not recommend and certainly puts me off booking another Premier Inn if this is their standard. A million miles from their flashy TV  advert.

author: Camille U
title: Dreadful experience
text:
Staff lovely but DO NOT STAY HERE IF THE WEATHRT IS HOT 
No air conditioning fan only in room need the windows open but this hotel is on a very busy and nousy road. We were awake most of the night with traffic noise as we couldn't close the windows as it was so hot in the room.. Dreadful experience

author: Sofia R
title: London trip
text: Return customer but unfortunately hotel looks tired, bar closes early 1105pm so no option for a drink after a day out. Breakfast options limited if you require gluten free food. Last time for me, room cleaning needs improvement as nail clippings on carpet and needed decorating as walls in poor condition. Wouldn't return. Great location for tube/train.

author: Oliver O
title: Good location and staff.
text: Great location, staff very friendly and helpful. Room very hot even with fan  - window only opened about 10 cms. When fan on very difficult to hear TV.  When having a bath it is impossible to reach sap container!

author: Alice B
title: Very warm and noisy
text:
Convenient location; however, I would avoid this location during the summer.  The air conditioning in this hotel is not working (although it does appear to have worked at some point in the past, as the control panels are still there, so I guess they have chosen not to maintain the system or turn it off to reduce electricity costs); this means that when your hotel room is unpleasantly warm, you need to open the windows.
Unfortunately, the convenient location is also a major road through London, meaning it's very noisy, with loud engines, horns and emergency sirens even during the early hours.

author: Rosie R
title: Overnight stay
text: Situated close to the station A friendly and welcoming hotel. The check in is either receptionist or self check in. The room was fairly large. Comfortable bed and good quality bedding. There is tv, wifi and coffee and tea making facilities. There is ample storage for a short stay plus a desk and chair plus an arm chair. The bathroom has a bath and shower.  There were only towels for one person. Everywhere is very clean. On a negative note. The air conditioning wasnt working and hasn’t been on a few of our visits.  The did provide a fan. It is a quiet hotel and no problem with noise.we ate in the hotel and the meal was fine. The staff very helpful. Breakfast is a good buffet style.

author: Pierre D
title: Sleeping in a hot house!
text: After we booked in we were told the air conditioning system was broken and would be fixed summer 2027!. The room was unbearable, over 30% heat with the ventilator blowing warm air into the room. I complained to Premier inn via their helpline and was told there was nothing they could do.

author: Harper H
title: Avoid Euston Premier Inn
text: Location was the best thing about this hotel . The rooms were disgustingly hot ,at one point the temperature in our room was 36°🥵 and all we had was a fan circulating the hot air around the family room.  I booked 2 rooms for my family of 5 costing near enough £900 and this hotel is so not worth this !!! Complained to reception about the room and asked to be moved or refunded to get another hotel and was told it couldn't be done. "Rest Easy" is their moto but it certainly wasn't for us ,we are now home exhausted from our weekend .... Rooms need an overhaul,carpets deep cleaned and bathrooms need redone .

author: Paolo Z
title: Unhuman
text:
Absolutely disgraceful service, 
Arrived very late after a long day of traveling. It took almost 20 mins for somebody to acknowledge me at the from doors to enter reception to only be told that they are fully booked, not in person, though the intercom, not welcoming at all, so I decided to check online if they was fully booked and they was not fully booked, so I asked if I could have a drink of water from thier fountain and they said only for people who are staying.. how rude no manners. I didn't feel safe

author: Mason F
title: Give it a miss.
text: Room is grubby, hardly the recent refurbished room description. The room is so hot, no air con - reception says it states it in the website (not that I can find) asked for a fan, brought one it was filthy and blowing out dust. Asked for a replacement and it didn’t work. Reception service is poor

author: Wyatt U
title: Broken A/C - Rooms too hot.
text:
We stayed for a night early August, hoping to be refreshed before getting the morning Eurostar. A month before we were told the A/C was broken. To be honest I thought it would’ve been fixed by the time we arrived. We had an advance rate so there was nothing we could do with the booking other than lose the £105 paid. The day we arrived it was a particularly warm day in London and when we checked in, the room felt hotter than outside.  
A fan was provided but all that did was blow extremely hot air around an extremely hot room. Our room faced Euston Road which is noisy 24hrs a day so we couldn’t sleep with the windows open. 
We got up in the morning for our train, exhausted and sweaty from what was the equivalent of sleeping in a sauna. 
I booked the hotel with A/C and when it broke the month before,  I wasn’t given any options for what I could do about this. 
I have spoken with customer service and they haven’t taken my complaint any further.

author: Brooke P
title: Avoid!!!
text:
Stayed last night for a concert. Arrived to the room and it was boiling. There was a stand up fan in there, which surprised us as lots of premier inns have air con. Went to go and turn it on and it was already on! The room was 30 degrees on the little screen display. We were only in there for a while and we were sweating, uncomfortable, and to be quite honest it was hard to breathe. 

We left for our concert, came back and the room was now 31.5 degrees! After a while, we went downstairs to ask if there was anything we could do…just to be told the aircon wasn’t working throughout the whole building (but worked in the reception??) and it was out of their control. We were offered another fan, and it was to be brought to the room. 

The fan obviously did not make it to us.

Going to sleep was an effort due to the heat and the noise of outside, light sleep for a couple of hours, then both of us being wide awake at 6:30 absolutely boiling,(probably our bodies screaming for help) as the room was now 32.5-33 degrees. 

We decided to sack off our original plans, get out of the hotel early and leave. Leaving the hotel was - literally - a breath of fresh air. There was no warning of the aircon not working before / during our stay, just a half arsed apology. I feel like coming off the back of a heatwave, it might be wise to let people know before hand if they’re going to boil to death in the rooms. You could not get comfy, anytime you moved NEVERMIND went into the bathroom your hair would be sticking to your neck. 

Also, no proper toilet roll, was paper sheets, and glasses in the rooms were dirty so couldn’t even have a drink! 

Absolutely do not recommend to anybody

author: Isla I
title: Great location
text: Great location and wonderful staff. I highly recommend this hotel for a short stay in London.

author: Alexander N
title: Room too hot for sleeping
text: The room was so hot that sleep was impossible. The air conditioning was set to low and fan speed to high but room temperature never fell below 32 degrees. So much for a guaranteed good nights sleep.

author: Rosie Z
title: Sweat box with bad nights sleep.
text: Had a very bad stay here for 2 nights, the room was over 30 degrees most of the time and if you open the windows which we had to at night to get a bit of cool air in it was very noisy. Would not recommend this hotel due to not being able to cool the room.

author: Freya H
title: Hell Hole
text: A/C hasn't worked for years, rooms unbearably hot & are health hazard. Have reported this place to  HSE. Don't stay here!

author: Ryan Z
title: It was amazing
text: Great customer service from Rashid

author: Ruby S
title: What More Could You Want?
text:
What an incredible weekend in New York! The Muse is in a fantastic location, close to tons of great restaurants and easy Metro access. The front desk team was excellent, especially Angel, who made us feel incredibly welcome.

We were in town to see Hamilton, which is literally about a two-minute walk from the hotel. We were also pleasantly surprised to discover The Pocket, an intimate jazz venue tucked into the lower lobby of The Muse. Such a cool addition to the hotel. Coffee at Little Opus was great as well. I didn’t catch the name of the barista who helped me, but she was wonderful.

All in all, a fantastic hotel in an unbeatable location with a great team. We’ll absolutely be back!

author: Samuel E
title: Top notch service and excellent location
text: Stayed here for a couple of nights when we wanted to visit NYC to show our 2 sons (11 and 7) the city for the first time.  Decided on The Muse based on the good reviews, location (near Time Square), available parking, and 2 queen bed rooms (as opposed to doubles).  Service was top notch (Angel at the front was particularly excellent), the room was spacious and clean, and the location was fabulous, a block or so off Time Square so near enough to everything, but not right in Times Square with the noise and crowds.  We’ll definitely consider staying here again next time we decide to visit the city.

author: Chloe C
title: Praise
text: I want to first praise the excellent service of Miss Bárbara. It makes all the difference, super professional and attentive. The hotel is a spectacle, the room is super clean and fragrant, towels are always new, the hotel staff is a 10. Perfect location, close to everything, highly recommend

author: Isla R
title: Wonderful Hotel right by Times Square
text:
My husband and I did a quick trip to New York, my first time there, for our Anniversary and stayed at The Muse.  This was an excellent place to stay.  The staff is remarkable!  They upgraded us to a great room on the top floor.  It was quiet (though we could hear Times Square, but it didn't bother us), clean, and very well laid out.  They have a great lounge in the basement, we just peaked in one night, we wish we actually stayed (but we were exhausted), and they have a great breakfast, snack bar.
They offer ice and water on the 17th floor and on the main floor (these were the closest for us) and it was so convenient to fill the water bottles we brought with us.
It was so close to everything.  6 minute walk to Rockefeller Center, about a 15 minute walk to the Empire State Building.  It took us about 20 minutes to walk to Central park, which was beautiful.  Such a walkable city!
We would definitely stay here again!

author: Ruby T
title: Excellent place to Stay in NY if visiting Times Square and/or Theaters!
text: This is an excellent hotel in a location that cannot be beat!  We were one block from Times Square but far enough removed that we didn't hear noise on the 14th floor. We were able to walk to all Broadway shows/theaters we wanted to. The subway lines were very nearby. There were plenty of delicious restaurants close enough to enjoy. Every single staff member we encountered was friendly and courteous and went out of their way to make us feel welcome. The hotel was clean and well maintained.  The room size was more than comfortable for 3 people in a 2 Queen Executive Room. The bathroom was huge with a Jack and Jill sink which was handy. The shower's water pressure was excellent (there were two options for water - a rain shower head and a hand held nozzle).  The water temperature was easy to maintain.  The breakfast was delicious and the person behind the counter was also super friendly, creating a nice, welcoming atmosphere.  The overall value was exceptional, and I will definitely be making this my hotel of choice when visiting NYC.

author: Sara X
title: My go to hotel for NYC
text: 3rd time staying here and never any issues. Rooms are spacious and clean. Staff is always friendly as well.  It can sometimes be noisy at night but it’s NYC so I expect it, nothing to do with the hotel

author: Hannah E
title: Service
text:
Amazing service !!!
Barbara from the reception is awesome !!!

author: Nora J
title: My stay at the Muse, NYC.
text: Excellent location if you want to be near Times Square, with a very helpful, friendly and professional hotel staff ( everyone was nice from the bellboy, housekeeping and front desk agents) .

author: Diego C
title: Concierge set the tone for a great visit. Thanks Barbara Los!
text: Arrived before check in time. The concierge was so helpful to store our luggage and we went for lunch. Upon return she gave us a special room seeing that it was my husbands birthday. She also handed me two coupons for celebratory drinks at the bar. Cheers to Barbara Los for making our short stay very special. Thank you!

author: Elena F
title: Great escape.
text: Excellent staffing and Excellent front desk staff.,Barbara Losgreat stayed j

author: Zachary H
title: Concierge Staff Barbara amazing!!!
text: Barbara Los was so incredibly kind and helpful! She assisted us with check in, and was very friendly and accommodated our requests! Beautiful hotel

author: Poppy O
title: Great hotel, clean, friendly
text: Lovely hotel with great service. Clean, neat, organized. Great waterfall shower head, and housekeeping even made our beds/replenished sheets without asking. Comfortable stay for us! Plus, we made it too see the Knicks take home the final 😀

author: Lauren U
title: Boutique Vibes w/ Premium Service & Great Location
text: The property and the hotel room exceeded expectations. Location perfect for getting where you need to go via subway or train; 5 min walk to Times Square but not IN Times Square (winning). The ENTIRE staff was incredibly welcoming and attentive to our sometimes funky questions and requests, lol. Barbara and Daniel at concierge will change your plans for the better so do not miss a chance to introduce yourself and state your intentions! Bartenders will amaze as well!

author: Chloe C
title: Great place to stay for work and fun
text: Love to stay at The Muse hotel, second stay and can’t say nothing but good things. Location is prime, access to favorite restaurants, pubs, all kind of places is very convenient, few blocks from Rockefeller, St Patrick’s, etc. Room was clean, well equipped and very comfy.  Awesome atmosphere in out out, nice music in the evening, pleasant bar and restaurant. Price wise I think nothing crazy, you pay what you expect to pay near Time Square. Service excellent, friendly and helpful staff. Room is quiet isolating from nightly craziness in the area. Highly recommended, staying there next time for sure.

author: Evan S
title: Amazing Hotel right next to Times Square
text: The Muse was fabulous! The Concierge, Daniel Mitchell, was warm and welcoming and ensured we had the best room available (a king suite which was sensational). He remembered our names throughout our stay and made us feel like rock stars! The rest of the staff at The Muse were all warm, helpful, and welcoming and we felt like we were back home when we returned to the hotel from our exploits in NYC. All in all it was an amazing experience in an insanely brilliant location (really enjoyable in every way). The Carnegie Diner on 6th avenue was just around the corner and proved to be our favourite restaurant in NYC with $7 happy hour margaritas!

author: Hugo H
title: The perfect stay
text:
The location is amazing, staff super friendly especially Ms  Yaevick Cuevas. 
The room was  wry spacious, overall an excellent experience!

author: Harry R
title: Great experience. Would highly recommend!
text: Location was great, rooms were very nice with very comfy beds, restaurant/bar was excellent and staff was friendly and helpful.

author: Megan F
title: The Best Hotel in the Theater District!
text: We travel to New York City about 5 times/year.  We ALWAYS stay at The Muse.  We discovered the Muse quite by accident.  We were looking for a reasonably priced hotel in the Theater District after our usual hotel closed.  That was more than ten years ago.  One of the first things that impressed us about the Muse is the size of the rooms!  They are HUGE by NYC standards.  Second, and most important to us, is the staff.  Always friendly, professional and truly caring about their guests.  The front desk staff, especially Yaevick, is top shelf.  Yaevick has recommended the best shows, the best restaurants and always is eager to help us in any way she can.  Daniel and Barbara are also front desk personnel who go out of their way to be helpful.  The housekeeping staff is exceptional.  Now that "Little Opus" is open, there are food and beverages available right beside the lobby.  A jazz club is opening soon, too.  If you are looking for a great place to stay, steps from Times Square, in the heart of the Theater District, then the Muse is for you!  The photo is the view of 46th Street from a room on the 12th floor.

author: Harper N
title: Awesome!!!!
text: My stay was super pleasant; I would definitely return to the same hotel. Yaevick at the reception was a very kind woman and helped me a lot with communication.

author: Thomas B
title: Love The Muse!
text: The Muse is my go-to hotel. I've been staying there for over 4 years now every time I visit New York and love everything about it. I'd like to give a shout-out to Barbara Los, also. She's a wonderful concierge and was really helpful during my stay.

author: Alexander H
title: Terrible customer service- they just did not care!
text:
There was an issue with our booking.                 (Booked with booking.com). The hotel claimed they did not have it even though booking.com confirmed the hotel had the reservation and there was no issue.

The person (male team member) on the desk needs re-training as he had no customer service skills whatsoever, rude and did not care. He gave the impression he had no idea what he was doing as he went back and forth from the the office asking someone else in the office for log in details.  

We were told the supervisor was on his way to 'sort it out', this was a hour and a half and still left waiting so we just left and booked another hotel down the road.  We are pursuing a refund through booking.com. But the lack of customer service was appalling as it was 11:30pm at night when we gave up and left. Disgraceful.

author: James K
title: Not good at all
text: Rubbish outside front of hotel, poor fitting glass tops to bedside units and a filthy window with bird droppings and stains on window. Tried to upgrade but said was largest room . Not a nice hotel

author: Ethan J
title: Terrible property
text:
The category is 4 stars, but for the quality of services offered, it should be 3.
Dated property that absolutely needs to be renovated.
Our room on the first floor without an elevator, small and uncomfortable, cramped entrance and with 5 narrow steps to get to the bed. Mattress worn on one side that created a dip (a real treat for the back!). Window glass filthy, with bird droppings. You could hear every single step taken by the occupants of the room above because their floor creaked loudly. To reach the bathroom (which is tiny) you had to go down 5 steps, which makes everything very inconvenient at night and it is necessary to turn on the light (disturbing sleep) to avoid falling. The bathroom door did not open completely because the towel rack blocked it. The only positive note about the bathroom is the size of the shower stall, which is comfortable. We should have had air conditioning in the room, but it did not work. When I pointed this out at the front desk, they told me that the malfunction was due to dust (which is not plausible because the wall controls wouldn't even turn on) and they offered to change my room, but they had no others available.
Very slow Wi-Fi network.
Breakfast: quite varied, especially for savory options, but little attention to service and cleanliness.
Very convenient location for the Queensway and Bayswater subway stations, just a few minutes' walk away, and located across from Kensington Gardens.
For £154/night (€180) B&B, I definitely expect much better.
I will never choose this property again in the future and I strongly advise against it.

author: Alice A
title: Beautiful hotel, shame about our supposedly superior room
text: Idea location short walk to the tube/bus etc. The hotel communal areas are beautiful with original stairways, original ‘theatre’ bar and lots of engravings, the frontage is stunning and welcoming. Our room, however, was tiny, cramped and hot, the air con didn’t work. The shower sprayed everywhere as shower screen too small. It was, however value for money and ok for one night. Whole place was very clean. Being in a side street hotel was reasonably quiet although our room had a very noisy extractor which we could not turn off. Staff were very attentive and polite especially the breakfast crew. Breakfast was lovely, lots of choice, very tasty, hot food was hot and there was plenty of it.

author: Dylan K
title: Don't chance a booking with this hotel.
text: We booked two rooms at this hotel for our family, one was suppose to  be a club level.  After our long flight from the states, we walked .8 miles from Paddington Station with our luggage, in the heat to this hotel, to be informed rudely and unapologetically, that they had rebooked us to their "sister" hotel, the Inhabit Queens Garden.  They told us that they had emailed us about the change, while we were in flight!  There was no offer to transport us to this  other hotel and so, we had to schlep our luggage an additional .6 miles to the new hotel.  We had originally planned on taking a two day trip to Paris and return to the Grand Royale Hyde Park, but due to our lack of confidence in this hotel, we cancelled out booking right away and stayed at a different hotel all together.   We have a travel agent who was on hold for hours trying to get our booking straighten out, with no response.  Never going to attempt staying at this hotel ever again.

author: Charlie W
title: Very disappointing
text: We have stayed here twice before and we were looking forward to this time but unfortunately the room we had was disgraceful, it was supposed to be a deluxe double it was a single at best the bed was so close to the curtains that you couldn't get into bed that side, the curtains were hanging off the rails so you couldn't close them properly, the headboard was disgusting, the carpets were filthy, the bathroom floor tiles were broken and moved when you walked on them. When we spoke to the receptionist about our issues they said "we are fully booked " that is not acceptable the room should never have been available in the first place.

author: Laura Q
title: Poor service, save your money.
text:
Location is fantastic right outside Hyde Park, nearby Underground stations make it super easy to get around. We stayed on the 7th floor for three nights in a room that was absolutely tiny and would only suit 2 people for one night. There was no room to unpack our bags, desk was tiny and cluttered. Bed was comfortable and room was nicely serviced each day. Bathroom and shower decent but shower door was tiny, hard not to flood the bathroom when taking a shower. Most shocking was the full on hole in the window in the actual glass itself. Air-con in the room was great and was left on before we arrived. Room and public areas were clean and well kept. No noise during day or night. 

Service was severely lacking. Two lovely girls at the check in desk the day we arrived. Breakfast staff were also very pleasant and breakfast was decent full buffet. There was a lady however on our second evening complaining about her room at the front desk and the receptionist couldn’t have seemed to care less. The hotel has no reservations department and their signs to match prices on their website is clearly a lie as I found a rate £200 cheaper on Trivago and there was no effort made for me to cancel and rebook directly. 

My sunglasses were stolen in the hotel lobby and I brought it up to three separate receptionists on different occasions and the concierge and there was zero concern made. The concierge actually told me to go and check my own room again when I knew full well I had left them in the lobby and exactly what chair they were left on. I had left them down in a fluster after waiting 15 minutes for my luggage which couldn’t be retrieved and we had to be brought to the basement to pick out our own luggage. At no point did any of the staff offer to take my details or even room number when I brought up my missing sunglasses which was super concerning… This whole situation is the reason I’d give the place only one star. My sunglasses were a gift to me and expensive, and the complete lack of concern was so disappointing. 

At another point the England match was on and we went to the bar early enough around 8.30pm and they had no wine except Chardonnay. No Coca Cola or Pepsi, and one of the staff members was sat in front of the bar watching the match on the TV.. not the most professional. 

As for value, I’m glad I booked via an OTA and didn’t pay full price for this hotel as I would have severely regretted it. Overall I would save your money and book any other hotel in the area. Not surprised this group is selling up their properties to larger groups as hospitality and guest satisfaction is definitely not their priority.

author: Ella B
title: Grand and royal indeed!
text: This used to be the house of Lillie Langtry, mistress of King Edward VII as the various rooms downstairs still show. It looks very grand indeed. The bedroom was not though but modern, clean and functional, which was reflected in the price. There was a good choice for breakfast and efficient service. But the main advantage of this hotel is its location in a safe and quiet street right next to Hyde Park and Queensway.

author: Erin B
title: Avoid at all costs. Worst hotel I've ever visited.
text: DO NOT STAY HERE! This hotel is such a scam! Air conditioning not working during summer. Lied to us about getting it repaired. Elevators not working. Room so small, I could not open my suitcase. Bathroom dirty. Window opened about 3 inches. We would have slept better on a bench in Hyde Park.  Staff was unhelpful. No ice machine. Requested a refund and was refused. So we ended up paying for TWO hotels for six nights in London because we left after one night. BEYOND AWFUL!

author: Leo L
title: A Mixed Bag
text:
I’ll start with the positives. The location was great for us. Very close to both Bayswater and Queensway tube stations and only a minute from Kensington Palace Gardens. The outside of the building, lobby and lounge areas were stunning and every member of staff we encountered were friendly and helpful. The shower was also warm and powerful and we appreciated the fresh drinking water provided in the lobby and in the rooms. 

But this is not a 4* hotel. We had a standard double room booked and it wasn’t the best. We had to be moved after our first night because the air con wasn’t working and it was very hot. Apparently they had a known fault so I’m not sure why we were placed in this room to begin with but the staff were very accommodating with moving us. Both rooms we stayed in were tiny, we could barely get around the bed in the first room. Both rooms also had extremely small beds, the second room especially. This was a small double at best and my husband and I struggled to get comfortable because it was so small. Despite the bed itself being small we also found the duvet to be too small for the bed. So neither of us slept great for our entire stay. 

If we’d paid less and had booked a 3* hotel the rooms wouldn’t have bothered us too much besides the small bed. But for a 4* I expect more than this hotel provided. Whilst our rooms were spotless and it was clear the staff were doing a good job, they were tired. Threadbare carpets, poor quality furniture, walls, doors and skirting boards all in need of a repaint. This theme continued in the hallways and corridors too. For these reasons we probably wouldn’t return.

author: Marta L
title: Fab hotel
text: This hotel is in a great position near underground and restaurants and bars. The rooms are small but who spends time in a room when in London. The a/c is excellent. Breakfast is brilliant, good selection of hot and cold foods. Staff friendly and helpful. 3rd stay here and 4th in September. Love it

author: Brooke A
title: Pleasant find
text:
This is a charming Edwardian hotel in a brilliant West London location. It’s just a five-minute walk from Queensway Underground station, making it an excellent base for exploring the city.

Although the hotel is quite old, it is clean, well maintained, and full of character. The staff are friendly, welcoming, and very well organised, providing excellent service throughout our stay.

One of the highlights was the breakfast, which offered one of the best selections of food I’ve seen in a hotel, with plenty of fresh and tasty options to suit everyone.

If you’re looking for a conveniently located hotel with character, great service, and an outstanding breakfast, I’d happily recommend staying here.

author: Evie X
title: Stay away
text:
I didnt. get to experience this hotel. I met up for checkin here after getting 3 messages about my checkin was aproaching on the hotels.com app from the hotel. Then i was told i was moved to another hotel, while i saw other people were checking in. They told me i received an email about this, which is weird because of all the spam on hotels.com, they didnt care to spam me about this, or send a text. 

However, i found the mail and it said i was transferred to a nice hotel in Mayfair. But they offered me a cab, and drove me to a not so nice hotel longer east, futher away from the area i was going to be in. 

Totally unacceptable service, communication and stay. Cant recommend to anyone.

They have not responded on any of my messages regarding this, so i believe they really dont care. You are all warned.

author: Harper C
title: Worst hotel completely deceptive description
text:
Worst hotel.
Description very different from what they provide.It was the tiniest space literally like cupboard where only bed no desk because no place to include basic piece of furniture.No ac like description on website Decevied could not get help from
Booinh.om

author: Oscar L
title: Great hotel
text:
A really charming hotel in the perfect location.
A huge shout out to a particular member of staff who made our day, Himadri the night receptionist/ auditor, delivered some of the most exceptional customer service we’ve ever experienced. Above and beyond! The hotel is very lucky to have him.

author: Hugo F
title: Hyde Park Hotels
text:
We spent two nights at Grand Royale Hyde Park and are very pleased with our stay. We got a spacious and cosy room with comfortable beds, and the hotel's classic decor gave a charming and elegant feel.

The location is hard to beat – Hyde Park is just a stone’s throw away and the area has plenty of restaurants, pubs and cafes. Paddington Station is also within easy walking distance, making it easy to get to and from Heathrow and beyond around London.

The staff were friendly and helpful, and the hotel offered a quiet and relaxing atmosphere despite the central location. For us this was a great choice, and we will gladly come back next time we visit London. Highly recommended!

author: Harper W
title: Poor customer service, air con faulty.
text: A very strange experience, slow check in , air con didn't work and the lift wouldn't go to floor 6 as the button was broken. For the money we paid id  expect more. We asked about the air con but were shunted off with ' your travel booking agency will have to sort that with a refund, we are fully booked' wouldn't go again for the cost which is unfortunate as the building is beautiful.

author: Grace Q
title: Avoid at all costs
text: Terrible Experience at this “Hotel”. One of the worst places I have ever stayed at. Terrible staff, filthy, hot and just uncomfortable. Very happy that I stayed just one night. Please avoid this dump! The only positive is the location! That said, it is above a tube line…

author: Adam Q
title: A Grand Few Days!
text: My husband and I stayed at The Grand  Royale Hotel Hyde Park for four nights. It is ideally located between Queensway and Bayswater tube stations. It was very very comfortable. A super room, with silent but very efficient AC. Teas and coffees replenished in full every day. Fresh fruit, chocolates and wine on arrival with access to fresh fruit and cool fruited water in reception all the time. Breakfast was perfectly varied and adequate for our needs. However, the best thing about The Grand Royale has to be the staff. Always smiling, always polite and extremely helpful. We’ve had a delightful stay and would love to visit again.

author: Mason U
title: Poor communication
text: Very bad experience; I had a room on the ground floor with a direct view of the trash can (I was supposed to stay there for 4 nights). The communication with the receptionist was typical of England; the neighborhood is very nice, and fortunately, I took some short walks in Hyde Park. Otherwise, a very good stay in London.

author: Katie I
title: Well located yet peaceful
text: Quiet location but close to vibrant areas and different metros for easy access to all of Paris. Clean, friendly staff, decent breakfast.

author: Megan L
title: Excellent stay at this well run & conveniently located hotel.
text: We enjoyed a perfect two night stay here. The staff are friendly & very helpful, the rooms are small but clean. Breakfast was more than adequate and items were frequently replenished. Most importantly, the coffee is good! There are also complimentary drinks & snacks in the lobby. The proximity of the hotel to Gare du Nord is a real plus. Overall then, highly recommended!

author: Morgan U
title: Wonderful stay - clean, comfortable, great location, and excellent hospitality.
text: I stayed at ibis Styles Paris Cadet Lafayette from 29 August to 5 September 2025 and had a fantastic experience. The hotel is clean, comfortable, and well located. A special thanks to Mr. Khemais, Ms. Merfat, and Mr. Alam for their exceptional hospitality and kindness-they truly made my stay memorable. Highly recommended!

author: Paolo Q
title: Worst customer service!!!
text: We recently stayed at this hotel and received the worst check in experience you could possibly imagine. Abdel the Front receptionist who greeted us was super rude and didn’t want to let us check in as there were 3 of us and he said it was not allowed. The attitude and tone was completely unacceptable for a hotel staff to address customers checking in. Eventually we checked in and were harassed by him continuously during our stay saying that we can’t stay here in the same room. Not something I ever ever experienced having stayed at many hundreds of Accor hotels worldwide. Hands down worst experience at a Accor hotel in over 12 years. Would not recommend staying here.

author: Poppy E
title: Excellent
text: Great Hotel, very welcoming, very helpful staff, very comfortable bed, breakfast on top

author: Sara U
title: Ibis in Paris: practical, good treatment and great location
text:
We stayed at this 9th arrondissement Ibis for a few days in Paris and the experience was pretty good. It is a chain hotel, with what you know more or less what to expect: simple, clean and functional rooms. In this case, it stands out for its location: in a quiet area, less than 5 minutes from the metro, and a walk from the Opera Garnier, the large boulevards and several areas with life and restaurants.

The room was small, but well distributed, with everything you need for a comfortable stay. However, an important caveat: many reviews recommend staying on the top floor, but I would not advise it. It is the roof, and being a typical Parisian building, it has a roof in the shape of a loft, which makes part of the room have to be crouched. In addition, the heat of the veneer roof is quite noticeable, which can be uncomfortable if it is hot.

Breakfast from 6 to 10 during the week. There is enough variety to start the day well, and the hours are extensive, which is appreciated. The staff was very friendly and attentive throughout, and a detail that makes a difference: free coffee and water at reception, ideal for recharging before or after leaving.

In short, a practical hotel, well located and well treated, ideal if you are looking for something functional and without unpleasant surprises when visiting Paris.

author: Olivia F
title: Comfortable but very small room
text:
This hotel was well situated, very close to Poisonaire metro and not far from Gare du Nord. It’s also close to a park, laundry, chemist and supermarket as well as numerous cafes. 
Our bed was comfortable, and there were spare pillows. The shower was lovely. 
Breakfast provided a good variety of cheeses, cold meat, boiled eggs, breads and croissants, juice etc. The coffee machine was always available during the day, which is a great idea. There is a bar but we didn’t use it. 
Our check in was quick and the staff member was very helpful,and friendly. 
The room was quiet, and there was a small lift as well as stairs.Housekeeping was always finished by the time we got back, after lunch.

author: Louis F
title: Bad room
text: Terrible for a person of 195 centimeters , the photos of the rooms are those of floors 1 to 5 but on the 6 you are in the attic the bathroom is for children in the shower I could not get into the minimal room I barely managed to open the suitcase 13 square meters 200 euros absurd, breakfast great good service of course no one speaks Italian only the owner a few words , the nice place close to everything but the room just bad

author: Hannah H
title: Nice hotel, well placed and friendly staff
text: We had a great stay here. The bedrooms were maybe not the biggest I've ever stayed in but great for the price and it was clean comfortable and friendly. well situated a couple of minutes walk fro poissionniere and cadet metro stations. nice area and short walk to lots of restaurants. nice breakfast and airy breakfast rooms. depsite rooms being quite close together no noise from rooms next door. It was quite warm at night but there is air con , we just slept with windows open and no noise from outside which was great. also very short walk to gare du nord and gare de l'est.

author: Evie C
title: Decent choice if you want to be close to Gare du Nord
text:
This was one of the smallest hotel rooms I’ve stayed in. It was basically a narrow, long-ish capsule. But considering that, it contained a single bed, a small table that folds out from the wall, an open wooden wardrobe, and a chair. If you’re a single traveller who’s okay with a tight space, and want to be near Gare du Nord, this kind of room is a good option. I would not call it cheap, though; you’re paying for being close to a transport hub. 

In hindsight, I might not pick this hotel again, because if you have luggage, it’s a bit of a trek to and from Gare du Nord - at least ten minutes, some of it uphill. Getting to and from the nearest metro station, Poissoniere, involves a set of stairs, but that’s only about a four-minute walk. Overall, it’s probably among the more budget-friendly hotels closest to Gare du Nord that is not in an iffy location.

There’s a little ledge running above the bed that you can use to keep things on, and a smallish shelf too. Also, a reading light. The fittings in the bathroom were nice and seem to have been installed recently. The shower is tiny, and you shouldn’t really try to turn around when you’re in there, but I (think) I have used smaller ones! In the room I was in, water tended to seep out of the shower onto the floor below, but not so much that it was a big deal. All-purpose hair and body gel is provided in the shower, and handwash by the sink. 

The “view” was of the walls of a building, but I’d rather have that than a nicer view that comes with more noise.

Breakfast is the usual Ibis Styles one - a cold buffet, with boiled eggs as the hot option.  The fresh orange juice (that you squeeze yourself) is a standout. 

There are a couple of well-rated restaurants at the square down the road, and a Franprix and Carrefour not far away.

author: Rosie G
title: Stay in Paris
text:
Nice stay at this hotel. Very friendly staff.
Cleanliness hotel and top room.
Very good breakfast.

author: Emma I
title: Exceptionally good place to stay in central Paris
text: I have stayed several times at this hotel, and it will always be my first choice for any trip to Paris. First, it’s beside the Metro at Poissonnière with easy links to central Paris and Gare du Nord. Secondly, the hotel staff are exceptionally good and have made every stay really good. It is also quiet and stylish.

author: Oliver O
title: Managment style : zero
text:
A well-run company can be recognised by the reaction of the management when problems arise.
At this hotel, the manager's reaction is very poor : the customer who reports proven complaints  (about the cleaning of the room ) is termed unreliable by the manager.
So no positive reaction from the management to reporting problems at all.

author: Laura W
title: Excellent stay
text: Pension in a quiet street; Welcome, room, breakfast, availability of staff and service all without objection. In addition it is ideally located near the metro (200m, Poissonnière station).This beautiful establishment of the ACCOR Group will be added to My Saves for my next stays in Paris.

author: Diego F
title: Good hotel
text: The staff are very friendly and helpful, and the breakfast is good value. It’s a short ten minute walk from the Eurostar terminal and some good restaurants near by. The price was quite high as we were there during the Olympics but at its normal price it’s good value

author: Alexander W
title: A very pleasurable stay
text:
We had been regular visitors to the lovely city of Paris over the years but hadn’t been for a while so thought a short five-day trip was needed to see what was happening in Paris, and to see the pre-Olympic preparations.

The first thing you require is a suitable hotel for your stay and hence we came across the Ibis Styles Cadet Lafayette.

Now, there are lots of hotels throughout Paris, that fit many a different budget and purpose. For us, we're looking at a base with the necessary amenities, namely a very comfortable bed, good breakfast, friendly staff and great location.

So, the Ibis Styles Cadet Layfette was selected, based upon location and price. As many of our visits to Paris are by Eurostar, we like a suitable base near-by the Gard du Nord train station, with this less than a brief ten-minute stroll. 

Our room was a first floor (of six I believe) near the elevator. The thing to highlight here is that the lift is very small, so two people at a time is quite cosy! However, we didn’t have any issues with noise that elevators can cause. Occasionally, you could hear the neighbouring rooms, but not intrusive.

The room is small, but then for us it is a base. The double bed was comfortable and large enough for the two of us. There were additional pillows, if required. The AC works well, and the window opens fully for fresh air, if required.

There is ample storage for the cases and hanging space. There was a drop-down table that, when up, did not affect your movement around the room. A couple of hooks allowed us to hang up our jackets/caps, without being in the way.

Side unit that you can place items upon, along with a couple of USB points and electricity sockets.

A sensible sized TV that received several stations, giving insight to French entertainment. The WIFI operated very well throughout our stay, throughout the hotel.

The ensuite bathroom had a shower and a wash basin, and as is often these days, each having a dispenser for soap. The toilet of course. Ample space. Importantly, hot water was always available for your shower and wash basin.

The hotel had very clear signs of a recent renovation, which made the ambiance very pleasurable.

Within the hotel, in the lobby you can help yourself to the 24/7 hospitality station for hot drinks and cold water. There is ample soft seating should you wish, too. Here also has access to the staircase, if you do not care for the elevator. At the end of your stay, they have secure baggage storage, should you require the service.

The breakfast area had adequate space. Just take a tray, plate, cutlery, and help yourself to the options. You can select from the meats/cheese; fruits, natural yogurt; small pancakes; Pain au chocolat; various breads for toasting or eating fresh, along with a selection of toppings; cereals; egg boiling facility too. Naturally, coffee and tea (including tea leaf option) are available. Help yourself! 

And you can obtain your very own orange juice with the juicer machine that two oranges provide a full glass of very fresh orange juice. Nice touch!

Your options therefore are varied, or have the same every day, but will give you good energy for the day ahead. Breakfast is available from 6am until 10am (11am weekends). After, we took our tray to the stacking area by the kitchen, but the staff are very prompt to keep the area clean and tidy, with freshly wiped tables after each use.

Check-in/check-out are very efficient, with the support of extremely friendly helpful staff. 

Staff throughout the hotel do speak good English. They will encourage you if you wish to practice your French, but no problem if you are limited!

Location of the hotel is on a quiet street, but within easy access to wherever you wish to visit in Paris. There are plenty of Metro stations within short distances, or you can just walk/wonder in any direction, seeing many things that you didn’t realise were there. The usual bakers and markets are almost on very corner, so getting additional supplies are easy, plus anywhere you look you are likely to find many of the restaurants and cafes that make Paris.

For the price, the friendly helpful staff, the location, the cleanliness and amenities that we required, the Ibis Styles Cadet Lafayette in Rue Pierre Semard, was a very good solution. And one we shall use again; we have no doubt.

author: Isla G
title: Great value, friendly and clean hotel in a quiet location, esp handy for Eurostar.
text:
Great value and  recently renovated,  friendly hotel. 
Lovely staff, esp Marion in Reception, who looked after us very well and replied to all our enquiries via email pre visit.
Clean and  pleasant well designed room with comfortable bed. Ample space and facilities, and a Juliette balcony with view of the lovely quiet Parisian city street.
Esp love the Hot drinks ( as being a coffee and tea drinker ) in lounge area  up to 10pm and cold drinks available anytime. Fresh and tasty breakfast with a very good selection to start the day. We were pleasantly surprised how nice this wee hotel was and would definitely look to book again if travelling on the Eurostar as very convenient for La Gare Nord.

author: Charlotte T
title: Perfect for a city trip coming from the Eurostar
text: A small hotel with renovated rooms, a warm welcome with luggage storage, a varied breakfast buffet and a very reasonable price. A 15-minute walk from the Gare du Nord, and 200 meters from the Poissonnière metro station, it is an ideal place for a city trip. To recommend.

author: Taylor X
title: Staying on a noisy building site.
text: A construction zone! If you're going to do renovations, close your hotel! Not only are the rooms absolutely tiny, I felt sick with the smell of paint. The walls are paper thin and not only can you hear the banging of construction, you can hear the rooms next to you! Shame on you Ibis!

author: Mathis K
title: Very good experience
text:
Super warm welcome, all the receptionists were very friendly.
Free luggage storage service and automatically offered.
Free unlimited water and coffee machine (very nice)
Close to a metro
Very good breakfast (very generous and varied)
Normal room not very big but it’s Paris. On the other hand, poor in terms of cleanliness.
 We will return there during our next stay in Paris.

author: Miguel O
title: Wonderful vacation in Paris
text:
My husband, our 15-year-old daughter, and I stayed in this beautiful hotel during the week of Ferragosto. 
The hotel is strategically located very close to the metro in a quiet and characteristic neighborhood of Paris full of life and charming venues.
Kind and helpful staff. 
Comfortable triple room. Adequate cleanliness.
