Is a legal way to add the breakfast cost.

Very bad practice.

Stay away from this hotel.

author: Freya R
title: Will not be back
text: Hotel facility is old and dated, the air conditioning broke during our stay, we slept in 80 degree room, beds were too stiff, dirty looking paint job in hallway. Not worth the amount we paid.

author: Andrea E
title: Good experience
text: Great location, close to the subway, convenient for getting around anywhere. Clean and the staff is helpful; perhaps the breakfast could be a bit more varied and the breakfast room a bit brighter.

author: Erin R
title: A nice place to come back to at the end of the day on my business trip!
text: Great hotel and great location in Chinatown!  The rooms are very nicely designed for smaller spaces expected of NYC.  One of the better designed rooms I have enjoyed in NYC hotels!  I had a terrific view of midtown and the Empire State Building which I loved while sipping coffee in my room!

author: Alice J
title: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ An Excellent Stay – We Would Definitely Return!
text:
We had a wonderful stay at the André Latin Hotel. From the moment we arrived, we were welcomed with warmth and professionalism. The front desk staff are exceptionally kind and always willing to help. A special thank you to Joël and his daytime colleague, whose outstanding hospitality made our stay even more enjoyable.

As Canadians visiting Paris during the heatwave, we especially appreciated the air conditioning. Unlike many European hotels, it was powerful enough to keep the room very cool, and we loved being able to adjust the temperature ourselves. After a long day of walking in the Paris heat, it was a real luxury!

Our room was a comfortable size, very clean, and we never had any issues with hot water. Everything worked perfectly throughout our stay.

The only minor suggestion would be to add a little more variety to the breakfast. The food was fresh, tasty, and of good quality, but a wider selection would be appreciated, especially for guests staying several days.

The location is also excellent, just a short walk from the Luxembourg Gardens and in a wonderful neighborhood that's easy to explore on foot.

Thank you to the entire team for making our stay so enjoyable. We highly recommend the André Latin Hotel and will gladly stay here again on our next visit to Paris.

author: Nathan A
title: Hotel Andre Latin
text: Hotel in a very convenient area of Paris, well connected especially to the RER and buses, and lively, full of restaurants and young people. The staff was very kind, especially all the guys at the reception. The room is very well-kept, with all the essentials. The breakfast is complete and satisfies everyone. An experience to repeat.

author: Wyatt N
title: Nice hotel, small rooms, in a great location in the 5th
text: I really liked this hotel. It was in a great location in the 5th, about a five minute walk from both the Luxembourg Gardens and the RER B (convenient for both airports), 10 minutes from the Pantheon, and about a 15-20 minute walk from Boulevard St-Germaine, and the fabulous Cluny Museum. The front desk staff were very friendly and helpful. The air conditioning in the room was good, which was important since I had a room on the 6th (top) floor. I'm only giving this hotel a 4 out of 5 (I'd give 4.5 if I could) because the rooms are very small, which isn't generally a problem for me, since I'm not a big person, but might be if you are tall. The bathroom was nice but very narrow, which means it might be a challenge for someone with long legs to use the toilet. I don't know if other rooms have larger bathrooms. Other than that, the room was comfortable. There were also a lot of restaurants/cafes nearby, so it was easy to find a local place to eat. I don't have an opinion about the breakfast since I didn't purchase it, as there were many cafes nearby.

author: Zoe C
title: Great hotel
text: 3 Night stay in July 26 for my 50th, daughters 21st and 18th birthdays. Great hotel, location zone 1. Our room had 3 single beds very comfortable. Ballon’s with champagne and macarons welcome. Lovely touch. Air conditioning in the room.  Very nice area. The staff are fantastic dry helpful and friendly. Would return again. Our room 559 x

author: Louis G
title: Good for a city break
text:
We stayed in March as a couple. The hotel is about 10 mins from the metro so good to access the landmarks of Paris.
Breakfast was nice but in a small basement. The rooms overall were small and we found them to be very hot. Also I think we were unlucky that building work across the road was incredibly loud so meant we couldn’t open the doors.

author: Ian R
title: Hotel Andre Latin
text:
We spent 3 nights in a triple room. It was ideally situated just outside the touristy areas but within easy reach of Gare de Nord and Notre Dame. Everything else was within reach by changing trains at Gate de Nord. 
The hotel was very clean and well maintained, the staff were very friendly and let me practice my french on them.
The breakfast was quite varied and refreshed regularly.

author: Megan Y
title: An address to remember and share
text:
Small charming hotel nestled in the heart of the 5th arrondissement.... Neat and delicate decoration Clean and cozy room 
The staff smiling and caring 
In short... A beautiful address

author: Ella S
title: Perfect!!
text: This hotel is absolutely gorgeous would 100% stay there again!! we payed about £300 for flights and hotel for 3 nights. The rooms and hotel were lovely, clean and safe! the location was great, not the most central but had access to metros, but we didn’t use them we walked everywhere or got ubers (about an hour walk to Eiffel Tower). But the area around the hotel was beautiful still plenty to do and lots of restaurants/cafes. Overall, would definitely recommend we went as a group of 3 girls and was exactly what we needed!!

author: Lily N
title: very good
text:
came with my wife who was to have an intervention at the nearby Curie Institute... Like everyone else, I note an excellence of the staff.The rooms are well, excellent matelats, and perfectly soundproofed, although ours , on the 3rd floor overlooking Gay-Lussac street. the neighborhood is quiet, many restaurants of all types are very close...The staff tells us some, like "the little lost ball" , not very far, perfect...
We have to come back soon, no doubt it will be there.

author: George H
title: Lovely quaint hotel in the Latin quarter; good metro and bus links. On the RERB route so convenient for airport
text: Visited November 2025 with my 18 year old daughter. Mum & daughter 3 day trip. We chose the Latin quarter as it's on the RERB route from Paris de Gualle airport. 10 minute walk from the metro. Lovely hotel. Hotel room was comfy. It was lovely & warm which was welcoming with it being in November. Good shower which is a must. Lovely French windows in the bathroom & room itself overlooking a main road but the traffic wasn't an issue. Coffee making facilities in the room. Breakfast was lovely.  Luggage room to leave your cases if needed . All in all couldn't fault it. Would visit again.

author: Alice Y
title: Nice hotel
text: Nice hotel, and room 305 quite spacious. Bathroom and modern décor. We stayed 4 nights. Everything was quiet and clean. Ideally located next to Saint-Jacques Street, close to the Pantheon and a 10-minute walk from Place de l’Odéon.

author: Sean W
title: Comme ci, comme ça
text: The good parts are the location - handy for RER from Gare du Nord or Charles de Gaulle and into town, or reasonable walk there down Rue St Jacque or Bvd St Michel. Lots of local cafes and some very reasonable restaurants nearby. Reception welcome was very good and quite quick, if you check in on line in advance. Cost per night cheaper than downtown. Breakfast available. Showers were hot. The less good parts were the rooms were either windowless, dark-walled labyrinths or tiny (some with single beds) and noisy. Housekeeping a bit hit or miss as to whether things were refreshed (tea, towels etc); after breakfast nothing other than a jug of water available, outside what you might have in your room. Didn’t ever see bar open, no coffee, no bottled water, no light refreshments to purchase. Fine if you don’t need anything, but unusual for a tourist hotel above pension/hostel class. Breakfast rooms  were oddly one for those who had booked it, located in the cellar, and one for those who chose to pay by the day. Both limited in size and at busier times guests seemed at a loss to know where to go. Selection was ok as standard ‘continental’ selection, nothing hot. Hotel seemed popular with school groups and was clearly a popular choice. Some things - design of the building, they cannot change, but I don’t think we’d use again.

author: Grace R
title: Fantastic hotel in great location
text: Really excellent hotel. Staff helpful and friendly. Rooms not large but lovely decorated, lots of clean towels lovely bathroom and tea and coffee making and water provided. Maid service daily. Luggage room available.The location is fantastic near RER B line so easy to use train, can walk to Notre Dame and lots of Bistros, bars and cafes in immediate area so you can walk on an evening. Will look to stay here again next year and thanks to the staff for a great holiday.

author: Giulia E
title: Exactly what you think a hotel on a trip to Paris should be
text:
Traveled to Paris with my son for a few days, and was looking for a fairly reasonably-priced yet nice and accessible hotel to stay in.  They exceeded even my highest expectations.  Staff was super friendly (including listening to my absolutely terrible French), and tried to help us out when we lost his medication for a little while.  The hotel was really charming and immaculately clean, and probably the best hotel showers I've ever had in my entire life.  The location was perfect:  walkable to the Metro/RER, Notre Dame, and Jardin du Luxembourg, with lots of nice brasseries and such around, although a number of them were closed due to it being August in Paris.  
If I ever get a chance to come back to Paris, this is the only place I'll ever stay.

author: Camille C
title: A lovely bijou hotel that is perfectly located
text:
The hotel is perfectly located at the Notre Damme area of the city.

Luxembourg RER line B station is 5 mins - takes you to Notre Dame (St Michael)/Gare Du Nord and Metro line 4 to Sacre Coeur.

Saint German is a 15-20 min walk away - so the hotel does incur St Germain accommodation prices.

 If you are on an Emily in Paris pilgrimage, the filming location for her house is 5 minutes walk.

The hotel has a bohemian feel about it. It is really clean and we had a really good housekeeping lady who kept the room very clean and tidy during our stay.

Breakfast was good and they had a toaster so you could warm your croissants!

The only downside is the hotel bar isn’t operational. We were assured that this is being corrected in the near future.

author: Evie O
title: Paris boutique hotel
text: Staff were great. This is a great hotel to stay in the 5th Arrondissement. Close to public transportation only 1 bus needed for Eiffel Tower. Continental breakfast available. Tub very deep so only get room with shower if mobility is an issue.  Restaurants within walking distance.

author: Joseph R
title: Stay at the André Latin Hotel
text: Very good location in the capital and very pleasant hotel. We really liked our room. She was clean and pretty. We already came last year and the hotel was not as clean as this stay. Everything is cleaner, including a hall that looks cleaner. Day and night! We would definitely recommend this hotel to our loved ones! We are grateful for the clean place of our family and have been conquered much more during this stay than during the previous stay. The staff is also very welcoming and attentive. Thank you very much for the kindness of the housekeeper! We recommend!

author: Lucas G
title: Great honeymoon
text:
Great hotel.
Convenient location, in a very nice central area that allows you to visit Paris both on foot and by metro within walking distance.
Cozy service, clean rooms and attention to detail.
Breakfast always fresh and plentiful, with friendly staff, great cappuccino and espresso.

author: Marco S
title: Very disappointing.
text: Really disappointed with this hotel. The room was tiny, with an internal window that opened onto the inside of a stair well. If there had been a fire on the landing we would not have been able to get out. There were renovation work going on, at one point we opened the window to find a man on a ladder inside the stair well spraying something around the window. There was a lot of noise and smoking which seeped into our room. I spoke to a 'manager' who just shrugged and said there was nothing she could do, as they had let their agents know of the building work. We looked at the listing on Eurostar and Booking.com, and the hotels own website and none of them mentioned any building work at all. We would not have booked otherwise. On the website they advertise a coffee shop and a bar, neither of these were open the whole time we were there. The breakfast was terrible, if you have any dietary requirements don't go to this hotel, very very limited choice. If you want to eat meat, cheese, donuts and croissants for breakfast then this is for you. I would not recommend this hotel.

author: Amelia H
title: Nice hotel but extremely responsive
text:
The hotel was really charmingly decorated with tasteful decor and the location was good. Walking distance to the Panthéon and Luxembourg Gardens. The negative is the extremely thin walls. Every time someone flushes water down the sink or climbs the stairs, you hear a lot. The fact that at the same time as we were there, several groups of young people also lived there did not help. Became extremely loud with running between rooms and slamming doors after 24.00. No one seemed to be watching the kids. Called the reception who promised to contact them. Calmer that night but doesn't take much to make it sound. Bring earplugs. 
Beds that were unusually hard. 
Reception staff were daytime almost like a movie. Never been so ignored and barely get a good morning back when you said hello. They really did their utmost to provide the absolute minimum of service. You can skip breakfast. Small selection and every morning confusion about which room we were going to. Nobody seemed to know. 
Would probably choose another hotel next time.

author: Luca A
title: Please do not book this hotel during hot weather (summer months), as no adequate aircon
text: This is a really nice small hotel well located very near Kings Cross. I stayed in a small double room, with the following facilities: hairdryer, two shelves - one with tea/coffee facilities, safe, large under bed space for luggage, wall mounted bed lights, extra blankets, openable window, nice clean shower room with lovely soap and shower gel, and a great shower, with removable shower head, and space for shampoo etc, shaver sockets, heated towel rail. However, the shelves didn't really provide much room, the sink also had little space for anything but toothpaste and a toothbrush, there was a traditional key that you had to hand in each time you left the building (!), you had to knock on the door to be kept in in the evening (!), and my room was up some narrow winding stairs. But the worst part was (and this is the reason for my rating): I understand that this is unusual, but I arrived in the middle of a heatwave in London - temp around 30 degrees every day. Even with heavy curtains blocking the window, and a rotating wall fan, the room was just too hot, and my level of comfort during my stay was virtually zero. I maybe slept for a couple of hours in a row interrupted by wakening due to the heat each night. It was pretty exhausting. A rotating fan is totally inadequate for this temperature. I ended up having to dampen a couple of towels to lie on during the night, couldn't even wear my short jammies! What's worse is that I was there to attend two concerts at Tottenham Hotspur stadium that required a lengthy walk to the underground station after a very long day queuing in the heat, both nights, and the thing I really needed was some good sleep. I would not book a room here during summer months again, given climate predictions. If you're used to that level of heat, then go ahead, but I imagine that most people who live in hot countries who can afford a trip to London are probably used to nice cold Aircon! My advice is that if you are staying in London during June, July, or August, only book a hotel with proper Aircon. Even if you have to pay a lot more. If not, you'll just be exhausted, having had no proper sleep for the length of your stay. I'm sorry to have to give this review, because the price was reasonable for the location, staff were friendly and helpful, and the room would have been fine in any other weather conditions.

author: Isabella U
title: I will be back
text:
The ideal solution for short stays in London.
Cleanliness and order in the rooms, reception always available to guests.
Various solutions regarding means of transport: trains, buses, and the subway.
Highly recommended.

author: Olivia U
title: Hotel very well located
text: Hotel near the Eurostar station. Subway and bus stations. Quiet friendly staff. Very clean room. The downside is the bathroom is very small no small shelf to put toiletries that is what is missing in the bathroom. Very comfortable bedding. I will return to this establishment if I come back to London

author: Dylan M
title: Convénient for Kings X and St Pancras
text:
Small room, small 4 ft 6 bed up against 1 wall . Slightly below Street level, no lift 
,down steep stairs but young reception staff were very helpful . Fortunately it was cool in the basement and a window with a fan light that opened. Clean and fine for 1 night. No breakfast but plenty of choice nearby and at the stations. Reasonable price for London.

author: Zachary O
title: Great stop for travellers
text: Picked this hotel for its proximity to Kings Cross/St Pancras - just a few minutes’ walk. Perfectly good for a two-night stay. Room was up 30-plus stairs - no lift and a task with a suitcase, but desk staff offered to help. Staff were great generally. The room was small and had a single bed, which was all I needed. There are spaces where you can slide bags etc to keep floor clear. The ensuite was modern and did the job. The free daily cookie was welcome, and the complimentary bottles of still and fizzy water were a godsend as the temperature passed 34C. The cooling was by fan, which helped but struggled with the heat. It’s a very busy part of town so expect noise from outside if you’re facing the road, or if Arsenal have just won the league. Was very grateful to be able to leave my luggage in storage after checking out. Recommended as a stopover for travellers.

author: Ian L
title: Useful to know this small hotel, given the location
text: Convenient for Kings Cross area in general, and much quieter than we expected.  To say our room + bathroom was 'compact' would be an understatement, but it was very clean and perfectly adequate.  There's no breakfast served, though, so one has to go out for that, and the nearby options aren't that great.

author: Ryan N
title: Escape
text: Horrible experience. The treatment given to the guest is the worst possible. I do not recommend this place.

author: George Q
title: Exceptionally clean and efficient tourist hotel in King X.
text: I spend 4 nights in this hotel selected for location and reviews. This is one of the cleanest tourist hotel in London I have ever stayed at. The room is made up every day. Initially we were given a basement room, they are not pleasant, and immediately given the choice of a top floor room in the building at the back. This was perfect, room small but functional, lots of TV channels, new sockets, modern bathroom, good bed. Staff is friendly and available. THere is a patio which must be pleasant in warmer months. Issues such as lack of AC, building work on Crestfield St like in all of London, steep staircase and no lift, all of this is clearly indicated and should surprise nobody. All in all a very pleasant experience and we may come back. We recommend in any case.

author: Sofia U
title: Great location for trains to Heathrow
text: 5 nights booked. There is a massive redevelopment of the block opposite the hotel. Construction noise from early morning to evening. Thankfully I was given a ground floor room in the hotel's annexe at the back. The room was next to the entry door so I heard voices, banging suitcases, etc frequently. Bought earplugs. No breakfast served. Staff were very nice. The room was basic, a little worse for wear but suited my holiday. The hotel is a few minutes walk from St Pancreas/Kings' Cross station with all its great cafes and public transport. The Piccadilly line goes straight from Heathrow to St Pancreas. I would stay there again and hopefully the huge complex opposite has been finished.

author: David J
title: Small can still be nice!!!
text: Small hotel close to Saint Pancras station, friendly and spotless, supercentile staff, great value for money, which is a real rarity in London

author: Kyle Q
title: Wonderful over night stay
text:
Once more a very nice over night stay at this spotlessly clean hotel.
It’s just across the road from Kings Cross and Eurostar 
Best of all are the wonderful lady’s on-the desk  
Yes rooms are small but it’s part of the fun

author: Ana T
title: Small break
text: Victorian style hotel near two railway stations. Rooms are recently renovated, there is a possibility to make coffee or tea directly in the room. Comfortable bed. There is an inner courtyard. Pleasantly surprised by the value for money. I recommend.

author: Freya I
title: Good hotel near to St Pancras
text: This is a good hotel, nothing fancy but clean and nice, with helpful staff. The location near St Pancras, is excellent! have stayed here sevreal times.

author: Rosie Q
title: Excellent value for money
text: Hotel with very very small rooms and this is the only bad news. Otherwise the Service staff is friendly, the cleaning is done well and the area where it is located is served by 8 lines between metro and various railways and several buses. I would say that for London prices it is also quite cheap. Would highly recommend

author: Erin T
title: DO NOT STAY HERE IF YOU VALUE YOUR BELONGINGS!!
text:
We stayed at the Crestfield for one night on July 8, 2025. We chose the hotel for its proximity to the King’s Cross and St. Pancras train stations and it was very convenient for that purpose. Sadly, that is where my compliments end. This hotel has a massive security problem, primarily driven by its bizarre practices. We needed to store our luggage there because our room was not yet ready. Instead of placing them in a secure, locked area, they were placed in a doorless closet that was off the main lobby. This was a room that any guest could access.

Things were no better with our room. We were instructed that we had to turn our key back in anytime we departed the hotel. We found this strange, as it’s the first time we’ve ever been asked to do this at a hotel but chalked it up to perhaps a London or Europe thing. We turned our key in and left the hotel for dinner and a theatre show. When we returned late that evening, we asked for our room key and were promptly handed it without any ask of our name, a show of ID or anything. We could have asked for any room number. Worse yet, anyone off the street could have asked for ours.

This all came to a boil when we awoke the next morning to prepare for our train travel to Amsterdam, only to find our three passports now missing from our travel backpack, which had been in the room the entire time. My daughter was also missing a packing cube full of her clothing items. We searched everywhere to no avail and spent that day scrambling with the US Embassy and a dozen other tasks to try to secure Emergency Passports. However, these passports did not allow us to travel to the Netherlands or France, forcing us to cancel the remainder of our trip and scramble to book travel back home.

The hotel staff initially attempted to turn the issue back on us, telling us we probably lost them in transit or something. They then of course promised that they had conducted a comprehensive investigation, reviewing video footage and talking to the staff member working that night. This of course is like asking the fox to investigate why chickens are missing from the coop. Predictably, they absolved themselves of any responsibility, offered us nothing for the massive emotional and financial damage inflicted, and appear to be carrying on with their bizarre “security” practices.

I’ve stayed at hotels before that were poor in quality, amenities, etc. However, this is the first time I’ve had items stolen from my room. This entire experience has been devastating for our family and has cost us thousands of dollars in the process.

Again DO NOT stay at this hotel if you value your personal items. There are hundreds of other hotels in London that will respect your possessions.

author: Ian H
title: Standard
text: The location was great a 5 minute walk from King’s Cross, room was standard with two single beds, fan instead of air on and there was towels provided but they were more like hair towels than body, when we got into our room a woman walked into it and then apologised and left (she used a key), very strange how you have to leave you room key when you leave and they don’t ask for verification or ID when you ask for it back ?

author: Charlotte L
title: Beware of no elevator, must be fit to haul luggage up stairs
text: Good location. Easy access to the metro. Cheap price for London standards. If I was younger I would have rated this place higher as it has everything you need, clean, bed, tv, bathroom. However, as I age I realize I need AC and I need an elevator as we both thought we were going to die pulling our luggage up the stairs, and we had big luggage. Then it was so hot I couldn’t sleep all night. These things are worth money, I realize that now on this trip. It makes such a difference to a middle aged out of shape couple.

author: Noah Z
title: Great hotel close to everything
text: Great hotel small room but very clean very nice staff.  Our second stay at the crestfield and we are still very happy about it.  Close to St pancrass and the main metro lines without the nuisances. We'll be right back.  Attention hotel without breakfast

author: Morgan E
title: Basic hotel near St Pancras w/ no lift or AC
text: Close to St Pancras/Kings Cross station. Many restaurants and fast food places nearby. Loved the location but not the construction happening across the street. If you’re traveling with heavy bags or have mobility issues, be aware there are no lifts and the staircases are narrow. No AC or fridges in room. It was cool at night so the no AC wasn’t an issue with the windows open but the 8:30am construction across the road wasn’t ideal. Carpets need refreshing but overall clean property with plenty of hot water and good water pressure.

author: Ella W
title: Not a friendly place
text:
I booked one night in this hotel on a Friday for a stay the following Tuesday. Only non refundable options were available which is what I booked. The next morning, less than 24h after booking, due to a medical emergency, I asked for a free cancellation as an exception to the booking rule given the nature of the cancellation of my trip and the very small period occurred between booking and requested cancellation. The hotel refused. And then also refused a change of date so I can use this in the future. 
It is their right of course. Just not a friendly place. Everyone should know.

author: Hannah A
title: Brilliant Hotel
text:
Spent three nights here with my daughter. The hotel was really easy to get to from the Gare du Nord, just a 10 minute walk. The staff were so friendly and welcoming when we arrived and throughout our stay. The room was spotlessly clean, the en suite was modern and the beds comfortable. 
We loved the courtyard garden and the fact it was so close a metro. It made getting to the Louvre, Pont Neuf and Montmatre really easy. 
The area the hotel is in, is a little run down and the view from the window wasn't the most picturesque but we would definitely stay there again.

author: George E
title: very good stay
text: Excellent breakfast, located right next to the subway station that goes to the center of Paris and close to the Gare de l'Est

author: Harry A
title: Good enough tourist hotel near Gare du Nord.
text: Fairly decent, if basic, tourist hotel with decent transport links a short walk from Gare du Nord. Think Premier inn or Travelodge. Aircon in rooms actually works, and although not cold enough safety a hot day out it meant sleep was OK. Breakfast not worth the money, and rooms are small with minimal furnishings. Good as an inexpensive tourist hotel though. Bonus: authentically surly Parisienne desk staff!

author: Holly B
title: Clean hotel, great service, and very well located.
text:
Quiet hotel, very well-insulated rooms, excellent bedding, and friendly staff.
Close to the Gare du Nord and Gare de l'Est, and 30 meters from the Louis Blanc metro station.

author: Grace F
title: Great for short break
text: This is a lovely clean comfortable hotel. Excellent a/c Paris was hot, nice breakfast room with outside terrace. Convient for eurostar 10 min walk. Excellent value. Used metro nearby and  bus to city centre, as walking in area was not pleasant.

author: William I
title: Excellent
text:
I recommend this hotel. 
Good welcome, cleanliness, nothing to complain about.
Very good location right in front of a subway station.

author: Erin E
title: Good base near a metro station
text:
A nice hotel just 10 minutes from the Gare du Nord in Paris.
Nice well-kept room with limited storage space, located near metro station.
A good base for exploring Paris.
The bed and pillows ensure a good night's sleep and breakfast for a good start to the day.
Friendly and helpful staff.
Very good value for money.

author: Antoine Q
title: Highly recommend, exceptional stay
text:
All members of staff were friendly, helpful and spoke more than 1 language 
Service exceptional 
Reception staff more than happy to offer advice on transportation and tourist attractions 
Onside underground parking available 
Reception can keep luggage secure after check out if required 
Every room was cleaned and checked daily with fresh towels daily as well 
Continental  Breakfast is available every day however is an extra charge to basic room rate

author: Freya A
title: Beautiful, very convenient hotel
text:
Hotel equipped with secure underground parking. Modern hotel in a lively neighborhood near the Canal Saint-Martin. Welcoming and very friendly staff.
Excellent value for money.

author: Mathis C
title: Ideal from every point of view
text: Warm welcome, great flexibility, charming staff, impeccable rooms, excellent breakfast, in short, it's 100% top value for money. It has become our regular hotel in Paris.

author: Molly H
title: Friendliness
text:
Welcome, kindness, information, cleanliness are the main qualities.
For me, close to the Gare du Nord+

author: Charlotte F
title: Excellent hotel close to everything!
text: Everything was excellent! Comfortable rooms, everything worked perfectly! The location is excellent with a subway stop very close by! The best part: the staff! As a family, we value the excellent service from the entire team, especially Mónica! This will be our hotel in Paris every time we return for a visit! 100% recommended!

author: Miguel T
title: Great stay
text:
We spent 2 nights at this hotel,
Nothing to say, just that for a weekend in Paris, the hotel is really very well located.
Right across from the Louis Blanc metro station, which takes you everywhere in Paris.
Breakfast is really very good; it has everything you need to start the day off right.
The staff is really very friendly, both at the front desk and the person at breakfast who is very kind.
Thanks again to you and see you next year.

author: Harper L
title: Lovely hotel
text:
Nice little hotel, the the room was comfortable and the staff were very friendly and helpful. It was very clean and we felt very welcome.

We were allowed to bring outside food in to their breakfast room for our evening meal and they opened the storage and got plates out for us.

My only complaint is they seemed to change our towels daily and that seems wasteful to me. There was no signage saying to leave your towels anywhere specific if you wanted fresh or wanted to keep them which is what I'm used to in other hotels.

If you struggle with noise I would not stay here as it's right next to the police station, however I had no problem sleeping though the sirens and found the bed comfortable and had a great night's sleep every night.

It's just down the street from a metro too which we found very convenient to travel around Paris

author: Ella Q
title: Perfect
text: Perfect hotel in every respect

author: Grace J
title: Nice room, comfortable
text:
Decent sized room for Paris standards, but so noisy!  The police station is on the side of the building, and we got woken up by sirens blasting at least twice during the night.

The breakfast was terrific, staff was helpful, and the room was comfortable.  They have this weird powdered soap in a strange dispenser, so bring all your won toiletries if you stay here.  

The bed was comfortable and there is a closet, lots of lights and outlets.  

I would recommend this hotel to anyone who is a heavy sleeper and not disturbed by noise.

author: Erin S
title: The breakfast and cleanliness were impeccable.
text: Well-located hotel with very convenient parking, very clean, varied breakfast with top-quality fresh products.

author: Poppy X
title: Fantastic experience, definitely recommend.
text: Hotel Paris Louis Blanc was a fantastic selection for a hotel near Gare du Nord. The staff was very polite, knowledgeable, and helpful to ourselves and others, including a sight impaired guest. The breakfast selection is plentiful and prepared well. We found our room cared for well by the cleaning staff. Our stay was during the heat wave and our room was very comfortable and there were cold drinks available in the lobby. The location is very convenient and safe, with the Police station nearby, as well as several fantastic restaurants, bars, and a small convenience store. 10/10 would recommend and visit again.

author: Carlos Q
title: Good location, comfortable room, nice breakfast, friendly staff!
text:
Good location: really close to metro station.
Small but comfortable room. Bathroom okay.Excellent air conditioning! In this heat wave really top comfort! 
Nice breakfast. 
And very friendly, helpful staff!

author: Ryan B
title: Nice to meet you at the Hôtel.
text: Nice, well-kept rooms. Location near Canal St Martin. Breakfast was okay with plenty of choice.

author: Laura T
title: Great Stay
text:
Good Location.  But it is a 20min walk into the central tourist locations.  Taxis were useful and cost around €12-15 back and forth. 

Hotel staff were very friendly and helpful.

Room clean and beds made up each day.   Stayed in junior suite and balcony area was great to chill.

Restaurants near by were good too

author: Luca W
title: Sympathy in the service = 5 stars, very friendly [especially Mr. Carlos]. Nice place, very clean. Breakfast exce
text: Very attentive attention [special thanks to Mr. Carlos]. Clean and careful place, very good breakfast. Concern with the client. Central location, easy access to any point of the city. I recommend!

author: Chloe H
title: Excellent
text: Excellent hotel from every point of view: comfort, welcome, location. Top-notch breakfast.

author: Chloe F
title: Getting to know Hotel FIUME
text:
Hotel Fiume is a nice establishment made even more pleasant by the attentive and available staff, with a special mention for the receptionists.
Away from the major hustle and bustle of tourist crowds, it is close to famous places such as Villa Borghese, Via Veneto, and well-connected by several means of transport to the city's most popular sites, not to mention a vast choice of nearby restaurants, as well as a large department store, La Rinascente. We spent ten pleasant days there.

author: Manon P
title: Stay at Hotel Fiume.
text:
Exceptional in every way. 
Wonderful, friendly staff, they speak Spanish
Super varied and complete breakfast 
Highly recommended 100%

author: Erin A
title: BEWARE building work next door will drive you nuts
text:
Our whole stay was spoiled by building work being completed at the cinema next to the hotel.  On our first morning we were abruptly woken at 7.30am by drilling and hammering that vibrated right through the room. We then faced 2 power cuts whilst getting ready and had to sit in the dark for 10 mins as we didn't want to open the curtains as there were workmen looking in which made us feel very uncomfortable. 

I complained at reception but was told that the hotel was at full occupancy and they could move us but not until 12 noon. This was not an option as we had booked a tour for this time so we couldn't wait around the hotel all day. We came to Rome to see the sights, not to sit and wait in the hotel for another room. 

When we returned later that evening we were told by reception that they had spoken to the builders and that they wouldn't start any building work until 9am and if they did start earlier the manager would get the police involved. So we went to bed hoping we could get a lie in.

However at 7.45 am the next morning it started again. I rang the receptionist who said they would sort it but the banging never stopped. We got dressed and got out of the room as the constant banging was unbearable. Once again I went to reception to be offered a room for the last night but we were checking out at 6.30am the next day  and our stay had already been spoiled. I asked for some financial compensation but they wouldn't give us any money back as they had offered us a different room even though we couldn't move at the time that suited them.

author: Sydney L
title: Great hotel in safe area of Rome
text: Lovely hotel in a nice area of Rome. Although not so close to many of the iconic sites, it is near the Villa Borghese, and the immediate neighborhood has plenty of shops, farmacias, and restaurants. The friendly and helpful staff is the best!

author: Marta V
title: Excellent hotel
text:
A short weekend stay lovely hotel with a friendly team we had breakfast every morning good location for the restaurants
Metro a short walk

author: Andrea O
title: I could not say the main point of my experience because it was all EXCELLENT..
text: Everything in the hotel is excellent. Comfort, location, service, cleanliness, breakfast, in short, everything is great, and the excellence is completed by the super friendly attention of all the staff, especially Carlos. We already have the desire to return

author: Rosie O
title: Traveling for fun and ending in Rome.
text: Great location. Not in tourist area but super convenient to everything by walking. For the price this is a great value. Rooms and bathrooms are large by EU standards. Very nice staff from first arriving to check in, breakfast, room service, and checking out. We’ve been lucky to not have bad experience with hotel staff anywhere in Italy just this staff was far above in their attitude and abilities.

author: Tyler V
title: Very good stay
text: Quiet and close to transport and shops

author: Paige S
title: Excellent
text:
The hotel has excellent professionals. It's very welcoming. I loved the room. The cleaning service is spectacular. The breakfast is excellent. 
I recommend for those who want to visit or pass by Rome. If I go back to Rome, that's where I stay.

author: Morgan V
title: Nice family stay
text: Nice hotel very well located. Staff were attentive and available. Nice comfortable rooms

author: Ruby Q
title: Watch out no air conditioning!!!!!
text:
On approach to hotel seems hide in the back streets. Enter the reception and the staff were super friendly and helpful with a typical Italian design reception.
The room was a good size on the second floor.comfy bed and great shower. Only issue which was a big one for us is the lack of air-conditioning. It has been around 22 degrees in rome and the room was extremely hot!!! We tried a.c but didnt work. Asked the reception multiple times over multiple days to fix but they did nothing and told to open the windows( we did this but it was so loud outside we could not sleep)
They gave us a tiny desk fan but honestly didnt do much. It has been a long few days here with no sleep for sweating. This has really let down the stay here

author: Rosie Q
title: excellent
text: perfect atmosphere, nice location, excellent service

author: Lucy E
title: Nice place, great stay
text:
Very nice room, new bathroom
Breakfast buffet very rich
Staff very friendly 
Location very good

author: Harper M
title: Lovely hotel in quiet area
text: Great hotel, reasonably close to the center (we like walking!) The area was safe and quiet with lots of really nice places to eat. The hotel was welcoming and staff helpful. The rooms were clean and had everything you need. We loved the little roof terrace, where you could sit and chill after a day sightseeing. Breakfast was great, lots of choice from pastries to hot food and fresh fruit. Overall a great experience.

author: Claire M
title: Amazing birthday stay at the hotel Fiumi and will recommend to family and friends.
text: Hotel Fiumi is an amazing hotel, even though it’s quite central to all the main things to see, it’s a very quiet hotel with a very happy staff who cannot do enough for you to make your stay special. The rooms are clean and was lovely to have a small Juliette balcony 🩷. The breakfast was lovely and very varied with amazing coffee in the morning and nothing was ever too much trouble for the kitchen team.

author: Megan F
title: Wonderful.
text: Wonderful hotel friendly staff and excellent food. Easy access to all you want to do and see in Rome with Taxi rank nearby. We would be very happy to stay there again.

author: James W
title: All perfect.
text:
Fantastic!
Everything was very nice, room clean, rich breakfast!

author: Taylor S
title: Wouldnt stay here again
text:
We were extremely dissapointed woth the hotel, the pictures make it look beautiful, but when you actually see the rooms they are very old, tired and dated.

The first room we were given we went down to reception to complain and was given another room but again, very dated.

Bathroom is tiny, you can barely get in the bathroom and close the door to use the toilet.
The double bed was hard

Location okish

Breakfast, don't waste your money. We paid for breakfast but ended up eating out on the second day.

I requested a refund for the boat cruise tickets and was told to email and i will receive a refund. I have emailed 3 times and been ignored each time. 

So so disappointed

author: Leo M
title: Good trip, stayed 10 days
text: Hotel met our expectations! A/C worked great, no problems with internet. Family of 3 adults. Transportation from Nord du Gare was easy. Staff was friendly. Shower head was not tight, but could hold it just fine. We did not do the breakfast, plenty of boulangeries to choose from. We used #4 metro the most to get around Paris and occasionally #7 a 10 minute walk.

author: Alice B
title: Unsanitary bathroom conditions
text:
We stayed at Avalon Hotel Paris Gare du Nord for one night after having a great experience at Avalon Cosy Hotel earlier in our trip. Unfortunately, this stay was a huge disappointment.

After my husband showered, we discovered the shower drain was severely clogged. Water pooled in the shower and eventually drained, bringing up black debris, hair, and other unsanitary material. Every time we used the bathroom sink, dirty water backed up into the shower again. It was clearly a maintenance issue that should have been caught before the room was rented.

The front desk staff were polite and genuinely tried to help. A staff member attempted to fix the drain, but the problem remained. We were told no comparable rooms were available, and the only alternative was for me to use the shower in a different room.

What disappointed us most was the lack of response afterward. I emailed management with photos and videos documenting the issue and even followed up weeks later, but never received any acknowledgment.

It's unfortunate because we had such a positive experience at Avalon Cosy Hotel. The front desk staff deserve credit, but the condition of the room and the complete lack of follow-up from management left a very poor impression.

author: Wyatt Q
title: It was okay.
text:
It was okay!
What was really good was that the room, although it was in the attic, had a functioning air conditioning unit.
This was very helpful given the outside temperature of 113°F.
10 € for breakfast was not worth it.... Getting such hard baguette in the middle of Paris is quite an achievement!
The location is perfect for train travelers.

author: Lauren V
title: HORRENDOUS
text:
Absolutely horrible hotel. SO BAD I LEFT and found somewhere else to stay.  Lobby and front desk were filthy. Lobby floor had several broken tiles and vending was empty. The front desk person did not know how to make an additional key. 
Not a great first impression. The room was no better, extremely small. The shower had mold in it and dripped water. I could not get hot water. I wish I took more pictures. This place needs to be condemned not taking peoples money and calling it a hotel. STAY AWAY!!!

author: Katie R
title: Amazing location
text:
A little tricky to find the entrance at first, the hotel being on the peninsula of a junction, and approaching from the wrong side, once we got in it was clear there was some work going on, which would have been nice to be advised up front.
But the staff were immediately friendly and attentive - allaying any fears as an English traveler that the French may not like us too much!
One of the ways to get up to our floor was unavailable, but the alternate route was fine - there was an elevator that is only big enough for 2 people at a time (lucky it didn't seem busy) but being an original lift it added to the Parisian charm.
The room was a good size, although the bathroom was not completely separate, with the sink in the room, the shower behind a wall, and only the toilet behind a locked door. I was OK with this, but my wife would have liked more privacy from the shower - again, something that would have been good to be informed of up front.
Some other amenities were lacking that you'd expect from most establishments - such as a hairdryer and basic storage like a shelf near the sink for toiletries, or drawers next to the bed.
All of this loses it a star, as otherwise, it was a very pleasant place to stay. The room was nicely decorated, the bed comfortable, and throwing open the windows to the Juliet Balcony and having a glass of wine as the sun went down, or a croissant in the morning was exactly what we wanted out of our experience.
Location is perfect, it's only a stones throw from Gare De Nord, and the whole area feels very trendy and lively, lots of great cafes, bars - and only a short walk from the artsy district around the Sacre Coeur, and 2 Metro Stations that can get your around most of the city.
There are also a number of supermarkets and shops in the area, so it was easy to grab a bottle of wine, a bottle opener, and some cheese to enjoy back in the room.
We didn't use the TV, or the breakfast service (so many cafes, boulangeries, and patisseries nearby we didn't feel the need) so can't comment on that, but the morning's seemed lively.
Who knows, the score might go down if I was able to compare with similar hotels in the vicinity, but as it was, we had a nice trip and I'd be happy to stay again, with a few small improvements.
