author: David K
title: Great location in Midtown
text: Spacious room for Manhattan nearby Times Square and 5th avenue. Staff was friendly.

author: Sophia N
title: 50th birthday in NYC
text: Very dated hotel & room, had rain water hitting AC unit that sounded like a child’s metal drum being hit next to your ear all night very disturbing when trying to get to sleep after a long day. No tea or coffee facilities, however the location is excellent & housekeeping was superb very clean room bedding changed daily & clean towels replenished everyday, wouldn’t stay again as the hotel room took shine off a great 5 days exploring NYC

author: Giulia Z
title: Exceptional Staff
text: My friend and I stayed here while we were in New York for a short period. Overall, we enjoyed our stay, but that was largely due to the truly exceptional staff. They were very helpful and very kind during the entirety of our stay. The room itself was quite small. In addition, the bathroom situation was rather unfortunate as the water from the shower would seemingly get everywhere. Also, during our stay, there was construction happening directly outside of the hotel, and they operated extremely early each morning. It was very loud, and it was hard to sleep at times even with the earplugs they provided. I'd like to think we would have enjoyed our stay more if we had visited when the construction was not taking place. However, on a more positive note, the location was ideal. We had no trouble traveling around, and there are lots of great places to eat nearby as well as things to do.

author: Charlotte Q
title: Historical Hotel Nice!  Our room so small and hot and no windows.  Very depressing.
text: The hotel St James is located so close to Times Square, Radio City, and everywhere else for those that like to walk.  The lobby is beautiful with air conditioning which makes what happens after disappointing.  There were two of us and we were given room 206.  Very very SMALL. I hate being negative but I am not exaggerating, I feel like I was in a hot closet for three nights.  There were windows but what you saw was an alley like darkness.  No fresh air.  I don’t know what other room they have to offer, but I will confirm that I won’t stay there again.  However, It’s very likely that I will never see New York again.  Too much traffic, toomany people, semi poor air quality.  Ask questions before you book a room here.

author: Evan A
title: Great location
text: It's my second time staying here. I stayedfor 4 days. Arrived early and staff were very accommodating for an early checkin. The room was spacious enough since it was only needed for some hours of sleep and clothe changing.The location is perfect....walking distance to broadway shows, restaurants and time square. The building I just loved; it's a beautiful structure built in 1901. Would definitely stay here whenever I visit again.

author: Benjamin T
title: Hotel St. James, New York, 26 May 2026
text: We had a good stay at Hotel St. James on 26th May 2026. The hotel location at Times Square was very strategic as many of the New York city’s iconic landmarks were located within a short walking distance. We had some issues with the wash basin/sink of our room which couldn’t be fully rectified even though the management was very cooperative in addressing the same.

author: Ruby S
title: Location, location, location!!
text:
This was a great "budget" hotel (compared to the surrounding hotels).  I went to NYC when the temperature outside was in the 50s so the room without AC or heat was perfect temperature.  Thus we never had to deal with that aspect, which I know alot of reviews complained about the radiator.  The location was awesome - literally down the block from Times Square and couple more blocks to Bryant Park.  
I had a room with 2 queen beds and it was roomy enough for me and my 2 children.  It was rainy and cold on our second night.  After our Broadway matinee show, dinner, and visiting Times Square stores, we grabbed a snack at the deli next door and munched in our room and watched a movie.  So it was fine for a night to just chill.
I personally loved the "oldness" of the hotel.  My kids and I marveled at the steep stairs.  The elevator was slow but perfectly functional.  The lounge area was perfect for our friends to hang out while waiting for me and my kids to stop by our room for various reasons.  
The hotel will hold your luggage.  However be aware that it is not in a secure,closed off room, just a hallway where anyone off the street can access.  Thus, do not leave anything valuable behind.  My son took the chance and left his Chromebook in his backpack there instead of lugging it the whole day in the rain.  It was fine, but definitely a bit nerve wracking to leave that unsecured.
My only complaint was there was definitely noise outside the window.  Our window faced another building across a small alley.  For some reason, in the morning (around 7-8am) there was a lot of what sounded like construction noise.  My daughter had ear plugs after the first night so she slept through.  So definitely bring the ear plugs.
Also if you have mobility issues, I am not sure if there is another way to access the hotel.  There are steps to the front door, which does not have an automatic opener.  I do not have any mobility issues, but it was a bit awkward going up the steps w suitcases and kids and opening doors.  The hallways are also very tight and narrow - not an issue for us, but just a heads up.
I would not hesitate to book another stay here.  Location really cannot be beat.

author: Daisy B
title: Great bones but a real disappointment
text: We arrived at the hotel and were immediately greeted by the smell of pot. The front desk service was lackluster bordering on laconic. The elevators and public spaces were shabby and the rooms were completely lacking in charm or even basic artwork. It's a shame - the location is great and the property has the bones of a great hotel. Maybe it recently changed management? Anyway, you can do much better for the same price in this area. I particularly recommend either the Iroquois or the Algonquin. Similar price range but better in every way (see my review of the Iroquois.)

author: Holly D
title: Just Basic
text: We have stayed here before and the experience was ok. We knew it was "basic," but its large draw is its exceptional location, just off Broadway/Times Square. This time the “basic” was more pronounced and our experience less comfortable. Our room was bare and the bed not very comfortable. The first night was so cold – the radiator inexplicitly did not turn on - we had to get a heater from the desk and extra blankets. Throughout most nights afterwards, the loud rattling of the pipes was disturbing. We’ll pay the extra bucks next time to upgrade our stay somewhere else.

author: Claire G
title: Great place!!!
text: Amazing service, clean, great location, comfy, great check in and check out, always someone available, and super cute!!!!! Not too loud, great value for money, and tons to do nearby. The lobby is super cozy and the room was perfect! Would definitely return !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

author: Mathis C
title: Great location
text: It’s what you expect for the price - the location is amazing, The hotel - staff helpful and welcoming, not much going on in the hotel but plenty just outside the door. The lifts were a little bit scary ! The room and bathroom were clean. Very basic hotel but you are in New York so you’re not  going to be in your room very much - bed was comfortable and shower was mostly hot.  We had a sofa in our room that wasn’t needed but had no draws or any storage- the wardrobe was blocked by the bed so that wasn’t useable and the safe was in there so again not able to be used. I would suggest get rid of the sofa and add some storage.  Other than that room was ok not too noisy and warm. But great location

author: Jack S
title: This is a 2 star hotel but 4 for location.
text:
This is a 2 star hotel right in the location you want to be. The wifi is unstable so if you rely on using it to book shows and tours it’s difficult.
The bathroom is the smallest one I’ve ever seen with a tub shower combo. No great place for curling iron or makeup mirror. But you can not beat the location to broadway Times Square or Rockefeller center. The elevators are also from the first elevators and there is stairs to get into hotel. The beds were hard at first but it didn’t matter after all the walking - I say I’d pay more and stay at better hotel next time but the location is awesome and the hotel is very quiet so I might book again. Book this if location is hit high priority.

author: Sophia O
title: Great location, thumbs up all around.
text:
Location ✔️
Clean✔️
Nice staff✔️
Good price✔️

Such a great visit. Tiny room that looked out on a “courtyard” (essentially another wall 20 feet away.) But I DID NOT care - I was in NY to be in NY! 

They will hold your luggage early or late. Super nice staff. Slooowwww elevators in this classic old building. I heard zero noise overnight. 

Will return!

author: Giulia E
title: Shopper beware and informed
text:
On our first night, during heavy rain and freezing temperatures (31°F), the windows in our assigned room would not fully close, allowing rainwater to trickle into the room. At the same time, the only heat source was a radiator with no temperature control, causing the room temperature to rise to approximately 78°F. With no ability to regulate the temperature and rain entering through the window, we were forced to turn the heat off entirely and endure the conditions for the night since it was already very late.

The second night presented another major disruption. Around 1:00 AM, a rooftop compressor from the neighboring building began cycling on and off, producing noise comparable to a semi-truck directly outside our 12th-floor window. We contacted the front desk and were eventually offered a room change at 1:00 AM.

The replacement room unfortunately had similar issues: again, there was no HVAC control beyond a radiator that could only be turned on or off, and the window air conditioner had been bagged and left in the window, allowing cold drafts and outside noise into the room.

Additionally, we were informed that the water would be shut off from 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM the following day, which required us to alter our plans.

The most difficult situation occurred on our departure morning. Checkout was at 11:00 AM, and when we woke up we discovered that the water was once again shut off. This meant we were unable to shower, brush our teeth, or properly prepare before leaving for an eight-hour travel day.

When we raised this concern with the front desk, we were told that a sign had been posted and that we should have read it. I asked why management had not communicated such an important service disruption through more reliable means—such as a text message, email, a notice placed inside each guest room, or even a message on the in-room phone system. I also pointed out that if English were not my first language, a paper sign posted somewhere in the building would not necessarily communicate that the water for the entire property would be shut off.

The response I received was simply that I “should have asked.” I then asked whether guests are expected to ask each day whether basic services such as running water will be available in their rooms.

author: Oscar Y
title: Great Budget Option
text: We used this hotel for a mother/daughter trip and it worked well for our purposes. The location is perfect. Our view was odd: our windows looked out on another building's windows, which were very close to ours. It seemed to be a co-working space. We kept our curtains closed the entire time because the people in those windows could clearly see right into our room. If you can deal with that, I highly recommend this hotel.

author: Hannah W
title: Fantastic location
text: Hotel in an extraordinary location, already this is priceless, two real minutes from Times Square, simple but warm rooms. Great value for money.

author: Lucas H
title: Hotel St. James-Great Location, Short on Amenities
text:
We stayed at Hotel St. James in Mid December 2025 and were overall satisfied with our stay.  If you are looking for a hotel close to Times Square at an affordable price this hotel could be for you.  

Positives:  Right on Times Square.  Our stay was hundreds of dollars less than other hotels in the area would have been.  Multiple subway stations are located within a few blocks.  Numerous eating establishments close by to include neighborhood delis, small and large restaurants and multiple fast food chains are located within a few blocks.  Rooms were clean and housekeeping staff were very efficient.  

Negatives:  The rooms are small and no frills.  No coffee maker, refrigerator or microwave.  No thermostat in the room to control temperature.  We were lucky enough to have a room with a window (not all rooms have windows to the outside) that we could open to let in cooler air to help regulate the temperature.  Our room was on the 2nd floor facing 45th street and the street noise was extremely noticeable.  Lots of horn honking and sirens blaring at all times of the night.  I will say by the 3rd night we were able to filter these sounds out and they became white noise for us. 

Since we used the room as a home base for sleeping during our stay, we were able to look past the negatives.  However, if you are going to spend alot of time in the hotel, you probably won't enjoy your stay.

author: Freya D
title: Pleasant surprise
text: We were there as a family. Very comfortable room (bedding very good and air conditioning) and clean, quiet for our part. The staff is very friendly. The hotel is located in a neighborhood steeped in Hindu culture. You will always have restaurants open and the train station and its brasseries are 200 meters away.

author: Mathis G
title: AWFUL
text: Stay away from this place, 40 degrees and the ac was broken moved to a different room and the door wouldn’t lock and the reception staff said nobody would come in after he said our room number out loud to the whole lobby. Absolutely rubbish service we were told we would be refunded and nothing has been done they lied to us and never gave our money back. Dirty rooms and the staff did not help once we had to move rooms 3 times due to the terrible quality

author: Erin T
title: Honestly, it's fine and they have air conditioning.
text: Honestly, I can't say anything really negative except for the neighborhood (almost across from the La Chapelle station), which is lively during the day but questionable at night. Good air conditioning in the rooms. You can walk to Gare du Nord and Gare de l'Est.

author: Manon N
title: NEVER AGAIN!!
text: Nice pictures on the website are very deceiving it was clean but the pullout bed was horrible hard and just uncomfortable. The only thing I will say is that this place had air conditioning and was fairly clean other than but never again. We were three women alone and the neighborhood  was dirty and really felt unsafe. The police sirens were many all night. We checked in  at one door to and had to walk alone to another door 5 doors down past men just leering at you, then you get into the smallest elevator I have ever seen. Also, no one at the front desk in this building. It just didn’t feel safe. And then I called for more towels and front desk couldn’t have someone bring the to us because she was there alone so if we wanted more towels we had to go down the tiny elevator, walk over to the other building, walk past all the leering men in a dirty sketchy neighborhood retrieve our towels and walk past again. Also, the bathroom had a glass frosted door which even if you are with family you can see them clearly using the toilet or get a few view of the out the shower not very private. And then let me say something about the location, the neighborhood is not what people tell you about Paris there are many homeless living on the the streets or in tents, the garbage is literally all over the street it smells and again, I can not stress this again, it did not feel safe for women. We only stood for two days before I could rebook a different hotel. Never again!!

author: Liam J
title: Despite the location, everything you could want and need
text:
Unfortunately, the Sure Hotel is located in a not so favourable area. But, if like me you needed to be located around here for an event/visit etc. this hotel is definitely the best place to go.

Perfectly clean room, not a single part of it made me feel uncomfortable. Very comfy bed, excellent shower pressure and temperature, plenty of wardrobe space, more than enough sockets (plug and USB A and C ports), tea, coffee, and best of all, outstanding air conditioning (it was nearly 40 degrees Celsius outside!).

If you want to go to Paris to be in Paris, stay in a nicer location. However, you are only going to stay in a place like this if you have a specific reason, or for a short stay. It therefore offers everything you need.

author: Grace T
title: Awful place
text:
We stayed at the hotel for one night on our way back from Disneyland.
The hotel is located in a very deprived of Paris and the reception and the rooms are in separate buildings.
Upon check-in the receptionist was really unpleasant and not very helpful. 
The room was small, which is to be expected from Paris, but it was also not cleaned to a good standard. The bathroom is separated by a frosted glass sliding door, which was extremely noisy and stiff and trying to open and close it. Plus if you put the light on in the bathroom, people in the room could see you sitting on the toilet. 
The shower drain was blocked so when having a shower, the water kept spilling out from the cubicle.
The worst thing in the room though was the non working air conditioning. It was a very hot week in Europe and not having a working AC when this is something advertised as an amenity is a massive let down. The air con was on but we couldn't adjust it because there was no remote in the room. There was also no way for us to turn it off so we had to put up with warm air blowing on us and the noise of it for the night. We tried contacting reception but the phone in the room also didn't work.
Additionally, out personal details were stolen from Best western and we were contacted about it only several months later. No service recovery was offered.
I wouldn't give this place 3* it claims to be. And I would much rather pay a bit more for a safer and cleaner room with working amenities, than ever stay there again.
I would not recommend it to anyone.

author: Amelia Z
title: I strongly advise against it.
text:
I strongly advise against it. 
My room on the ground floor facing the street was noisy, with a leaking toilet, a clogged sink, a shutter that did not close completely, and a breakfast that was nothing special...

author: Rosie A
title: Worst Hotel On The Planet
text: First of all the location is UNSAFE for solo women travelers and families. The staff are exceptionally rude and hysterical. They play games like “mother may I” with diamond members even should one say “there is no bottled water in the room” the staff answers “because we do not like you” although you’ve not met before. Then when complaining to manager Clariss or front desk Destinee, should you say the noise is unbearable, the shower is cold water, the heating not working, they deflect and absolutely freak out as if you have hexed them when pressed to the point of saying “WTF” so they take your key out of your hand and keep you locked out of your room until they feel sadistically satisfied with their immature and abusive behavior. Try it out. Drop the “f word” out of exasperation and you will see the most insane drama of the century. These service people, except for Saiid, need mental health debriefing. Travelers who pay good money to stay in calm quiet hotel will find the nosiest and most uncomfortable lodging in the world when staying at Sure Best Western Gare du Nord, and bait switched to another hotel building several buildings away that has no front desk nor security. At 11pm a man came to my door to sell drugs. There was also a party next room that stayed up until dawn. I want a refund. Read the reviews. 3 out of 4 travelers say AWFUL, BAD, DON’T STAY HERE.

author: William F
title: Good location near Gsrd du Nord and Metro
text:
Very Close to Gard du nord Fantastic breakfasts for  French Hotel.. 
Small room with bed pushed up against the wall difficult to get out. Receptionists very friendly and helpful.

author: Alice O
title: Utterly awful
text:
Don't stay here, probably the worst hotel I've ever stayed in in my life.
So angry about the whole experience I can't even write about it

author: Oscar R
title: Forget it
text: Crap. I have stayed in 2 star hotels that are better. Room is small and can barely fit our bags in. The building actually moves/shakes. Heating didn't work. Took 2.5 hours to find parking after having to download an app to get access. It looked like we had arrived in India as there are dozens of restaurants an nearly all are Indian. Elevator was so small, 3 people max. Only saving grace was the receptionist.

author: George V
title: Satisfactory
text:
Location - Near Gare du Nord however this did not strike me as being a wealthy posh area full of tourists . The building the hotel is in must be very old but the conversion to a hotel was done very sensibly. Some features such as the lift and spiral stairs are a bit unusual but understandable.
Rooms - I had a single room the size of which was acceptable. The ensuite was satisfactory for one person. My room was clean and in good condition . I couldn't find a bin in the room
Value- Good value for money for Paris. The noise level was ok but i was not facing the main road. I didnt hear much apart from pigeons
The level of service from the staff was very good . My big negative is that i had a fraudulent scam message the day before i arrived saying that my booking was not secured. This caused a lot of concern which is not something I want to experience before traveling. It also makes me worry about the security of my data. I have never had this experience before with a hotel reservation

author: Henry C
title: Quick 1 night stay for Gare Du Nord Station
text:
We only stayed for a 1 night trip and chose this location for convenience to be close to Gare Du Nord station. It was a 10 minute walk down a very uneven pavement which was not ideal with heavy suitcases, The hotel was average, the staff at check-in were pleasant and they let us into our room from 12:30pm which was really helpful. The room was spacious enough for 2 but we weren’t keen having the bed pushed up against the wall as it was inconvenient having to crawl out the end. The walls are very thin and you can hear a lot of noise, banging, people talking out in the hall etc. The area itself was not the best and felt quite intimidating with the amount of hooded men lingering between the hotel & train station. 

It’s unlikely we would stay again, mainly due to noise and the area feeling run-down and crowded with intimidating people.

author: Amelia T
title: Horrible.
text:
I strongly recommend this hotel. I stayed 4 days with my cousins and the experience was very disappointing.

First of all, a sum of money disappeared from our room, which is extremely serious. Besides, the sheets gave off a bad smell.

The hotel is located in a very unsafe area. Another serious problem is key management: we were handed a key belonging to the cleaning staff, and we realized it after mistakenly entering another room one evening.

A deposit of €150 was requested upon arrival, with the guarantee that it would be released within 3 days of check-out. However, our departure took place on 2 January and, to date (26 January), the amount has not yet been returned. Despite an e-mail exchange with the hotel, the staff claim to have released the money and refer us to the bank. After checking with the hotel, it turns out that the hotel has not yet released the deposit.

I find this lack of professionalism unacceptable. I am very disappointed with this establishment and the handling of this situation.
